title: Consultancy service to develop National Oil Transformation Plan and capacity building
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND PETROLEUM KENYA PETROLEUM TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO DEVELOP NATIONAL OIL CORPORATION OF KENYA (NOCK) TRANSFORMATION PLAN REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Ref: KE-MOE-8323-CS-QCBS Credit No. 55260 KE Project ID No. P145234 . The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Kenya Petroleum Technical Assistance Project (KEPTAP) whose overall objective is to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Kenya to manage its petroleum sector and accruing wealth for sustainable development. It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments under the contracts for provision of consultancy services for the development of National Oil Corporation (NOCK) Transformation Plan. The duration of the consultancy assignment includes 1) the diagnostics and the development of the transformation plan to take a maximum of 6 months and 2) support to NOCK during the initial phase of implementation for a period of maximum 1 year, but not exceeding the expected closing date of KEPTAP: 21 February 2021). Objective The objective of this assignment is to develop and support the implementation of the ‘National Oil Transformation Plan’. This Plan is envisaged to be a 15-year long term strategic blueprint that is aligned to the country’s development agenda and which takes cognizance of the growing potential of Kenya and East Africa as emerging hydrocarbon provinces and the opportunities for NOCK to tap into. The scope of the assignment will include but not be limited to: - Establishing a robust business model (based on the recommendations of the institutional review as well as macro analysis and scenarios of how the oil and gas sector is projected to evolve) that identifies a defining value proposition and business focus for the National Oil Corporation of Kenya Define a path for the Corporation to develop a robust natural gas business, initially focused on tapping into the regional and global supply of natural gas and eventually leveraging into any future natural gas discoveries in Kenya to develop LNG and a natural gas industry Outline strategies for National Oil Corporation of Kenya to spearhead the agenda to position Kenya as a leading petroleum trading and upstream services hub Pursuit of local, regional and international opportunities that will serve to position the Corporation as among Africa's leading oil and gas companies Building the requisite human resource capacity and capability to support the Corporation's transformation agenda Building a strong financial base backed by a sound long term strategic financing plan to enable the Corporation participate in opportunities in Kenya, across the East African region and beyond Establishing support structures for enabling the National Oil Corporation to implement the transformation plan leading to a robust oil and gas agenda for Kenya focusing on among others the legal and institutional frameworks and operating model. The Ministry of Energy and Petroleum (MoEP) through the Project Management Unit (PMU) (Client) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultant”) to indicate their interest in providing the consultancy Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Assignment. The short-listing criteria include; Years of relevant international experience in developing major transformation plans preferably for national oil companies, Experience in business strategy advisory, demonstrated previous experience with national oil companies in a similar exercise of developing long term Strategic Plans and transformation agendas. Demonstrate in-depth awareness of Kenya and Regional Oil and gas opportunities. National Oil is committed to foster local content. Therefore, international entities working in consortium with suitable and qualified indigenous firms will have an additional advantage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers January 2011 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest . Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality & Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: Monday to Friday: 08.00 to 17.00 hours. Complete Expressions of Interest documents in plain sealed envelopes with consultancy reference and name clearly marked on top should be delivered in person, or by email to the address shown below or placed in the tender box at our offices on the 24th Floor, Nyayo House, Kenyatta Avenue by Thursday 3rd August 2017 at 1100 hours Kenyan local time. title: Review and Update Current  Oil and Gas Standards .
notice_text: MINISTRY OF INDUSTRY TRADE AND COOPERATIVES (MOITC) Kenya Petroleum Technical Assistance Project (KEPTAP) REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Credit No. TF-A3418 Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to review and update Oil and Gas Standards Reference KE-MOITC-11597-CS-QCBS The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank’s International Development Assistance (IDA) towards the cost of the Kenya Petroleum Technical Assistance Project (KEPTAP), whose overall objective is to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Kenya to manage its petroleum sector and wealth for sustainable development. It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments under the contracts for provision of consultancy and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services to review and update Oil and Gas Standards. The objective of the Consultancy is to review existing standards for upstream, midstream and downstream Oil and Gas, identify gaps in standardisation and provide recommendations. The consultancy will run for a period not exceeding six (6) months from the date of contract signing. The scope of the assignment will include but not limited to:- The scope of work for this consultancy will be to assist KEBS and MOITC to review existing standards for upstream, midstream and downstream Oil and Gas, determine standardization deficiencies or gaps that may hinder local participation and integration into the supply chain of the petroleum sector , identify key potential standardization areas in upstream, midstream and downstream to support local supply of goods and services to the Oil and Gas Industry, and pprovide recommendations for addressing these gaps. The specific tasks to be undertaken include among others : Standards Development The scope of work will involve the following: Review existing standards and the National Standardization Plan 2017-2019 (NSP) to identify Oil and Gas Standards required by the industry and produce a Gap Analysis Report so as to incorporate omitted areas of standardization for inclusion in the NSP; Benchmark standards against other East African as well as West African countries. Assess the capacity of KEBS staff to effectively develop oil and gas industry standards and identify gaps in the skills and competencies for the secretariat to develop the necessary standards; Quality Assurance Department Assess the capacity of KEBS staff to effectively carry out quality assurance in the oil and gas industry and identify the skills and competencies needed. Review existing product certification schemes in line with international best practices for the Oil and Gas industry and make recommendations on how to implement new certification schemes in Kenya and develop local capacity to audit/assess/certify. KEBS National Quality Institute and Certification Body Review the existing training on management systems and identify gaps with reference to oil and gas industry requirements Assess the capacity of KEBS staff to effectively train for oil and gas industry and identify the skills and competencies required; Review the existing certification and accreditation scopes provided by KEBS CB and identify gaps with reference to oil and gas industry requirements Inspection and Market Surveillance Departments Review the existing market surveillance practices and identify gaps with reference to oil and gas industry requirements Assess the capacity of KEBS staff to effectively carry out surveillance for oil and gas industry and identify the skills and competencies required; Metrology Department Assess the existing capacity of KEBS Metrology department including equipment, and staff skills and competencies and identify gaps that could hinder support to the oil and gas industry Testing Department Assess the existing capacity of KEBS Testing department including equipment, and staff competence and identify gaps that could hinder support to the oil and gas industry Identify gaps in Personnel Certification for Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) with respect to oil and gas industry Market Appraisal Identify laboratory services providers in Kenya that can deliver services to the oil and gas sector to the required standard. The client requires basic data on each with regard to: Identify gaps of laboratory service providers. Assess which laboratory services could be done by independent providers and which services should be done by KEBS facilities. 8. Recommendations Make recommendations on bridging the gaps identified Develop a clear strategy and related implementation plan based on the above analysis, with sequenced activities. MOITC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:- The Consulting Firm should demonstrate relevant years’ of experience in Standardisation with experience in Oil, Gas standardization and proven experience in Africa and provide no more than three (3) examples of experience in the last ten years of relevant assignments with evidence of delivery. This REOI is available for download on the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Cooperative website: http://www.industrialization.go.ke/ The KEPTAP project document is available here: http://search.worldbank.org/all?qterm=KEPTAP&_Top/country=Kenya&_Top/topic=Energy. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers January 2011 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. The consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality & Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: Monday to Friday: 08.00 to 17.00 hours. The Completed Expression of interest and accompanying documents must be submitted by Tuesday, 1st August, 2017 at 10.00 hrs (East African Time) in plain sealed envelopes and clearly marked “EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) TO REVIEW OIL AND GAS STANDARDS” and should be mailed or deposited in the Tender Box provided on the 16th floor NSSF Building, Block A, Eastern Wing, addressed to; The Principal Secretary State Department for Investment and Industry Ministry Of Industry, Trade and Cooperatives Social Security House, Block A, 23rd Floor P.O. GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE (GPN) KENYA WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP) Project ID No. P156634 The Government of the Republic of Kenya has applied for financing in the amount of US$ 300 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kenya Water and Sanitation Development Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, related services and consulting services to be procured under this project. The project will include the following components: Component 1– Rehabilitation and expansion of urban water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region. Sub-Component 1 . 1 Support to coastal counties: This subcomponent will provide finance to counties and their WSPs that are connected to the bulk water system for the construction and rehabilitation of water distribution and sanitation systems in urban areas, and for Technical Assistance (TA) to improve their performance. Sub-Component 1.2 Support to coast bulk water services provider: This subcomponent will support Coast Water Services Board in the rehabilitation, expansion and extension of parts of the bulk water system. Component 2 –Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in marginalized northeastern counties of Kenya . This component will finance short, medium, and long-term investments to increase access to water and sanitation services in Wajir town and in the communities near the Dadaab refugee camp in Garissa County. Technical Assistance (TA) will also be provided to support the Counties and the WSPs to expand and improve the services. Component 3 – National Performance-based Financing (PBF) Subcomponent 3.1: Support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments and activities - This will finance construction of new or rehabilitation of existing water and sanitation infrastructure for the WSPs/WSBs, with a specific focus on expanding coverage and improving services. Subcomponent 3.2 – Technical Assistance for national performance-based financing (PBF): This sub-component will finance a program of activities designed to strengthen Water Services Regulatory Board’s capacity for management, implementation and coordination, and M & E of the National PBF. Component 4 – Project Management This component will finance the management activities associated with the implementation support, including establishing and implementing a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system and training of implementing entities on safeguard and fiduciary policies. Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers, for Goods, Works, Non-Consultancy Services and Consultancy Services, July 2016. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND PETROLEUM KENYA PETROLEUM TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DEVELOPMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL INFORMATION MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR THE PETROLEUM SECTOR IN KENYA. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Ref: KE-MOE-8371-CS-QCBS Credit No. 55260 KE Project ID No. P145234. 1. The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank’s International Development Assistance (IDA) towards the cost of the Kenya Petroleum Technical Assistance Project (KEPTAP) whose overall objective is to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Kenya to manage its petroleum sector and accruing wealth for sustainable development. It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments under the contracts for provision of services for Development of Environmental and Social Information Management System. The consultancy will run for a period of six (6) months. 2. Objective The objective of this assignment is to study the current National Environment Management Authority (NEMA) operations within its functions and licensing regime for the petroleum sector and design an Integrated Environmental and Social Information Management System which among others can process, store, disseminate and archive all relevant information emanating from NEMA operations in reference to its mandate in the petroleum system. 3. The scope of the assignment will include but not limited to: - i.Study the processes of submission of reports, receipt and dissemination of information in NEMA; ii.Study the nature of information and records generated by NEMA and received from external sources, how the information is processed, stored and disseminated to intermediate and end users; iii.Study the current NEMA licensing and information management system with a view of identifying which processes will integrate with the current existing EMIS; iv.Study other Environmental Information Systems (ENVIS) managed by other relevant Lead Agencies and evaluate options to synergize with the ESIMS applicable for NEMA based on information needs assessment; v.Study the existing infrastructure to determine its adequacy to support the envisaged EMIS and make appropriate recommendations; vi.Develop an interim report containing findings from the tasks above; vii.Design an effective, efficient and simple to use mobile incident reporting system including required action and follow – up alert system; viii.Draft a System Design Document and Functional Requirements document for proposed ESMIS; ix.Make recommendations for required equipment and hardware; 4. The Ministry of Energy and Petroleum (MoEP) through the Project Management Unit (PMU) (Client) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultant”) to indicate their interest in providing the consultancy Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Assignment. The short listing criteria include; The Consulting Firm should have been in operation as a designer and developer of Management Information Systems for a minimum period of Ten (10) years advising government authorities. The Consulting Firm must have undertaken at least three (3) similar assignments including successful implementation. Should demonstrate experience in at least two assignments involving Information needs assessment, workflow analysis, system architecture design, and integration with other systems using Microsoft Navision and Share point within the last five (5) years. The Consulting Firm should demonstrate continuous involvement for the last five (5) years in information management systems, computer hardware, network planning and designing, computer applications/programming, Tele-communication networks and data storage management. 5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers January 2011(“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 6. title: Consultancy services to develop a National Petroleum development Master Plan  for Kenya that supports Vision 2030
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND PETROLEUM STATE DEPARTMENT OF PETROLEUM KENYA PETROLEUM TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO UNDERTAKE KENYA NATIONAL PETROLEUM MASTER PLAN REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Ref: KEPTAP/MEP/CS-31/2016-2017 Credit No. 55260 KE Project ID No. P145234 . The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank’s International Development Assistance (IDA) towards the cost of the Kenya Petroleum Technical Assistance Project (KEPTAP) whose overall objective is to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Kenya to manage its petroleum sector and wealth for sustainable development. It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments under the contracts for provision of consultancy services to develop a National Petroleum Master for Kenya. The consultancy will run for a period of 9 months. Objective The Consultancy develop the Kenya National Petroleum Master Plan (KNPMP). The Master Plan will focus on the Crude oil value chain, Natural Gas value chain and Refined Products value chain. The scope of the assignment will include but not limited to:- Review and study the existing literature including the constitutional references, existing and draft policies, laws and regulations including the Energy Bill and Energy Policy, environmental laws, draft local content laws, Vision 2030, Pwc study report and its gaps identified by NPMP technical committee and its recommendations among others Formulate a Vision for the development of oil and gas sector as well as the formulation of a competitive strategy for upstream, midstream and downstream value chains in consideration of international & regional aspects Provide a detailed description of the policy and investment decisions the GoK would have to take for the development of its petroleum sector, the order and timing of these decisions (hierarchy), and the criteria to apply when making these decisions. Support the draft of policy positions regarding the decisions that the GoK would like to make in both political and technical context. Prepare the priority of additional studies and research needs, the timing of these studies and a detailed description of the scope to be addressed by these studies. Develop a Risk analysis matrix with mitigation measures and offer guidelines and tools on identification, assessment and management of Oil and Gas sector risks Develop Monitoring and Evaluation Tools which include necessary milestones and review mechanisms. Provide on-the-job Training: on petroleum master planning to the seconded staff which will ensure continuity and sustainability of the planning. And Develop an Implementation Framework for capacity building on application of the KNPMP. The Ministry of Energy and Petroleum (MoEP) (Client) through the Project Management Unit (PMU) now invites Eligible Consulting Firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: The consultant must demonstrate fifteen (15) years’ experience of developing Oil and or Gas master plans, the consultant to provide at least 3 Oil or Gas Master plans for government(s) undertaken in the last 10 years with at least two Petroleum (Oil and or Gas) Master Plans in Africa and include the country (ies), Names or organization and addresses of clients and their signed testimonials, Demonstrate proven experience in similar environment preferably in Africa. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers January 2011 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. title: Technical Assistance to assess Judiciary's training needs  and develop a comprehensive  training plan for building the capacity of all Judicial Officers
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA THE JUDICIARY JUDICIAL PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (JPIP) CREDIT No. 5181-KE, PROJECT ID 105269 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI) TRAINING NEEDS ASSESSMENT FOR THE JUDICIARY- FIRM REF NO: JPIP/EOI/06/2016-2017 The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Judicial Performance Improvement Project (JPIP) , being implemented by the Judiciary of the Republic of Kenya , and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the Consultancy services for Training Needs Assessment. The specific objectives of the consultancy are: To ascertain the level of knowledge and skills of employees within the various cadres; To determine the knowledge, skills and abilities required by employees in order to use their knowledge elements adequately for them to perform their current tasks effectively; To determine the knowledge, skills and ability gaps of judiciary employees; To ascertain the behaviour that the employee must adopt to enable them meet the job requirement (attitude); To determine training needs of staff in the Judiciary; and To recommend appropriate interventions to the Judiciary to assist employees. The Judiciary now invites eligible firms to express their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications, capacity and relevant experience to perform the services. The Consulting firm must: i)Provide information on its background and organizational structure of the company including staff with professional qualifications, curriculum vitae of the key staff. Key staff should include The Team Leader, Human Resource Expert and Legal Expert ii)Be legally registered and operational for the past three (3) years. iii)Have valid Tax compliance certificate. iv)Provide Audited accounts for past two (2) years. v)Provide evidence of conducting training needs assessment of similar scope for the past two (2) years. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers published in January, 2011 “Consultant Guidelines”, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. title: Review of the Human Resource Function at the Central Bank of Kenya
notice_text: THE NATIONAL TREASURY FINANCIAL SECTOR SUPPORT PROJECT CONSULTANCY TO REVIEW THE HUMAN RESOURCE COMPONENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF KENYA REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT) Ref: FSSP/PIU/CBK/25/2016-17 Credit No: 5627 KE Project ID No: P 151816 1. The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Financial Sector Support Project (FSSP) whose overall development objective is to strengthen the legal, regulatory and institutional environment for improved financial stability, access to and provision of, affordable and long term financing. It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments under the contracts to Review the Human Resource Component for the Central Bank of Kenya to be implemented over a period of six (6) months. 2. Objective of the Assignment The overall purpose for this consultancy is to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of the Human Resource function i.e. people management systems including processes and to make recommendations to CBK management on long-term solutions / interventions to ensure optimal organizational effectiveness. 3. Scope of the Work The Consultant is expected to conduct the following activities: Conduct a diagnostic review of existing Bank structures; Propose revised structures to enhance organizational effectiveness and enable the Bank meet the demands of a dynamic financial sector and also achieve its principal objectives; Advise on the best options of migrating to the new structures across the CBK; Assist in HR policy review and revision through consultation with HR Department to ensure that the HR policies are relevant to the strategic goals of the CBK; Review and design a transparent result based Performance Management system that ensures objective performance planning and assessment of achievements to enhance productivity; Review the Bank’s compensation and benefits structure / allowances and create linkage to performance, recognition and promotions; and identify internal inconsistencies and inequities and make recommendations on how to address them. In addition, establish coherent salary ranges and overlaps that allow progression within grades. Review existing HR policies, processes and practices and align with human resources international best practices; Review job descriptions and profiles for each position in conjunction with the Heads of Departments and Line Managers; Review and validate the Job Evaluation results previously carried out and develop an appropriate grading structure that is linked to remuneration structure. Develop a fair and equitable career management structure that supports career progression, succession planning, leadership development and learning; Develop training framework that will support capacity building, motivation and development at all levels; Review and recommend improvements on employee welfare programs and medical benefits to promote a healthy workforce 4. The National Treasury (the Client) through its Project Implementation Unit (PIU) now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. Consultants should provide their most recent profiles showing their experience, qualifications, capabilities, references and details of past experience especially in the area of their expertise etc. The Consultant should have gained solid and tested experience in Human Resources Management, organizational transformation, and change management. He / she should not possess less than ten (10) years’ of extensive and progressive experience in Human Resource Management in a large busy public sector institution, multilateral development, inter-governmental organizations or a private sector organization at senior management level. The shortlisting criteria are; (a) At least an undergraduate qualification in a business related field with bias in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Law or Public Administration; (b) At least five (5) years of experience in HR consultancy, in particular Salary Surveys, Competency Profiling, Organization Development, Job Analysis, Job Evaluation and Change Management; (c) Demonstrated experience working with multidisciplinary teams; (d) Knowledge and experience of project management, policy development and research; and (e) Experience in emerging market jurisdictions. 5. The expression of interest is also open to interested firms who may wish to propose individual consultants. In such cases, only the experience and qualifications of the individuals proposed shall be taken into account in the selection process and not the firm’s corporate experience. Consequently, the ensuing contract agreement will be signed directly with the successful individual. 6. buyer: Ministry of Environment, Water and Natural Resources
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, WATER AND NATURAL RESOURCES KENYA WATER SECURITY AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE PROGRAM (KWSCRP) Project No.: P117635 Credit No. IDAQ7950 CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION Request for Expression of Interest Consultancy Services for Detailed Design and Construction Supervision of Mwache Check Dam and Demonstration Irrigation Project CONTRACT NO.: MEWNR/KWSCRP-2/009/2014-15 The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kenya Water Security and Climate Resilience Project(KWSCRP-2) and intends to apply part of the proceeds from this financing for payment of consulting services for supporting Kwale County in undertaking detailed design and construction supervision of Mwache Check Dam and Demonstration Irrigation Project. The consulting services include detailed geotechnical investigations, hydrology study, detailed design of the check dam, water abstraction system and pilot irrigation scheme, tender documentation, tendering and construction supervision of the check dam. The check dam, which is in KwaleCounty,is about 14.0 m high with a reservoir capacity of about 3 MCM.The dam is intended to: (i) retain the sediments before they reach tothe main Mwache dam to be constructed downstream which will supply portable water to the Mombasa area; (ii) ensure that soil carried from the catchment, due to erosion, by the flow does not end up in the main Mwache dam. The maintenance of the check dam should include a schedule of silt removal, for example after each rainy season, or as the design engineer, based on the expected catchment sediment yield may design for; (iii) supply water to a 100 Ha of demonstration irrigation project to be developed adjacent to the dam. The scope of the assignment includes: (a) Hydrological analysis, geotechnical study and materials investigations which include drilling exploratory boreholes, on site and laboratory test of foundation and construction materials; (b) Design of the check dam, irrigation water intake works, pump station and instrumentation; (c) Design a sediment management strategy and plan for the removal of the sediments from the check dam,managing both water and sediment to enhance the usability of the live storage of the check dam and the main reservoir; (d) Design of 100 Ha of pilot irrigation project; and (e) Supervision of the contractors' work and support to all procurement matters related to the project. 4. The duration of the services is expected to be 24 months. 5. The Ministry of Environment, Water and Natural Resources now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short-listing criteria are: (a) Organization's capacity and experience in design and construction supervision of similar projects which include dams and small holder drip and sprinkler irrigation projects (provide brochures, description of designs undertaken and supervision experience) ; and (b) Availability of appropriate skills among key staff. 6. The Government of Kenya has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Service Improvement Project-AdditionalFinancing (WaSSIP-AF), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 2. The consulting services ("the Services") include: a. Establish feasible water supply zones (District Metered Areas-DMAs) for all the WSPs except Mowasco (Mowasco is currently undertaking Zoning of its coverage area) using the distributionlines and water pressure as indicators. The consultant will advise onthe best positioning of the Zonal meters to serve each DMA to improvebilling efficiency. b. Use a water balance standard IWA approach to establish a baseline non-revenue water data for each pre-determined water supply zone (DMAs) of all the WSPs and establish a water audit system in such away so as to be able to account efficiently and accurately for all water produced or lost (NRW). c. Develop a program to ensure that all the customers served in each WSP are 100% metered. d. Establish, promote, institutionalize and assist in implementing Water Demand Management and Water Conservation/saving best standard practical approaches to control and reduce the NRW in all 8 WSPs as much as possible while using the available resources. e. Carry out a detailed diagnosis of technical conditions of the 8 WSPs, make recommendations to eliminate the weaknesses, prepare an Action Plan, and prioritize the actions based on minimal funds requirements and the most cost efficient which will ensure the WSPs becomes more efficient and self-sustaining. Prepare Specifications and Tender Documents for a software in all the WSPs for determining a Water Balance with provision for entering 95% confidence limits for all data entry items and NRW. The software should meet the international standard and come with at least a two(2) year maintenance contract provided where applicable. h. Promote Participation, Partnership,Active Cooperation and Solidarity for the sustainable management of the NRW at both institutional and customer level. Organize one stakeholder's dissemination work shop for a maximum of 100 participants under the cost of the client. i. Propose performance based incentives for utility staff which will promote efficiency and quick reduction of losses. Prepare specifications, tender documents for supply and installation, supervise installation and commissioning of the following in all the WSPs while focusing on quality ,efficiency and effectiveness: § Zonal, Master and Customer meters with couplings, strainers and seals. § Meter testing and servicing bench with all required accessories § Sectional Valves § Repair Kits. Identify at least two WSPs for which a Performance-Based Leakage Reduction and Management Services Contract can be designed, determine the performance indicators for these contracts, prepare bidding documents for these proposed contracts in accordance with the World Bank's standard bidding document for Performance-Based Leakage Reduction and Management Services (Output-based ServiceContract), assist in the evaluation of these contracts and supervise them. GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE Date : 27 th February 2015 Country: Kenya Name of Project: Kenya Petroleum Technical Assistance Project (KEPTAP) Credit No . 5526-KE Project ID No . P145234 The Republic of Kenya has received financing in the amount of US$ 50 million being an IDA Credit from the World Bank toward s the Kenya Petroleum Technical Assistance Project (KEPTAP) whose objective is to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Kenya to manage its petroleum sector and wealth for sustainable development impacts. The project will run from July 24, 2014 to February 28, 2021; the project effectiveness is 24 October 2014. Owing to the successful discovery of oil and gasand hence the heightened interest by Oil Companies to invest in Kenya's petroleum exploration opportunities, there is an encouraging upwardtrend in petroleum exploration activit ies in the country. This implies that the chances for Kenyato become a petroleum produc ing country are increasing by the day pointing to an exponential increase in the volumes of activities in the entire petroleum sector . The above development has made it imperative forKenya to prepare early enough to confidently confront the practical challenges that accompany the growth of the petroleum industry which takes place under very complex technologi cal requirements and environmental safeguards. For that matter, the Government of Kenya will need to increase the level of expertise required to manage the petroleum sector sustainably. Throughthis project, the GoK intends to build its human capital and to implement robust institutional reforms with a view to ensuring efficient manage ment of the country's oil and gas resources and the revenues that it will accrue. Further to that, the project will assist Kenya to effectively and efficiently manage the likely macro-economic consequences and the attendant impact on economic development . The ultimate goal of the capacity building initiative is to ensure that all Kenyans will equitably benefit from the oil and gas resources along the whole value chain. The Government of Kenya therefore intends to apply part of the proceeds received from World Bank on payments for goods, related services and consulting services that will be procured in the process of implementing this project during the first 18 months up to 31 December 2015. The project will include the following:- COMPONENT A: Petroleum Sector - Reforms and Capacity Building The objective of this component is to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Kenya (GoK) major institutions engaged in the development and governance of the petroleum sector to allow them to execute their mandates in a way that is conducive to investment while ensuring that safeguards and safety standards are metin accordance with international standards, including through the following: Sub-component A.1: Petroleum Resource deals Sub-component A.2: Petroleum Vision, Policy and Communication Sub-component A .3: Legal, Regulatory and Institutional Reforms Sub-component A.4: Managing the impacts Sub-component A.5: Institutional Reform and Strengthening of NOCK and KPC Contracts to be procured under this component will include the following: 1) Consulting Services: Undertake skills gap analysis Transactions Advisor for a variety of Government petroleum negotiations including capacity building; Institutional Review and preparation ofdevelopment plan; Technical assistance for drafting and finalizing a comprehensive Petroleum Policy National Communications Strategy (NCS) and definition of clear responsibilities for the various communication targets Carry out a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA) Conduct Gender Assessment to identify potential gender-specific impacts and opportunities ofthe petroleum sector Development of a resettlement action plan framework and policy Support through consultancies and resident advisor(s) further work on the legal and regulatory framework; health impacts of upstream activities and update of policy, legislation and implementation plan; regulatory impact assessmentsand guidelines and procedures for the implementation of recommended reforms Update legislation, regulations and protocols related to oil spill preparedness Institutional design studies of newly identified institutions Commercialization study Financial advisory services Development of a transformation plan Public awareness campaign Identify gaps regarding a National Oil Spill Contingency Plan and make recommendations 2) Goods: Purchase of environmental monitoring equipment, health & safety compliance measuring equipment, vehicles andoffice equipment. COMPONENT B: Revenue and Investment Management- Reforms and Capacity Building The objective of this component is to support strengthening of GoK's capacity to manage revenue streams from the petroleum sector for sustainable development impacts, including through the following: Sub-component B.1: Revenue Management. Sub-component B.2: Transparency and Accountability. Sub-component B.3: Public investment management . Contracts to be procured under this component will include the following: 1) Consulting Services: Build capacity to design and implement the fiscal framework for oil and gas. Contract a Resident Advisor for fiscal modeling Studies to be undertaken on fiscal policy for resource rich countries Development of policy option(s) and design studies for Sovereign Wealth Fund Development of action plan for achievement of compliance with internationally recognized transparency standards 2) Goods: Purchase of equipment (e.g. IT infrastructure). COMPONENT C: Sustainable Impact of Oil and Gas Industry Reforms and Capacity Building The objective of this component is to support strengthening GoK's capacity to integrate the petroleum sector in its broader economy, including through the following: Sub-Component C.1: Strengthen Upward and Downward Linkages Sub-Component C.2: Education and Skills Development. Contracts to be procured under this component will include the following: 1) Consulting Services: Conduct demand and supply-side analysis of standards, operational and contractual requirements; and identification of local content opportunities Skills assessment and mapping of skills initiatives at the Ministry level Strategic support for development of national skills framework for the oil & gas sector COMPONENT D: Project Management The objective of this component is to support the GoK in managing and coordinating the Project and building its procurement, financial management, safeguards management, and monitoring and evaluation capacity through the provision of technical advisory services, training, acquisition of goods, and operating costs. 1) Goods: Purchase of equipment (e.g. IT infrastructure). Procurement of contracts financed by the WorldBank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank's Guidelines: Procurement under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits (January 2011 edition), and is open to all eligible bidders as defined inthe guidelines. Consulting services will be selected in accordance with the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers (January 2011 edition). Specific procurement notices for contracts under the World Bank's international competitive bidding (ICB) procedures and for contracts for consultancy services will be announced, as they become available, in UN Development Business and in technical magazines, newspapers and trade publications of wide international circulation and in local newspapers . It is intended that part of the proceeds ofthis credit be applied to eligible payments under the contracts for provision of the above Consultancy services for a period of one (1) year (renewable). 1. OBJECTIVE The objective of this assignment is to support the Directorate of Public Debt Management to implement the framework for FCCL. The consultant will help in the implementation of theframework as well as in the review of projects for FCCL. 2. SCOPE OF WORK In order to achieve this objective the Consultant will work with the Directorate of Public Debt Management aswell as coordinate with the PPPU, Budget Division-NT, Contracting Authorities and any other agencies or stakeholders involved in managing the FCCL. The assignment will include: a) Establishing, institutionalizing and maintaining the tools, models and formats included in the FCCL guidance issued by the PPPU, including but not limited to the long term fiscal planning tool, excel models for calculating values of guarantees, project risk profiles and other required information formats. b) Collecting all information required for project assessment and for the preparation of all reports included in the FCCL guidance issued by the PPPU, by coordinating withthe PPPU, Budget Department, Contracting Agencies, Transaction Advisors and others as required. c) Reviewing individual projects for FCCL at both feasibility stage and post-bid stage, valuing guarantees, updating the long term fiscal planning tool to assess the long term fiscal effect of the new project and recommending to Director General - DPDM/PPPU for approval or other decision, with cogent and comprehensive comments. d) Creating and maintaining models for the purpose of measuring and managing FCCL in excel or other software as decided by the PPPU and as outlined in the FCCL guidance issued by the National Treasury for measuring, monitoring and managing the FCCL. e) Preparing all reports on FCCL as required under the FCCL Guidelines issued by the National Treasury including material on FCCL for the Annual Debt Report of the government, the Debt Management Strategy and other publications of FCCL f) Institutionalizing these tasks into the Directorate of Public Debt Management through capacitating counterpart(s) embedded into the DPDM. g) Organizing training and discussion workshops and meetings as required for the performance of all of the above functions. 3. title: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR PRE-FEASIBILITY STUDIES OF PRIVATE SECTOR RENEWABLE ENERGY MINI-GRIDS
notice_text: MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND PETROLEUM EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR PRE-FEASIBILITY STUDIES OF PRIVATE SECTOR RENEWABLE ENERGY MINI-GRIDS The Government of Kenya has received financing from the IDA for Kenya Electricity Expansion Programme (KEEP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services for Pre-feasibility Studies of PrivateSector Renewable Energy Mini-grids. The GoK has sought World Bank assistance for rural electrification in the proposed Kenya Electricity Modernization Project (KEMP). The KEMP intends to include an Off-grid Electrification Component. The component will support green-field mini-grid investments to be undertaken by the private sector in partnership with the public sector. The mini-grids are likely to serve communities with households, public sector facilities, businesses and industrial loads, typically with about 200 to 3,000 connections (customers). Majority of customers are likely to be households. The development strategy is to remove the principal constraints to engaging the private sector to partnerwith public sector to deliver electricity services to large number ofconsumers, powered by renewable energy sources. By mitigating these constraints and enhancing confidence, future expansion of services can proceed without or with more limited government or donor support. In this regard, the Ministry of Energy and Petroleum is thus seeking to procure a short term consultancy,to identify and characterize the optimal renewable electricity hybridmini-grid projects to be developed and operated by the private sector. The study will suggest the framework and propose the necessary instruments required for implementation. The study will be conducted withina period of not more than six (6) months. In particular, the Consultant will:- 1. Baseline Characterization : Investigate the 12 diesel and hybrid mini-grids operated by KPLC and characterize them ; 2. Site Screening : Undertake site visits and screen the 40 greenfield mini-grid sites identified by MOEP, REA and KPLC rank them and recommend 30 sites and the service territory they would cover. 3. Field Data Collection for 30 sites and GIS Mapping: colle ct data on t owns, villages and other community, distance to nearest LV, MV or HV grid or substation, layout of village includingmajor loads, houses, roads, any environmental or social considerations that may affect electricity service and on wind , solar or other renewable resources , f or the 30 selected sites and prepare a GISdatabase and maps: 4. Load Forecasting : Design and test survey instrument and conduct rapid assessments of demand and demand growth for households, public sector institutions, water supply, commercial and industrial loads for the selected sites. 5. Least Cost Electricity Supply : Using HOMER or any other models, conduct modelling studies and other assessments to determine the optimal configuration of renewable energy . 6. Network Reticulation and Connections : For a target connection rate of 65% of households plus other loads, prepare pre-feasibility level MV and LV network reticulation plans for the first three years. 7. Investment Requirements and Financial Viability: Estimate at a pre-investment level, the investment costs by the third yearand conduct a financial analysis to determine the levelized fixed tariff premium (dollars per kWh) required , assuming that the consumers pay the electricity tariff approved by ERC. 8. Recommendations : Based on these assessments recommend the preferred business model(s) and for the 30 sites, prepare a summary of financial, servicesand other outcomes, BOQ of principal requirements, investment requirements, grant support requirements, risks and risk mitigation plans. The Ministry of Energy and Petroleum now invites eligible consultants to indicatetheir interest in providing the services. Interested consultants mustprovide information indicating that they are qualified to perform theservices (e.g. brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.). Interested firms must submit the following information: (i) Experience of the firm to undertake works of similar nature (provide list of studies conducted of a similar nature in the last 10 years) (ii) Capability of key personnel, including their qualifications and competence in undertaking the consultancy works. Such personnel must include specialists in the following disciplines; a) Renewable Energy and Rural Electrification with BSc degree or Equivalent; b) Project Economic and Finance/Transactions Specialist(s) with BSc/BA degree or equivalent, c) System Engineering expert with BSc degree or equivalent d) Survey Design Specialist with BSc/BA degree or equivalent. Knowledge of renewable energy technologies and Rural Electrification is a must for all the specialists. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications, but one can only belong to ONE consultancy Eligible firms are requested to submit their " Expression of Interest" for this assignment to: The Principal Secretary Ministry of Energy and Petroleum Nyayo House P. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA MINISTRY OF LAND HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (MoLH&UD) NAIROBI METROPOLITAN DEVELOPMENT (NMED) REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION) Nairobi Metropolitan Services Improvement Project (NaMSIP) Credit No. 51020-KE. Contract No. MoLH&UD /NMED/NaMSIP/TA-26 /2013-2014 Assignment Title: Preparation of Feasibility Study, Design and Bidding Documents for Energy Audit in the Five Counties in the Nairobi Metropolitan Region Reference No . (asper Procurement Plan): 8 The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Nairobi Metropolitan Services Improvement Project (NaMSIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services ("the Services") include Preparation of Feasibility Study, Design and Bidding Documents for Energy Audit in the Five Counties in the Nairobi Metropolitan Region. The overall objective of the energy audit is to identify energy savings and conservation measures, identify opportunities for energy generation (i.e. though solid waste management measures, among others) if any, and propose implementation modalities for the implementation of the proposed measures. Based on the report, the consultant will prepare bidding documents in compliance with the World Bank guidelines and Nairobi Metro 2030 strategy programmes under the safety and security pillar. The services to be carried out will include but not be limited to: a) Review the findings of a previously conducted energy efficiency study for the Nairobi City County . b) Study and analyze the energy consumption and subsequent costs within the five counties; c) Identify (i) potential energy conservation measures and (ii) potential energy production opportunities; d) Develop a draft set of prioritized investments/policies to reduce the energy costs; e) Conduct a "crude" political economy analysis by gathering stakeholder (including the ministry and the counties) feedback on the draft set of prioritized polices and investments; f) Recommend a close-to-final priority set of investments (or combination of policies and investments) for each county/the metropolitan region based on the analysis above. For priority investments: g) Carry out pre-feasibility studies to answer any questions from above in order to develop the final prioritized list of investments for each county and then combine these priorities in a priority list for the metropolitan region; h) Prepare economic justification of investment by either cost benefit analysis or, for small works, below US$ 500,000, by cost effectiveness; i) Consult stakeholders (including the ministry, counties, potential financing partners), and recommend final set of investments and accompanying policies to be adopted; j) Prepare draft & final engineering designs for the final set of the three highest ranked investments in the metropolitan region; k) Prepare bidding documents for the finalized set of investments according to World Bank guidelines and Engineer's Estimate for the agreed works; l) Draft terms of reference for the client's review, which should include the technical composition, of a team which will evaluate the bids and supervise the works; m) Prepare relevant operations and maintenance manuals where necessary. The services are expected to require approximately six months. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF kENYA MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, WATER AND NATURAL RESOURCES KENYA WATER SECURITY AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE PROJECT GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE Project ID No. P117635 The Government of Kenya has applied for financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kenya Water Security and Climate Resilience Program (KWSCRP). Kenya Water Security and Climate Resilience Project Phase 1 ( KWSCRP-1) is the first investment operation under KWSCRP. The Government will implement the project over 7 (seven) years , and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, related services and consulting services to be procured. The project development objectives of KWSCRP-1 are to: (i) increase availability and productivity of irrigation water for project beneficiaries; and (ii) enhance the institutional framework and strengthen capacity for water security and climate resilience for the country. Co-financing under KWSCRP-1 has been requested from the German Development Bank (KfW) for Lower Nzoia Irrigation Scheme Phase 1 (refer below). The Co-financing Agreement for the Lower Nzoia Irrigation Scheme Phase 1 is expected to be effective by December 31, 2013. The project will have three inter-related components supporting the project development objective: (i) water resources development; (ii) effective water sector institutions; and (iii)support for project implementation Component 1 will support climate resilience and water security for economic growth by financing the Lower Nzoia Irrigation Scheme Phase 1 and by progressively building a longer-term investment pipeline. Component 1 includes two sub-components: (i) Water Sector Investments and (ii) Water Investment Pipeline. The Lower Nzoia Irrigation Project-Phase I, to be financed under this component, will be the first investment in the Kenya Water Security Project series. Located in Siaya and Busia Counties in Western Kenya near the town of Kisumu, this public irrigation scheme would irrigate about 4,000 hectares and would comprise the following components: a. Construction of the irrigation and drainage infrastructure; b. Support to agricultural production and establishment of market linkages through a value chain approach; c. Support to the efficient operation of the scheme as well as to progressive transfer of responsibilities and decision making from the National Irrigation Board (NIB) to farmers organizedin Irrigation Water Users Associations (IWUAs). Component 2 will support the current sector institutions, as well asthe preparation, implementation and full functioning of the new and proposed legal and institutional framework resulting from alignments with the Constitution of Kenya 2010. It will also support integrated and participatory basin planning, including developing the requisite knowledge base and building capacity and institutional partnerships for effective water management and planning. The overall objective of this component will be to strengthen the enabling institutional and legal framework to sustainably advance Kenya's vast water sector investment program in order to achievewater security and climate resilience. To this end, Component 2 includes two sub-components: (i) support for water sector transition and reforms and (ii) strengthening water management and planning. Component 3 .will support the establishment of the PMU to provide for effective project implementation through the completion of the KWSCRP-1 and throughout the reform period (that is, prior to the launch of the reforms, during thetransition, and during the post reform period). Specifically, this component will finance the required office space, goods (e.g., vehicles), equipment (e.g., computers), staff, consultant services, travel, training and operating costs that will allow the PMU to carry out its responsibilities for project implementation. These responsibilities include project management andcoordination, procurement and financial management, project monitoring and evaluation (including impact evaluation), social and environmental safeguards management and oversight, and strategic project communications and outreach. The main contracts under the project are the following: Works Construction of Lower Nzoia Irrigation and Drainage Construction of operational centresin sub basins - min. infrastructure. Construction of self-contained rooms, offices, kitchen, drying floor, packing centres and cold rooms in the project site. Construction of sheds, stores and staff offices, preparation of nursery, Office Up gradation (incl. operational control rooms, documentation centre) Goods Farm machinery, equipment and supplies Hydromet ITequipment Meteorological Monitoring equipment Surface Water Monitoring equipment Ground Water monitoring equipment Information/Technology Equipment Water Quality Laboratory Equipment Office and computing machinery, equipment and supplies. Motor vehicles and motorbikes. Consultancy Implementation Consultant to support the National Irrigation Board (NIB) in implementation ofthe lower Nzoia project. Implementation Consultant (support to transition and legislative reforms in the Water sector ) Implementation Support Consultants to undertake Legislative reforms in Water Sector Implementation Support Consultant to undertake Capacity building of water sector institutions including induction workshops Technical Staff and Advisors for PMU Legal, accounting, auditing, business, managementand related services. Architectural, engineering, construction and related technical consultancy services. Consulting services will be selected in accordance with the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers (January 2011). The KWSCRP envisages financing of several multipurpose and single purposed dams under study during implementation in various parts of the country. As part of coordination and supporting the implementation of the project activities, the Government of Kenya wishes to hire a Dam Safety Panel of Experts (DSPE) - Dam Engineering Design and Construction for missions with an estimated duration of 10 days permission . DSPE will consist of at least three (3) permanent members covering the areas of (i) dam engineering design and construction, (ii) hydrology, and (iii) geotechnical engineering respectively, one of whom will be appointed as the Chairman of the Panel, responsible for coordinating its activities, presiding at meetings, making finaldecisions and preparing the Panel's reports. The Panel Chairperson will assist the Client to identify other experts, subject to specific requirements, to be mobilized for implementing specialized tasks. Objective of the Consultancy and Scope of Services The overall objective of the DSPE is to provide independent review and recommendations to Government of Kenya for ensuring that safety issues of dams to be financed by the KWSCRP are adequately addressed in terms of design, construction, operation and maintenance as required by the Dam Safety safeguard policy (OP4.37) of the World Bank. The safety assessment of dams and associated structures will be carried out in line with relevant legislation, current guidelines, standards, regulations of the Republic of Kenya, as well as the international standards, such as International Commission on Large Dams (ICOLD). In addition, DSPE will provide the Client with suggestions on necessary solutions to increase the safety of the dams andits associated structures to the acceptable safety standard corresponding to international practices. DSPE will be established at design phase and will be maintained throughout the project construction phase and even the first period of operation phase. The Panel will be maintained on an on-call basis and will operate through periodic working missions at various stages of design, construction and operation phases of the dams. The DSPE Dam Engineering Design and Construction Expert in coordination with other panelists will review and assess all relevant technical / safety related aspects of the project. 6. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA ___________________________ THE JUDICIARY REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST EXTENSION OF SUBMISSION DATE (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION) PROJECT: JUDICIAL PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT PROJECT Credit Number 5181 Assignment Title: CORRUPTION MAPPINGAND DEVELOPMENT OF A GOVERNANCE AND ANTI-CORRUPTION (GAC) STRATEGY/PLAN. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES, RISK MANAGEMENT SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) COUNTRY : K enya PROJECT NAME : Kenya Electricity Expansion Project Credit No. : KE-47430 Assignment Title : Implementation of the Enterprise Risk Management Program Project ID number : P103037 The Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of increasing electricity connections country-wide both rural and urban areas. title:
RECRUITMENT OF AN EXTERNAL AFFAIRS EXPERT 
FOR THE PUBLIC PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP SECRETARIAT (PPPU)
IN KENYA
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA MINISTRY OF FINANCE RECRUITMENT OF AN EXTERNAL AFFAIRS EXPERT FOR THE PUBLIC PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP SECRETARIAT (PPPU) IN KENYA The Government of Kenya (GoK) in conjunction with the World Bank is implementing an Infrastructure Finance and Public Private Partnerships Project (IFPPP) whose overall development objective is to increase private investment in the Kenyan infrastructuremarket by improving the enabling environment to generate a pipeline of bankable PPP projects. This objective will be achieved through the provision of technical expertise and building capacity to implement the Government's Public Private Partnership (PPP) National program in Kenya . The Public Private Partnerships Secretariat (PPPU) at the Ministry of Finance is looking for a highly motivated local expert, for a period ofone (1) year renewable for a further term of one (1) year, to fill the position of: External Affairs Expert (1 Post) The PPP External Affairs Expert is expected to perform the following tasks: · Supervise creation and operation of PPF and relationship with donor organizations · Manage PPF and CVG Funds and relationship with donor organizations · Manage promotional activities of PPPU and PPP projects' and investor relations · Establish and maintain relationshipswith major international donors and multilateral organizations · Confer with other managers to identify trends and key group interests and concerns or to provide advice onbusiness decisions · Communicate training plans for focusgroups, PPPU staff, consultants, instructors and line ministry representatives and other stakeholders working with the PPPU to major donors · Ensure efficient use of donors funding and support to PPP Unit (administrative and reporting component of fund management) · Ensure donors' database is up-to-date and accurate · Plan and implement the PPPU website and supervise the updating process · Ensure efficient management of PPP Project Facilitation Fund (administrative and reporting component of fund management) · Act as a secretariat for PFF Management · Issue periodical reports to donor organizations on funds utilization · Execute public relations programs & strategies designed to create the public image for PPP Unit · Establish and maintain relationshipswith representatives of Press, media community and public interest groups · Execute communication of informational programs and publications · Arrange public appearances, conferences (locally & internationally), workshops for the PPP unit to increase awareness and to promote PPP knowledge · Consult with media entities or pressto arrange promotional campaigns in all types of media · Execute effective communication withAuthorities/line ministries · Execute training plans for focus groups, PPPU staff, PPP Nodes staff, consultants, instructors and line ministries representatives and other stakeholders working with the PPPU · Develop & coordinate press releases, PPPU publications and media updates with the press community · Keep track on conferences and seminars to obtain information for use in training programs, or to inform management of training program status · Ensure the PPPU database is up-to-date and accurate · Coordinate Investors' conferences · Carry out any other assigned duties related to PPP. QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: · A minimum of university degree in Communication/Public Relations /Marketing ora related field is necessary. · Prior experience in dealing with donor organization is a plus. · Strong awareness of Kenya's market and public opinion. · Strong relationship with media figures and agencies. · Excellent knowledge of English spoken and written. · Team leadership and multitasking skills is necessary. · A Communications / Public Relations expert / Marketing Executive with at least 7-10 years' experience in the field of marketing & media campaigns. · Should have successfully carried out a public awareness campaign. Complete Application documents (curriculum vitae with details of your qualifications, experience, day and evening telephone numbers, email address and names of three referees) with Position reference andname clearly marked on top should be emailed or sent to the address below. notice_text: FINANCIAL AND LEGAL SECTOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT CONSULTANCY TO EVALUATE AND DETERMINE THE RATE OF COMMERCIAL CASE CLEARANCE REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST Ref: FLSTAP/LS/JUD/EOI/08/2012-2013 Credit No. 3992 KE Project ID No. P083250 . This request for Expression of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice (GPN) for this project that appeared in United Nation Development Business No. 674 of March 16, 2006and was updated in UN Development Business No. 707 of July 31, 2007. The Government of Kenya has received a credit from the International Development Association and a Grant from the UK Department for International Development (DFID) towards the cost of the Financial and Legal Sector Technical Assistance Project (FLSTAP). It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments under the contracts for provision of the above Consultancy services and is for a period of 6 weeks. 1. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT The main objective of the consultancy is to determine the rate of case clearance of commercial cases within the Commercial Division of the High Court of Kenya between the year 2007 to December 2012; and compare improvements if any, in the performance of commercial courts the period under review; identify, apportion and attribute the relevant factors that may have contributed to the changes and improvements to case clearance ratios. 2. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTANT SERVICES) RE-ADVERTISEMENT COUNTRY: KENYA NAME OF PROJECT: NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT PROJECT CONSULTING SERVICES FOR A STUDY OF GROUNDWATER RECHARGE TO MZIMA AND OTHER ASSOICATED SPRINGS CREDIT NO. 4277 KE PROJECT ID. NO. WRMA/NRM/EO1/1 The Water Resources Management Authority has received financing from the WorldBank towards the cost of the Natural Resources Management Project andintends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services. One of the key objectives of theNatural Resources Management Project is to strengthen the capacity ofWRMA to effectively discharge its mandates. One of the functions is collection of water resources data, analysis and dissemination to stakeholders for decision making. It is also charged with the responsibility of water apportionment and allocation. WRMA therefore needs adequate information to make decisions especially on long term water allocation plans. Mzima springs forms a critical water source for Mombasa and other Coastal areas. It is suspected that there has been a decline in discharge over time. This could affect the long term planning for water sources for Mombasa and coastal areas. These fears and the possible impacts of climate change on the long term discharges from the springs needs to be investigated. The Specific objectives of this study are:- 1. To define and map the area or areas which constitute the rechargezones for the Mzima springs aquifer, and to define the geometry of this aquifer. These areas include the Chyulu Hills. 2. To quantify mean annual recharge to the recharge zone or zones, and describe parameters that are likely to lead to variation in natural recharge including the effects of climate change. 3. To determine whether has been a long term variation in dischargevolume from the aquifer and the possible causes of the variations. 4. To evaluate the water balance of the aquifer. 5. To determine the relationship between Mzima springs and other springs associated with Chyulu Hills. 6. To determine whether there has been a long term variation in discharge from these springs and their possible causes. 7. To describe the measures that should be put in place to protect the recharge areas from land uses that are likely to jeopardize recharge. 8. To make recommendations as to whether this aquifer unit should be given "Special Aquifer" status (sensus stricto Water Resources Management Rules 2007) 9. Make recommendations on the need to balance dry season abstraction against demands for downstream including the river reserve. 10. To define the limits of a groundwater conservation area or areas that might be gazette in order that the recharge areas or areas are protected in future. 11. To recommend a suitable long term aquifer monitoring network including automatic weather stations at the Chyulu Hills. The Water Resources Management Authority now invites eligible consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc. Emphasis will be more on the competence of the firm to undertake this consultancy during evaluation). The services include analysis of the wind data collected to date, development of updated wind map, undertaking pre-feasibility studies and proposing an appropriate mechanism for offering sites to potential investors. In particular the consultants will undertake the following: 1. Analyze already collected data and produce updated wind map(s) for Kenya 2. Undertake pre-feasibility studies for sites where data has been collected 3. Elaborate plans for further development and maintenance of wind data in Kenya 4. Prepare a Wind Sector Prospectus and Wind Development Plan 5. Build capacity in the public sector in the field of wind energy 6. Propose an appropriate mechanism for offering sites to potential investors The Ministry of Energy now invites eligible consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (e.g. brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.). The short listing criteria of the Consultant are: 1) Track record in wind data collection, wind power modeling and wind power analysis, preparing (pre-) feasibility studies for wind parks and experience in designing concepts for attracting developers of wind parks. 2) Experience in transmission and grid integration issues pertinent to wind park development in a developing country setting. 3) Experience in environmental and social safeguards aspects of developing wind parks in developing countries. 4) Number of assignments conducted in similar conditions (developing country setting) 5) Availability of staff with appropriate skills The Consultant is requested to provide a brief outline of the technical approach and methodology for carrying out the study. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a subconsultancy to enhance their qualifications. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the procedures set out in the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers (May 2004, Revised October 1, 2006 & May 1, 2010).
