notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION) KENYA MINISTRY OF NAIROBI METROPOLITAN DEVELOPMENT Nairobi Metropolitan Services Improvement Project (NaMSIP) Credit No. IDAQ7590 Assignment Title: Interdisciplinary Land-Use and Transport Metropolitan Analysis within the Nairobi Metropolitan Region Reference No . MONMED/NaMSIP/TA-08/2011-2012 The Government of Kenya has received a Project Preparation Advance for financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Nairobi Metropolitan Services Improvement Project (NaMSIP) , and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services ("the Services") include Interdisciplinary Land-Use and Transport Metropolitan Analysis within the Nairobi Metropolitan Region , with an implementation period of 4 months. The services to be carried out will include but not be limited to: a) Making a set of recommendations on the transport coordination and land use layout of selected commuter train stations and their areas of social and economic influence within one kilometre radius (3.14 km 2 ); b) Develop different scenarios of institutional arrangements for the objectives to be attained under the proposed centralities (public, private, or public-private partnership), as well as the instruments for management of the assets ; c) Set up a road map and make recommendations on schemes of jurisdictional interaction in the centrality areas touching on different topics such as land use and planning, basic services, infrastructure, housing, environment, governance, management and finance issues in all the stations proposed by the Kenya Railways Corporation. The work will contribute to cross-cutting analysis in the broader metropolitan planning processes on land and housing, social services provision, competitivenessand transport connectivity, and infrastructure finance issues in these urban centrality areas ; d) Develop recommendations on how to improve interdisciplinary planning in the intermodal centrality areas e) Develop recommendations for transit oriented developments within the stations f) Make recommendations for main streets re-development concepts g) Determine and propose the local growth vision for each area around the commuter stations h) Develop guidelines and designs for pedestrian friendly standards for each area around the commuter stations i) Propose development control, zoning and regulations for adoption by each town j) Prepare design and bidding documents for a limited number of investments identified under this assignment. The Ministry of Nairobi Metropolitan Development now invites eligibleconsulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: experience in, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff etc . The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and CostBased Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. The Government of Kenya has received a credit from the InternationalDevelopment Association and a Grant from the UK Department for International Development (DFID) towards the cost of the Financial and LegalSector Technical Assistance Project (FLSTAP). OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT A Consultant will be hired to prepare the RPF in compliance with World Bank and Kenya policies. The RPF document defines roles, responsibilities, procedures and compensation matrixes to guide the preparation of the Individual Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) during implementationfor the subprojects that may cause involuntary displacement and mandatory land acquisition of land owned or used by individuals, families or other entities. 2. SCOPE OF WORK The RPF shall clarify resettlement principles, organizational arrangements and design criteria to be applied to sub-projects to be preparedduring project implementation. Subproject resettlement plans consistent with the policy framework will be subsequently submitted to the World Bank for approval after specific planning information becomes available. In preparing the RPF, the Consultant will: (i) Review relevant Government of Kenya laws and procedures regarding land take and compensation; (ii) Review relevant RPFs prepared for other recent World Bank-funded projects in Kenya in the Roads, Railway, Energy sectors (e.g. –Kenya Transport Sector Support project; Kenya Electricity Expansion Project, EastAfrica Trade and Transportation Facilitation Project, Kenya Metro) (iii) Undertake a reconnaissance field survey in the selected counties/local government areas likely to be proposed for project activities. This Request for Expression of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice (GPN) for this project dated 30 th August 2010. 2. The Government of Kenya has received funding from the International Development Association (IDA), the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA) and the Agence Francaise de Developpement (AfD) towards implementation of the Kenya Municipal Programme (KMP). The Programme intends to apply part of the proceeds of the funding to payments under the contract for the provision of consultancy services for audit and verification of the assets and liabilities of the KMP beneficiary local Authorities (LAs). 3. The KMP has four components: Institutional development; Strategic and participatory planning for urban development and capital investment;Investment in infrastructure and service delivery improvements; and Program management, monitoring and evaluation. Part of the institutional development component is to assist the Government of Kenya in its devolution effort. It is on this basis that this assignment will be undertaken in conjunction with the Task Force on Devolution which was Gazetted by the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Local Government toassist the Government in developing the policies and necessary legislations to facilitate implementation of devolution as part of the implementation of the Constitution. 4. One of the mandates of the Task Force is to rationalizing the existing local authorities and clearing any financial obligations that may be outstanding and in the process assist the County governments in building their capacity to govern effectively and provide the services forwhich they are responsible. This mandate can only be fulfilled if allthe assets and liabilities of the local authorities are audited and verified and also a debt resolution and settlement policy and procedures are agreed to facilitate the transfer to the county government. 5. To comprehensively undertake this assignment within the short periodavailable for the Task Force to give out its final report by June 2011, the scope of services will be as follows: Audit and verification of all the assets and liabilities in the 15 KMP beneficiary LAs: Nairobi, Mombasa, Nakuru, Nyeri, Kisumu, Garisa, Kakamega, Embu, Eldoret, Kericho, Naivasha, Thika, Machakos, Kitui and Malindi. This exercise will include the following: i. Identification and confirmation of existence and ownership of all the assets owned by each local authority; ii. Valuation of all the assets in the local authority; iii. Preparation of the necessary asset register; iv. Verification of and reconciliation of all the debts owed to and owedby each local authority; and v. Confirmation with the debtors and creditors on the indebtedness. 6. The Permanent Secretary, Office of the Deputy Prime Minister and Ministry of Local Government (ODPM&MoLG), now invites qualified auditfirms and registered valuers to indicate their interest in providing the services. A firm/consortium may express interest in any one Group or all the Groups and should indicate itsinterest in priority order. 8. It is expected to take approximately six (6) months to undertake theservices for each Group and the services will run concurrently. 9. The consultants will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers, May 2004, and revised in October 2006 and May 2010. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT The Ministry of Lands would like to procure the services of a consultancy firm to undertake a study to identify and document the legal and extra-legal constraints which hinder the use of land as collateral in access of credit from financial institutions. The consultant is expected to provide clear recommendations towards the development of unifiedlegal and regulatory framework for the creation, perfection and enforcement of security interests over land. 2. Make recommendations on the legal, institutional and administrative framework that that would give effect to increased use of land as collateral in accessing credit from banks and financial institutions. Consult widely within Kenya and liaise with relevant institutions andconsider the existing and available literature on the subject, and must take into account the ongoing implementation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Kenya's Sessional Paper No. 3 of 2009 on the National Land Policy and the Ministry of Land's Strategic Plan. SCOPE OF WORK The consultant will: · Carry out a comprehensive study of the deposit taking SACCO societiesalready licensed and SASRA's supervision mandate and make policy recommendations based on international best practice; · Determine the appropriateness of adopting full risk based supervisionand/or necessary blends with compliance based supervision; Develop a risk-based supervision manual and documentation for the Authority including a training manual; · Develop an RBS evaluation tool and rating parameters in line with the requirements of risk based methodology i.e. a tool that provides sufficient linkage between risk parameters and mitigants. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE KENYA ELECTRICITY SUPPLY SYSTEM STUDY KENYA Electricity Expansion Project CONSULTING SERVICES Credit Number 4743. Project ID No P103037. Addendum: This Notice appeared in the Kenya media on December 16, 2010. Firms that replied to the earlier notice by the deadline of 11.00 am (East Africa time) on 21 January 2011 need not reapply . Background The electricity supply system in Kenya is challenged in the delivery of a consistent supply of electrical power of acceptable quality and reliability. The transmission and distribution system is severely constrained, particularly during peak hours, when system voltages in parts of Nairobi, Western and Mt. Kenya Regions drop below acceptable levels. This occasions power supply interruptions, despite availability of adequate generation capacity to meet demand. To address this anomaly, the Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Energy Sector Recovery Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards a detailed study of the interconnected electric power supply system. The project will be implemented by the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC). ERC, established under the Energy Act, 2006, is an autonomous energy sector regulatory agency, with responsibility for economic and technical regulation of electric power, downstream petroleum activities and renewable energy sub-sectors. Objective of the assignment The objective of this study is to analyze the power supply system during normal and fault conditions, carry out system modeling, load flow studies, establish reactive power requirements, transmission constraints and recommend remedial measures complete with economic and financial analysis, taking into account the ongoing and committed projects, toenable corrective actions to be taken in optimizing the design, function, operation, protection and control of the system. Scope of services The scope of System Study shall include:- (1) Appropriate network studies for the system as it exists and as itexpands in the near term (of three to five years). (2) Determination of reactive power compensation requirements to maintain desired system voltages and optimal transmission efficiency and recommend the best compensation equipment at optimal locations in the network. (3) Making of recommendations for optimization measures and necessaryimprovements for the power supply system, as it exists now and expands in the nearterm in accordance with the Least Cost Power Development Plan (LCPDP), to meet agreed system reliability standards. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA OFFICE OF THE DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER AND MINISTRY OF FINANCE FINANCIAL AND LEGAL SECTOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT CONSULTANCY ON REVIEWING AND REDRAFTING THE PROPOSED CAPITAL MARKETS (REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST) REGULATIONS 2009 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST Ref: EOI/PIU/08/2010-2011 Credit No. 3992 KE Project ID No. P083250 This request for Expression of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice (GPN) for this Project that appeared in United Nation Development Business No. 674 of March 16, 2006 and was updated in UN Development Business No. 707 of July 31, 2007. The Government of Kenya has received a credit from the InternationalDevelopment Association and a Grant from the UK Department for International Development (DFID) towards the cost of the Financial and LegalSector Technical Assistance Project (FLSTAP). It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments underthe contracts for provision of consultancy for the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) on " Reviewing and Redrafting the Proposed Capital Markets (Real Estate Investment Trust) Regulations 2009 " . This consultancy is expected to take a period of 30 man-days . 1. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT i. Carry out a review of the legal and regulatory environment which would be applicable to a REITS instrument; ii. Carry out a needs assessment for REITS by consulting with institutional investors and real estate developers. The review should assess the type of investment which REITS would be used for by looking at the demand for different property types (residential rental, residential sale, commercial # retail, industrial or office); iii. Based on the findings of these reviews and the identification of the most viable operational framework for the Kenyan capital markets, the Consultant will then be expected to review the Capital Markets (Real Estate Investment Trust) Regulations 2009 and the relevant section of the draft Securities Industry Bill and draft Securities Industry (Collective Investment Scheme) Regulations developed by the Authority to establish the need, if any, for amendments to or redrafting of the same to provide a conducive environment for the issue, listing and trading of Real Estate Investment Trusts in Kenya. In addition, appropriate interim amendments to the current Capital Markets (Collective Investment Scheme) Regulations 2001 should be identified to allow for the introduction of REITS pending enactment of a robust framework. 2. SCOPE OF WORK The consultant is expected to carry out the assignment in two phases as below: Phase I: a) Reviewing the current and proposed legal and regulatory framework which would apply to REITS in Kenya including market oversight capacity, intermediary licensing, listing and trading requirements and reportingrequirements. Of particular importance would be the need to review the tax framework which would apply to REITS as well as transfer provisions under land statutes and potential changes required; b) Engage with stakeholders in both the private and public property development sectors to determine varying needs and perspectives across different sub-sectors ranging from low to middle and high income residential for rental or sale properties as well as commercial developments ranging from office space, to retail space or industrial property, targeting the full spectrum of opportunities; c) Review previous reports commissioned by the Authority on the establishment of Real Estate Investment Trusts to identify recommendations forimplementation and areas for refinement and adjustment; d) Develop a final report on the legal, regulatory, fiscal and operational requirements and structures to create a facilitative environment for the pooling of public and private funds for real estate investment; e) Carry out a stakeholder sensitization workshop, and where conclusionsand recommendations differ from those of earlier exposed Consultancy reports, to build industry consensus on the final recommendations to be submitted to the Authority for adoption; f) Where possible consider examples of REITS which have been establishedin other jurisdictions, especially in emerging markets and where appropriate provide details of best practice based on these examples. Phase II: a) Review and where appropriate redraft the draft Capital Markets (Real Estate Investment Trust) Regulations 2009 or in the alternative the relevant sections of the Securities Industry Bill and the draft Securities Industry (Collective Investment Scheme) Regulations in line with the recommendations arising from the Phase I final report that are adopted by the Authority; b) Draft appropriate interim amendments to the Capital Markets (Collective Investment Scheme) Regulations 2001 to allow for the introduction of REITS pending enactment of a robust framework; c) Prepare draft legal and regulatory amendments to other relevant laws of Kenya necessary to facilitate the implementation of the proposed REITS regulations; d) Alongside the draft legal and regulatory amendments provide a clear reasoning for each of the changes based on the assessments reports of Phase I and also on best practice for REITS frameworks. This document will assist in supporting the Government and Legislative decision makers in the adoption and timely enactment of the proposed legal and regulatory framework. 3. EXPERTISE REQUIRED The consultant should demonstrate, in writing, their suitability and understanding of the assignment and must have extensive experience gained from providing similar consultancy work in a similar legal jurisdiction. The Consultant should have practical experiencein either the design and implementation of legal and operational regulatory frameworks for capital markets instruments generally and REITs specifically or practical experience in the establishment and operation of REITs in a similar legal and developmental environment. The Consultant should also evidence prior experience in the development and drafting of capital markets regulatory frameworks as well as implementation of proposed frameworks. 4. buyer: FINANCIAL AND LEGAL SECTOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA OFFICE OF THE DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER AND MINISTRY OF FINANCE FINANCIAL AND LEGAL SECTOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT CONSULTANCY TO CONDUCT PIPELINE ANALYSIS OF PUBLIC PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP (PPP) PROJECTS REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST Ref: EOI/001/2010-2011 Credit No. 3992 KE Project ID No. P083250 . This request for Expression of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice (GPN) for this project that appeared in United Nation Development Business No. 674 of March 16, 2006 and was updated in UN Development Business No. 707 of July 31, 2007. The Government of Kenya has received a credit from the InternationalDevelopment Association and a Grant from the UK Department for International Development (DFID) towards the cost of the Financial and LegalSector Technical Assistance Project (FLSTAP). It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments underthe contracts for provision of Consultancy to conduct p ipeline analysis of Public Private Partnership (PPP) projects. This consultancy is short-term consultancy expected to take a period of three months. 1. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT The main objective of this assignment is to identify and prioritize potential PPP projects which have a high degree of success with minimalrisks to the Government. 2. SCOPE OF WORK The consulting firm shall undertake the following specific tasks: 1. Identify : a. All major projects currently proposed as PPPs in Kenya by line Ministries and other government agencies. This will include analysis of current national and sectoral planningdocuments (e.g., Vision 2030, the first Medium Term Plan, capital planning performed by the various Ministries) and information obtained through face-to-face meetings with the major Ministries involved in energy, transport, water, irrigation, sanitation, housing, health, tourism, education, information communications technology, trade, local government, and other areas where PPPs may be relevant. b. Potential public projects which are not currently proposed as PPPs and which could present good opportunities for PPP. 2. Collect and assess the available technical and economic information relating to these projects. 3. Conceptualize the projects based on the available information. 4. Rank the identified projects in order of probability of success as PPPs, based on a simple and robust project prioritization and ranking criteria. The top five projects ranked with the highest probability of successshould be subject to a higher degree of analysis. Based on information availability or other factors, the parties may agree to increase or decrease the number of "highly probable" PPPs to be analyzed in greater detail. This ranking should also identify which projects are, in theConsultant's opinion, both feasible and bankable as PPPs using current project design and the proposed type of PPP (management contract, lease, Build Own Operate Transfer (BOOT), Build Operate Own (BOO) , etc). 5. Identify the critical path items necessary to successfully implement all identified projects. Such items could include additional technical/economic appraisal, feasibility analysis, legal analysis, environmental analysis and (where possible) financing gaps to be filled. 3. EXPERTISE REQUIRED The consultancy should be conducted by a team with practical and recent experience in Public Private Partnership issues in developing countries and preferably in Sub-Saharan Africa. The competences required ofthe consultants are as follows: · Extensive expertise in PPP development, preferably with experience indeveloping countries; · Excellent analytical skills and sectoral expertise relevant to the investigation of key Public Private Partnership policy issues including efficiency of capital deployment, feasibility analysis and long-term finance; · Substantial track record of participation in infrastructure PPPs in sub-Saharan Africa, and/or the emerging economies of the Far East as feasibility consultant, transaction advisor, equity investor, lender, orother key role; · Substantial track record in successfully undertaking similar policy support roles providing high level advice on PPPs to government; · Skills and demonstrated track record in effective training and mentoring of professional technical staff; The firm engaged for this assignment must have key personnel that should include, as a minimum, the following: 1. A Team Leader who is an expert in policy formulation with at least 10years overall experience in PPP development, promotion and implementation in emerging economies, including such experience in sub-Saharan Africa. The Team Leader must have a Masters Degree or equivalent in a relevant field (e.g. Finance, Economics, Engineering, etc); 2. A Feasibility Specialist with at least 5 years of experience in PPP development in sub-Saharan Africa and/or emerging economies of the Far East, and a Masters Degree or equivalent in Finance, Economics, Engineering or a related field. A Finance Specialist with at least 5 years of experience in PPP development, and a Masters degree or equivalent in finance, economics or a related field 4. The Government of Kenya has received a credit from the International Development Association and a Grant from the UK Department for International Development (DFID) towards the cost of the Financial and Legal Sector Technical Assistance Project (FLSTAP). It is intended that part of the proceeds of this creditbe applied to eligible payments under the contracts for provision of consultancy for the Capital Market Authority (CMA) on "consultancy to carry out a Quantitative Impact Study (QIS) and develop a comprehensive risk based capital adequacy framework for stockbrokers and investment". This consultancy is expected to take a period of four months. 1. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT The main objective of this project is to develop a comprehensive RiskBased Capital Adequacy System for brokers and investment banks and build capacity in the Authority's Risk Based Capital Adequacy surveillance skills. 2. SCOPE OF WORK (i) Review the current legal and regulatory framework for risk management for stockbrokers, Investment banks, Stock Exchange and Clearing and Settlement Corporation (CDSC); (ii) Review current capital adequacy requirements for stockbrokers, investment banks, stock exchange and clearing and settlement corporation against best risk management practices, and identify weaknesses; (iii) Assist CMA develop a comprehensive risk based capital adequacy (RBCA) system of returns and monitoring processes; this should take into account the influence of financial accounting standards on net capital rules and internal controls of intermediaries. This should also include the effect of bond issues by licensed intermediaries on their capital adequacy and long term financing options. (iv) Undertake a Quantitative Impact Study (QIS) and develop a marketconsultation paper for publication. (v) Present findings of the QIS and discuss the proposed capital adequacy framework with internal and external stakeholders. (vi) Assist CMA to develop an in house process to analyse the RBCA returns and provide an early warning system, maintained on a monthly basis. This will be accomplished by paying particular attention to: # Risks in proprietary positions, including concentration risks, # Risks in any margin finance provision, # Risks in the repledging of client securities, # the concentration of risks in holdings # the use of reverse repo lending and repo borrowing and # bond trading exposure (vii) Provide proposals on requirements to automate the required RBCAmonitoring, develop a return of RBCA data that should be submitted monthly by licensed entities. This data will be uploaded into an appropriate database for subsequent analysis and develop associated Excel spreadsheets for analysis purposes. (viii) Advice on additional powers if needed by the Authority to enforce the proposed regime. (ix) Undertake training of staff on risk based capital adequacy, riskprofiling and models for continuous monitoring. 3. EXPERTISE REQUIRED The consultant should have the relevant professional qualification with an experience in capital market legal and regulatory expert with substantial experience in implementation of the International Organization of Securities Commission's (IOSCO) Principles of Securities Regulation (Principles) in both developed and developing markets. Previous experience in the design and implementation of RBCA systems is required. 4. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF KENYA OFFICE OF THE DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER AND MINISTRY OF FINANCE FINANCIAL AND LEGAL SECTOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROJECT CONSULTANCY ON IDENTIFICATION OF POLICY OPTIONS FOR ENHANCING OUTREACH, SAFETY AND EFFICIENCY OF THE PAYMENTS CARD INFRASTRUCTURE REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST Ref: EOI/PIU/02/2009-2010 Credit No. 3992 KE Project ID No. P083250. This request for Expression of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice (GPN) for this Project that appeared in United Nation Development Business No. 674 of March 16, 2006 and was updated in UN Development Business No. 707 of July 31, 2007. The Government of Kenya has received a credit from the InternationalDevelopment Association and a Grant from the UK Department for International Development (DFID) towards the cost of the Financial and LegalSector Technical Assistance Project (FLSTAP). It is intended that part of the proceeds of this credit be applied to eligible payments underthe contracts for provision of consultancy for the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) on "Identification ofpolicy options for enhancing outreach, safety and efficiency of the payments card infrastructure" . This consultancy is expected to take a period of four months. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT The assignment will identify and analyse policy options to encourage inter-operability of the payment system infrastructure in Kenya with aview to enhancing efficiency, safety and effective competition in thefinancial sector, leading to improved access to financial services. SCOPE OF WORK A consulting firm is to develop and provide evidence-based policy analysis for the Government and regulators. Specific analysis is needed on payments infrastructure of bank and non bank payment service providers (such as mobile operators) and its impact on the current and futurefinancial landscape in Kenya. The team should sufficiently cover the three broad areas as outlinedbelow: Investigate institutional arrangements across a number of countries Preliminary identification of the range of policy options and the comparative strengths and weaknesses of each can be best understood by analysing the institutional arrangements in other markets. In choosing the countries to study the broadest range of options will be sought from ' laissez-faire', moral suasion, self regulation, to various forms of regulatory or even direct marketintervention. For each country context examined, the aim should be to first identify the structure of the payments system infrastructure in the market, measure the extent of interoperability and sharing of infrastructure and the likely impact on efficiency and access. Drawing from this, the significance of policy intervention (from legislation and regulation through incentives to moral suasion) in realising the particular structure needs to be assessed. It will be important to identify relevant background features of thewider environment which may make lessons from the other context studied more or less relevant to the Kenyan position. Analysis of the Kenyan payments system infrastructure An in-depth assessment of the current position in the Kenyan paymentssystem infrastructure, looking to explore the same structural issues analysed across other countries in 1 above. This will provide a basis for benchmarking Kenya against other environments and determining where the key areas of interest lie from a policy perspective. Analysis of available policy options An analysis of the strengths, weakness and risks of the various policy options open to Kenya will be required, based strongly on an understanding of Kenya's current position and trajectory of development. Potential application of approaches which have proven successful elsewhere in achieving the desired policy outcomes need to be carefully assessed for their potential applicability to the Kenyan environment. Most obviously the question of consistency with Kenya's wider economic policy needs will be considered. However specific institutional factors may need to be considered (for example, competition regulatory capacity). EXPERTISE REQUIRED The consulting firm should have extensive experience relating to financial sector policy analysis and have in-house capability to: (i) undertake in-depth analytical research of comparable payment environments without the need for extensive primary research; and (ii)assess competition policy issues in the financial sector. Experience in various parts of the developing world, including Africa is an added advantage. buyer: National Information and Technology Authority - Uganda
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) UGANDA UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET) PROJECT ID-P171305 LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980 REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/25-26/00053 ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO CONDUCT AN EXTERNAL AUDITS, VULNERABILITY, AND PENETRATION TESTING The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority - Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project - Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services to conduct an External audits, vulnerability, and penetration testing. The consulting services (“the Services”) include conducting External audits, vulnerability, and penetration testing. The primary goal of this project is to identify and address vulnerabilities and to ensure compliance with national and international cybersecurity standards, namely the National Information Security Framework (NISF) and ISO/IEC 27001:2022. The NISF is Uganda's mandatory national information security standard governing all Government Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs); it defines the minimum information security controls that Government agencies, as well as private- sector companies that own or operate protected computers, must apply to reduce their vulnerability to cyber threats. ISO/IEC 27001:2022, an internationally recognized standard for information security management systems, is used as a supplementary reference for global benchmarking. While the NISF provides the primary compliance baseline specific to Uganda's public-sector context, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 ensures findings are aligned with international best practice. This effort aims to strengthen the cybersecurity posture of Uganda's Government digital services, fostering a secure and resilient digital environment that supports the efficient delivery of public services The Implementation period of the assignment is 25 Weeks from the date of signing the contract. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.nita.go.ug/opportunities/bids-and-tenders The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Shortlisting Criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are: The Consulting Firm shall be a legally registered organization in Uganda or overseas, Proof of legal registration must be included in the proposal submission and be valid for the year of operation. The Consulting Firm shall be a legally registered and authorized to provide cybersecurity assessment and penetration testing services by NITA -U. The firm must demonstrate previous experience in cybersecurity consulting, specifically in conducting Vulnerability Assessments and Penetration Testing (VAPT). The firm should provide evidence of successful execution of at least five (5) similar assignments of comparable type, scope, and complexity, preferably involving Government institutions, critical national infrastructure or Data Centers and Operational Technology (OT) or Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. The firm shall demonstrate depth of expertise, quality of reporting, and experience in conducting Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) assignments. To facilitate this assessment, the firm shall submit at least two (2) redacted VAPT reports from previously completed assignments of similar scope and complexity. The submitted reports will be reviewed to evaluate the firm's methodology, technical rigor, clarity of findings, risk-rating approach, quality of recommendations, and adherence to recognized cybersecurity standards and best practices. The firm must have the current ISO 27001 Certification Submit the firm’s organogram to demonstrate the firm’s technical and managerial capability; The consulting firm must demonstrate the ability to field a team of experts with the required qualifications and experience for the assignment. These shall include at least: Team Leader / Senior Cybersecurity Consultant (1), Two (2) Penetration Testing Experts, Two (2) Cybersecurity Risk and Compliance Analysts, and Two (2) Systems and Infrastructure Security Experts. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, 3.16, of the World Bank’s ‘ Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. MOES-USEEP/SRVCS/2024-2025/00113 The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Secondary Education Expansion Project (USEEP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for procurement of service providers to implement Accelerated Education Programme (AEP) in 8 centres under the Uganda Secondary Education Expansion Project (USEEP) separated into two assignments as below: Assignment 1. a) Kikuube -Kiziranfumbi SS b) Kamwegye - Biguli SS c)Kyegegwa – Bugjubuli SS d)Kampala- Old Kampala SS. Assignment 2. a) Kiryandongo – Panyandopl Self-Help SS b) Madiokollo -Okollo SS, c)Koboko- Longira SS d)Adjumani - Ofua SS. The consulting services (“the Services”) include; providing students who have missed the opportunity to enroll in lower secondary school at the appropriate age or who dropped out of school for various reasons (displacement, pregnancy, etc.), with a fast-track learning opportunity to ‘catch-up’ and re-join students of the same education level group in lower secondary. The service provider will put in place and operate functional AEP centres in existing secondary schools in refugee and host communities as shown in above the above lots. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.education.go.ug or can be obtained at the address given below. The Ministry of Education and Sports now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: A service provider/s with at least 3 years’ experience and a track record in implementation and administering AEP at lower secondary education level. Proven experience of having implemented activities in the different refugees and host communities, including undertaking assignments in designing and implementing programs that target vulnerable persons and other related issues, within the last eight years. Presence of core competences of; Country Director/\Chief Executive/Executive Director; Head of Programs/Program Officer; Finance and Admin Officer; Human Resource (HR) officer; Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL); Communication Officer (CO); AEP Lead Teacher and AEP Teachers Having connection with community organizations within the refugee and host districts with AEP lower secondary evidenced by with signed MoUs or Agreements. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Both assignments will be executed simultaneously. Hence, in order for a firm shortlisted in both packages to be contracted for both packages, it must propose different Key Experts in each package in both Technical and Financial Proposals once issued with the RFP. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated November 2020. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (Monday to Friday, 09:00 – 17:00 hours, except on public holidays). Reference No.: UG-MOGLSD-494509-CS-CQS The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of implementing the Generating Growth Opportunities and Productivity for Women Enterprises (GROW) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services. The Project Development Objective is to increase access to entrepreneurial services that enable women entrepreneurs to grow their enterprises in targeted locations, including host and refugee communities. The Project is being implemented by the Ministry of Gender, Labor and Social Development (MGLSD) jointly with Private Sector Foundation Uganda (PSFU) as an implementing Entity. The Consulting Services ("the Service") include conducting a study on the effect of tax regimes on the growth of women-owned businesses in Uganda. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at https://mglsd.go.ug/procurement/ The Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are the following: The consultancy firm/research team must demonstrate expertise in tax policy analysis, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) development, and women economic empowerment and gender-focused research. The proposed research team should include: Development Economist, Public Policy Expert or Labour Economist/Team Leader; PhD or Masters degree in economics, Public Policy, Business Administration, or a related field with at least ten (10) years of experience in tax policy analysis, MSMEs, and gender-focused research. Must have authored or co-authored at least two (2) publications in internationally recognized peer-reviewed journals or reputable academic platforms. Publications should be relevant to areas such as taxation, gender and development, MSME policy, or inclusive economic growth. Tax Policy Specialist; Masters degree in taxation, Economics, or Public Finance, with at least seven (7) years experience in business taxation. Gender Specialist; Masters degree in Gender Studies, Development Studies, or a related field with experience in gender-inclusive policy research and qualitative data collection methodologies. Business and Entrepreneurship Expert; Masters degree in Business Administration, Entrepreneurship, or a related field with extensive experience working with MSMEs. Statistician/Data Analyst; Masters or Bachelors degree in Statistics, Econometrics, or Data Science with experience in handling large datasets and economic analysis. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF UGANDA MINISTRY OF WATER AND ENVIRONMENT Request for Bids Works (Two-envelope Bidding Process, Without Prequalification) IRRIGATION FOR CLIMATE RESILIENCE PROJECT (ICRP) PROJECT ID: P163836 CONSTRUCTION WORKS FOR MATANDA ROLLER COMPACTED CONCRETE DAM IN KANUNGU DISTRICT RFB NO: MWE/WRKS/24-25/00002 The Republic of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Irrigation for Climate Resilience project (ICRP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Construction Works for Matanda Roller Compacted Concrete Dam in Kanungu District . The Ministry of Water and Environment now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Construction Works for Matanda Roller Compacted Concrete Dam in Kanungu District. The Scope of Works comprises; (a) Dam works: The Scope of Works comprises drilling and grouting for dam foundation, construction of a 32m high Roller Compacted Dam (from dam foundation to crest), founded at 6m depth at lowest point within the rock. The dam shall have a 35m wide stepped spillway on the embankment. The spillway (Overflow) section of the dam will be 25.0m high from the foundation). The watertightness of the body of the dam is ensured by upstream watertightness using Grout-Enriched vibratable Roller-Compacted Concrete (GEVR) zone, thickness 1.5m for external concrete. The GEVR zone shall be produced by placing grout directly on the previously compacted RCC lift. Then loose RCC is placed over the grout and internal vibration is used to draw the grout up into the RCC to produce the water tight facing. There will be a 3-span precast C40 concrete bridge (supported over 2 concrete piers) over the spillway. The spillway shall have concrete flip bucket energy dissipator, discharging into a downstream channel. This downstream channel shall have 8m high reinforced concrete training walls. The bed for 35m length of the channel will be constructed with 1.5m thick Rip rap aggregates on 0.5m thick bed. Major bills of quantities include: 18,251m3 of earth excavation, 191,823m3 of rock excavation, 108,189m3 of RCC placement, 10,393m3 of vibrated concrete, class 25 – 30, for the spillway and intake gallery (b) Outlet Irrigation Pipe (about 100m): Other works shall include construction of a reinforced concrete inlet chamber (6m-wide by 6m high) and concrete gallery barrel for the irrigation pipes (2No). The construction shall entail installation of (2No.) 1.2m diameter pipes within the outlet barrel. One of pipe will be plugged with a stop valve and will be used to supply water under Phase 2 of the project. The other pipe will supply water for Phase 1 (4420Ha) of the command area. (c) Access roads: The Scope of Works comprises of opening up and construction of access road to the dam site and diversion of the 2.2Km community road. The existing community road will be submerged by the reservoir water at Full Reservoir Level. Both roads will be constructed as Grade A- marrum roads. MWE/CONS/24-25/00021 ASSIGNMENT: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR FORMULATION OF A NATIONAL IRRIGATION MASTER PLAN FOR UGANDA. Government of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Irrigation for Climate Resilience Project (ICRP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for Formulation of a National Irrigation Master Plan for Uganda. The objective of this assignment is to prepare a comprehensive National Irrigation Master Plan for Uganda to enable prioritized investments that improve water management and agricultural productivity, including improved resilience to impacts of climate variability and change, through approaches that are economically viable, socially desirable, and environmentally sustainable. The Consulting services (“the Services”) will entail; Irrigation Infrastructure Development (Agronomy Assessment, Irrigation Water Demand Assessment, Assessment of Irrigation Potential Area, Delineation, Categorization and Mapping of Irrigation systems and schemes, Integrated Water Resources Management and Availability, identification and classification of a ladder of options for small holder farmers, schematic designs for irrigation systems and schemes, and Environmental and Social Assessment), Enabling Productive Irrigation Agriculture Services, Sustainable Institutional Development of Irrigation Agriculture, and Irrigation Investments, Financing, and Implementation Planning. The implementation period of the assignment is 12 Calendar Months. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.mwe.go.ug/library/tendersprocurement The Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE) now invites eligible Consultancy firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultancy firms should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they meet the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are: Minimum of 15 years of core business as a consultant in undertaking strategic planning for Water Resources Infrastructure Development Projects. The Consultant shall demonstrate experience in carrying out at least one (01) large scale water infrastructure strategic planning project in the last 10 years of a value of at least US$ 0.75 Million. The assignments must include significant engineering infrastructure such as dams, bulk water supply systems and or large-scale irrigation systems i.e., 3,000ha and above. The Consultant must demonstrate experience in carrying out at least two (02) Feasibility Studies and design assignments for medium to large scale irrigation i.e. 3,000 ha and above, in the last 10 years. The Consultant must submit the firm’s organogram to demonstrate technical and managerial capability. Presence of appropriate skills among staff in the areas of: Irrigation Engineer, Water Resources Expert, Geographical Information Systems – Remote Sensing (GIS-RS) Expert, Hydraulic Engineer, Dam/Geotechnical Engineer, Soil Expert, Agronomist, Agribusiness Specialist, Social Development Specialist, Irrigation Management / Institutional Expert, Environmental Specialist, Financial and Economic Analyst ( Please do not submit CVs and bio data of experts at this stage). For criteria (ii) and (iii), The Consultant must attach Contract Agreements and Completion Certificates of the completed similar assignments in English, in addition to an elaborate description of actual scope and value of work undertaken. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’ November 2020 [Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) Method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulation November 2020. Information and clarifications can be obtained not later than three days to the date of submission at the address below during office hours (Monday to Friday, 08:30 – 17:00 hours, except on public holidays). Expressions of interest (One original plus three copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below on 10th January 2025 at 11:00 a.m. The packages must be clearly marked as; " Expression of Interest for consultancy services for Formulation of a National Irrigation Master Plan for Uganda." MOH/CONS/23-24/00231 The Government of Uganda has received funding from the World Bank towards the cost of the Electricity Access Scale-up Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include supporting the Ministry of Health during the procurement, supervision and monitoring of the Energy Service Companies for the electrification of 350 Public Health Institutions through an energy-as-a-service model. The duration of the consultancy is a minimum period of 37 months, pending closure of the EASP. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be accessed at https:// www.health.go.ug/ The Ministry of Health invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: At least ten (10) years working experience in designing, installing, commissioning, and maintaining solar systems in Sub-Saharan Africa. Experience in designing, installing, commissioning, and maintaining standalone solar PV systems in Sub-Saharan Africa. Experience conducting comprehensive economic analysis of solar projects. Experience in implementing or supporting government procurement programs involving installation of solar systems for large numbers of institutional systems in Sub-Saharan Africa. Experience in installing and using remote monitoring systems for multiple solar systems, including use of data aggregation platforms. Experience in at least three (03) years similar assignments involving support to governments in preparing eligibility requirements/assessments, energy needs assessments, detailed engineering designs, installation, and maintenance of solar energy systems of capacities between 5-30 kWp systems. Possession of experts qualified in renewable energy, electrical or mechanical engineering, computer science, procurement, environment management, and sociology. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers, July 2014 Revision (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. notice_text: Assignment Title: Procurement of Individual Consultant - Health and Safety Specialist on Koboko-Yumbe-Moyo Road Project (1No.) Reference No.: UNRAISRVCS/2020-2021/00082 1.0 Background The Government of Uganda has received for a grant of US$ 130.8 Million (United States Dollars One Hundred Thirty Million, Eight Hundred Thousand) equivalent from the World Bank to support its refugee resettlement programme and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for Consulting services to be procured under this project. The objective of this role is to ensure that the implementation of Component 1: Road development of Koboko - Yumbe - Moyo is in conformity with Uganda's Occupational safety and Health laws, the World Bank (WB) Environment and Social Framework and international standards. Special attention shall be paid to risk management throughout the project management cycle for infrastructure development, supporting the development and implementation of Health and Safety Management System and its integration with Environment Social Management System at UNRA and Project level. The Uganda National Roads Authority (UNRA) now invites eligible and qualified candidates to apply for the position of Individual Consultant - Health and Safety Specialist (1 No.) on Koboko-Yumbe-Moyo Road Project. 2.0 Duties and Responsibilities Focal point for management of Health safety on the project; strategic planning for health and safety in liaison with UNRA Project Management Unit! Team. 2. Ensure implementation of National regulatory, World Bank's and UNRA requirements on Health and Safety on the Project. 3. Conduct and review risk assessment and enforce preventative measures on Health and Safety and maintain a Project Health and Safety Risk Register. 4. Participate in project Environmental and Social Impact Assessment Process (ESIA) to integrate health and safety aspects at Project and UNRA level. 5. Undertake monitoring of Project health and safety and supervision of project works, including development of monitoring checklists, implementation of H&S management plans, including training, conduct of regular/daily tool-box meetings on H&S, compilation of periodic (quarterly, semi-annual, and annual) progress reports, to ensure compliance with relevant Health and Safety requirements, including provision and use of appropriate PPE; and evaluate and review project performance Health and Safety and report to Management. 6. Provide feedback to the Planning and procurement process for the project to ensure that (a)the Health and Safety requirements are properly reflected and priced in contract documents, (b) Health and Safety milestones are included in the contractor's certificates for payment, and (c) conditions of approval for the NEMA certificates and other statutory approvals are well considered, implemented and accordingly advise UNRA and project implementation teams. 7. Work with Social Development and Environment Specialists to support the production and review of health, safety, social and environmental management plans, on a regular basis and ensure these are up to date at all times. 8.Advise project staff, contractors, consultants, implementing partners and other stakeholders on various health and safety related to project implementation. 9. Develop review and implement training plans for Health and Safety including; initiating, organizing and conducting training for UNRA and project teams: contractors, consultants and other stakeholders and ensure full and accurate health and safety training records are maintained. 10. Establish a full programme of documented Health and Safety inspections, audits and checks on the project. This will include; undertaking audits and or coordinating audit processes, reviewing audit reports, developing audit Terms of Reference, procurement of service providers to identify issues or non­ conformities, and enforce necessary actions where unsafe acts or processes that seem dangerous or un healthy are detected. 11. Participate in regular site meetings to report on relevant Health and Safety matters and to provide necessary advice. 12.Assist UNRA and project to meet Health and Safety standards and to prepare for and meet the requirements of external audits for IS045001; and undertake regular auditing of the system inline ISO 45001. 13.Act as a link between UNRA and World Bank Consultants, Contractors, Communities and respective local governments on Health and Safety Issues. The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received a grant of US$130.8 million from the World Bank towards the cost of supporting its Refugee Resettlement Programme, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for Review and Strengthening of the Environment, Social, Health and Safety Management Systems (ESHSMS) at UNRA. The Consulting Services ("the Services") to be provided include; (i) Undertake a gap-analysis with the aim of closing all identified gaps in the existing system. (ii) Upgrade the Safety Management System (SMS) from OSHAS 18001 to ISO 45001. (iii) Integrate the Safety Management System (SMS) with the Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS). (iv) Develop new standards, procedures, guidelines that may be currently missing in the existing manuals. (v) Institute ESHS performance measurement mechanisms. Set objectives and targets for implementation. (vi) Review the projects' Environment, Social, Health and Safety Management Systems and advise on continuous improvement. notice_text: MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND MINERAL DEVELOPMENT ELECTRICITY ACCESS SCALE-UP PROJECT (EASP) REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR OPTIMIZATION STUDY FOR ELECTRICITY DISTRIBUTION AND CONSUMER CONNECTION STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS TO SUPPORT ACCELERATED ELECTRICITY ACCESS IN UGANDA The Government of Uganda (GoU) has received funding from the World Bank towards the cost of the implementation of Electricity Access Scale-Up Project (EASP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) involves a study to assess the country’s distribution grid and consumer connection material standards and specifications and make recommendations of appropriate least-cost distribution material standards and specifications that optimize the cost of grid expansion and connections while meeting predefined levels of quality of electricity supply and safety. It is envisioned that the study will include technical reviews of distribution network and connection material standards and specifications including but not limited to switchgear, poles, conductors, accessories, transformers, meters, ready-boards, etc. To justify the rationalization of standards and specifications, the consultant will also undertake a cost-benefit analysis (CBA) of the proposed low-cost distribution network and connection standards for each consumer category and estimate the associated costs and potential cost savings associated with the adoption of the tailored standards. Specific attention will be given to the following; Assessment and Optimization of Current technical specifications and standards: The Consultant will review the existing distribution network standards and specifications, including 33kV and 11kV networks, to evaluate their appropriateness for the energy needs of different consumer categories in the context of GoU’s broader efforts to achieve universal electricity access. Development of customized fit-for-purpose electrification approaches, distribution network and connection standards and specifications for each consumer category: This will cover distribution network standards and specifications for all applicable materials including switchgear, poles, conductors, transformers, meters, and other key accessories, and connection material standards and specifications for zero and one pole connections, including infrastructure costs, supply and installation for each consumer category. Engagement with Stakeholders: The Consultant will identify key stakeholders including different consumer segments and facilitate inclusive stakeholder consultations to obtain input and feedback on the existing and proposed distribution network and connection standards and specifications, and the proposed fit-for-purpose electrification technologies and approaches that are necessary to drive accelerated electrification. These may include, but not be limited to, Electricity Regulatory Authority (ERA), Uganda Electricity Distribution Company Limited (UEDCL), Umeme Limited, existing Electricity Distribution Utilities, Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS), select large electricity consumers, among others. The assignment will be carried out for a period of Six (6) months. The objectives of the assignment are to:- Review existing distribution network and connection material specifications and standards in Uganda and identify opportunities to develop differentiated low-cost standards and specifications based on energy needs and usage characteristics of the different consumer categories, i.e., residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, and industrial users. Assess the feasibility of adapting new electrification technologies, approaches, and/or standards to meet the needs of each consumer segment and generate optimized standards and specifications of distribution infrastructure and connections to cater for the requirements of each consumer segment. Conduct a cost-benefit analysis of proposed low-cost distribution network and connection standards and specifications for each consumption level and estimate the potential cost savings associated with the adoption of tailored standards, considering installation, operation, maintenance, safety, and availability of locally manufactured materials. Develop distribution network and connection specifications and standards that optimize the cost for different consumer categories based on usage characteristics and overall energy needs. The main purpose is to get a communication specialist will provide communications support and assist the project team to formulate and disseminate more and better information about the project under the guidance of Public & Corporate Affairs Department - UNRA The Uganda National Roads Authority (UNRA) now invites eligible and qualified candidates to apply for the position of Individual Consultant- Communication Specialist Koboko – Yumbe -Moyo Road Project . Scope of works Situation Analyses and Stakeholder Mapping Carry out Situation Analysis and Stakeholder Mapping for the project. Work closely with the project teams. Provide a note summarizing the findings of the Situation Analysis and Stakeholder Mapping with clear recommendations that will feed into the communication strategy and hence implementation Develop a project Communication Strategy and implementation plan. Based on the results of the Situation Analysis and Stakeholder Mapping, Develop a communication strategy and implementation plan in line with the existing UNRA standards. The implementation plan should incorporate activities that will enable effective engagement with all the stakeholders in order to create more awareness and understanding about the Project in a timely and cost-effective manner. The consultant will work and guide the UNRA Public & Corporate Affairs team with the project team in implementing the plan developed and approved. The final Communication implementation Plan shall include the following: Communication activities that will deliver regular and factual messages to all stakeholders about the project Detailed communication activities linked to the identified, agreed and documented specific project milestones Communication activities that will promote consultations and induce a two-way information flow between the client and stakeholders on project matters A framework for responding to misinformation and providing factual information using the most appropriate medium of communication. title: Recruitment of 2 No. Internal Auditors
buyer: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development
notice_text: MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND MINERAL DEVELOPMENT (MEMD) ELECTRICITY ACCESS SCALE-UP PROJECT (EASP) JOB OPPORTUNITY The Government of Uganda (GoU) received funding from the World Bank for the implementation of the Electricity Access Scale-up Project (EASP) to be implemented over a period of five (5) years. EASP will support GoU’s efforts to increase access to electricity for households, refugee host communities, industrial parks, commercial enterprises and public institutions. This is intended to spur socio-economic transformation, in line with Uganda’s Vision 2040, the National Development Plan (NDP III), Electricity Connection Policy (ECP) 2018 and to meet the Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7) of achieving universal energy access by 2030. EASP activities will build on earlier Government initiatives in the energy sector, to support the expansion and strengthening of the electricity distribution network, scale-up service connections within the network, and increase access to off-grid electricity in refugee host districts (outside the existing electricity distribution network), and to clean cooking services and technologies. A Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and Project Coordination Unit (PCU) have been established at the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD) to implement activities relating to grid expansion and connectivity, including scaling up of last-mile connectivity while supporting the necessary network expansion and strengthening through the construction of grid extensions, upgrades, and intensification. The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development, therefore, invites suitably qualified Ugandans to apply for the position of Internal Auditor which exist under the EASP to support the PIU and PCU. Job Title: Internal Auditor Contract Duration: Three (3) years renewable on satisfactory performance Duty Station: The Internal Auditor will be based at the head office of the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development, Kampala, Uganda, with occasional travel to project implementation areas/sites for monitoring or as and when the need arises. Reports to: Senior Internal Auditor Persons Specifications a) Qualifications Possession of a Bachelor of Commerce, Finance, or Business-related degree is required. Possession of Master of Business Administration is an added advantage. Possession of full qualification in any of the Professional accounting or auditing certification, such as ACCA, CPA, CIA, etc. is required. Proficiency in IT/MS Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) b) Experience At least 4 years of relevant work experience with donor-funded projects in the Government of Uganda in either the Accounting or Auditing Field. c) Competencies Technical Financial management Accountability and financial reporting Leadership and Human Resource Management Analytical skills and Strategic thinking Monitoring and Evaluation skills Procurement, Disposal and contract management Knowledge of Electrification policies Information and communication technology Behavioral Assertiveness and Self-confidence Communicating effectively Ethics and Integrity Self-control and stress management Concern for quality and standards Application Procedure. Application letters should be addressed to the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development, and sent to the Ministry Postal address P. O. Box 7270 – Kampala OR hand-delivered to the office of the Assistant Commissioner, Human Resources Management on the First Floor, Block A, Room No. A111 OR sent a zipped pdf application folder on www.memd.go.ug The application should have a detailed CV, National ID, certified copies of academic transcripts and certificates, Daytime telephone contact, and three referees. Deadline: 29th July 2024 at 4:00 pm Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted PERMANENT SECRETARY

title: Recruitment of Finance Officer (Accountant)
buyer: Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries
notice_text: Project UGANDA CLIMATE SMART AGRICULTURAL TRANSFORMATION PROJECT ( P173296 ) Sector MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE ANIMAL INDUSTRY AND FISHERIES (MAAIF) NOTICE OF EXPRESSION OF INTEREST POSITION: FINANCE OFFICER (1-POSITION UCSATP NPCU HEADQUARTERS) Background The Government of Uganda has received funding from the World Bank towards financing a six (6) year Uganda Climate Smart Agricultural Transformation Project (UCSATP). The overall Project Development Objective is to ‘Increase productivity, Market access and resilience of selected value chains in the project area (69 districts) and to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency’. The Project is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF). In order to support the effective and efficient overall management and implementation of project, MAAIF seeks to recruit the services of Finance Officer to support the Senior Finance Officer in Project Implementation. Objectives of the Assignment The UCSATP demands establishment and monitoring of predictable and efficient accounting systems and procedures in place, as per guidelines of the Government of Uganda and World Bank and ensure transparency and efficiency in the process. For this purpose, the NPCU of UCSATP will recruit Finance Officer with adequate experience to support the Senior Finance Officer and the Accounts and Finance Coordination Unit in day-to-day functional activities, administrative support by performing duties of budget execution, processing accounting transactions, providing basic book keeping and participation in preparation of periodic financial reports in the areas of finance and accounting functions and to ensure compliance with the procedures and requirements of the World Bank. Key roles and Responsibilities Support the Senior Finance Officer in preparation of project Workplans and budgets for NARO and NAGRC&DB and ensure sufficient annual budgets for the project are appropriated by parliament and disbursed from the World bank. Assist the Senior Finance Officer to maintain and oversee the day-to-day project financial transactions including maintain appropriate financial records and supporting documentation of all project expenditures and other transactions in accordance with the Government of Uganda and World Bank Financial Management Guidelines Undertake internal controls of the project in liaison with the internal auditor, Assist the Senior Finance Officer in managing stock and petty cash on a daily basis and ensure proper accountability and replenishment to support immediate project activities. Assist the Senior Finance officer in preparing and analysing advance schedules to preparing for retirement of advances and arrange accountability status updates to components. Prepare payments transactions authorized by the NPC UCSATP and extract payment vouchers and attach supporting documents and maintain a proper filing system for the project. Ensure that all payments for the project are made and recorded in accordance with the approved budgeted/planned and the laid down accounting procedures and operational guidelines including those in the Project Implementation Manual (PIM) with guidance of the Financing Agreement. To ensure that all the payment vouchers are adequately supported with appropriate source documentation, duly authorized for payment a property filed to facilitate easy retrieval and reference Ensure timely transfer of funds to Agencies, Institutions departments and individuals; Assist the Senior Finance officer in collation of all documents covering financial transactions of the project on daily basis and preparing them for the Project’s authorizing process Assist the Senior Finance Officer in updating the financial ledgers and generate pre-set financial reports on monthly basis by the 15th of each following month Assist the Senior Finance Officer in ensuring that approved bank accounts are maintained at adequate levels to enable scheduled payments to be made without delay, undertake timely cash flow projections and to observe good treasury and cash management practices. Assist the Senior Finance Officer in preparing monthly/financial reports for NARO and NAGRC in line with Financial and Accounting Regulations and International Accounting Standards (IASs). In liaisons with the Senior Finance officer ensure that funds for the Project are accounted for properly in accordance with conditions of the legal agreements, that all expenditure to be financed under the project is recorded accurately and accordingly in agreement with the Finance Management regulations To ensure that all the project fixed assets are correctly identified and physical verifications carried out on a regular basis to ascertain existence and condition (s) and that all fixed assets are adequately insured. Assist the Senior Finance Officer in preparing withdrawal applications and other accompanying documentation as required for periodic replenishment of the Designated Accounts, or for Direct Payments to suppliers Assist the Senior Finance Officer and Monitoring and Evaluation Officer to monitor and update the project budget to align with financing agreement and project work plans. Performing any other tasks as may be assigned by Senior Financial Management Officer from time to time. Qualifications, Skills and Experience: Qualifications The ideal applicant should be in possession of an Honors Bachelor’s degree in any of the following fields: Commerce (Accounting), Finance, Business Administration (Accounting) or any other related field majoring in Accounting from a recognized institution. A Post Graduate Diploma or Masters in any of the above relevant fields will be an added advantage. Competences Must have completed at least stage two of the accreditation to Professional Accountancy bodies such as ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA; Computer literacy with knowledge of use of accounting software applications; Knowledge of Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS). At least three (3) years’ experience of Finance and Accounting experience. Must have experience in public sector and externally funded projects. Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Experience in providing hands on capacity building, training, and support supervision. Knowledge of International Financial Reporting Standards and International Standards on Auditing. Experience in interpreting financial and project management reports and determining appropriate remedial actions.
