title: LOT 1: Preparation of 2 Micro Catchment Management Plans for Selected Micro Catchment around Water Sources in Ora and Anyau Sub Catchments
notice_text: THE REPUBLIC OF UGANDA MINISTRY OF WATER AND ENVIRONMENT REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST ( CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION ) UGANDA INTEGRATED WATER MANAGEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOAN NUMBER P163782 ( REFERENCE NO. MWE/CONS/19-20/00036/1/2/3) ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR PREPARATION OF MICRO CATCHMENT MANAGEMENT PLANS FOR: LOT 1: TWO (2) MICRO CATCHMENTS AROUND SELECTED WATER SOURCES IN ORA AND ANYAU SUB CATCHMENTS LOT 2: TWO (2) MICRO CATCHMENTS AROUND SELECTED WATER SOURCES IN LAROPI AND AYUGI SUB CATCHMENTS LOT 3: TWO (2) MICRO CATCHMENTS AROUND SELECTED WATER SOURCES IN NYIMUR AND MUTUNDA SUB CATCHMENTS The Government of Uganda (GoU) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Integrated Water Management and Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Preparation of Micro Catchment Management Plans for: Lot 1: Two (2) Micro Catchments around selected Water Sources in Ora and Anyau Sub Catchments; Lot 2: Two (2) Micro Catchments around selected Water Sources in Laropi and Ayugi Sub Catchments; and Lot 3: Two (2) Micro Catchments around selected Water Sources in Nyimur and Mutunda Sub Catchments. The consulting services (“the Services”) include (i) conducting assessment/Situational analysis for management and development issues related to water resources, (ii) carrying out Stakeholder engagements, (iii) undertaking Water Resource Assessments, (iv) undertaking Strategic Social and Environmental Assessment, (v) Evaluating options for water resource development and management and formulate alternative plans, (vi) preparation of costed investment and management measures in the priority micro catchment areas to feasibility study level, and (vii) developing the Micro Catchment Management Plans. The implementation period of the assignment is 6 months for each lot and is expected to commence in August 2020. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.mwe.go.ug/library/tendersprocurement. The Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capability and experience are: A Minimum of five (5) years of core business as a consultant in undertaking Water resources related planning, for sustainable management and development. Submit the firm’s organogram to demonstrate the firm’s technical and managerial capability. Experience of at least two (2) similar assignments of similar scope, nature and value Experience in similar conditions with at least one (1) similar project in Sub-Saharan Africa or other countries in the world at similar level of development as Sub-Saharan Africa. Presence of appropriate skills among staff in the areas Integrated water resources management; Catchment management; project management; stakeholder engagement; Water system simulation modeling; economic and financial analysis of water projects; and environmental safeguards & social safeguards management. (Please do not submit CVs and bio data of experts). The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’ July 2016 revised November 2018 [Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications in the form of a joint venture and/or lead/ sub-consultancy. Consultants shall indicate clearly whether the association is a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Consultants submitting Expression of interest (EoI) for more than one (1) lot must demonstrate capacity to undertake/execute the multiple assignments (multiple lots) concurrently. A separate EoI shall be submitted for each lot. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank procurement regulation. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (Monday to Friday, 08:30 – 17:00 hours, except on public holidays). Expressions of interest (One original plus three copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by courier) by 17th March, 2020. The packages must be clearly marked Expression of Interest for Preparation of Micro Catchment Management Plans for: Lot 1: Two (2) Micro Catchments around selected Water Sources in Ora and Anyau Sub Catchments OR Lot 2: Two (2) Micro Catchments around selected Water Sources in Laropi and Ayugi Sub Catchments OR Lot 3: Two (2) Micro Catchments around selected Water Sources in Nyimur and Mutunda Sub Catchments Address: Procurement Department Attn: Head, Procurement and Disposal Unit Ministry of Water and Environment Headquarters Plot 3-7, Kabalega Crescent, Luzira P.O.BOX 20026, Kampala, Uganda Email: kateregga9@hotmail.com/david.cheptoek@gmail.com

MEMD/CONS/19-20/00243/ERT The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received a Credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Energy for Rural Transformation Project III (ERT III) and intends to use part of the proceeds of the Credit towards payment for Consultancy Services to undertake Consultancy Services training of uncertified formally trained electrical installation personnel (wiremen). The objective of the assignment is to identify and train 1,000 uncertified formally trained practitioners/electrical installation personnel to ensure that they get equipped with knowledge and practical skills required to make electrical installations that meet both technical and safety requirements in accordance with existing laws and regulations. The proposed training will be conducted at selected Training Institutes in Uganda, namely, Uganda Technical College – Bushenyi, Uganda Technical College – Lira, Uganda Technical College – Kyema, Uganda Technical College – Elgon, Nakawa Vocational Training Institute, Arua Technical Institute and Rukungiri Technical Institute. The scope of services under the assignment will include not limited to: Work with MEMD, ERA and technical Training Institutes to identify unlicensed electrical installation technicians who will be trained at the selected Training institutes of Uganda Technical College – Bushenyi, Uganda Technical College – Lira, Uganda Technical College – Kyema, Uganda Technical College – Elgon, Nakawa Vocational Training Institute, Arua Technical Institute and Rukungiri Technical Institute. Vet the selected wiremen to ensure they meet the minimum academic qualifications for each training i.e Electrical Craft Part II for domestic installation training and Electrical Craft Part III for industrial installation training; Carry out training needs assessment for each of the regions to identify the gaps. Annex 1 provides a list of the indicative training areas which should only serve as a guide. The Consultant will be required to carry out a more detailed needs assessment. Develop appropriate training curriculum/content to address the identified gaps. Design and produce appropriate training materials (handouts, booklets, etc) for the theoretical and practical training. These materials will be provided to each participant during the training. The Consultant will identify and build capacity of 2 (two) existing instructors from each of the 7 (seven) Training Institutions. The instructors should meet minimum experience and qualification requirements. The instructors will work alongside the Consultant under his terms and conditions Provide training disposable items such as cables to facilitate the practical training Administer exam(s)/assessments to each of the participants either during the training period or at the end of the training session, but prior to the candidates being interviewed by ERA’s Installation Permits Committee (IPC). Liaise with ERA to ensure that the IPC is available to conduct interviews for the trained candidates immediately after completion of the training. MEMD/CONS/2019-2020/00265/ERT Background The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received a Credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Energy for Rural Transformation Project III (ERT III) and intends to use part of the proceeds of the Credit towards payment for Consultancy Services to undertake Consultancy Services for Identification of public institutions to be electrified with solar installations and development of an alternative payment option for energy in preparation of the Uganda Energy Access Scale-up Project (EASP). The objective of this assignment (study) is to design a sustainable framework for universal access to adequate and reliable electricity services to prioritized public institutions in Uganda. The scope of services under the assignment will include not limited to: a) Situational Assessment The situational analysis will determine the current electrification status of public institutions in Uganda, commencing with the Health centers, schools, water supply schemes and administration buildings in coordination with the Ministries of Health (MoH), of Education and Sports (MoES), of Water and Environment (MoWE), of Local Government (MoLG), and of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD), to establish their assessment of the situation, including planned interventions in existing off-grid supply sources, current roll-out planning to existing and new facilities and an in-depth analysis into technical and financial challenges being faced towards reliable cost-effective energy provision to these facilities. b) Planning / Needs Assessment of required off-grid solar installations This will focus on determining if these installations actually require interventions, the forecast the load pattern at each institution and categorize them into various groupings depending on the present and future energy loads. c) Standard Designs of Installations by Type Based on Tasks a & b, design standardized solar-powered service packages appropriate for the facilities with different ranges (4-6) of capacities. The designs should utilize the latest technologies that enable long-term system sustainability, particularly focusing on optimizing storage through high-cycle, deep-discharge batteries. d) Financial and Economic Feasibility Analyses Undertake financial analyses from the Service Providers position to determine the expected amortized cost to the beneficiaries. e) Roll-out Program / Prioritization Following the above analyses, if required, adjust the sequence and timing of the roll-out program. Furthermore, in consultation with the client establish a suitable scoring system for assigning electrification priority to the earmarked sites. f ) Development of an Implementation Strategy Duration: The duration of the assignment is expected to take eight (08) calendar months from the date of contract signing. MWE/CONS/19-20/00020) The Government of Uganda (GoU) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Integrated Water Management and Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Assessing and Managing the Use of Groundwater Resources and Developing a Strategy and Policy for Sustainable Development and Management of Groundwater Resources in Uganda The consulting services (“the Services”) include (i) undertaking a detailed assessment of the availability (quantity and quality), distribution and demand for groundwater resources in different hydrogeological terrains in Uganda, (ii) identifying threats and pressures and assessing potential impacts of human activities and climate change on groundwater resources, both spatially and in time, including mapping of hot spot locations where key extreme pressures are likely to be experienced, (iii) proposing strategies to address the identified threats and pressures so as to ensure sustainable development, protection and management of groundwater resources in Uganda to support various activities, and (iv) developing guidelines, strategy and policy for holistic and sustainable development, protection and management of groundwater resources in Uganda. notice_text: ADVERT MINISTRY OF EDUCATION AND SPORTS PROCUREMENT OF TWO CIVIL ENGINEERS AND A PROJECT ADMINISTRATOR UNDER THE UGANDA SKILLS DEVELOPMENT PROJECT 1.0 Background. The Government of Uganda has received funding from World Bank to support the Uganda Skills Development Project (USDP) whose objective is to enhance the capacity of institutions to deliver high quality and demand driven training programs in the Agriculture, Construction and Manufacturing sectors. The purpose of USDP is to create a scalable model for high quality vocational and technical training which is linked to labor market needs for specific sectors. The model comprises of establishing Centers of Excellence (CoE) with a network of vocational institutions (with well-prepared students; well-trained faculty; high quality, relevant curricula; adequate facilities and equipment; teaching resources and assessment systems), and an institutional framework that encompasses development sector skill councils. The project will work with four colleges, 12 network institutes and will focus on three sectors of manufacturing, construction and agriculture. The Uganda Skills Development Project (USDP) under Component 2 shall support Improving Quality and Relevance of Skills Development through upgrading three Uganda Technical Colleges (UTC) at (Lira, Elgon, and Bushenyi) and Agricultural College (Bukalasa) to Centres of Excellence (CoEs), offering competency-based training of high quality in low-level (artisans), medium-level (craftsman) and higher-level (technicians) skills demanded in selected trades/occupations in the manufacturing, construction, and agriculture sectors of the Ugandan economy. This is planned to be achieved through forging a partnership with internationally recognized twining institutions for international Accreditation, Curriculum review and adaptation training of faculties of the college among others Under this project there will be upgrading of physical infrastructures as well as construction of new modern workshops and classrooms with the latest equipment in the four colleges and their networking Vocational Training Institute. As a result, the Ministry of Education and Sports would like to recruit qualified and experienced professional Ugandans for the post of Civil Engineer (2) and an Administrator. Details of person specifications are as below; 2.0 RESPONSIBILITIES AND PERSON SPECIFICATIONS 2.1 CIVIL ENGINEER (2) 2.1.1 Job Purpose The engineer will be responsible for the Construction Management and engineering functions of the Projects in liaison with Construction Management Unit of the MoES, to improve the technical supervision and monitoring mechanism of the Ministry and ensure better quality completion of constructed facilities within the stipulated contract periods. 2.1.2 Key Responsibilities and Duties. a) Review existing guidelines including specifications, bill of quantities, architecture and working drawings of all facilities provided under the project; b) Review by the group collectively and by the quantity surveyor, particularly, the priced bill of quantities, including the rate analyses of the different items of works and finalize the rate analyses based on first principles of all items of works of the different facilities provided under the project; c) Review the bid evaluation reports, check the arithmetical corrections and comparison of bids of the responsive bidders, and the recommendations of award by evaluation committees and submit recommendations to the Project Coordinator for onward submission to Assistant Commissioner, Procurement & Disposal Unit through the Assistant Commissioner /Construction Management Unit for review and decision making; d) Review the genuineness and validity and monitor and track the performance bonds and bank guarantees and ensure, that these are always updated till the handing over of works, supplies and services; e) Review and synthesize the monthly reports, identify problems and suggest recommended actions to enable the senior management to make timely decisions so that works and services are not compromised in terms of quality and timely completion and delivery; f) Prepare and submit monthly, quarterly and annual reports that give a comprehensive picture of the works, supplies and services by institution/Lot/region/ and nationally, including cumulative disbursement to Assistant Commissioner/ Construction Management Unit (AC/CMU) through the Project Coordinator with copies to Head IDA projects, Commissioner BTVET, Assistant Commissioner/Procurement and Disposal Unit (AC/PDU); g) Review requests for contract variations, process these requests and submit appropriate recommendations through the project coordinator to AC/CMU for necessary and timely action; h) Undertake periodic field trips as may be required by AC/CMU and Project Coordinator to check particularly the problematic sites, and submit appropriate remedial action to ensure both quality and timely completion; i) Initiate the preparation of simple repair and maintenance handbooks to ensure that the new facilities provided and equipment supplied are properly maintained and provide the training to the College/Institute Principals and staff in charge of repair and maintenance; j) Organize and take part in the pre-final inspection of completed works and services, undertake random check of rectification of defects and assist in the final completion of construction sites and handing over of the completed works and supplies to the MoES/LGs/College/Institute authorities; k) Participate and provide sound technical advice in all technical meetings related to civil works and services, whether these meetings are held in the Ministry or at the Colleges any; l) Any other duties assigned by the supervisor. 2.1.3 Person Specifications. (i) Minimum qualification of a Bachelor degree in Civil/Building Engineering (ii) A post graduate qualification in construction management will be an added advantage (iii) At least eight (8) years of experience in building/civil engineering works, five (5) of which should be in handling complex engineering cost estimates and tender documents and processes; (iv) Experience in design and construction of education and training infrastructure and facilities is an advantage (v) Good command of spoken and written English and adequate computer skills required to discharge their responsibilities in the related area of expertise. (vi) Proven experience in cost estimation and preparation of tender documents for civil works contracts with complex engineering and electro-mechanical services. (vii) Experience in the management of civil and building works contracts in the public sector or large reputable private sector organizations. (viii) Being a member of the Uganda Institution of Professional Engineers is an added advantage. 2.1.4 Duration of Assignment The appointment will be for a period of two years renewable upon satisfactory performance and the availability of funding. 2.1.5 Reporting The Civil Engineer shall administratively report to the Project Coordinator / ARSDP/USDP through the DPC/ARSDP / USDP. He will work under close guidance from the Head of Construction Unit Ministry of Education and Sports. 3.0 PROJECT ADMINISTRATOR 3.1.1 Job Purpose To ensure that high quality project office administration and management procedures are achieved. 3.1.2 Key Responsibilities and Duties The main responsibilities and duties of the Project Administrator shall be as outlined below: - (i) Give support to Project Coordination Unit (PCU) in all office administrative transactions; (ii) Arrange for all PCU meetings (internal and external), (iii) Support and facilitate activities of visitors at PCU offices; (iv) Ensure that the office facilities are clean at all times including the reception area; (v) Monitor the physical and functional state of general equipment, vehicles as well as furniture, and report faults to the engineering team for technical guidance; (vi) Ensure that office utilities (e.g. electricity etc.) properly used without wastage; (vii) Ensure that project vehicles are properly used according to the Ministry’s regulations and guidelines; (viii) Supervise receipt, delivery and processing of correspondences and handling general enquiries in consultation with the Project Secretary; (ix) Ensure that the Offices are opened before 8:00 am and closed after 5:00 pm (x) Ensure that internal errands for staff including delivery of documents to relevant Offices are effected; (xi) Manage all travel (Local and abroad) arrangements for PCU or stakeholders sponsored by Skills Projects; (xii) Provide support (e.g. visa processing, work permits acquisition etc.) to all foreign stakeholders visiting or working on Skills Projects under IDA Portfolio; (xiii) Manage the Administrative Desk at meetings, workshops and functions organized by PCU; (xiv) Take minutes during PCU Meetings and follow up on agreed action points; (xv) Arranging Boardroom bookings, arranging local travels and, occasionally, travelling with project teams to support Administrative functions; (xvi) Oversee the Printing, Photocopying and scanning and organizing office documents in the required order; (xvii) Supervise all the support staff (secretaries, office assistants, and drivers) in the PCU to ensure that they perform their work accordingly; and, (xviii) Perform any other duties assigned by his/her supervisors. 3.1.4 Person Specifications a) Minimum qualifications of a honors Bachelor’s Degree in Secretarial and Administrative studies, Social Work and Social Administration, Social Sciences (Administration option), Bachelor of Business Administration (Management Option) from a recognized University. b) A post graduate qualification in Management, Business Administration, Public Administration or related field is an added advantage c) At least six (6) years of practical experience in office administration, project work, or related work with a public or private organization. 3.1.5 Duration of Assignment The appointment will be for a period of two years renewable upon satisfactory performance and the availability of funding. 3.1.6 Reporting The Project Administrator shall report to the Project Coordinator - ARSDP & USDP under close guidance of the Deputy Project Coordinator. 3.1.7 Duty Station The duty station will be Kampala 3.1.8 HOW TO APPLY Applications should be accompanied by detailed Curriculum Vitae, copies of certificates and testimonials and at least two competent referees, one of whom must be from your current or previous employer and should be received not later than 10:00 am on 14/12/2018. They should be addressed to the Commissioner Human Resource Management, Ministry of Education and Sports- 4th Floor, Embassy House, P.O Box 7063 Kampala 3.1.9 PROCUREMNENT SCHEDULE The procurement schedule is subject to minor changes as follows; Activity Date a. notice_text: The Republic of Uganda Rural Electrification Agency Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST ADVERT Country: Uganda Name of Project: Energy for Rural Transformation Phase Three – ERT III (Uganda) Credit No.: 5653 Project ID.: P133312 Procurement Reference No.: REA-ERT III/SRVCS/18-19/00055 Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Independent Verification Agent for 87,000 (ERT-3 87K) connections The Government of Uganda (GoU) has received funding from the World Bank towards the implementation of the Energy for Rural Transformation (ERT) Project Phase III, and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards consultancy services for verification of electricity connections. The consulting services (“the Services”) for the assignment will go towards implementing connections under the new Electricity Connections Policy (ECP) and will be implemented on an Output- Based Financing (OBF) approach which Government continues to implement through the Rural Electrification Agency (REA). REA wishes to procure the services of a competent and reputable company which will be contracted as an Independent Verification Agent (IVA) to verify the delivery of outputs against which a subsidy will be disbursed for a period of 24 months. The scope of consultancy services: The IVA will verify baseline data and subsequent results data for project results monitoring, as set out in the ECP Implementation Manual. The IVA will be required to complete a desk-based verification of all eligible connections installed by each LDC in all regions of Uganda under the project, and to physically inspect and verify 10% of the connections in each batch. It is estimated that 87,000 connections will be completed by the LDCs. The IVA will be provided with a list of connections and requested to perform the verifications of these connections. The LDCs shall provide detailed information to REA about the connections that they have installed. This information shall be entered into the connections database and cross-checked against earlier information on connections verified before disbursement of the output based subsidy can be done. The IVA will verify LDC claims and report to REA who will confirm the IVA findings with the database before a recommendation for subsidy disbursement is made. The IVA is to ensure that there is no duplication of connections to be refunded. In doing this, the IVA will carry out a duplication test across all other previous batches and across other connections funded projects. The IVA will maintain up-to-date databases for all the connections verified and will submit these to REA at the end of each quarter. The Rural Electrification Agency of the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in provision of the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short listing criteria are:- i.Consultant must have demonstrated previous experience of at least 3 assignments in: (a) Verification/audit and utility management (including familiarity with utility metering and billing procedures). (b) developing surveys, sampling, collecting, compiling and analysing data; (c) Knowledgeable in culturally appropriate practices needed to work with the project’s target population. (The experience in areas (a), (b) and (c) above may be obtained from the same assignment or from different assignments but all areas must be covered) ii.Availability of appropriate skills/expertise including expertise in; auditing, power distribution engineering, GIS and Database management as well as IT systems and database manipulation. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. notice_text: MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND MINERAL DEVELOPMENT REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO DEVELOP NATIONAL ELECTRIFICATION STRATEGY Project Name: Grid Extension and Reinforcement Project (GERP ) PROJECT ID NO: P133305 PROCUREMENT REFERENCE No.: MEMD/CONS/2017-2018 /00523/GERP 1.The Government of Uganda (GoU) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Grid Extension and Reinforcement Project which is aimed at increasing availability and efficiency bulk electricity supply and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services to develop National Electrification Strategy. 2.The consulting services (“the Services”) include but not limited:- (i) Review current GoU electrification plans, policies, strategies and all electrification undertakings with the view of identifying not only bottlenecks but also opportunities to achieving targeted access rates. These will include but not limited to the Generation and Transmission development plans, Rural Electrification Strategy and Plan, ongoing and planned projects under the Rural Electrification Program, Electricity Connections Policy, GIS master plan, etc. The Consultant will also review Umeme’s investment plans and the electrification master plans of the various service territories with the view of coming up with one harmonized National Electrification Strategy. (ii) Review the electricity sector legal, institutional and regulatory framework to identify gaps in the planning, coordination and implementation of electricity access expansion in the country, and propose ways of addressing them. This task shall benefit from the Diagnostic Review of the Distribution Sector to be implemented concurrently with this assignment under GERP. The Consultant therefore shall be required to work closely with the Consultant conducting the Diagnostic Review when carrying out this task to harmonize synergies. (iii) Assess capacities of key entities involved in planning and implementation of the national electrification programs with the aim of identifying capacity gaps to implement a National Electrification Strategy. The assessment shall be extended to among others service providers, technicians, wiremen, contractors. (iv) Review the electricity sector capital investment strategies and control mechanisms, identify gaps and propose ways of addressing them. (v) The Consultant shall also develop a robust monitoring and evaluation (M&E) framework and oversight mechanisms to be employed in order to track performance, implementation progress and results on the ground. 3.The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. 4.The shortlisting criteria is as follows:- (a) Demonstrate previous experience in at least two assignments of similar nature and scope in the following areas (the experience in these areas may be obtained from the same assignment or from different assignments but all areas must be covered) :- (i) Proven experience in the preparation of electrification strategies and programs that integrate grid and off grid technologies in developing countries. (ii) Experience in the design of systems for electrification of rural areas in developing (non-OECD member) countries. (iii) Demonstrated knowledge and understanding on different business models to promote off-grid technologies in a sustainable manner. (b) Presence of appropriate skills among staff in the areas of Project Management, Planning and Design of urban and rural power distribution systems, Project implementation strategies of power distribution systems, Business models to promote off grid technologies, Financial modeling/planning of electric utilities and off grid companies and Legal and regulatory aspects of the electricity sector in Uganda to support both grid and off grid technologies. (c) Experience of at least two assignments in sub-Saharan Africa. 5.The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants by World Bank Borrowers dated January 2011 (revised July 2014) (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 6.Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. notice_text: MINISTRY OF HEALTH REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (EOI) FOR THE POSITION OF PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST (01). The Projects are implemented through the existing institutional arrangements of Government whereby the respective Departments at Ministry of Health and other Government Parastatals are responsible for implementation of the respective components of the Projects. The Government wishes to engage the services of suitably qualified candidate to fill the vacant post of a Procurement Specialist under the Projects as described below: Objective of the assignment; The objective of this assignment is to ensure timely implementation of the procurement process in accordance to the procurement plan which will guarantee timely acquisition of goods, works and services. The selected Consultant is expected to play a key coordination role between all stakeholders in in the procurement cycle. Reporting; The Procurement Specialist will report to the Project Coordinators of URMCHIP, URHVP and EAPHLNP, but will be in charge of execution of procurement under the Project. 4.0 Responsibilities and tasks : Coordinate procurement functions between the component coordinators and Procurement and Disposal Unit. In consultation with the Component Coordinators, the Procurement Specialist shall prepare, review, adjust (where applicable) and monitor the implementation of Project Procurement Plan Ensure timely submission of all project procurement plans requiring review and approval by the World Bank In consultation with different Ministry line departments, prepare bidding documents for acquisition of goods, works and services Make sure that the World Bank procurement guidelines are followed at all the different procurement stages including obtaining no objection where required during the procurement process In liaison with the procurement unit, participate and provide procurement guidance during the evaluation of bids Participate in contract negotiation (for consultancies) and technical discussions ( for goods and works) and procurement guidance Contribute to the preparation of Quarterly Project Progress Report Provide procurement guidance in the preparation of draft contract agreements and ensure that they are forwarded to Solicitor General (SG) and organize the contract signing after SG’s clearance Contribute to the regular performance appraisal of the consultants to ensure they are in line with their Terms of Reference; In consultation with user departments, appraise and prepare a report regarding the performance of all service providers (suppliers, contractors and consultants ) to achieve set key performance indicators (KPI’s) and administer maintenance contracts Ensure the project records are well kept and maintained for completeness and safety Manage equipment warranties, insurance and contractor performance securities. Provide advice to the Project Coordinator on all procurement issues Any other assignments by the Project Coordinator. 5.0 Qualification and competence: The applicant must be a Ugandan national with a Honors’ degree in any of the following areas: Procurement and Logistics Management, Business Administration, Engineering, Economics, Commerce and Law from a recognized University or institution. The applicant should have a post graduate training /qualifications in procurement, logistics or Supply Chain. title: Consultancy Services for development and dissemination of National Civil Registration & Vital Statistics (CRVS) Policy and Strategy.
notice_text: THE REPUBLIC OF UGANDA MINISTRY OF HEALTH Uganda REPRODUCTIVE Maternal aND Child Health SERVICES Improvement Project (URMCHIP). REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DEVELOPMENT AND DISSEMINATION OF NATIONAL CIVIL REGISTRATION & VITAL STATISTICS (CRVS) STRATEGY. PROCUREMENT REFERENCE N o.: MOH-URMCHIP/SVCs/2017-18/00064 The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the implementation of the Uganda Reproductive Maternal and Child Health Services Improvement Project herein after referred to as the “Project”. The objectives of the Project are to: (i) to improve utilization of essential health services with a focus on reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health services in target districts; and (ii) Scale up birth and death registration (BDR) services. The project is composed of the following components: (i) Results-Based Financing for Primary Health Care Services; (ii) Strengthen Health Systems to Deliver RMNCAH Services; (iii) Strengthen Capacity to Scale-up Delivery of Births and Deaths Registration Services and (iv) Enhancing Institutional Capacity to Manage Project Supported Activities. The Project is being implemented through the existing institutional arrangements of Government whereby the respective departments at Ministry of Health and NIRA will be responsible for implementation of the respective components. Under component III, the Project seeks to hire a consultant to develop and disseminate the National Civil Registration & Vital Statistics (CRVS) Strategy under the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA). NIRA was established by the Registration of Persons Act 2015 (ROPA) as a specialized Authority for the registration of persons, the registration of births and deaths and the issuance of the appropriate certificates. Scope of the consultancy services: Conduct a situational analysis for CRVS to identify main stakeholders, strengths, threats, opportunities, challenges and lessons. In addition, review best practices from the region to identify applicable lessons for the local context. This should specifically include: review the CRVS processes in NIRA, Local Governments, the health sector and existing processes on birth, death and causes of death, and adoption, and marriage, and divorce, considering the full life-cycle of CRVS from vital event notification / declaration to collation and dissemination of vital statistics reports. Undertake business process analysis of existing civil registration processes for deaths and causes of death, adoptions, marriages and divorces; observation of formal and informal registration practices at a local level; identification of existing opportunities i.e. pilot projects that could be scaled for civil registration. Develop objectives, actions and implementation arrangements for the CRVS Strategic Plan. The implementation arrangements should include: stewardship, coordination and accountability structures, roles and responsibilities of stakeholders, implementation risks and the mitigation measures. Describe financing of the Strategic plan including a detailed costing of proposed strategies, mapping of available resources and strategies on bridging the financing gap. Develop a monitoring and evaluation framework and implementation road map for the CRVS Strategic Plan with clear outputs and outcomes, performance indicators and corresponding targets over the life of the strategic plan and should make provisions for reviewing performance of the strategic plan. The Ministry of Health on behalf of NIRA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above consultancy Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short listing criteria is: At least 10 years’ experience in Development and management of CRVS systems. Evidence of preparation of at least two National CRVS Strategic Plans or Policies. Evidence of handling large sets of data including on CRVS Availability of staff with knowledge in Public Health, Economics, Statistics or Demography, Public Health, Strategic Planning and Social Sciences. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers , January 2011,Revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications. The type of association whether a joint venture or a sub consultancy should be clearly indicated in the Expression of Interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection Based on Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 17:00 hours (Local time). Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) by 10:00 am, on 18th May, 2018. The Ag. notice_text: Invitation for Bids The Government of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Second Kampala Institutional and Infrastructure Development Project (KIIDP2) , and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Design and Development of the Property Management Information System, City Address Model (CAM ) and the KCCA Corporate GIS The Kampala Capital City Authority, the implementing agency for the project, invites sealed bids from eligible bidders for Design and Development of the Property Management Information System, City Address Model (CAM) and the KCCA Corporate GIS The Scope of the CAM/CAMPV System KCCA is seeking the services of a vendor to design and develop a Computer Aided Mass Property Valuation Information System, City Address Model (CAM) and The KCCA Corporate GIS (CAM/CAMPV System). The vendor will also use the existing data to carry out mass valuation using the developed system based on a suitable model. The developed system will support the sales comparison, cost and income (rental) approaches to value. The CAM/CAMPV scope shall include the following: I. Development of a City Address Model that will enable KCCA to monitor infrastructure investments on the ground and support local revenue mobilization. II. Enhancement of the capacity of GIS to address KCCA needs including the development of an urban land use database at plot, village and parish levels, linking urban services management with revenue functions. Specifically, this should lead to the establishment of a Corporate GIS. III. Carrying out the functions of valuation, revenue data base management & Document management, information & reports management, assessment, billing, enforcement, notification, revenue projections & simulations, dispute resolutions including appeals and objections, provide an audit trail and tax payers’ education. IV. Interfacing with the existing revenue management systems like eCitie which manages payment processing and any other relevant systems like the SMS platform for communication and other Relational database driven systems. V. Building capacity of staff on how to use, maintain and regularly improve or extend the developed systems in order to ensure that updates/changes in revenue administration and valuation rolls for both the supplementary and subsequent main valuation are taken into consideration for posterity. 4. Bidding will be conducted through the International Competitive Bidding (ICB) procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Procurement of Goods, Works and Non-Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers Jan 2011 revised July 2014), and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Guidelines. In addition, please refer to paragraphs 1.6 and 1.7 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 5. The Qualification requirements among others include: a) Having developed and implemented at least three (3) CAM/CAMPV similar Systems. b) Shall have at least 12 years of working experience with public sector in ICT, Property management system, City Address Module incorporated with GIS in implementation of projects worth USD 3 million. c) Shall have evidence/ certifications of establishment of internationally recognized or home-grown quality process in software development of CMMI Level 5, ISO/IEC 27001, TMMi Level 5. d) Must demonstrate average annual turnover of at least USD $9 million over the past three years, i.e. (2016, 2015 and 2014) e) Must provide a certificate of engagement and proof of availability of all the proposed staff for the project signed by the staff f) Shall demonstrate local presence in Uganda to provide timely post implementation support, assimilate well with the different local cultures during implementation, and offer continuity after implementation. This Invitation for Bids (IFB) follows the General Procurement Notice (GPN) for this project that appeared in UNDB online on June 01, 2017. 2. The Government of Uganda represented by the Ministry of Agriculture Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF) has received credit from the International Development Association towards the cost of The Agricultural Technology and Agribusiness Advisory Services (ATAAS)- Uganda, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this credit to payments under the agreement(s) resulting from this IFB: Supply, Installation, Commissioning and Maintenance of an e-Voucher System for Government of Uganda. 3. MAAIF developed the Agriculture Cluster Development Project (ACDP). The main project objective of ACDP is to raise on-farm productivity, production and marketable volumes of selected agricultural commodities in specified geographical clusters. The project will support activities designed to raise both productivity and overall production of maize, beans, cassava, rice, and coffee in 42 selected Districts grouped into 12 high-potential agricultural areas termed “clusters. Core beneficiaries of the project will be farmers, especially smallholders, selected from their farmers’ associations, which will include rural producer organizations and/or co-operatives, and other value chain actors at the local, district and cluster level. 4. For participating farm households, support under e-voucher scheme will take the form of: (1) a time-bound partial and diminishing matching grant (subsidy) to help finance the purchase of key inputs and on-farm storage facilities and (2) targeted training in the most effective use of these inputs. Participating households will pay for a portion of the cost of the inputs and use the subsidy to pay for the remaining portion. For each participating household, this support will be provided for three consecutive crop cycles. The key instrument that will be used for the delivery of ACDP support to beneficiaries will be the e-Voucher. 5. The Ministry of Agriculture Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF) as the implementing agency for the project now invites sealed bids from eligible Bidders for the Supply, Installation, Commissioning and Maintenance of an e-voucher management system for the Government of Uganda . 6. The Pilot phase: The ACDP E-Voucher scheme will initially be piloted for a period of twelve months (Year 0) in five of the districts in five clusters, and on one commodity per cluster to reach 5,000 farm households. The five districts and commodities for the pilot are: Kalungu (coffee); Iganga (maize); Nebbi (Cassava); Ntungamo (beans) and Amuru (rice). Thereafter, it will be scaled out progressively to cover all the 42 districts by year three, after successfully piloting it in the five districts as described in this bid document. 7. The Roll out phase: The project will be rolled out to 450,000 households in total by Year 3 of the project. 8. title: Consultancy Services for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) of the Impact of the Isimba Hydropower Project on the Kalagala Offset Area
buyer: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development
notice_text: THE REPUBLIC OF UGANDA MINISTRY OF ENERGYAND MINERAL DEVELOPMENT ENERGY FOR RURAL TRANSFORMATION PROJECT - III Project ID No. P133312 CONSULTANCY SERVICES Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) of the Impact of the Isimba Hydropower Project on the Kalagala Offset Area PROCUREMENT REFERENCE NUMBER: MEMD/CONS/2015-2016/00348/ERT III REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST The Government of Uganda (GoU) has applied for financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Energy for Rural Transformation Project – III and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultant services. The GoU is undertaking the development of the Isimba Hydropower Project, located some 40 kilometers downstream of the Bujagali Hydropower Project. A Kalagala Offset Area (KOA) was set aside as part of the development of the Bujagali Hydropower Project. As part ofproject preparation, the GoU prepared an ESIA for the Isimba Hydropower Project ("Isimba ESIA"). The government now wishes to complement the Isimba ESIA with an additional Environmental and Social Impact Assessment focused on the impacts of the Isimba Hydropower Project on the KOA ("KOA ESIA"). The objectives of this consultancy are to prepare: (i) a KOA ESIA that comprehensively addresses the expected environmentaland social impacts of the Isimiba Hydropower Project on the KOA and corresponding mitigation measures; and (ii) a Long-term Conservation Options (LTCO) Report that would identify options for ensuring a firm legal status and sustainable funding for the KOA. The KOAESIA should be undertaken consistent with the World Bank safeguards policies. Both the KOA ESIA and the LTCO Report should provide a solid information base for the GoU of Uganda to engage with the World Bank in finding a mutually acceptable solution that would make Isimba Hydropower Project consistent with the spirit and intent of the Indemnity Agreement for the Bujagali Hydropower Project of 2007. The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the required services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are: 1. At least 10 years of experience in Environmental and Social Impact Assessments. 2. Specific experience of successfully completing environmental and social impact assessments for at least three similar infrastructure projects in the last 10 years. 3. Specific experience of successfully completing environmental and social impact assessments for at least two large hydropower projects (at least 100 MW in size each) in the last 10 years. The two hydropower projects could be part of the list of projects prepared in response to the requirement of the paragraph immediately above (requirement #2). 4. Specific experience of successfully completing at least one environmental and social impact assessments following World Bank safeguards policies in the last five years, 5. Presence of skills in the following areas: i. freshwater aquatic ecology, including experience with the freshwater ecosystems of tropical Africa; ii. environmental and natural resource management; iii. environmental and power system economics, including experience in working with the tourism; iv. legal environmental analysis, including experience with protected areas; v. social science; and vi. hydropower engineering. 6. Experience in working in developing countries. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants by World Bank Borrowers dated January 2011 (revised July 2014) ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. The Expression of Interest shall specifythe nature of association i.e., whether joint venture or sub-consultancy and shall indicate the lead firm. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultants Qualifications selection method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. Interested consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours (0900hours to 1700hours). Expressions of interest (One original plus five copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below by January 18, 2016. The packages must be clearly marked: Expression of Interest for consultancy services for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) of the Impact of the Isimba Hydropower Project on the Kalagala Offset Area – Proc.Ref No. MEMD/CONS/2015-2016/00348/ERT III Head, Procurement and Disposal Unit Ministry of Energyand Mineral Development Amber House, Plot 29/33 Kampala Road 1st Floor Room C109- Kampala- Uganda Email: hpdu@energy.go.ug ; with copies to: s.mukazi@energy.go.ug

notice_text: Ministry of Water and Environment REDD+ READINESS PREPARATION SUPPORT Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: Project ID: P124296 ADVERTISEMENT CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DEVELOPMENT OF A REDD+ STRATEGY FOR UGANDA'S NATIONAL REDD+ PROGRAMME REFERENCE NO: MWE/…../…../….. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST SELECTION BASED ON CONSULTANT'S QUALIFICATION (CQS ) The Government of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank's Forest Carbon Partnership Facility (FCPF) toward the cost of the REDD+ Readiness Preparation Support, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services ("the Services") include the: 1. Preparation of a National REDD+ Strategy. This national REDD+ strategy should also enjoy strong international recognition and be the basis for mobilizing investment and results based phases of REDD+. The Preparation of a National REDD+ Strategy shall involve the following specific tasks: a) Undertaking a complete assessment of the potential strategic options identified in the R-PP and other relevant national plans such as those past and current development, climate change, forest, agriculture, energy including biomass energy, land use & land management, finance, private sector, poverty reduction, community development, wetlands, water resources, biodiversity & wildlife conservation, mining, infrastructure, urban development, environment, local government, health, social & gender, education, governance & law enforcement, disaster, information; as a basis for elaboration of these options for addressing the identified drivers of deforestation, forest degradation, conservation of forest carbon stocks, sustainable management of forests, and enhancement of forest carbon stocks; and prepare a draft Options Assessment report. b) Undertaking a feasibility assessment of the draft options identified in (a) above in terms oftheir socio-economic, political and institutional perspective; full opportunity costs; full implementation costs; full transaction costs; full institutional costs and other costs and benefits; including how they relate to people's livelihoods, alternative income generation potential and full costs of biodiversity protection; governance; national development policies and strategies; and policy, legal and regulatory implications; risks associated with the specific strategy options and ways to manage and mitigate them; cost of implementation; including costs of citizen participation, compliance and risk management and mitigation; c) Using the product from the above processes, prepare a draft REDD+ Strategy Options (measures,actions and interventions) Paper; and undertake/facilitate full and effective consultations on it. Using the inputs from the consultations on the "REDD+ Strategy Options (measures, actions and interventions) Paper" Prepare and submit a 1 st Draft REDD+ Strategy and a costed Action Plan. d) Basing on the above, undertake/facilitate full and effective Disclosure, dissemination, feedback and national validation, and publication of the validated REDD+ Strategy and a costed Action Plan; e) Prepare a practical tool that could be used to integrate the REDD+ Strategy with Forest Reference Emissions Levels (FREL/RL), National Forest Monitoring System (NFMS), system for promoting and respecting REDD+ safeguards, National Greenhouse Gas Inventories & the National Communication Process. Further information on the assignment can be obtained from the Ministry of Water and Environment website: http://www.mwe.go.ug/. title: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR STRENGTHENING NATIONAL FEEDBACK AND GRIEVANCE REDRESS MECHANISM FOR REDD+ FOR UGANDA’S REDD+ PROGRAMME
notice_text: The Republic of Uganda Ministry of Water and Environment REDD+ READINESS PREPARATION SUPPORT Loan No./Credit No./ GrantNo.: TF014956; Project ID: P124296 ADVERTISEMENT CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR STRENGTHENING NATIONAL FEEDBACK AND GRIEVANCE REDRESS MECHANISM FOR REDD+ FOR UGANDA'S REDD+ PROGRAMME REFERENCE NO: MWE/SRVCS/14-15/00018 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (Consultants' Qualification Selection (CQS)) The Government of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank's Forest Carbon Partnership Facility (FCPF) towards supporting Uganda's nationalREDD+ Readiness, and intends to apply part of the grant for consulting services. The consulting services ("the Services") include: Strengthening National Feedback and Grievance Redress Mechanism for Uganda's REDD+ Programme. This work will review opportunities for functional grievance redress mechanisms at three levels- project/community county and national levels. Based on the review of existing structures make recommendations for Feedback and Grievance Redress Mechanism (FGRM) to ensure presence of simple and practical procedures that ensure complaints are properly recorded, responded to, and reported and allow for effective escalation for unresolved issues; and awareness and accessibility to grievance redress in a way that is consistent with the scope and reach of the national REDD+ policy dialogue process. Uganda has conducted a preliminary assessment- scoping out the various grievance structures that exist in the country including the purpose and usage of those structures. During implementation phase of REDD+ readiness, Uganda will conduct an analysis of the various structures, identifying gaps and resources (human, administrative, financial technical capacity, etc.) needed for the effective functioning of these FGRM structures. The mainobjective of this assignment is to build upon the framework assessment already undertaken by the Government of Uganda during the formulation phase and the SESA findings that identify potential sensitive issuesand undertake an assessment of existing capacity of institutions including customary mechanisms to handle grievances and support their strengthening specifically for REDD+. Specifically; i. to undertake an assessment of existing national institutional capacity for feedback and grievance redress; so as to: a. identify existing and potential conflict and grievances that could arise during REDD+ readiness, and implementation of REDD+ Strategy/ activities. b. identify mechanisms that can detect, prevent and minimize the escalation of, and resolve conflicts and grievances. ii. Strengthen policy, legal and institutional framework for managing grievances and Conflicts that can assist in handling/ addressing stakeholder concernsand issues relevant to REDD+ implementation. This will include: a. Recommendations/training for staff tasked with performing the function, i.e., receiving requests and initiating the right process to respond to them, at least for the duration of the FCPFReadiness Preparation grant, in either an existing or new institution; b. Proposal for capacity building on REDD+ issues in identified agencies/ stakeholders to be engaged in FRGM; c. technology for access points to the function; and d. cost of setting up, and operating the database ofrequests or complaints in identified FGRM structures The [Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE)] now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Short-listing criteria are as below : i. Experience in the design and/or implementation of at least 4 similar assignments, focusing on FGRM in natural resources management or other sectors ii. Experience in the Africa continent. Specific experience in East Africa region is desirable iii. Demonstrated availability of skills in thefollowing areas: legal, social and policy analysis, and conflict management iv. notice_text: PUBLIC PROCUREMENT AND DISPOSAL OF PUBLIC ASSETS AUTHORITY REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) Uganda - Strengthening Readiness for e-government Procurement in Uganda Grant No.: TF017113 Assignment Title: E-GP PROJECT MANAGER Reference No : PPDA-WB/CONS/13-14/004 The Government of Uganda has applied for financing from the World Bank towards strengthening readiness for Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) in Uganda, , and intends to apply part of the proceeds for recruitment of an E-GP Project Manager. The goal of the e-GP Project is to effectivelysupport the Government with the introduction and implementation of e-procurement in Uganda as part of the on-going Public Financial Management Reforms that aims at enhancing efficiency and transparency in public procurement. The Public Procurement and Disposal of Public Assets Authority (PPDA) now invites eligible candidates to apply for the position of e-GP Project Manager. The successful Candidate shall be responsible for the day to day management of the implementation of e-procurement under the oversight of the Executive Director and providing professional competence in project management to thee-GP Project. The e-GP Project Manager shall be engaged against a one(1) year time-based contract renewable upon the requirement and satisfactory performance. 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Government of Uganda developed and adopted the e-government strategic policy framework 2010 together with the IT policy and cyber laws as commitment towards improving governance through application of information and communication technology. Given that Government spends over half of its budget through public procurement; it was highlighted as one of the key Government functions to be transformed by introducing electronicprocurement (e-procurement) systems. E-procurement is part of the Public FinancialManagement (PFM) reforms that aims at enhancing efficiency and transparency in public procurement. E-procurement is an initiative that can generate major efficiency gains with the benefits such as: (i) improved transparency in procurement procedures and practices, (ii) efficiency throughoutthe procurement process and reduced procurement cycle time, (iii) confidentiality, integrity and authenticity of all transactions and data between the procurement entities and the suppliers, and (iv) enabling an electronictrail of documents stored in the Procurement Management Information System. E-procurement is an initiative that can generate major efficiency gains with the benefits such as: a) Improved transparency in procurement proceduresand practices. b) Efficiency throughout the procurement process and reduced procurement cycle time. c) Increased competition and transparency. d) Confidentiality, integrity and authenticity of all transactions and data between the procurement entities and the suppliers. e) Enabled electronic trail of documents stored in the Procurement Management Information System. Implementation of e-procurement is being spearheaded by the PPDA under the oversight of the Ministry of Finance through the e-procurement steering committee. 2.0 Objective OF THE ASSIGNMENT The Project Manager shall be responsible for the day to day management of the implementation of e-procurement under the oversight of the Executive Director. The following objectives are designed to meet that goal: a) Ensure the e-GP project is clearly defined. b) Identify the project risks and develop a strategy to manage those risks. c) Determinethe project resource requirements and budget accordingly. d) Effective management of all contracts related to the project. e) Meet all Quality Assurance standards for Project Management. f) Disseminate the requisite knowledge and capability within the Government of Uganda to support the effective operation of the E-GP. 3.0 Scope of the Services The e-GP Project Manager will provideprofessional competence in project management to the e-GP Project . The Project Managers' responsibilities include: a) Lead and manage the technical team that will provide critical support for the implementation of the e-GP project. b) Updating and maintaining a Project Charter outlining management structures, reporting and coordination arrangement, staffing requirements, and projectplan; c) Supportingthe e-GP Technical and Steering Committee key decision making throughprovision of documentation and communication of agreed specifications, goals, objectives, scope, outputs, resources required, budget, schedule, project structure, roles and responsibilities; d) Developing and updating detailed project plans, budgets for the project and supplemental Plans (Risk, change, capacity building, monitoring and communication management plans) and obtaining the requisite approvals. e) Monitoring the project's progress against the approved plan and budget and provide formal progress reports to the Executive Director on a monthly basis. f) Ensuring the availability of the system infrastructure (with regard to the help desk, support, training, information technology [IT] infrastructure and network connectivity); g) Coordination and review of consultants' reports and advise the e-GP Technical Committee on the quality of the outputs, particularly as they pertain to the project goals and objectives. h) Preparing and maintaining a Risk Management Plan which identifies and analyses risks to the project. The Risk Management Plan should provide strategies to manage the risks for the duration of the project identifying risks and implementing strategies to manage them; i) Preparing for and coordinating e-GP Technical and Steering Committeemeetings and acting as a communication focal point to the e-GP Technical and the Steering Committees; j) Maintaining all project documentation and make them avail them to the Quality Assurance requirements that the e-GP Steering Committee may establish. k) Taking responsibility for deliverables as defined in the project plan; l) Ensuring that the e-GP project utilizes 'best practice' in large-scale project management, including quality management principles. m) Ensure that all project documentations are securely kept and available. n) Promptly respond to all communications and handle issues. o) Act as theSecretariat for the oversight committees for e-GP 4.0 Deliverables The Project Manager will report to the Executive Director PPDA and in particular will be responsiblefor- a) Inception Report on the third week of the first month after contract signing. An outline of the constraints and assumptions affecting the planning process iii. A listing of the critical success factors considered iv. An outline of the high-level Project Risks that have been identified v. A high-level description of the Project Scope vi. List of prioritized issues to be resolved showing who is responsible for addressing those issues. c) Submission of quarterly performance reports of the Project Team Members and the Consultants to the Executive Director. d) Submission of an Assignment Completion report on completion of the contract. 5.0 CONTRACT TERMS The Project Manager will be engaged on a one (1) year time-based contract renewable upon business need and satisfactory performance. P109224 CR. NO. IDA47690 1. The Government of Uganda has received a credit from the InternationalDevelopment Association towards the cost of the Agricultural Technology and agribusiness Advisory Services PROJECT (ATAAS) and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services ("the services") include conducting a feasibility study to determine the Information Communication Technology Infrastructure needs for the National Agricultural Research Organisation (NARO) and the National Agricultural Advisory Services (NAADS) and supporting them in overseeing implementation of the system. The objective of the study is to identify and determine appropriate ICT infrastructure and systems needed to be implemented to enhance and promote efficiency in the critical business functions of NARO and NAADS, as well as support linkages between research, extension and farmers and other key stakeholders throughprovisioning of timely information to either party for decision making. Specific objectives include: (i) Review and document all existing literature, data and information processing and delivery methods, systems and procedures within NARO and NAADS including all their operational offices in Uganda. (ii) Develop an analysis of the ICT requirements that need to be implemented in all NARO and NAADS operational offices/stations to increase internal individual organisational efficiency in support of the development informational requirements for the farmers while allowing interoperabilitybetween existing and new ICT systems. (iii) Identify appropriate ICT solutions that will strengthen research, extension/advisory and farmer relationships through efficient information sharing and knowledge management. (iv) Develop detailed technical requirements for the appropriate ICT infrastructure systems that will support implementation of identified ICT solutions in support of information sharing and knowledge management between NAADs and NARO and ultimately the farmers. (v) Assistwith the selection of ICT systems implementation vendor and provide support in overseeing implementation. 2. The National Agricultural Research Organization now invites eligible and qualified consults ('Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and experience to performthe Services. This shall include technical and managerial capabilities of the firm including relevant experience on similar assignments, core business and years in business, summary profiles of staff in the firm etc 3. Minimum Qualifications of the Consultant : a) The consultant should have a minimum of 10 years of relevantproven expertise and knowledge in similar undertakings in Africa especially in Uganda. The Government of Uganda (GoU) has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of Transport Sector Development Project (TSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for ConsultancyServices for the Development of a Model for the Estimation of the Cost of Road Accidents to the Economy. 2. title: Consultancy  Services for design of a unified network solution with infrastructure and Implementation Plan for interconnecting Health facilities for voice and data communication
notice_text: THE REPUBLIC OF UGANDA MINISTRY OF HEALTH UGANDA HeALTH SYSTEMS STRENGTHENING PROJECT REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (EOI) CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR design OF a unified network solution with infrastructure and Implementation Plan for interconnecting Health facilities for voice and data communication PROCUREMENT REFERENCE N o .: MOH-UHSSP/SVCs/2012-13/00003 1. This request for Expressions of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this project that appeared on the UN Development Business on-line on 16 th February 2011. 2. The Government of Uganda has received a Credit from International Development Association towards the cost of Uganda Health Systems Strengthening Project (UHSSP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this credit to payments under the contract for consultancy services for design a unified network solution with infrastructure and Implementation Plan for interconnecting Health facilities for voice and data communication . 3. The overall objective of the consultancy is to design a unified network solution that will strengthen the functionality of health facilities by providing voice (VOIP) and data communication in the sector for data collection and proper information management. The specific objectives of theconsultancy are: a. To undertake a comprehensive assessment of the existing e-Health communication systems for a sample of 1 NRH, 2 RRH, 2 GH and 4 HCIV. This includes an assessment of: i. Appropriateness of existing networks (voice & data) to the services offered at each level. ii. Availability of relevant human resources to provide frontline support. iii. Condition of all existing computing infrastructure (hardware and software) and their appropriateness for the level of service provided by the health facility. iv. Capacity and interoperability of available computing and network infrastructure with respect to the health care services offered. b. To provide a detailed design of a unified network system for the health sector, cognisant of existing systems and forthcoming technological solutions. c. To propose new networks and communicationinfrastructure for UHSSP health facilities at their different levels and develop a master plan for the infrastructure with drawings, specifications and bills of quantities. The consulting services ("the Services") shall include an assessment of the current state of communication networks and development of a network framework for the health sector. Specifically it will include An assessment of : i. the available ICT and health-related documentation within the sector and those of other health systems with best practices. ii. adequacy of the existing computing and network hardware and software in relation to the schedule of services rendered at respective levels. iii. any other relevant documentation needed for the development of effective and efficient delivery of services by the health facilities. Detailed assessment of the available staff and recommendations of necessary cadre and training requirements in the context of this network infrastructure. This is to ensure proper acquisition, use and maintenance of technological solutions. Carry out detailed study of the central server room infrastructure and propose designs based on best practices, to accommodate remote connectivity from all districts, hospitals, health related facilities and stakeholders. Remodelling the design and provision of the following services among health facilities: i. Functionaland fully equipped computing infrastructure control rooms (server rooms). ii. Local area networks (LANs). iii. Innovative solutions that can be implemented ateach level of healthcare. Design a secure post-disaster data recovery system that will be a failsafe beyond the functionality of the ministerial server room. Propose respective knowledge management solutions to automateinformation accessibility and presentation, to respective developmentpartners and scholars putting in consideration patient information security & information rights of use. g. Development of detailed designs, specifications, bills of quantities, confidential cost estimates and tender documents for the proposed network solution that will be funded by UHSSP with World Band funding. The Ministry of Health now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short listing criteria are: a. Experience in designing and setting up ICT networks and communication systems. b. Experience in development of e-communications systems in countries with similar economic conditions like Uganda. c. Work experience as an ICT consulting firm of at a least five years. d. Availability of qualified and skilled personnel. 6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers , May 2004 revised October 2006 and May 2010 ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications. A Consultant will beselected in accordance with the Selection Based on Consultants' Qualifications (CQS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. 9. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 09:00 to 17:00 hours (Local time). 10. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below ( in person or by e-mail) by 10:00 am, on 17 th December 2012 . The Procurement Specialist, Uganda Health Systems Strengthening Project Ministry of Health, Room D108, Plot 6 Lourdel Road, KAMPALA, UGANDA.
