title: Comprehensive situation assessment and preparation of a Water Management Zone WMZ strategy;as well as Catchment water resources development and management plans for Kyoga WMZ and Upper Nile, and a Water Resources Information System in 4 lots
notice_text: MINISTRY OF WATER AND ENVIRONMENT WATER MANAGEMENT & DEVELOPMENT PROJECT REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTANTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) [ UGANDA ] Project ID: P123204 Reference No . MWE/SRVCS/12-13/01527a Assignment Title: Lot 1: Comprehensive situation assessment and preparation of a Water Management Zone WMZ strategy and action plan for Upper Nile WMZ, Lot 2: Preparation of two(2) Catchment water resources development and management plans in Kyoga WMZ, Lot 3: Preparation of two(2) Catchment water resources development and management plans in Upper Nile WMZ, Lot 4: Detailed assessment of requirements for Water Resources Information System. This Request for Expressions of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this project that appeared in the UN Development Business online (UNDB online - GPN No. WB2813-08/12) on 22nd August 2012, and in the regional media – the East African Newspaper on 3rd September 2012. The Government of Uganda has applied for financing from The WorldBank towards the cost of the Water Management & Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for eligible payments under consultancy services for the following assignments; Lot 1: Comprehensive situation assessment and preparation of a Water Management Zone WMZ strategy and action plan for Upper Nile WMZ - The assignment under Lot 1 will run for 12 months. Its objective is to conduct a situational assessment for management and development issues related to water resources, evaluate alternative strategies for managing and developing water resources within the Upper Nile WMZ, prepare and cost a Water Management and Development Strategy for theUpper Nile WMZ on the basis of consultations with stakeholders and the situational analysis and formulate an action plan based on the agreed strategy Lot 2: Preparation of two (2) Catchment water resources development and management plans in Kyoga WMZ The assignment under Lot 2 which will run for 10 months is intended to prepare Catchment Water Resources Development and Management Plans for two catchments in the Kyoga WMZ through an integrated and participatory catchment planning process. The plans would consits of two elements; first, a number of agreed investments ininfrastructure and other interventions; and second, various water management interventions and actions meant to help resolve conflict, conserve and protect the catchment and its natural resources, and ensure equitable access to and use of water resources. Investments will be prepared to pre-feasibility level. Lot 3: Preparation of two (2) Catchment water resources development and management plans in Upper Nile WMZ, The assignment under Lot 3 will run for 10 months and its objective is similar to that of Lot 2. Work will involve preparation of the Catchment Water Resources Development and Management Plans for two catchments in the Upper Nile WMZ through an integrated and participatory catchmentplanning process. The plans will consits of two elements; first, a number of agreed investments in infrastructure and other interventions; and second, various water management interventions and actions meant to help resolve conflict, conserve and protect the catchment and its natural resources, and ensure equitable access to and use of water resources. Investments will be prepared to pre-feasibility level. Lot 4: Detailed assessment of requirements for Water Resources Information System. - The assignment under Lot 4 will run for 10 months. Its objective is todesign and prepare an implimentation plan to develop a Water Information System (WIS) covering all water-related data, under-pinned by a Hydrological Information System (HIS). The HIS will include an upgraded hydrologic network to collect primary data on surface, ground water, meteorology, and water quality at the required intensity and frequency; time-effective transmission; and data processing,analysis and storage. In addition to HIS data, WIS will also include secondary processed data from water sector stakeholders at specified formats and frequency; spatial datasets from remote sensing, and existing topographic, bathymetric, ecological and environmental, and socio-economic surveys; Information Management System (IMS) with Hydrologic Design Aids (HDAs) to process data into higher level information products; Knowledge Management System (KMS) with interfaces to DSS and external models; and a Data Dissemination System (DDS) to facilitate data access and sharing. The Ministry of Water and Environment now invites eligible consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services including brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff,proof of legal status, knowledge and specific experience, training, monitoring and impact evaluation, promotion of private sector participation). The assignments implementation period ranges between 9 and 12 months commencing in July 2013. The short listing criteria, is not limited to but, will include experience in at least 5 similar assignments of which 2 should have been in Sub- Saharan Africa, and presence of appropriate skills among staff in the areas of situation analysis, strategy preparation and formulation, water resources management and action plans as well as water resources information systems. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers [January 2011] ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. International Firms should associate with local (Ugandan) firms in order to build local capacity. The form of association, where applicable, should be indicated in the Expression of Interest. A consultant will be selected in accordancewith the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. Expressions of Interest (One original plus five copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below.The packages must be clearly marked with the Lot number and the tiltleof the assignment, for example, "Lot 1: Expression of Interest for Comprehensive situation assessment and preparation of a Water Management Zone (WMZ) strategy and action plan for Upper Nile WMZ" Consultants expressing interest in more than one Lot should demonstrate capacity,and that they qualify to executethese Lots. Written Expressions of Interest must bedelivered to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e- mail) by 11.00 hours, 7th December2012. notice_text: Ministry of Water & Environment WATER MANAGEMENT & DEVELOPMENT PROJECT THE WORLD BANK PROJECT ID: P123204 GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE 1) The Government of the Republic of Uganda has applied for a loan from the World Bank in the amount of US$ 135,000,000.00 towards the Water Management & Development Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds to paymentsof goods, works, consulting services, and related services to be procured under this project. The project will be implemented by the Ministry of Water and Environment, and National Water and Sewerage Corporation. 2) The project consists of three components: Component 1: Investment in Integrated Water Resources Development and Management: This component will beconducted under the Directorate of Water Resources Management (DWRM).It includes three sub-components; (i) identification, preparation andimplementation of selected priority investments through a participatory catchment planning process in the Kyoga and Upper Nile Water Management Zones (WMZs), (ii) Improvement of the national water resources monitoring and information systems, and (iii) Kalagala offset sustainable management plan. Procurement under Component 1 will include consulting services for comprehensive assessment and preparation of WMZ strategies and action plans for Kyoga and Upper Nile, preparation of catchment water resources development and management plans in the two WMZs, feasibility studies for various investments such as multipurpose dams, as will be identified in the catchment plans in Kyoga and Upper Nile WMZs, capacity building & facilitating the work of Catchment Management Organizations (CMO) inparticipating WMZs and detailed assessment of requirements for a Water Resources Information System. Component 2: Infrastructure Investments in Urban Water Supply and Sanitation/Sewerage and Catchment/Source Protection: This component includes (i) Town Water Supply and Sanitation under National Water and Sewerage Corporation (NWSC) including construction, improvement and expansion of priority watersupply infrastructure and sanitation/sewerage services in the municipalities of Arua, Gulu, Ishaka-Bushenyi, and Mbale. Procurement under this sub-component will include provision of consulting services for feasibility studies, detailed design and construction supervision of thewater supply and sewerage networks of the municipalities in Arua, Gulu, Ishaka-Bushenyi, and Mbale including the respective upgrades of thewater treatment plants and waste water treatment plants. In addition,works contracts will be procured for construction and expansion of water supply and sewerage networks in the towns aforementioned, and (ii)Town Water Supply and Sanitation implemented by Directorate of Water Development (DWD). The project activities under this sub-component will include provision of consultancy services for design review, detailed design and construction supervision of water supply schemes in Butaleja-Busolwe, Budaka, Kadama, Tirinyi-Kibuku, Busia, Pallisa, Kumi-Nyero-Ngora, Rukungiri, Katwe-Kabatoro and Koboko. Works contracts will also be procured under this sub-component for construction and expansionof water supply systems in the aforementioned towns under DWD. Component 3: Strengthening Institutions for Effective Project Implementation. This component will support overall coordination and implementation of the project by the respective departments and directorates of Ministryof Water & Environment (MWE) and NWSC and will be coordinated by the Water Sector Liaison Division (WSLD) of MWE. Procurement under this component will include recruitment of individual consultants to cover staffing gaps and purchase of stationery, furniture, and other low value goods to support project execution. 3) Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank's Guidelines: Procurement under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits ( January 2011 ), and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the guidelines. Consulting services will be selected in accordance with the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers ( January 2011 ) . Specific procurement notices for contracts to be bid under the World Bank's International Competitive Bidding (ICB) procedures and for contracts for consultancy services will be announced, as they becomeavailable, in UN Development Business and dgMarket , and in local and regional newspapers: The New Vision , The Daily Monitor and The East African . 4) Interested eligible bidders who wish to be included on the mailing list to receive invitations to bid under ICBprocedures, and interested consultants who wish to receive a copy of advertisement requesting expressions of interest for consultancy contracts, or those requiring additional information, should contact the address below: The Head, Procurement Procurement and Disposal Unit Ministry of Water and Environment Plot 22/28 Port Bell Road, Luzira P.O. This request for Expressions of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this project that appeared on-line in UN Development Business on 2 nd March 2011. 2. The Government of Uganda has received a Credit from International Development Association towards the cost of East African Public Health Laboratories Networking Project (EAPHLNP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan to payments under the contract for e ngagement of a Consultant for Consultancy services to provide Technical Assistance to Laboratories in Uganda to achieve ISO 15189 Accreditation. 3. The objectives of the consultancy are: a. to design and implement quality improvement projects at satellite laboratory sites under the EAPHLNP in Uganda. b. to provide technical assistance to the satellite laboratories under the project to achieve ISO 15189 accreditation using the WHO/AFRO Stepwise approach. The specific objectives of this consultancy includes among others; i. Training the laboratory staff at the satellite laboratory sites in Good Clinical and Laboratory Practice (GCLP). ii. Assisting the satellite laboratories sites prepare for stepwise accreditation by guiding in writing the required (Standard Operating Procedures) SOPs and other normative documents. iii. Assessing the project laboratory sites progress towards accreditationwith the aim of identifying gaps in performance. iv. Assisting the satellite laboratory sites in implementing of Quality Improvement Projects (QIPs) in line with the gaps identified during theassessments. v. Training laboratory mentors into mentoring laboratories, Laboratory assessors and (Strengthening Laboratory Management Towards Accreditation)SLMTA processes. vi. Advise the Laboratory accreditation and Networking Technical Working Group (LABANW TWG) on setting up an External Quality Assessment Schemefor the laboratories in the network with view of scaling it up to other laboratories in the region vii. Advise LABANW TWG on how to steer the laboratories in the network towards accreditation. The estimated duration for the assignment is 24 months . 4. The Ministry of Health now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short listing criteria are: a. Experience in at least 3 similar assignments in guiding laboratories to international accreditation. b. Experience in at least 3 similar assignments in implementation of Laboratory Quality Improvement Projects in Public health Laboratory services settings in countries with similar economic conditions like Uganda. c. Work experience as a consulting firm for a minimum of five years. d. Availability of appropriate skills among staff. 5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers , May 2004 revised October 2006 and May 2010 ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. 6. notice_text: UGANDA MINISTRY OF ENERGY AND MINERAL DEVELOPMENT SALE OF FEASIBILITY STUDY REPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN OIL REFINERY IN UGANDA Background, Following the discovery of commercial oil and gas reserves in the country, the Government of Uganda through the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development commissioned a feasibility study for the development of an oil refinery in the country. The feasibility study, conducted by Foster Wheeler Energy Limited UK, commenced in January 2010 and was successfully completed in August 2010. This study assessed the crude production potential, size and configuration of the refinery, location, financing options, social and environmental assessment, among others. In addition, a comparative analysis of constructing a refinery versus acrude export pipeline was done. The study findings showed the development of a refinery in Uganda is not only feasible but is better optioneconomically than a crude export pipeline. Sale of report: The ministry of Energy and Mineral Development now seeks to avail contents of the Feasibility Study Report to interested parties. The overall report includes the following sections: Upstream Production Analysis, Market Survey, Refinery Configurations, Financial Analysis, Site Selection, Crude Pipeline Analysis, among others. The complete report can now be purchased from the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development. title: VACANT POSTS
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF UGANDA MINISTRY OF HEALTH REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST MOH-UHSSP/SVCS/2010-11/00008 1.0 Introduction. The Government of The Republic of Uganda has received for financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost ofthe Uganda Health Systems Strengthening Project (UHSSP). The Project objective is to deliver the Uganda National Minimum Health Care Package (UNMHCP), with a focus on maternal health, newborn careand family panning through improving: human resources for health; physical health infrastructure; and management, leadership and accountability for health service delivery. Implementation of the Project is mainstreamed into the Government Systems through the existing Institutional arrangements. The Government wishes to engage the Services of suitably qualified candidates to fill the vacant posts under the UHSSP project as specifiedbelow: 2.0 Human Resource for Health(HRH) MIS Advisor The objective of the Technical Assistance is to strengthen and consolidate the Human Resource Management Information Systems at the Ministry of Health for effective and efficient implementation of the human resource functions. 2.2 Reporting The position holder will work directly with the MoH to provide technical assistance in the areas of strategic human resource information management and use. This will be a full time position. The primary counterparts will the heads of HRD and HRM Divisions. The TA will be answerable to the Under Secretary (Finance and Administration) in the MOH. 2.3 Responsibilities and Tasks: In accordance with the Project Objectives, the HRH MIS Advisor shall; i. Ensure the functioning of the HRMIS to provide reliable HRH data ii. Focus on developing capacity for use and sustenance of the HRMIS iii. Work closely with the Ministry of Health's Human Resources team and Resource Center team to implement data collection plan and related forms. iv. Ensure current accurate data entry and data quality. v. Participate in and supervise activities of data entry, which include entry of new records as well as entry of data updates collected from all levels of district health facilities. vi. Ensure system is operational with current, accurate data. Coordinate efforts with all HRIS stakeholders. vii. Maintain access accounts to database ensuring appropriate user policies and security is enforced. viii. Communicate regularly with technical, applications, and operational staff, to ensure overall database integrity and security. ix. Generate reports as needed for Ministry of Health staff and related stakeholders. x. Provide training for database users and support for developing regular and ad hoc reports so that key users are confident in using the HRISto respond to information needs. xi. Develop a culture among the key stakeholders of using data for decisions making and as new features are implemented, ensure all staff are informed of new features and are properly trained. 2.4. Qualifications and Competences. i. The applicants must be Nationals of East African Community with a Masters d egree in Computer Science, Information Technology or closely related field from a recognized University / Institution. ii. Knowledge of database software and development including Open Source systems (Linux, Apache, PHP, MySQL) iii. Experience in operations research, working with government and donorsand in working as leader and manager in multi-sectoral environment iv. A minimum of three-years related database management experience Demonstrated competence to assess priorities and manage a variety of activities in a time-sensitive environment and meet deadlines with attention to detail and quality. vi. Ability to work as an effective team member in a complex and fast paced environment. vii. Strong verbal and written English language skills. Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to interact professionally with diverse people, clients and consultants 2.5 Deliverables i. HRMIS reports ii. Monthly, quarterly and annual HR technical reports related to the assignment. iii. Progress reports on specific tasks of the assignment. iv. Completion Report of the assignment. 3.0 Human Resource for Health Policy Advisor 3.1 Objectives of the Assignment The objective of the Technical Assistance is to strengthen and consolidate the human resource management information systems at the Ministry of Health for effective and efficient implementation of the human resource functions. 3.2 Reporting The position holder will work directly with the MoH to provide technical assistance in the areas of strategic human resource information management and use. This will be a full time position. The primary counterparts will the heads of HRD and HRM Divisions. The TA will be answerable to the Under Secretary ( Finance and Administration) in the MOH. 3.3 Responsibilities and tasks: In accordance with the Project Objectives, the HRH Policy Advisor shall; Interpret the recommendations in the restructuring report and developimplementation strategy and plan for consolidation of human resource management functions at the Ministry of Health. Advise on competences required for the key positions in the structurefor consolidated HRH functions at the MoH, and provide technical support in the staff recruitment. Provide technical support in developing and implementation of mechanisms for ensuring harmony and coordination of plans, activities, reports, and decisions within the HR divisions in the MoH, as well as with key stakeholders in the MoH and the health sector through the Human Resource Working Group.  SENIOR COMMUNICATIONS SPECIALIST (1 NO.)
notice_text: Government of Uganda Transport Sector Development Project (TSDP) Project ID No.: P092837 Request for Expression of Interest For TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO UGANDA NATIONAL ROADS AUTHORITY (UNRA): SENIOR COMMUNICATIONS SPECIALIST (1 No.) Procurement Reference No.: UNRA/Services/2010-11/00020/05/01/xx Introduction This request for Expression of Interest follows the General Procurement Notice for the TSDP Project that was published online on the UNDB and the Development Gateway Market websites on 17 th July 2010. The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank and DFID towards the cost of the Transport Sector Development Project (TSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds topayments for the provision of Technical Assistance for Capacity Building to UNRA. Objectives of the Assignment This service aims to develop and increase institutional capacity of UNRA in the area of Strategic Communications by preparing and implementing a robust and innovative communications strategy aimed at promotingpublic awareness of UNRA's activities and results; and building a solid reputation for the authority as an efficient public service delivery entity in Uganda. 3. Terms of Reference and Scope of Services The Specialists' scope of work shall include: - Under the general guidance of the Executive Director of the Uganda National Roads Authority (UNRA), responsible for the conceptualization, planning, development, execution, monitoring and evaluation of an organization branding, advocacy and communication strategy to promote the Authority's image, activities and programmes both in Uganda and abroad; Formulation of the Communications Strategy shall include undertakingof communications audit, a stakeholder mapping and desk review. The consultant shall also establish a communications baseline either through previous strategies or researches carried out in the sector addressing public perceptions of the roads sector or a media content analysis covering the last two years. Maintain a media profile for all relevant issues and support follow-up on Special Issues of Public Interest such as Road Safety, Road Sector HIV Awareness, Environmental Conservation, Resettlement of Roads Project Affected Persons, Gender Mainstreaming, Good Governance and Accountability, etc; Manages media activities such as organizing visits to project sites, facilitating photo coverage and TV footage, radio interviews and special events, and utilizes both web-based and traditional media when appropriate to generate and maintain public interest on National Roads issues, and tell the story of UNRA's contribution to national economic development. Develops a strategy to get National Roads issues into the public domain, and strengthen political will in support of UNRA's mission and objectives, (including communication assessment and analysis, developmentof a communication plan, strategic use of resources and involvement in key programme processes, especially situation analysis, reviews and evaluations); In coordination with the Executive Director, UNRA, participates in global advocacy activities by planning visits to International Forums and/or workshops, including preparation of information materials (e.g., press releases, programme summaries, country fact sheets and media kits), and necessary logistic arrangements; Advises the Executive Director and the UNRA Corporate Communications team on the effective use of tools of mass communication, including press briefings and conferences and media interviews, to achieve organizational objectives; Adapts and disseminates advocacy materials to identified target audiences, arranging translations into local language(s), as necessary. Identifies the need for additional materials/activities, such as radio and television programmes, publications, photographs, websites, etc., toadvocate and promote organizational goals within the country, and manage their production and distribution to the target audiences; Adequately assist in standardizing the Authority's management reports, press releases, speeches and briefing notes (for the Executive Director) including coordination of the drafting of the Authority's reportsto external stakeholders; Ensure quality of reports, project proposals and other written material. This includes standard layout, translations, branding, coherence with proposal / report guidelines, statistics and budget review. Perform any other duties as may be assigned by the Executive Director. 4 . Reporting The Communications Specialist will report to the Executive Director. The Specialist shall also work closely with the UNRA Corporate Communications Manager and the Project Coordinator. 5. Key Results / Outputs Key Tasks Design a phased, budgeted and consultative communications strategy for the Roads Sector in Uganda. Ensure quality materials of UNRA for media / development partners / stakeholders / public for in-country and international advocacy and resource mobilization purposes. Provide timely and quality material in support of UNRA activities forinternal and external use. Assist UNRA in standardizing reports and publications Ensure quality assurance Preparation and submission of quarterly reports as part of the quarterly reports to the World Bank within 45 days from the end of the quarter. Expected Outputs Communications strategy for the Roads Sector to be submitted within two months of the commencement of the Specialist's services UNRA branding, advocacy and communication strategy to be submitted within two months of the commencement of the Specialist's services. Press releases, speeches, briefing notes, fact sheets throughout the duration of the contract. UNRA reports and proposals ready for submission to donors throughout the duration of the contract. Quality assured for all type of reports, proposals, concept papers and management reports throughout the duration of the contract. Quarterly reports on Communications Activities in UNRA are submitted throughout the duration of the contract. 6. Required Qualifications and Experience Advanced university degree in Communication, Journalism, Public Relations or equivalent professional work experience in the communication area combined with advanced university degree in a related discipline; At least ten (10) years progressively responsible professional work experience in communication, print and broadcast media and programme monitoring and evaluation, of which two years should be in developing countries. Working experience with a large organization like UNRA will be an added advantage. The Specialist shall also be experienced in designing and implementing development communications strategies. Advanced ability to express clearly and concisely ideas and concepts in written form; specific skills in writing press releases, speeches, articles / stories for traditional and electronic media, report writing and editing; Proven ability to conceptualize, plan and execute ideas, as well as impart knowledge and teaching skills; Proven ability to effectively manage relationships with media, government officials, the general public and Development partners; Strong working knowledge of computer systems and applications including DTP, specifically interactive digital media and Red Dot; Proven ability to work both independently and as part of a team; Ability to work in an international and multicultural environment; Excellent team player; High organizational capability; Fluency in English. Service Time The assignment shall be for a period of Two (2) years including a 6 months probation period. title: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR CHIEF GOVERNMENT VALUER
notice_text: The Republic of Uganda SECOND PRIVATE SECTOR COMPETITIVENESS PROJECT (PSCP II) PRIVATE SECTOR CHIEF GOVERNMENT VALUER CREDIT NUMBER: 3975-UG PROJECT ID NUMBER: P083809 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST The Government of Uganda is in the fourth year of implementing the Land Component of the Private Sector Competitiveness Project II (PSCP II) with funding secured through the World Bank. This undertaking includes efforts to rehabilitate, modernize and update service delivery procedures, land records, maps and other legal instruments that comprise the Land Registration system. This program is a critical component of the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development's (MoLHUD) Land Sector Strategic Plan (LSSP) to systematically transform and improve its ability to deliver land services efficiently. The Ministry of Lands Housing and Urban Development would like to recruit a Chief Government Valuer to fill an existing vacancy in the Valuation Division. This will provide leadership, supervision and also help deal with PSCP II generatedwork flowing through the Valuation Division. This is a position that requires comprehensive knowledge and extensive specialized experiencein land valuation, land administration and real estate management anddevelopment. 2.0 Objective The overall purpose of the Chief Government Valuer is to provide needed expertise, advice and technical support to the MoLHUD in fulfilling her statutory and administrative obligations. To assure technical quality and legal compliance regarding the valuation of land and real estate interests on behalf of the Government of Uganda. 3.0 Scope of the Assignment The main task of the Chief Government Valuer is to provide technically sound land valuation expertise, administrative and advisory serviceswith respect to all matters pertaining to the valuation of governmentland and real estate interests, and to contribute to PSCP II implementation demands according to schedule and in accordance with internationally recognized best practices and standards. The Chief Government Valuer will serve on behalf of the Government ofUganda as an officer of the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Development and will assist the Client in decision making, quality assurance andcontrol of Government land valuation cases. He or she will assist in the development of regulations and guidelines for managing estate agents and modern valuation techniques, land market analysis and applications using professionally accepted hardware and software to facilitate the implementation of PSCP II Land Component activities and ensure that implementation schedules and quality standards are met. 4.0 Specific Duties of a Chief Government Valuer The specific duties of the Chief Government Valuer are as follows: q Heading and supervising the Valuation Division, including Planning and Budgeting for the effective delivery of the valuation function. q Provide input on valuation during the review and development of land administration policies, legislation, standards, regulations and guidelines q Monitor and report on the implementation of land administration policies, laws, standards and regulations that relate to valuation. q Advise Government on the real property valuation q Value Property for purchase and compensation by Government. q Value Property for rent by Government q Assess Stamp Duty q Advise Government on Rating Properties q Supervise the compilation, proper custody and update of valuation records. q Provide technical support, support supervision and training to local governments and other Stakeholders on matters regarding or incidental to valuation. q Assist the Ministry management personnel in the strategic implementation of the PSCP II Land Component as needed. q Any other official duties that may be assigned from time to time 5.0 Key Outputs q Technical input and leading in the planning and budgeting process of the Valuation Division. q Valuation inputs during the review and development of land administration policies, legislation, standards, regulations and guidelines provided. q Implementation of land administration policies, laws standards and regulations monitored and reported. q Valuations undertaken on behalf of the Government. q Valuation technical staff supervised, mentored to assure their technical and professional development and appraised. q Compilation, proper custody and update of valuation records supervised. q Technical support, support supervision and training to local governments and other Stakeholders on matters regarding or incidental to valuation provided. q PSCP II Land Component data and operations processed in a timely manner to prevent bottlenecks in implementation schedules 6.0 Minimum Qualification: 6.1 Academic qualifications: q Honors Bachelors degree in Land Economics or related discipline q A Post Graduate qualification from an accredited University in Valuation, Land Law, Surveying, Land Management or Land Administration. q A Masters Degree in any of the above fields will be an added advantage 6.2 Additional Knowledge and Skills q Should have competence in land Administration policies, legislation, standards and regulations and professional ethics of the practice of valuation in Uganda or other Commonwealth countries. Discretion and sound judgment in applying professional expertise to legal and administrative issues. q Computer literate preferably with some experience in modern valuationtechniques, Land market analysis and applications using professionally accepted hardware and software. Strong analytical ability to conduct research on a range of valuation, land market and land administration issues, including those of a unique and/or complex nature q Planning and organizing # Ability to develop clear goals; identifies priority activities and assignments, allocates appropriate amount of time and resources to ensure that timelines for responses to staff and other deadlines are met; uses time efficiently. q Should possess good supervisory skills with strong interpersonal and communication skills and ability to lead a team of skilled professionals and technical support staff. q Performance management # Ability to delegate the appropriate responsibility, accountability and decision-making authority; makes sure that roles, responsibilities and reporting lines are clear to staff members; regularly discusses performance and provides feedback and coaching to staff; encourages risk-taking and supports creativity and initiative; actively supports the development and career aspirations of staff; appraises performance fairly. q Fluency in oral and written English is required. The CGV shall communicate, compile and submit all reports in the English language, in hardcopy and in electronic format whenever required. 6.3 Experience q A minimum of 12 years working experience in the field of land administration with at least 3 years exposure to management at a level of Principal Government Valuer within Government or an equivalent level in areputable organization. q Preferably registered with the relevant professional body. q Demonstrated progressive responsibility and experience in land valuation, land administration and management. q Experience in the application of Government regulations and rules, policies and procedures with respect to valuation as well as experience in decision-making processes in public service organizations and/or supervisory experience in managing in a team environment is an added advantage. 7.0 Reporting requirements The Chief Government Valuer shall report to the Commissioner for LandAdministration in the MLHUD and S/he will liaise with the Land Component Secretariat/PSCP II, of the Ministry on matters pertaining to the PSCP II and work closely with the Project Implementation Unit of the PSCP II of the PSFU. 8.0 Duration of the Assignment q The expected duration of contract for the Chief Government Valuer is two (2) years, renewable only at the discretion of the Accounting Officer. The Expression of Interest for those who responded to the earlier advert will also be considered so they need not re-submit 5. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers (Current Edition) 6. Interested consultants may obtain further information from the Director, Land Management at the address below during office hours i.e. 8.30am-5.00pm. The Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development Attention: Mr Justin L. M. Bwogi Plot 13/15 Parliament Avenue P.O.Box 7096 Kampala, Uganda Tel No.0414 252663 Email: bwogi@mlhud.go.ug 7. notice_text: MINISTRY OF EDUCATION AND SPORTS REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST COUNTRY : Uganda NAME OF PROJECT : Uganda Post Primary Education and Training Program (UPPET) ASSIGNMENTS : Consultancy Services to Design and Operationalize the Secondary Teacher Development and Management System for Uganda LOAN/CREDIT No. : 4570-UG PROJECT ID No. : P110803 PROCUREMENT REF. No. : MoES/Srvcs/09-10/3222. This Request for Expression of Interest (EoI) follows the General Procurement Notice for this project which appeared in the DG Market of August 18 th 2009 and New Vision and East African Publications of August 13 th and August 17 th 2009 respectively, and is open to all eligible bidders as defined inthe World Banks' Guidelines for Selection and Employment of Consultants (current edition). The Government of Uganda has secured financing from the World Bank towards support for the implementation of the Uganda Post-Primary Education and Training Project (UPPET) and wishes to apply some of the proceeds to financing the Consultancy Services to design and operationalize the Secondary Teacher Development and Management System (TDMS) for Uganda. The overall goal of TDMS-Secondary is to improve teacher quality anddevelopment for overall improvements in secondary school students' learning and competency levels. TDMS- secondary is intended to enhance the effectiveness of teaching and learning through; increased availability of well trained secondaryschool teachers; institutionalized in-service training of serving teachers, head teachers and education managers; enhanced support to Education Managers, School Managers and Administrators and, enhanced community participation in schools activities. The principal objective of the assignment is to conceptualize and design TDMS-Secondary System that is capable of producing qualified teachers of desired training levels and quality in a cost effective manner on one hand, and a system of teacher development that is holistic, integrated, institutionalized and dynamic on the other. In order to achieve this, a consultancy input will be outsourced to assist the Teacher Education and Instructor department refine the TDMS-Secondary concept and design a relevant system for its operationalisation and delivery. The proposed system is envisaged to cover all Secondary Teacher Training Institutions (i.e. the National Teachers' Colleges and Universities) as well as serving teachers located in network of all Secondary schools (both government aided and private). The Ministry of Education and Sports now invites eligible consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, knowledge and working experience with public procurement and financial systems and procedures in Uganda and those of the World Bank, etc.). Consultants may associate to enhance theirqualifications. The Government of the Republic of Uganda and the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank have embarked on the implementation of a US$211.56 million Local Government Management and ServiceDevelopment (LGMSD) Programme, under which the World Bank will provide a credit amounting to US $ 55 million. The objective of the LGMSD Programme is to enhance Local Governments' ability to plan and manage human and financial resources for effective and sustainable delivery of Local Government services. Through a sub-component of LGMSD Programme, Government will provide specific support to Northern Uganda for purposes of strengthening LocalGovernments (LGs) in the region as sustainable structures for improvement of service delivery and governance. This effort will include preparation of structure and detailed plans for 30 selected and newly formed Town Boards in northern Uganda. Under the sub-component: Support to the Local Governments in NorthernUganda, of the Local Government Management and Service Delivery Programme, the Ministry intends to engage teams of physical planning consultants to prepare the structure and detailed plans for the selected town boards in Northern Uganda. The exercise will also serve as a public sensitization campaign on the value of physical planning in fostering sustainable development. The objective of this consultancy is to prepare, through a consultative and participatory process Structure Plans and Detailed Plans for the selected town boards in northern Uganda, ready for the approval by the Town and Country Planning Board . In carrying out this task, the successful consultant(s) will be expected to carry out extensive consultations with the key stakeholders, conduct socio-economic surveys and analyses, physical and environmental studies, after which they will prepare Structure and Detailed Plans, ready for approval by the Town and Country Planning Board. notice_text: THE UGANDA ROAD FUND BOARD VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT The Uganda Road Fund was set up by Act of Parliament with the mandateto finance the routine and periodic maintenance of public roads in Uganda. The Uganda Road Fund Board has the responsibility to oversee theperformance of the Fund, while the day to day business of the Fund isto be carried out by a Secretariat headed by an Executive Director. The Board now seeks to fill the remaining vacancies in the URF structure and accordingly invites applications from suitably qualified individuals for the following positions: Manager, Monitoring and Evaluation Management Accountant Monitoring and Evaluation officer Systems Administrator Head, Procurement and Disposal Unit (PDU) Procurement and Disposal Assistant The Road Fund is a new entity and the Secretariat will need energeticand dynamic people with the drive necessary to deliver on a demandingbusiness plan. Consequently, only candidates who meet the requirements of the positions will be considered for further evaluation and interview. Brief descriptions of each position are given here; further details may be obtained from the address below: Manager, Monitoring and Evaluation The successful candidate will report to Executive Director and join the Fund Management Team to guide the Secretariat through its development processes, and ensure that it efficiently and effectively carries out its functions. The Fund Management Team drives the strategic direction and output quality of the Secretariat through clear business planning and robust management frameworks. It also takes the lead in development of policies, procedures, strategies and plans for the Fund. The team provides effective leadership to Secretariat staff by guiding staff; promoting the Fund's mission andvalues; providing technical leadership; enhancing strategic capability, and providing service excellence in respective disciplines. The Manager, M&E will be responsible for developing, maintaining and operating an ongoing monitoring and evaluation program for effective monitoring of revenues and performance of activities of designated agencies supported by the Fund; developing a work program for the M&E team and managing workloads and work streams to ensure the program is deliveredaccording to plan with value addition; developing key performance monitoring indicators (KPI) for both the agencies and Secretariat, mapping M&E results unto organizational objectives and goals; ensuring compliance with all internal policies and procedures and relevant legislative provisions; producing M&E reports on specific issues from time to time in the respective projected workplans for each quarter; design and implement studies, surveys, mid-term and annual reviews and propose improvements to the procedures and principles used in the M&E programs; monitor laws and other sector provisions to ensure compliance with all applicable requirements, and develop and implement applicable research and training programs. Applicants must possess: First degree in civil engineering, economics, statistics, or project planning and management from a recognized University /or institution; and Postgraduate qualification in the development of monitoring and evaluation systems, civil engineering, business administration, management or commerce; At least 10 years work experience with excellent knowledge of the road sector in Uganda especially the classification, administration and funding systems; Registration status in Uganda and/or membership of a relevant professional body; Proven strategic thinking capability and management experience at senior level with strategic focus in a large and complex organization with multiple revenue streams; Ability to rise above details, to summarize overall patterns, assess value, and see trends; Experience in leading and motivating staff including developing staffpotential, encouraging ownership and providing for two-way communication; Experience in effective business planning: delegation, managing workloads and work streams, budgeting and monitoring costs, and ensuring compliance ; Experience in building/fostering relationships and change management; Experience in monitoring and evaluating road sector programs, monitoring & evaluation generally, and in the methods used to determine priorities, with an understanding of the principles of road management. Understanding of effective information delivery techniques including education, marketing and communications. Age limit # not more than 45 years. Management Accountant The successful candidate will report to and support the Manager, FundManagement through the provision of efficient and effective financialaccounting services to ensure that the Board and Fund Management Teamhave at their disposal relevant, accurate and timely financial management information. He/she will manage the work of an assistant accountant, ensuring compliance with all Fund policies and procedures as they relate to management accounting and generally contribute to the work of the Fund Management division. Key Responsibilities will include planning and budgeting, monitor performance against budget, working with integrated financial management system, preparing payroll and ensuring correctness, monitoring receivables/payables, liaising with external auditors, reporting. Qualifications and Competencies Applicants must possess a Bachelors degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a similarly relevant discipline obtained from a recognized institution of higher learning. The applicant must have attained full (chartered) membership of a recognized accounting professional institution (e.g. ACCA, CPA, CIMA) and have at least 5 years working experience in accounting and financial management with skills in preparing financial reports. In addition the applicant must have: Membership of ICPAU or equivalent body; Understanding of international Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and familiarity with current best practices in accounting in Uganda; Good practical knowledge of integrated computerised financial management systems; Experience in dealing with external organizations such as URA, commercial banks, government departments, development partners; Good verbal and written communications skills Ability to work as part of a small team, consult and share information, deliver accurately and to delaines; Awareness of organizational goals and ability to propose and initiatechanges in work programmes; Recognition of need for confidentiality with regard to payroll and other financial data. Age limit # not more than 40 years. Monitoring and Evaluation Officer The successful applicant will report to the Manager, M&E and offer professional support in monitoring and evaluating activities undertaken by the Fund. This will involve collection of information required for monitoring of revenue to the Road Fund; monitoring of designated agencies' performance, and analysis of monitoring information to identify variances and trends and reporting findings. Key responsibilities will include contributing to the work programme for the monitoring and evaluation team; supporting implementation of ongoing monitoring and evaluation programmes; monitoring income and expenditure of the Fund; evaluating the performance of designated agencies against key performance indicators (KPIs), monitoring network metrics and trends, and assessing value for money invested and reporting. Qualifications and Competencies Applicants will possess a Bachelor's degree in civil engineering, economics, statistics, or development studies from a recognized university. A Masters degree in highway or pavement engineering, transport planning or transport economics will be an added advantage. Applicants should at least be Associate Members of a recognized professional institution and should have gained a minimum of five (5) years work experience, which should have embraced strategic planning and M&E experiencewithin the transport or road sectors in Uganda or in a similar environment. In addition the position holder shall be able to demonstrate: A thorough understanding of the principles of road maintenance planning, asset management and investment appraisal preferably with work experience within the transport or road sectors in Uganda; Experience in the application of these principles, including application of industry standard computerized highway management and decision support systems; Conversant with workflow management systems to guide decision making; Fully computer literate, with detailed knowledge of industry standardbusiness applications. Age limit # not more than 40 years. Systems Administrator The succes s ful candidate will report to Manager, Corporate Services and be expected to take charge of the Fund's information processing system including designing, operating and maintaining all the necessary hard and software, as well as networks; ensuring the integrity and security of the Fund's database infrastructure taking all the necessary steps to mitigate potential risks and threats; Manage all Fund records including storageand file classification, archiving and retrieval procedures in such away that brings efficiency to the internal operations processes of the Fund, and timeliness of interface with external stakeholders. Key Responsibilities shall include: Designing, introducing and operating an integrated information processing system linking a number of databases; Creating, installing and maintaining a LAN; Developing, and operating the Fund's website; Undertaking routine tasks associated with operating and controlling the installed computer systems and networking printers; Overseeing and undertaking operations that control data processing, peripheral equipment and communications network; Monitoring and maintaining computer hardware, software, communicationsystem and ancillary equipment; Ensuring security and backup of organisation files Performing record management activities and ensure uniformity and standardization of practices; Performing overall records appraisal, file classification and archiving of files in keeping with approved professional standards and methods; Assessing and costing training needs and identifying suitable training opportunities; Qualifications and competencies An Honours first degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or equivalent. A Master's degree in computer science, information technology, business administration or a related discipline will be an added advantage. Must be a Certified CISCO Network Associate (CCNA), at a minimum. Microsoft certification will be an added advantage. Maintains a good understanding of the work environment and trends, organizational performance, and the political and regulatory climate andidentifies potential opportunities, risk and issues before they arise. Actively looks for opportunities to improve services and support organizational change. Maintains awareness of overall organizational goals, and looks for opportunities to contribute organization-wide. Gathers all relevant information, utilizes an analytical and logical approach to problem solving, and accurately assesses impact of decisions in particular areas of the business and overall. Age limit # not more than 40 years. notice_text: Road Development Program Phase 3 (RDPP3) Project Project ID No. P074079 RECRUITMENT OF AN AXLE LOAD ADVISOR UNDER A SHORT TERM TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE (TA) TO UGANDA NATIONAL ROADS AUTHORITY (UNRA) The Government of Uganda has received a credit from the InternationalDevelopment Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Road DevelopmentProgram Phase 3 (RDPP3) Project and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this credit to payments under the contract for consultant'sservices for an Axle Load Advisor. The primary aim of these services is to design a robust and effectiveshort, medium and long term axle load control strategy for UNRA aimedat curbing prevalent overloading on the Ugandan roads. The consultantshall: Carry out a situational and SWOT analysis of the current axle load management arrangements and practices under UNRA. Based on best practicein the East African and COMESA, advise how UNRA operations can be aligned in consonant with weigh bridge and axle load control practices inthese regions; Develop a strategy for raising public awareness on axle load control,current legislation and enforcement. Advise on and update standards and specifications required for the development of new fixed weigh in motion weighbridges and portable weighbridges; Develop ways of ensuring that weigh bridge operations are efficientlyand transparently carried out; Assess viability of commercialization of either part of or the entireaxle load operations and viability of implementing a weight-distance charging system on the national road network; Prepare terms of reference for consulting services to develop an axleload management strategy and preparation of required infrastructure investment plan Experience and Qualifications Civil Engineer with a university degree in a Transport/ Highways Engineering and at least 15 years relevant experience covering road pavement design, road research, axle load control and axle load assessments. Should be experienced and familiar with the institutional environmentin Uganda Able to keep to tight schedules and manage a team to do the same; Must be a team player, comfortable working with all levels of senior management and junior staff, with ability to mentor, coach and train staff. Must have a high level of computer literacy, especially in MS Word, Excel; understanding of the functioning of databases is strongly desired; Must be fluent in English so as to be able to communicate (speaking, reading, writing) Durations, Terms and Conditions of Appointment The duration of this contract shall be for an initial period of 6 months, renewable. Reference No: RW-RAB-527660-CS-QCBS The Government of Rwanda has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Commercialization and De-risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for hiring a consultancy firm for design Review of Warufu 20 m high earth fill dam and 3,000ha irrigation system. The Terms of Reference (TOR) related to this assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest. The Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB) / Commercialization and De-risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above Services. The shortlist will contain five (5) to eight (8) firms . The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fourth Edition September, 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. TERMS OF REFERENCES FOR DESIGN REVALIDATION AND UPDATE OF WARUFU DAM AND IRRIGATION NETWORK (3,000 HA COMMAND AREA) LOCATED IN GATSIBO AND NYAGATARE DISTRICTS Project Background The World Bank approved $300 million in financing under the International Development Association’s (IDA’s) grant, credit, and scale up window to help the Government of Rwanda increase irrigation, commercialization, and access to finance and insurance for farmers and other value chain actors in Rwanda’s agricultural sector. The Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project (CDAT) will support the Government to provide services and create an enabling environment for the private actor throughout the agricultural value chain. It will finance public investments in the seeds sector, develop and rehabilitate irrigation systems on over 17,600 ha, provide accompanying land husbandry development on about 11,000 ha in surrounding water catchment areas to increase productivity and promote climate smart agriculture. The project will also support commercialization by helping farmers access to markets and availing matching grants for investments in mechanization, post-harvest infrastructure and processing equipment. An innovation challenge fund will invest in particularly innovative solutions for the sector that can be brought to scale. The project is nationwide and is foreseen to directly benefit at least 235,000 households, including women and youth. In partnership with financial institutions, the Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project will seek to enhance access to affordable financial services and products in the agricultural sector. This can be achieved by providing long-term financing, reducing risks and challenges faced by agricultural value chains through strengthening market linkages and scaling up agriculture insurance. In this regard, part of the project’s funds will finance the consultancy services to revalidate and update the design of Warufu dam and irrigation network (3,000 ha gross command area) located in Nyagihanga, Gatsibo, and Ngarama Sectors of Gatsibo District, and Mimuli Sector of Nyagatare District. Site Description Warufu site is located on the border of Gatsibo and Nyagatare Districts which is a semi-arid zone with average annual rainfall of 900mm, and temperatures ranging from 210C to 280C. The Warufu site is a multi-purpose project aiming at developing 3,000 ha irrigation system, providing drinking water supply of 5,000m3/day to 240,000 people and generating 1,260 MWh/yr electricity sufficient to light about 4,000 houses in the project area. It involves a 20 m high dam (above river bed level) to store 25 Million m3, 3,000 ha irrigation system, and land-husbandry technologies in the irrigation area and catchments. Water supply outlets for hydropower and domestic water supply will also be provided. The detailed study was developed and approved by the former LWH, World Bank funded Project under MINAGRI in 2017. Figure 1- : Warufu Large Dam and Hillside Irrigation command area (3,000ha) This consultancy service is related to the design revalidation and updating of Warufu Dam on the Warufu River, and the command area. The proposed dam site is located 0.7 km upstream of the road bridge next to Nyagahanga town. The dam is reached from either the Kayonza – Kagitumba asphalt road and then the earthen road near Kabarore Gatsibo, or the Kigali – Byumba asphalt road and then the Byumba – Nyagatare asphalt road to Nyagahanga town where the dam site is located. The coordinates of the dam axis are E 524,795/ N 4,821,009. Brief Description of the Dam components Warufu Dam has the following components: Warufu dam is a homogenous embankment dam incorporating a cofferdam, with a concrete frontal spillway, chute and stilling basin and a diversion/intake/outlet works system designed to release water for irrigation, hydropower, environmental compensation flow and domestic water supply, as well as to ensure bottom outlet operations. Associated rehabilitation of existing roads affected by the new reservoir and ancillary works. The dam crest is at +1,546.60 m elevation, with the full supply level (FSL) of the reservoir at +1,543.50 m. The minimum supply level (MSL) that has been determined for irrigation is +1,533.40 m, ensuring a live storage volume of 22.6 MCM. The intake structure provides the possibility of abstraction to a lower level at +1,533.00 m to allow for additional abstraction as sediment accumulates in the reservoir. The maximum flood level (MFL) for the routed flood of 10,000 years return period (81m3/sec) is 1,545.93 m. The dam crest width is 7.0m and the dam embankment slopes are 3:1 (H:V) at both the upstream and downstream faces, and the same is valid for the cofferdam. The dam height is 26.1 m from the lower elevation of the cutoff, whereas 20m from the river bed level. The entire cofferdam will be incorporated in the upstream section of the embankment during the construction of the dam. The diversion works consist of a cofferdam and a steel diversion pipe. The total length of the diversion works is 146 m, with inlet invert elevation at +1,525.60 m and outlet invert elevation at +1,525.15 m, corresponding to a longitudinal slope of S=0.003. The proposed diameter of the diversion pipe is selected based on the routed design flow of 11.8 m3/sec, for T=5 years return period, and the elevation of the cofferdam crest is set at +1,533.50 m. The nominal diameter of the pipe is D=1.6 m and steel lining thickness of 8.2 mm. Warufu dam has a frontal concrete spillway on the left abutment. The spillway design flow is 81m3/sec, corresponding to 10,000 years return period, with the exception of the stilling basin, the design flow of other spillway components is only 35m3/sec, corresponding to 100 years return period which shall validated. Designing all spillway components with 10,000 year flood shall be considered during the design review. The spillway works consist of three components, namely: The spillway control section, the chute and the stilling basin. The outlet pipe will serve for diversion during construction but later it will be used for both water supply and bottom outlet after the completion of the works. A vertical concrete intake shaft square in plan with openings equipped with trashracks on all four sides and a short steel pipe section of 1.6m nominal diameter will be constructed to convey water to the diversion pipe. Grooves have been provided at the openings, where stop logs can be placed in the future in order to isolate the reservoir from the outlet system. At the downstream end of the outlet pipe a concrete structure (valve chamber) will be constructed to house the equipment required for the flow control accompanied by an impact type stilling basin for energy dissipation of the released flows. The works in the valve chamber include: The short extension of the outlet pipe and the installation of a taper section for the gradual transition from 1.6 m to 1.1 m diameter and a short pipe section of 1.1 m diameter, where two butterfly valves of 1,100mm diameter will be placed to regulate the bottom outlet operations, whenever required. An access manhole is provided on the 1.6 m diameter section which will be used whenever internal inspection of the outlet works is necessary. The construction of 800mm diameter branch of the main pipe for irrigation, hydropower and compensation flow releases. This will be equipped with a butterfly valve and a flow regulation needle valve, both 800mm diameter. The branch is then separated into two pipes of equal diameter, one leading to the nearby future power station and the other directly to the downstream riverbed. A 250mm branch of the main pipe will also be provided for the domestic water supply connection and will be equipped with valves. Brief Description of the Irrigation component The Warufu project command area is located mostly in Gatsibo District with a downstream section extending into Nyagatare Districts. The irrigation scheme is divided into upper and lower pressure zones with a total of 3,000ha gross (2,545ha net) and the Conveyance System that conveys the water to the head of the irrigation network. Water released from the dam flows down the stream to a stream diversion structure which diverts water into a 7km long concrete lined canal leading to the command area., A smaller upper regulating reservoir will support irrigation of the upper irrigation zone, and a larger lower night storage reservoir will support irrigation of the lower irrigation zone., During the day water from the canal water will be used to irrigate the upper zone, and fill the lower reservoir whereas during the night generating hydropower. Gravity irrigation will be employed by pipe networks for each zone from their respective reservoirs. Salient features of the Irrigation component: Conveyance System Stream Diversion

title: Recruitment of 2nd Senior AI/ML Engineer
buyer: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning
notice_text: Republic of Rwanda Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning P.O Box 158 Kigali, Rwanda ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST Recruitment for Individual Consultant Services (2nd Senior AI/ML Engineer) for the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) Background The Government of Rwanda (GoR) is implementing the Revenue Improvement and Spending Efficiency (RISE) Program-for-Results (PforR) Operation with support from the World Bank. The Program aims to strengthen domestic revenue mobilization, improve efficiency in public spending, and enhance transparency and accountability in public financial management systems. The Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) supports end-to-end public financial management processes, to improve operational efficiency, data quality, risk management, and decision support, IFMIS intends to implement AI and Machine Learning (ML) solutions that enhance forecasting, anomaly detection, process optimization, and user support, while maintaining strict requirements for security, auditability, compliance, and system performance. Objective The Government of Rwanda seeks to engage two (2) Senior AI/ML Engineer Individual Consultants through a single competitive selection process, from which two separate contracts will be awarded to the first and second ranked candidates. Each consultant will be engaged under an independent contract and will be individually accountable for the full scope of duties described in this Terms of Reference. The consultants will design, develop, deploy, and maintain AI/ML solutions that enhance IFMIS business processes and analytics. Their work will focus on building production-ready, explainable, secure, and maintainable AI capabilities that seamlessly integrate with the IFMIS architecture and data environment. Although each consultant will operate under a separate contract, they are expected to collaborate within the same technical ecosystem to ensure timely delivery, coherence, and continuity of AI/ML operations across the IFMIS platform. Scope of the Services Under the supervision of the Financial Systems Development Programme Manager the two senior AI/ML Engineer Individual Consultants will work closely with IFMIS business teams, data engineers, software engineers, security teams, and stakeholders in the delivery of the assignment. The two consultants will operate within the same technical environment and are expected to coordinate their efforts to maximize efficiency, ensure continuity of AI/ML operations, and meet agreed delivery timelines. The Individual Consultants will: Implement the already identified and approved AI/ML use cases for IFMIS by working with IFMIS business team and technical stakeholders to confirm objectives, clarify business rules, validate data readiness, define measurable success criteria, and translate each use case into a practical delivery plan. This includes confirming expected outputs, usage in IFMIS workflows, integration touchpoints, and operational constraints such as auditability, performance, security, and compliance. Assess and prepare the required IFMIS datasets needed to deliver the approved AI/ML use cases, including profiling data quality, defining cleaning and validation rules, and implementing feature engineering logic that is traceable and reproducible. Work closely with data engineering and database teams to ensure data pipelines support reliable training and inference, with proper documentation of data lineage, feature definitions, and consistent alignment to IFMIS master data structures. Design, develop, train, and evaluate machine learning and/or NLP models aligned to the approved IFMIS use cases, selecting appropriate approaches and baselines and improving them iteratively based on agreed metrics. Define evaluation methodologies, performance thresholds, and validation processes that fit the operational and governance needs of IFMIS, including explainability requirements where decisions must be justified to auditors and business owners, and ensuring that model outputs are stable and reliable under real-world transactional behaviors. Package and deploy models into production-ready services for integration with IFMIS modules through agreed integration patterns, such as REST APIs, scheduled batch inference, or event-driven processing where applicable. Implement MLOps practices to ensure repeatable training, version control for models and features, automated deployment pipelines, and operational monitoring for reliability, latency, errors, and performance trends, including clear rollback mechanisms and controlled release approaches to reduce risk in production environments. Ensure that all AI/ML implementations comply with IFMIS security and governance requirements by applying secure-by-design practices, enforcing appropriate access controls, protecting sensitive data, and ensuring encryption and secure logging practices are applied as required. Produce governance documentation that supports traceability and audit readiness, including model documentation, training data provenance, feature references, assumptions, limitations, and risk considerations, ensuring that AI/ML outputs remain defensible and aligned with institutional compliance expectations. Produce comprehensive technical documentation supporting the full lifecycle of the delivered AI/ML solutions, including architecture descriptions, data flows, API specifications, deployment guides, and operational run-books. The Engineer will also conduct structured knowledge transfer to IFMIS technical teams through walk-throughs, training sessions, and handover support to ensure internal capacity to operate, monitor, maintain, and enhance the AI/ML solutions beyond the assignment period. Provide in-depth technical support to the IFMIS Administration team to investigate, troubleshoot, resolve, and escalate complex user-reported and system-generated incidents, collaborating with relevant technical teams to ensure timely resolution. Requirements for the Consultant The individual consultant should have the following demonstrable profile: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field; a Master’s degree is an added advantage. Minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience in AI/ML engineering, including delivery of production-grade ML solutions beyond experimentation, with demonstrated ownership from model development through deployment and operational support. Strong proficiency in Python for ML development and data analysis, including core libraries such as NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn; experience with at least one deep learning framework (e.g., TensorFlow or PyTorch); knowledge of Java/Spring) is an added advantage. Familiarity with Large Language Models (LLMs) and applied NLP, including prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, and evaluation of LLM outputs; ability to integrate LLM-based capabilities into enterprise applications with appropriate safeguards (privacy, access control, auditability, and hallucination mitigation) Proven ability to design, train, evaluate, and optimize ML models (e.g., classification, regression/forecasting, anomaly detection, clustering and/or NLP), including clear definition of metrics, validation strategy, and model selection aligned to business requirements. Experience applying responsible and explainable AI practices suitable for audit and governance needs, including model interpretability approaches (e.g., SHAP/LIME or interpretable baselines), documentation of assumptions/limitations, and reproducibility of experiments. Demonstrated capability to integrate and deploy ML models within enterprise systems using modern deployment practices, including API-based inference (e.g., FastAPI/Flask) and/or batch scoring pipelines, containerization (Docker), and CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitLab CI). Working knowledge of data pipelines required for ML solutions, including data preparation, feature engineering, validation, and orchestration using tools such as Airflow (or equivalent), as well as an understanding of streaming/event-driven patterns where applicable. Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational databases (PostgreSQL and/or Oracle), including ability to analyze high-volume transactional data and apply performance-aware querying and data extraction approaches. Familiarity with MLOps practices and tools for experiment tracking, model versioning, and lifecycle management (e.g., MLflow or equivalent), including basic monitoring concepts such as data drift, model performance tracking, and operational alerting. Strong understanding of SDLC and proven involvement in key phases including requirements analysis, solution design, development, testing, deployment, and production support, with practical experience working in Agile environments (Scrum/Kanban). Strong analytical, interpersonal, and communication skills, with ability to collaborate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and to translate business needs into implementable technical solutions. Ability to work independently and as part of a wider team, conduct code reviews, ensure quality standards, and maintain well-documented, secure, and maintainable deliverables. Excellent fluency in English or French; working knowledge of the other language is an added advantage. The Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning now invites eligible consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services through E-Procurement (www.umucyo.gov.rw )

Background The Government of Rwanda has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Revenue Improvement and Spending Efficiency (RISE) Programme-for-Results (PforR), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Consultancy Services to Provide Certified Financial Analyst (CFA) Training to Government of Rwanda Staff and High Performing Students. The assignment aims to strengthen professional financial management capacity and contribute to Rwanda’s ambition of becoming a competitive international financial centre through the development of internationally certified finance professionals. In this context, the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. 2. Objectives of the Assignment The main objective of the assignment is to provide professional CFA training and examination preparation support to Government of Rwanda Public Financial Management (PFM) staff and high performing students in order to: Strengthen sustainable professional capacity in Public Financial Management occupations across Government institutions and Government-funded projects; Support Rwanda’s ambition to establish a competitive international financial centre through the development of internationally certified finance professionals; Enhance Rwanda’s financial sector skills base in asset management, climate finance, wealth management, philanthropy, and FinTech; and Improve examination pass rates and progression of candidates across CFA Levels I, II, and III. 3. Scope of Services The scope of services includes, among others: Delivery of CFA tuition for Levels I, II, and III; Revision sessions, mock examinations, and remedial classes; Provision of study materials and online learning support; Monitoring and reporting on attendance and academic performance; Provision of qualified CFA charterholder trainers; and Support for examination preparation and candidate progression. 4.
