title: Recruitment of Individual Consultant to Provide Technical Assistance for Monitoring and Evaluation of Road Projects for RTDA.
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT (IC)) SELECTION) Country: RWANDA Project: LAKE VICTORIA TRANSPORT PROGRAM-SOP1, RWANDA (P160488) Reference No.: RW-RTDA-431878-CS-INDV Assignment Title: I ndividual Consultant to Provide Technical Assistance for Monitoring and Evaluation Road projects to RTDA. Dear Sir/Madam; Background information In the framework of the implementation of its strategy to strengthen the national road network and opening rural areas, the Republic of Rwanda is realizing several road construction and rehabilitation projects. The LVTP SOP1 Rwanda (Ngoma-Nyanza Road), KLP Connect (Kigali Logistic Platform), FRDP (Feeder Roads Development project) and Rwanda Emergency Connectivity restoration (RECOR) are the main transport infrastructure projects under implementation by RTDA with the Fund of World Bank (IDA). Those projects will play a pivotal role in enhancing the regional EAC network by reducing travel distances for transit traffic originating from Tanzania, traversing the Rusumo border through Burundi and the Eastern DRC in the South. Furthermore, they will enhance connectivity between Southern Rwanda and stimulate a significant potential market in the hinterland of Lake Victoria. These initiatives will expand the existing logistics infrastructure by integrating the Ngoma-Nyanza Road corridor, which is part of the East Africa Central Corridor, with the KLP situated in Masaka/Kigali. Additionally, the FRDP will bolster all-season road connectivity to agricultural market centers in ten (10) selected Districts. It is envisaged that the proposed upgrading scheme will promote regional and international trade, as well as stimulate growth of the local economy. Ensuring sustainable roads connectivity, which is paramount in transport sector, The Rwanda Emergency Connectivity restoration (RECOR) project is established to restore the connectivity across the country, mainly for roads hit by the floods and landslides to ensure harmonized economic development of the country and the region. To realise the project development objectives, the Rwanda Transport Development Agency (RTDA) through Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) as the lead dealing with coordination for restoring the physical infrastructure and strengthening the institutional framework for transport, one of the main assigned roles is monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of development projects namely the abovementioned priorities. Therefore, as part of the LVTP components, the WB/IDA has allocated funds to seek technical assistance aimed at facilitating and strengthening its Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) systems and practices. This support is intended to enhance the capacity of the SPIU to effectively manage development projects. It will also enable the SPIU to expand its options and provisions for capturing new indicators, establishing baseline datasets, and setting target values for World Bank projects in the pipeline. Furthermore, this assistance will facilitate the assessment of the economic benefits associated with these projects. Duties and responsibilities Objective of the assignment: The Main objective of this position is to strengthen the monitoring and evaluation systems and practices of RTDA, with a focus on monitoring and evaluation of transport development activities aligned with the second generation of National strategy for Transformation aspirations. The M&E expert will play a pivotal role in developing and implementing an integrated M&E system tailored to RTDA’s needs, fostering data-driven decision-making. The expert will also assist RTDA in the collect, treatment and reporting of the indicators to test and adjust the systems designed. Scope of Work Under the immediate supervision of the SPIU coordinator, the M&E expert will perform the following tasks: Lead the preparation and development of the Second generation of National strategy for Transformation for the Transport Sector. Conduct a comprehensive situational review and assessment of NST1 implementation and identify the needs for the second generation of National strategy for Transformation. Provide recommendations aligned with the RTDA mission and vision, the Transport Policy, and Vision 2050 to inform the development of the second generation of National strategy for Transformation. Take charge of spearheading the formulation of the second generation of National strategy for Transformation strategic plan for the Road Transport Sector within the Rwanda Transport Development Agency (RTDA). Provide strategic guidance to RTDA in aligning with the expectations of the Government of Rwanda and other development partners, ensuring coherence and effectiveness in meeting their objectives. Assist in the development of the RTDA IMIHIGO (performance contracts) and contribute to the entirety of RTDA's planning and budgeting cycle. Review and update RTDA Monitoring and Evaluation Framework and Plan Review and update the existing M&E Framework and plan aligned to Government of Rwanda and development partners’ Reporting requirements; Based on the framework, develop simple and user-friendly monitoring format and guidelines for efficient data collection and reporting. Participate in the preparation of the LVTP, KLP Connect, FRDP and RECOR Annual work plans and monitor its implementation. Contribute to the implementation of result framework by: Tracking the progress of LVTP, KLP Connect, FRDP and RECOR projects set annual targets and set indicators, in line with the theory of change. Prepare M&E presentation for the World Bank follow up missions and development partners regularly. Track the implementation progress of Agreed actions from the Missions Aide Memoire. Serve as a focal person in charge of Monitoring and Impact Evaluation for the LVTP, KLP Connect, FRDP, and RECOR projects. Collect necessary primary and secondary data for monitoring and evaluating RTDA projects. Working in necessary coordination with the other relevant implementing agencies with the assistance of M&E officers to review, update and strengthen RTDA specific M&E frameworks and/or systems, collect necessary data and undertaking necessary analysis of the data collected, evaluate the project implementation in term of achievement of project development objectives and compliance with the project development objectives. Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to collect, analyse, and report data on transport development activities, focusing on key performance indicators (KPIs) and project outcomes. Utilize advanced analytical tools and techniques to derive actionable insights from the collected data, facilitating evidence-based decision-making. Review LVTP, FRDP, KLP connect and RECOR project documents including but not limited to: Strategic plan, Mid Term Review, monthly and quarterly reports, Impact Evaluations reports among others). Assist in the review of different ToRs developed under the LVTP, FRDP, KLP connect and RECOR projects. Assist RTDA to prepare annual monitoring and evaluation plan in consistent with M&E Framework. Facilitate the development of the MTR, ICR, Impact Evaluation and other surveys conducted within LVTP, FRDP, KLP connect and RECOR projects. Review/update Recording and Reporting Forms and Formats for RTDA Review and update recording and reporting templates and formats for RTDA projects that meet reporting requirement of the World Bank. Support RTDA in testing, modifying, and finalizing the recording and reporting forms and formats. Capacity Building of RTDA Staff on Monitoring and Evaluation Conduct M&E Capacity needs assessment within RTDA Staff. Deliver training sessions to RTDA staff, including field personnel, to enhance their M&E skills and promote a culture of data utilization, Knowledge sharing and learning. Prepare Monthly, Trimester and Annual Reports of RTDA Assist the SPIU to compile periodic progress data for monitoring and evaluating RTDA projects. Actively Participate in the compilation of the SPIU monthly, quarterly, and annual progress reports as required by development partners, with special focus on LVTP and other World Bank funded projects. Utilize impactful storytelling methods tailored to the Rwanda Transport Development Agency's (RTDA) specific projects, sectors, and programs to efficiently and effectively collect impactful data. Enhance development impact storytelling through compelling data visualization techniques and regular reporting to key stakeholders, ensuring effective communication of RTDA's achievements and contributions in the transport sector. Support documentation and dissemination of results and lessons learned from LVTP, FRDP, KLP Connect and RECOR Projects. Field Monitoring and Monitoring Report Writing Organize on the job monitoring field visit on the construction sites with RTDA M&E staff and support them on the use of monitoring techniques and data collection methods. Guide RTDA M&E staff to prepare field monitoring report and facilitate feedback mechanisms for continuous improvement. Provide inputs to the weekly report before submission to MININFRA by RTDA. Perform other Works Assigned by the SPIU coordinator. Facilities to be provided by the client. RTDA will provide a conducive office space with furniture, internet, and security to ensure confidentiality of documents. RTDA will provide the consultant with access to projects’ documents relevant to the assignment, including previous studies, legal texts and regulations, specifications, results frameworks for the projects. Qualifications and Experience Qualification and background requirements for this position: A master’s degree in one of the following: Monitoring and Evaluation, Project Management, Business Management, Economics, Information Technology, Transportation engineering/planning, transport economics, or any field relevant to these domains cited. Additional academic degree in any of the civil Engineering domain would be an added advantage. At least 7 years of relevant experience working as a monitoring and evaluation expert/specialist, preferably in the industry of transportation infrastructure. Working experience with national agencies implementing World Bank funded development programs/project (At least 2 projects/programs). In addition, having worked with other international funded programs/projects is an advantage. Skills and experience in data collection and validation, data assessment evaluation, and development of Monitoring and Evaluation systems Skills and experience in data collection, data assessment evaluation, and building Monitoring and Evaluation systems. Strong analytical skills with proficiency in data collection, analysis, and reporting. Skills and experience in developing; M&E frameworks, M&E plans, and projects M&E reports formats. Experience in training, capacity building and setting up Web-based/automated Monitoring and Evaluation systems will be a distinct advantage. Experience in designing electronic data collection systems, preferably in the use of Survey CTO application or any other ODK (Open Data Kit) based application. Excellent skills in data management and statistical analysis, including use of software such as Stata, R, SAS or python and Excellent MS Office skills, including advanced Excel skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including demonstrated capacity to synthesize evidence into effective presentations and actionable recommendations for broad range of audience. Fluency in written and spoken English. Knowledge of French will be an added advantage. notice_text: Tender Nº: 08/07/2024/BRD/HC&CS/CS Assignment Title : Request for Expression of Interest (EOI) to hire Individual consultant for REF Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Procurement Approach : Individual consultant Background: The Government of Rwanda, represented by the Ministry of Infrastructure (MININFRA), in collaboration with the Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD) and Energy Development Corporation Limited (EDCL), is implementing the Renewable Energy Fund (REF) project financed by Strategic Climate Fund-Scaling-up Renewable Energy Program (SCF-SREP) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase electricity access in Rwanda through off-grid technologies and facilitate private sector participation in renewable off-grid electrification. Objective of the assignment: The main objective of the consultant is to prepare the borrowers’ ICR for REF. They will draw upon inputs and analysis under the supervision of the BRD team and participate in consultation meetings with the World Bank team on the draft findings. Scope of Work Under the direct supervision of BRD, the consultant will undertake the following tasks: Prepare a workplan for the ICR setting out the methodology for its preparation and timeline. Assess the context, rationale, and relevance of the objectives, design, and implementation arrangements of REF during preparation and at completion. Assess REF’s outcome against the agreed objectives. Assess key factors and events pertaining to the World Bank and BRD and the external environment during preparation and implementation, that affected performance and outcomes. Evaluate BRD’s own performance during the preparation and implementation of REF with special emphasis on lessons learned that may be helpful in the future. Evaluate the performance of the World Bank during the preparation and implementation of the project, with special emphasis on lessons learned. Describe any proposed arrangements for future operation. Reference N o RW-RAB-326333-CS-QCBS The Government of Rwanda has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Commercialization and De-risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services of hiring a Consultancy firm to carry out an Environmental Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) & Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) for Kageyo site. The Terms of Reference (TOR) related to this assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest. The Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB) / Commercialization and De-risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expression of Interest (EOI) will include: core business and years in business, relevant experience, technical and managerial capability of the firm. The shortlisting criteria are: The firm should have a vast experience in consultancy services with specific references and contracts in Environmental Impact Assessment studies related to irrigation infrastructure or water management infrastructure; The firm should be a registered member of Rwanda Association of Professional Environmental Practitioners (RAPEP) and figure on the 2023-2024 RAPEP list of authorized firms to conduct environmental assessment studies. The shortlist will contain five (5) to eight (8) firms . The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fourth Edition November, 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the criteria set out in the Request for Proposals. Expressions of interest must be delivered through e-procurement system on www.umucyo.gov.rw by the time indicated in the system. TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT/ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR IRRIGATION DEVELOPMENT AND LAND HUSBANDRY FOR KAGEYO CDAT SITE BACKGROUND Introduction Rwanda is committed to become an upper-middle income country by 2035 and a high-income country by 2050. A modern and high performing agriculture sector, well integrated into regional and global supply chains, is one of the country’s key drivers of growth. The required transformation in agriculture needs to be built on competition and innovation and achieve higher productivity rates through private sector-led investment and development. Rwandan agriculture is mostly rain-fed, and therefore more exposed to weather-related risks, especially to severe, frequent, and prolonged dry spells occurring during the cropping seasons. Rwandan agriculture is mostly rain-fed, and therefore more exposed to weather-related risks, especially to severe, frequent, and prolonged dry spells occurring during the cropping seasons. Irrigation investments have significant potential to address these challenges and to improve the productivity of farmers who depend on rain-fed agriculture, through improving yields and increasing cultivation in the dry season. Irrigation scheme requires infrastructure investment, operation and maintenance costs and Farmers in drought-prone areas requires adequate infrastructure to cope with such conditions. The expansion of the irrigation network is the only way to expand the effective land area and reduce climate-related production risks through improved technologies and practices. It is in this regard that the “Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project’’hereafter “CDAT project” will invest in expanding and upgrading the irrigation area infrastructure through development of irrigation facilities including dam construction, diversion weirs at Kageyo site and the land husbandry development. The Kageyo CDAT Project site is situated in Kayonza District, Eastern Province of Rwanda. Therefore, these Terms of Reference (ToRs) are for consultancy services to provide Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board with the full study for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment of Hydro-Agricultural development works for Kageyo site (2000ha of command area and 100ha of land husbandry). In addition to these ToRs, the study will be conducted in accordance with World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), the provisions of the laws and regulations that govern EIA in Rwanda, and will require application for EIA Clearance to Rwanda Development Board (RDB). CDAT project The Government of Rwanda (GoR) is pursuing its efforts to accelerate private sector-led growth and further reduce poverty. This is performed through the implementation of various sustainable development programs and projects. The “Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project’’ hereafter “CDAT project” is among the development projects designed under the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), funded by the World Bank (WB) for a period of 5 years. The objectives of the project are to increase the use of irrigation and commercialization among producers and agribusiness firms in supported value chains and to increase access to agriculture finance. The project beneficiaries are farmers’ cooperatives, commercial farmers and small and medium-sized agri-enterprises. The project has four components. Component 1: Value Chain and Infrastructure Development , it aims to increase marketable volumes in supported value chains and provide targeted climate sensitive infrastructure support. The component will finance public goods such as irrigation infrastructure, land husbandry, extension provision, and research and development of improved seeds. Under this component, they are 3 subcomponents : (i) Irrigation rehabilitation and development focuses to expand the irrigated area and increase marketable output from irrigated agriculture, (ii), Land husbandry with objective to protect the watershed areas that drain to the irrigation sites under Subcomponent 1.1, increase the productivity of these areas, and prevent soil erosion , Innovation and services for agri-business value chain development aims to increase value addition and marketability by addressing critical constraints that directly affect the commercialization of the targeted value chains. Component 2 : Agricultural Finance and Insurance, the objective of this component is to increase access to financial products and services to farmers and cooperatives for the commercialization of the sector. Under this component, 2 subcomponents have developed: (i) Scaling up agricultural finance to set the foundation for expanding the supply of affordable financial services and products, (ii) Strengthening agricultural insurance by strengthening the quality and effectiveness of agriculture insurance offered through the NAIS, which seeks to de-risk the agricultural sector using market-based insurance mechanisms and fitness solutions. Component 3 : Covers project management to ensure the smooth implementation of the project and will support all aspects of project management such as: (i) project staffing and their training; (ii) procurement and financial management; (iii) environmental and social risk management and compliance; (iv) monitoring and evaluation; (v) equipment and operating costs; (vi) communication and knowledge management. Component 4: Contingency Emergency Response Component will allow for rapid reallocation of the project’s uncommitted funds in the event of an eligible emergency. Therefore, various activities were developed under these components and subcomponent and their implementation requires carrying out civil works related to the rehabilitation of existing or development of irrigation infrastructure. Under subcomponent 1.1, works related to pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, preparation of detailed designs, construction supervision and quality assurances, construction of irrigation water abstraction, delivery, distribution, and drainage structures will be implemented in 31 irrigation schemes identified in different districts countrywide. Rehabilitation of irrigation and drainage network canals and construction of hydraulic structures (diversion weir, water intake, drops, small bridges, culverts, etc.) may present some environmental and social risks, particularly relating to potential economic displacement, community health and safety, and protection of biodiversity. It will finance public investments in the seeds sector, develop and rehabilitate irrigation systems on over 17,600 ha, provide accompanying land husbandry development on about 11,000 ha in surrounding water catchment areas to increase productivity and promote climate smart agriculture. title: Consultancy to hire an implementing partner to conduct English Proficiency training and certification of teachers.
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST Country: RWANDA Reference No: RW-REB-417096-CS-QCBS Assignment Title: Consultancy to hire an implementing partner to conduct English Proficiency training and certification of teachers. Background Rwanda has made significant strides in improving its education system over the past few decades. However, challenges remain, particularly in ensuring that teachers are adequately equipped with the necessary skills and knowledge to deliver quality education to students. Recognizing the critical role of education in human capital development, the Government of Rwanda, with support from the World Bank, has initiated the Rwanda Quality Basic Education for Human Capital Development (QBE) project. The project is part of the Government of Rwanda's broader efforts to improve education quality and outcomes, in line with its Vision 2050 and the Education Sector Strategic Plan. The Government of Rwanda has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Rwanda Quality Basic Education for Human Capital Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. Rwanda Basic Education Board (REB) is looking for a recognized and highly experienced firm to train, assess and certify Rwandan teachers in English Language Proficiency. The service provider must be specialized in delivering large-scale training, assessment, and globally recognized certification of the English language (specifically in the skills of reading, writing, listening, and speaking) to teachers using immersive digital tools to address challenges of scale, urgency, and cost-effectiveness. Additionally, the contracted firm should leverage REB’s harmonized manuals as a complementary tool to its training program to further contextualize content for the classroom realities of Rwandan teachers. The firm will adhere to internationally recognized standards and best practices when training and assessing teachers, including monitoring the increasing teacher use of English as a medium of instruction in the classroom, and work closely with REB on the certification of teachers. Objectives and purpose of the assignment The overall purpose of the assignment is to train, assess, and certify teachers in Rwanda on English Language Proficiency. The mode of instruction must be effective and may include in-person, hybrid, and online components. Assessment must lead to an internationally recognized certification according to teachers’ level of proficiency. The assessment of teachers' language proficiency should cover all four language skills (i.e. listening, speaking, writing, and reading) and categorize their levels according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages [CEFR] with the ability to benchmark test results with international standardized English tests such as International English Language Testing System (IELTS) and Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL). Training and assessment should result in increased and effective use of the English language by teachers with students in the classroom. The firm will be responsible to conduct an assessment of pre-service teachers as part of their recruitment process: Scope of the assignment The firm will be required to carry out the following tasks: Assess and certify teachers who are already trained on 6 modules: Administer a large-scale standardized English test to the already trained 9,545 teachers to evaluate their English Language Proficiency on the CEFR scale Certify and provide digital certificates to teachers in line with their level of English Language Proficiency. Include those who are certified below B2 CEFR in cohort 1 Deliver English and communication skills training to Cohort 1 teachers: Administer placement tests to 28,455 teachers to evaluate their English language proficiency on the CEFR scale. Conduct training of 10,000 pre-primary, primary and lower-secondary in-service teachers as part of Cohort 1 (including teachers who have been trained on the 6 REB manuals but have not been certified at B2 level of higher). Once full-scale training is complete, certify teachers at their respective final language level and provide automated digital certificates (with the ability to customize program certificates). The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.reb.gov.rw The shortlisting criteria are: A letter expressing the Interest to the assignment addressed to DG REB Demonstrated successful experience of the firm at least 10 years of experience in the consultancy services of the same nature Description indicating that they have performed at least two similar assignments with same nature, equivalent to at least $ 1.5Million at each assignment and covering 2,000 trainees successfully performed in 1year period or above Availability of appropriate skills among staff. Firms may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture to enhance their qualifications. The nature of association should clearly be stated in the Expression of Interest. In case of joint venture, the firm leading the joint venture should be mentioned. Joint venture partners must be jointly and severally liable. Eligibility criteria, establishment of the short-list and the selection of a consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method paragraph 7.3 of Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Fifth Edition September 2023 under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants.Please note that interest expressed by a consulting firm does not imply any obligation on the part of REB to include it on the shortlist. TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR HIRING INNOVATION CHALLENGE FUND TECHNICAL ASSISTANT FOR CDAT PROJECT CDAT Project Overview The World Bank approved $300 million in financing under the International Development Association’s (IDA’s) grant, credit, and Scale up Window to help the Government of Rwanda increase the use of irrigation and commercialization among producers and agribusiness firms in supported value chains, and to increase access to agricultural finance. The Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project (CDAT) will support the Government to provide services and create an enabling environment for the private actor throughout the agricultural value chain. It will finance public investments in the seeds sector, develop and rehabilitate irrigation systems on over 17,673 ha, provide accompanying land husbandry development on about 10,986 ha in surrounding water catchment areas to increase productivity and promote climate smart agriculture. The project will also support commercialization by helping farmers access markets and availing matching grants for investments in mechanization, post-harvest infrastructure and processing equipment. A CDAT challenge fund will invest in particularly innovative solutions for the sector that can be brought to scale. The project is nationwide and is foreseen to directly benefit at least 235,000 households, including women and youth. In partnership with financial institutions, the Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project will seek to enhance access to affordable financial services and products in the agricultural sector by providing short and long-term financing and reducing risks and challenges faced by agricultural value chains through strengthening market linkages and scaling up agriculture insurance. The project development objectives indicators are: Increase in share of agricultural produce sold by participating producers. This fund is designed to promote innovation in agriculture value chains and increase access to finance through a competitive and transparent application process. The facility will provide participating startup with non-refundable grants. Grants will be provided on a milestone basis to eligible, competitively selected businesses and would be limited to use on specific activities related to their subprojects. In the context of the CDAT project, the primary goal of the facility is to encourage and mainstream innovation, providing incentives for new technology-oriented market entrants to tailor their solutions to precisely meet challenges identified in the agri-food chains. This involves the enhancement and modernization of various agricultural activities, including post-harvest handling, processing, and marketing systems. The CDAT project will finance the establishment and operation of an Innovation Challenge Fund, which will increase access to finance through an open, competitive, and transparent application process. Beneficiaries will receive a grant of up to 70 percent of the investment costs and with the 30 percent beneficiary contribution being either in cash or in-kind. The objective is also to scale-up solutions developed by value chain actors and other service providers in the agri-food chains. Objectives of the Grant The Fund seeks to: Scale up the reach of agri-food sector innovations with potentially transformative impacts on the sector. Provide new technology-oriented market entrants and value chain actors with technical assistance support to accelerate milestone achievement and to precisely tailor their solutions to the needs and challenges of CDAT Project and CDAT beneficiaries. Provide challenge owner or CDAT beneficiaries with necessary technical assistance to facilitate technology adoption and innovation update; Scale up agri-tech solutions developed by innovators, value chain actors, and service providers within agri-food chains. MINICT will oversee the challenge competition through Hanga Pitch Fest while BDF will be in charge of administration and management of the grant. Business Development Fund, LTD The Innovation Challenge Fund will be administered by BDF, considering its extensive experience in managing grants in Rwanda. The BDF is a public sector entity that provide partial credit guarantees mainly to SME and agriculture loans. Agriculture is one of the focus sectors of the BDF guarantee scheme. BDF also provides matching grants and technical assistance support to agriculture SMEs. Considering its extensive experience in managing grants in Rwanda, the BDF will manage the matching grant for the project. BDF also has extensive experience in providing technical support to cooperatives and SMEs, which beneficials to prepare viable business proposals. Hanga Pitch Fest Hanga Pitch Fest is a unique platform to showcase tech-entrepreneurs and creative talents from all over the country and promote the use of technology and innovation in the Rwandan market. The festival is organized by the Government of Rwanda through Ministry of ICT and Innovation and Rwanda Development Board (RDB) and Rwanda Information Society Authority (RISA). The Hanga Pitch Fest also provides an opportunity to match selected startups to potential investors such as Angels and venture capital investors as well as Private Sector business leaders Activities of the Assignment The consultant’s primary responsibilities will be to coordinate all pertinent technical assistance required to implement innovations funded by the Challenge Fund on both the supply and demand sides. In addition, this will involve working with relevant stakeholders, innovators and CDAT Project beneficiaries to identify capacity building gaps and needs (as they change), offer technical guidance, guarantee efficient planning, seamless execution, sufficient quality assurance, monitoring, maintenance, and support. The consultant will also be responsible to coordinate the implementation of all digital innovation activities under the CDAT Project. The Government of Rwanda through MINAGRI/RAB developed five hillside irrigation schemes in the Eastern province at Musheri and Matimba Sectors pumping from the Muvumba River to center pivot, portable sprinkler, drip and hydrant hosepipe irrigation systems. Pressurized irrigation systems require proper operation and maintenance as most of the systems include pump stations, sediment settling basins, filtration, center pivots, portable sprinklers, etc. The systems have been in operation since about 2012 and are in need of rehabilitation and improvements. Project Site Description The project area includes 5 pumped irrigation schemes with a total of 900 ha net as summarized in the Table below. Each scheme has an intake on the Muvumba River, a sediment settling basin, and a pump station powered by REG electricity which supplies the pipe network feeding pressurized water to the irrigation system. The mentioned 5 irrigation schemes namely Lot 4, Lot 5 and Sections A, B and C are located in Musheri & Matimba Sectors. All schemes pump directly to the irrigation systems except for Lot 5 which first pumps to a reservoir above the scheme on the hill then feeds the irrigation network by gravity. The schemes with direct pumping experience frequent shutdowns due to power outages. High sediment deposits at the intakes and sediment settling basins have resulted in maintenance issues including much labor for removing sediment manually. Undersized sediment settling basins have resulted in much sediment being pumped into the pipe networks, clogging sprinkler nozzles, and wearing out pumps. Originally Lot 4 included 90 ha of drip but was damaged by farmers and converted to hydrant hosepipe irrigation. Lot 5 is the only lot with a reservoir (2,400 m3) and the center pivot irrigation system comprises a total of 4 pivots. Site Description Muvumba Perimeters (P) 4 and 5 are located in Nyagatare Sector, Nyagatare District in Eastern Province about 7km South of Nyagatare Town on the newly constructed Rukomo-Nyagatare paved road. Similarly, the studies will determine the needs/demands and the potential for multipurpose infrastructure development. The study will be carried out in two phases; prefeasibility and feasibility. The prefeasibility study will select, examine, and rank various alternatives for flood control and developing community-based irrigation scheme(s). If the prefeasibility study results in alternatives that seem reasonable to the Client, then the Consultant will proceed with the feasibility study. The feasibility study will examine selected alternatives and provide design drawings, cost estimates, and economic analyses sufficiently accurate to enable decisions to be made on project viability. In addition, the definition of the project components, organizational arrangements and procedures will be detailed enough to permit the executing agencies to use the study as guidance on project implementation. The Consultant should take into consideration the World Bank policies, guidelines and safeguards requirements, especially those for environmental and social impact assessment as well as dam safety to prepare the studies. SCOPE OF THE STUDY General The study will entail prefeasibility and feasibility studies that include preparation of designs, cost estimates, and implementation arrangements for the finally agreed development alternative for flood control and irrigation development, multipurpose infrastructure and watershed management associated with the project. The pre-feasibility and feasibility studies will comprise analyses related to: (a) basin-wide water resources (qualitative and quantitative), (b) drainage and flood management, (c) watershed management plan, (d) topographic survey, (e) geologic and geotechnical investigations, (f) soils and agronomy, (g) cropping patterns and crop water requirements, (h) headwork (dam/diversion and/or pump) and related multipurpose hydraulic structures, (i) irrigation infrastructure, (j) overall agricultural potential and support services including market and value chain development for maximum water resource use (l) land tenure, (m) environmental and social analyses, (o) institutional analysis, (p) water management and operation and maintenance, and (q) economic and financial analysis in close consultation with farmer communities and other stakeholders. This project must adhere with international best practice, policies/guidelines and safeguards. The Consultant shall define in consultation with the Client and other stakeholders the scope of the project options, assess the practicability of the development, and provide the basis for decision making on the choice of design options. The Consultant shall define the benefits (direct and indirect) and costs, and determine financial feasibility, economic justification and cost recovery. The Consultant will adopt participatory approaches to ensure the optimal involvement of stakeholders from national to community levels, during the study. In planning and scheduling of the tasks, the Consultant should note that not all tasks will be conducted in linear fashion and the Consultant should propose a schedule on how the tasks can be scheduled to meet the objectives of the assignment and for optimal linkage/sequencing. Project Description The Mwogo River is one of the main tributaries to the Nyabarongo and Akagera Rivers with its catchment extending into Nyungwe Forest and the furthest source of the Nile. Just upstream of the proposed site there is an existing scheme in Huye District that irrigates about 360 ha of rice. The proposed new area begins at the border with Nyanza District and runs 22 km downstream all the way through the District and into Ruhango and Nyambagabe Districts. Several tributaries enter the Mwogo along the way with the Rukarara being the most significant which includes some irrigation areas that are within the scope of the study. In total there are about 1,096 ha of gross area to be considered for new development and 66 ha in the upstream scheme which needs improvements (see figure below). The main difficulty in developing this long, narrow, and flat command area is the frequent and heavy flooding which of course increases as you move downstream and a number of tributaries join. The Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project (CDAT) will support the Government to provide services and create an enabling environment for the private actor throughout the agricultural value chain. It will finance public investments in the seeds sector, develop and rehabilitate irrigation systems on over 17,600 ha, provide accompanying land husbandry development on about 11,000 ha in surrounding water catchment areas to increase productivity and promote climate smart agriculture. The project will also support commercialization by helping farmers access markets and availing matching grants for investments in mechanization, post-harvest infrastructure and processing equipment. A CDAT challenge fund will invest in particularly innovative solutions for the sector that can be brought to scale. The project is nationwide and is foreseen to directly benefit at least 235,000 households, including women and youth. Site Description Kanyegenyege marshland (137ha) is located between two administrative sectors of Kinazi and Busoro respectively in Ruhango and Nyanza Districts of Southern Province outflowing into the wide Akanyaru marshland. The source of water is a permanent stream which is diverted into canals to supply water to the crops by surface irrigation. The last development of the marshland was done in 2014 and provided the irrigation infrastructures including weir intakes, open canal irrigation and drainage networks, various hydraulic structures and access roads. However, those infrastructures are in a dilapidated state due to the continuous invasive sand deposits coming from the sandy soils of the watershed and erosive destruction by floods. Moreover, during severe droughts, the water in the river is not enough and the upstream part takes all the water into the fields while the downstream part lacks sufficient water to meet the crop requirements. Flooding is also an issue observed in the furthest downstream part due to the rise and backflow of Akanyaru river. Flooding also occurs throughout the command area because the river bed or main drainage line is very small and cannot accommodate floods. Site Description The Rubuyenge-Burakari site is located in Southern Province, between Districts of Ruhango and Nyanza, along Ntongwe-Kigoma-Busoro Sectors and Kibirizi and Ntyazo Sectors. The project area is accessible through the asphalted national road NR1-Kigali-Huye-Akanyaru, by diverting at the Kigoma Power Post, and driving downwards to Murinja Cell in Nyanza District to access the right bank, and Kareba Cell in Ntongwe Sector on the left bank, for about 17km taking about 20 minutes. The irrigation scheme was developed in 2005 by Quick-Win Marshland Development Program (QWMDP) under Rwanda Ministry of Agriculture (MINAGRI) funds. The investments made were intended to develop diversion and irrigation infrastructures. The marshland is managed by famers through two cooperatives; CODEBA at Rubeyenge with 515 members, and COPRORIZ at Burakari with 400 members. The following map depicts the schematic layout of the Irrigation Scheme. The developed marshland irrigation scheme covers 417 ha with the Rubuyenge zone (231ha) at the upstream (including the left branch of Kamirantama) and the Burakari zone (186 ha) at the downstream of the complex (including the left branch of Kantwari). The largest part of the catchment is located in Nyanza District. The upstream part is within both Ruhango and Nyanza Districts while the major downstream part is only located in Nyanza District. Local farmers have made some arrangements to divert water from the stream in order to irrigate cropped land of Rubuyenge zone without any formal irrigation infrastructure. Part of Burakari was developed but as of today only one intake out of the two established remains active to divert and deliver irrigation water to Burakari zone. The other intake was completely destroyed by floods. Most infrastructures of Burakari zone including irrigation canals, drops, and offtakes, are generally in a degraded state and no longer function effectively due to excessive siltation coming from upstream. The existing intake at the junction of both zones does not withstand the silt-sand deposits coming from Rubuyenge - Burakari stream, and often overtops depositing silt-sand over about 10 Ha of land near this intake. Sand depositions at the intake reduce its diversion capacity and hence less water is available to the downstream zone. In addition to that, Rubuyenge zone has no access road. And, Rubuyenge – Burakari stream bed is gradually deepening at the downstream end while its stream banks are continually collapsing due to heavy flood flows and absence of adequate bank protection, hence, enlarging the stream width. A CDAT challenge fund will invest in particularly innovative solutions for the sector that can be brought to scale. The project is nationwide and is foreseen to directly benefit at least 235,000 households, including women and youth. In partnership with financial institutions, the Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project will seek to enhance access to affordable financial services and products in the agricultural sector by providing short and long-term financing and reducing risks and challenges faced by agricultural value chains through strengthening market linkages and scaling up agriculture insurance. Site description Rwangingo-Karangazi scheme is located in Nyagatare and Gatsibo Districts, Eastern Province and was developed on 930ha of area in 2016-2017 mainly for rice production. The scheme is equipped with an irrigation dam of 10m height and 3,750,000 m3 of capacity, a main irrigation canal on left side 29km long with various hydraulic structures, and secondary and tertiary irrigation and drainage networks. Currently, the marshland is being used for rice grown on 245 ha while 677 ha have been dedicated to maize and pulse crops production. The scheme is long and narrow and is bordered on the right side with a large papyrus swamp collecting all drainage water from the scheme and surrounding hills to make a natural water reservoir. During the rainy season the swamp water raises and invades the developed plots and affects the farming activities whereby around 40% of cultivated land is flooded which causes damage to crops as well as plots and irrigation structures. On the left side of the scheme, a long main canal of 29km conveys water released from the dam with many offtakes on its course to irrigate the crops inside the scheme but also supplies water for livestock and for irrigating horticulture crops by pumping from the canal outside the scheme. This canal is porous in different sections and has lost its initial designed dimensions due to lack or maintenance which causes a lot of water losses. Also, many structures and equipment regulating and distributing the water in the canals and plots are damaged due to the same reasons. title: Endline survey for SAIP Project
buyer: Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board
notice_text: The Government of Rwanda received grant from the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP), Grant No: TF0A8221 to be administrated through World Bank_ International Bank for reconstruction and Development (as trustee) to implement the Sustainable Agricultural Intensification and Food Security (SAIP) Project, and wants to use portion of proceeds to finance the Endline survey including data collection, analysis and reporting as part of Project Impact Evaluation and Implementation Completion Report (ICR). The Terms of Reference (TOR) related to this assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest. The Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB) / Sustainable Agricultural Intensification and Food Security (SAIP) Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest by providing the above Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expression of Interest (EOI) will include: core business and years in business, relevant experience, technical and managerial capability of the firm. The shortlisting criteria are: Demonstrated prior experience in large household surveys, qualitative surveys and experience in preparing assessment reports or projects completion reports. The survey firm must have conducted at least three surveys of the similar magnitude within the last 5 years with proven certificates of good completion with contracts. The firm must have knowledge of local formalities and customs in the implementation of household surveys. Experience in agricultural data collection is preferred. Specific experience, with proven certificates of good completion with contracts. The shortlist will contain five (5) to eight (8) firms. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September, 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the criteria set out in the Request for Proposals. Expressions of interest must be delivered through e-procurement system on the Date and time indicated by e-procurement system. TERMS OF REFERENCE BACKGROUND AND PROJECT DESCRIPTION The Government of Rwanda received grant from the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP), Grant No: TF0A8221 to be administrated through World Bank_ International Bank for reconstruction and Development (as trustee) to implement the Sustainable Agricultural Intensification and Food Security (SAIP) Project, and wants to use portion of proceeds to finance the Endline survey including data collection, analysis and reporting as part of Project Impact Evaluation and Implementation Completion Report (ICR). SAIP project focused on consolidating and expanding the results obtained under the World Bank- funded projects, namely LWH and the RSSP3, and other selected MINAGRI-developed schemes. These operations demonstrated that the sustainability of the outcomes achieved depend, to a large degree, on the robustness and strength of the producers’ organizations, their entrepreneurial skills and their negotiation capacity with commodity buyers, other value chain actors, and their entrepreneurial capacity. The project has four components: (1) Institutional strengthening, Agriculture Productivity enhancement and nutrition improvement which aim at strengthening farmers organization for improved agricultural productivity and healthier household nutrition, (2) Irrigation and water use efficiency with an objective of promoting technology and best practices for increased availability and efficiency use of water for irrigation to increase productivity and increase farmers’ resilience to climate volatility; (3) Market linkages and Value Addition investment support which aim at enhancing market linkages and value addition by strengthening the capacity of farmers’ organization and other value chain actors and by improving their access to finance and (4) Project management and technical assistance which is the component that supports all aspect of project management including coordination, monitoring and evaluation, communication and knowledge management and the technical assistance. The core objective of the SAIP is “To increase agricultural productivity, market access, and food security of the targeted beneficiaries in the project areas”. The Project development Objective performance indicators are the following: Percentage increase in harvested yield of targeted crops Percentage increase of produced commodities in targeted value chains marketed by participating producers; Food Consumption Score; Number of farmers adopting improved agricultural technology, disaggregated by gender. The project is implemented in nine (9) districts namely: Karongi, Rutsiro and Nyabihu in Western province, Rulindo in Northern Province, Rwamagana, Kayonza, Gatsibo and Ngoma in Eastern province and Nyanza in Southern province. OBJECTIVE 2.1. General objective SAIP would like to conduct (i) Endline survey of the project to assess the status of Project implementation, as measured against the Project’s performance indicators and targets, as well as (ii) prepare the Implementation Completion Report (ICR) including the assessment of the following; overall progress in Project physical and financial implementation to date, results of monitoring and evaluation activities, progress on procurement and disbursement, and Project implementation arrangements. 2.2 Specific objective Specifically, the consultancy service is to undertake households’ data collection, which will generate information that will inform the Endline status of households living in areas targeted by the Project. A survey will be done on a sample of residents in targeted areas to measure their socio-economic Endline status with much consideration on the project Result Framework Indicators and other social-economic indicators not necessarily in the RF. Other off-farm enterprises and value addition businesses for selected value chains as a result of access to matching grant program will also be analysed to have the baseline values for corresponding indicators. On the other hand, the consultancy service will prepare the ICR by reviewing existing documentations, in particular M&E database, annual action plans and budgets, quarterly, semi-annual and annual reports, financial reports, Mid-term review reports, Aide-memoirs, Project Appraisal Document, Financial Agreements, Project Implementation Manual, Financial and Accounting Manual, hold interviews with Project staff and beneficiaries. The Project will provide the maximum assistance and input in this regard, including provision of data and any needed assistance to produce a good report. The completion report shall therefore cover all activities in the three components of SAIP, explaining activities and their achievements by component and sub-component, success stories/impacts, lessons learnt, issues and way forward in each component. The report shall also highlight issues encountered during project implementation and summarize recommendations for further interventions. 2.3 Data The data to be collected for the Endline survey will come from comprehensive, multi-module household survey. The data will allow the project to establish the Endline situation of households living in areas targeted by the project. Additionally, data from the Matching Grant beneficiaries in various aspect of value chains including but not limited to primary production, aggregation, post-harvest handling and value addition will be collected from individual farmers, farmers’ organizations (SGH or Cooperative) and SMEs supported by SAIP project. The data to be collected are from season B 2023, Season C 2023 and Season A 2024 for Karongi, Rutsiro, Nyanza, Rwamagana, Gatsibo, Kayonza, Rulindo, Ngoma and Nyabihu project intervention Districts. The data collected will help the project to report on the following indicators, which are part of the results framework. Harvested yield of targeted crops, including maize, beans, Irish potatoes, vegetables and fruits. Percentage of produced commodities in targeted value chains marketed by participating producers Food consumption score Farmers adopting improved agriculture technology Farmers reached with agriculture assets or services Producer-based organizations supported People receiving improved nutrition services and products Increase in annual net revenues made by beneficiary cooperatives Area provided with new/improved irrigation or drainage services Farmers benefiting from the project supported small-scale irrigation interventions Users paying water fees to the water users associations Increment of Water Use Efficiency Volume of agricultural production processed by post-harvest facilities established with project support Farmers organization - buyer linkages established Amount of credit mobilized by farmers and farmers’ organization Beneficiaries satisfied with the services provided by the project In addition to the RF indicators, data on other social-economic indicators not necessarily in the RF will be collected and analyzed to inform the preparation of ICR: Job creation Household incomes Household assets accumulation Entrepreneurship development Youth and gender participation Data collected will be disaggregated by sex wherever possible. 2.4. The survey firm will be expected reach at every household. The Consultancy firm's main role will be; the review of the survey questionnaire, sampling, support in the whole process of enumerator training, pilot, collection and supervision of data collection, analysis of data and reports writing. Two (2) reports are expected; Endline Survey report and Implementation Completion Report. Focus group discussions for 12 sampled project supported cooperative and 8 WUAs . Structured interviews for 24 sampled project supported matching grant beneficiaries in different value chain categories i.e (i) primary production, (ii) post-harvest handling and (iii) value addition. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted for (a) other key stakeholders (local goverment officials from the districts project interventions), (b) parteners including RYAF and FAO and (c) service providers including Mechanization equipment suppliers, irrigation equipment suppliers, Greenhouses suppliers Secondary data review to complement all the collected data with the comprehensive review of the existing reports and documentation from MINAGRI/RAB. TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR AN ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT/ ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR IRRIGATION AND LAND HUSBANDRY REHABILITATION FOR NYARUBOGO CDAT SITE BACKGROUND Introduction Rwanda is committed to become an upper-middle income country by 2035 and a high-income country by 2050. A modern and high performing agriculture sector, well integrated into regional and global supply chains, is one of the country’s key drivers of growth. The required transformation in agriculture needs to be built on competition and innovation and achieve higher productivity rates through private sector-led investment and development. Rwandan agriculture is mostly rain-fed, and therefore more exposed to weather-related risks, especially to severe, frequent, and prolonged dry spells occurring during the cropping seasons. Irrigation investments have significant potential to address these challenges and to improve the productivity of farmers who depend on rain-fed agriculture, through improving yields and increasing cultivation in the dry season. Irrigation scheme requires infrastructure investment, operation and maintenance costs and farmers in drought-prone areas require adequate infrastructure to cope with such conditions. The expansion of the irrigation network is the only way to expand the effective land area and reduce climate-related production risks through improved technologies and practices. It is in this regard that the “Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project’’ hereafter “CDAT project” will invest in expanding and upgrading the irrigation area infrastructure through development of irrigation facilities including diversion weirs at Nyarubogo site and the land husbandry development. The Nyarubogo CDAT Project Site is situated in Muyira and Kibirizi Sectors, Nyanza District, Southern Province. Therefore, these Terms of Reference (ToRs) are for consultancy services to provide Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board with the full study for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment of Hydro-Agricultural development works for Nyarubogo site. In addition to these ToRs, the study will be conducted in accordance with World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), the provisions of the laws and regulations that govern EIA in Rwanda, and will require application for EIA Clearance to Rwanda Development Board (RDB). CDAT project The Government of Rwanda (GoR) is pursuing its efforts to accelerate private sector-led growth and further reduce poverty. This is performed through the implementation of various sustainable development programs and projects. The “Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation Project’’ hereafter “CDAT project” is among the development projects designed under the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), funded by the World Bank (WB) for a period of 5 years. The objectives of the project are to increase the use of irrigation and commercialization among producers and agribusiness firms in supported value chains and to increase access to agriculture finance. The project beneficiaries are farmers’ cooperatives, commercial farmers and small and medium-sized agri-enterprises. The project has four components. Component 1: Value Chain and Infrastructure Development , it aims to increase marketable volumes in supported value chains and provide targeted climate sensitive infrastructure support. The component will finance public goods such as irrigation infrastructure, land husbandry, extension provision, and research and development of improved seeds. Under this component, they are 3 subcomponents : (i) Irrigation rehabilitation and development focuses to expand the irrigated area and increase marketable output from irrigated agriculture, (ii), Land husbandry with objective to protect the watershed areas that drain to the irrigation sites under Subcomponent 1.1, increase the productivity of these areas, and prevent soil erosion , Innovation and services for agri-business value chain development aims to increase value addition and marketability by addressing critical constraints that directly affect the commercialization of the targeted value chains. Component 2 : Agricultural Finance and Insurance, the objective of this component is to increase access to financial products and services to farmers and cooperatives for the commercialization of the sector. Under this component, 2 subcomponents have developed: (i) Scaling up agricultural finance to set the foundation for expanding the supply of affordable financial services and products, (ii) Strengthening agricultural insurance by strengthening the quality and effectiveness of agriculture insurance offered through the NAIS, which seeks to de-risk the agricultural sector using market-based insurance mechanisms and fitness solutions. Component 3 : Covers project management to ensure the smooth implementation of the project and will support all aspects of project management such as: (i) project staffing and their training; (ii) procurement and financial management; (iii) environmental and social risk management and compliance; (iv) monitoring and evaluation; (v) equipment and operating costs; (vi) communication and knowledge management. Component 4: Contingency Emergency Response Component will allow for rapid reallocation of the project’s uncommitted funds in the event of an eligible emergency. Therefore, various activities were developed under these components and subcomponent and their implementation requires carrying out civil works related to the rehabilitation of existing or development of irrigation infrastructure. Under subcomponent 1.1, works related to pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, preparation of detailed designs, construction supervision and quality assurances, construction of irrigation water abstraction, delivery, distribution, and drainage structures will be implemented in 31 irrigation schemes identified in different districts countrywide. Rehabilitation of irrigation and drainage network canals and construction of hydraulic structures (diversion weir, water intake, drops, small bridges, culverts, etc.) may present some environmental and social risks, particularly relating to potential economic displacement, community health and safety, and protection of biodiversity. The Government of Rwanda committed to implement CDAT Project in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), national environmental laws and regulations, and International Environmental and Social Conventions that Rwanda is signatory. It is within this regards that different safeguards instruments have been prepared for CDAT Project and disclosed on World Bank and RAB websites. The available project level safeguards instruments include: Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), Labor Management Plan (LMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Master Emergency Preparedness Plan (MEPP), Master Emergency Response Plan (MERP) and Pest Management Plan (PMP). In addition to the above-mentioned safeguard instruments, the consultant will refer to the Project Appraisal Document (PAD) also available on RAB website. SITE CONTEXT AND OVERVIEW CDAT Project interventions at Nyarubogo site are the irrigation & land husbandry of the Marshland. Activities to be conducted in Nyarubogo Marshland are mainly the construction of two dams and rehabilitation of irrigation drainages and networks. The objective of the ESIA for the works related to the Nyarubogo marshland rehabilitation and development (320ha) is to assess the potential environmental and social impacts and propose mitigation measures which will effectively address the impacts and inform the project preparation process of the potential impacts of different alternatives, and relevant mitigation measures. The various irrigation and land husbandry supporting arrangements are needed to boost rice agriculture production at this site by upgrading the concrete canal from earth to lined canal; raising the dyke with a short concrete wall of 1 m high; watershed protection, and rehabilitation of diversion structures. The marshland site is located in Nyanza District in Southern province, precisely between Kibirizi and Muyira sectors. There is a bank of water called the Lake of King Rudahigwa, dividing the Marshland into two parts. Hence, the first dam will be located at the border of Muyira and Kibirizi sectors in Rwotso cell which is in Kibirizi sector whereas the second dam will be located between Migina cell and Nyamiyaga cell in Muyira sector. Figure 1: Nyarubogo site location CONTEXT AND JUSTIFICATION The scope of this environment and social assessment is restricted to 320 ha of Nyarubogo Marshland for the construction of two dams and rehabilitation of irrigation canals and drainages. The irrigation system proposed is to construct two dams in the same stream and catchments. One dam will be located upstream where water is low and will have a capacity of 86,000m3 while the downstream dam will have a retention capacity of 450,000m3. In total, the water retention in the reservoirs will be 536,000m3. The retention heights will be 10m and 8.6m respectively and the reservoirs will inundate an area of 3.5 and 30 m2 respectively. 3.1 . However, aspects relating to increasing access were implemented under Energy Development Corporation Limited (EDCL) through the Projects Implementation Support Agreement (PISA) signed between both corporations. Implementation of the project began in May 2016 and was completed October 31st, 2022. The objectives and results of the programme are presented in the table below . Project name Project description Rwanda Electricity Sector Strengthening Project-RESSP Objective: Enhance the operational efficiency of the utility and increase electricity access. 2. Components: Electricity Sector Capacity Strengthening Increased Access to Electricity Services Technical Assistance and Project Implementation Support 3. Outputs: People provided with access to electricity under the project (additional 324,000 people will get access to electricity by connecting about 72,000 households, of which 50 percent are female beneficiaries), Improved performance of electricity sector in Rwanda: (i) Reduction in commercial losses (from 7.6 percent to 4 percent); and (ii) Reduction in Energy Not Served in Kigali City 15KV network (up to 0.2GWh)) Since the inception of RESSP, the project has managed to provide electricity access to over 83,000 households and productive users (including public institutions, health centers, schools, etc.) through the extension of on-grid power networks countrywide and reduced energy not served in Kigali City 15KV distribution network (total annual Gigawatt-hour (GWh)) from 2.56GWh in 2015 to 0.2GWh. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI) Kigali, on 22 June 2023 Ref No: RW-REG/EDCL-344186-CS-QBS Project: Rwanda - Energy Access and Quality Improvement Project Tender Name: Hiring a consultant to design loan product for Clean Cooking financing. BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT In a move to support the Government of Rwanda’s target to reduce the percentage of households that use firewood for cooking from a baseline value of 79.90% in 2017 to 42% by 2024, BRD in collaboration with the Government of Rwanda (GOR) and the World Bank launched a Clean Cooking Results-based Financing (CC-RBF) subsidy under the Energy Access and Quality Improvement Project (EAQIP). The project is financed by the World Bank to a tune of USD 17 Million equivalent to Rwandan Francs 17 billion and is implemented by BRD in partnership with Energy Development Corporation Limited (EDCL). The subsidy is designed to address the affordability of clean cooking technologies through the reduction of cooking stove prices with varying subsidy amounts allocated to the beneficiary categories with the objective of reaching the lowest income population in Rwanda. PROPOSED DUTIES AND RESPONSABILITIES OF THE CONSULTANT BRD also intends to provide loan facilities in the clean cooking sector. The credit will be directly granted to clean cooking companies and/or on-lent through participating financial institutions (commercial banks, microfinance institutions, SACCOs) as it is being done in other renewable energy projects. The Bank therefore would like to recruit a consultant with expertise in clean cooking to develop a clean cooking lending product for BRD. The consultant is required to design loan products for a number of clean cooking technologies/fuels such as financing LPG, electric cooking stoves/cookers, and other green cooking technologies. The consultant is also expected to design a loan product that can be financed against RBF subsidy receivables. The consultant is required to also conduct a detailed risk analysis across a variety of clean cooking options and propose a workable risk mitigation matrix. S/he should be capable of designing modern analytical tools for the identification and quantification of the risks and establishing a fair risk-based premium for the bank. The lending package should be able to provide comprehensive information about the clean cooking technology, technical specification, international and regional practices, demand side risk, supply side risk, and the mapping of available suppliers in the Rwanda market. Sincerely, Done at Kigali, on 12/06/202 Gentile UMUSHASHI Félix GAKUBA Head Procurement Management Services Managing Director TERMS OF REFERENCES FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR GIS NETWORK DATA COLLECTION, CUSTOMERS MAPPING & INDEXING INTRODUCTION: New and digital technologies have been unlocking opportunities to collect, manage and analyze large amounts of data in a relatively cost-effective way. Still, given current challenges, it is prudent that their use for energy statistics is complementary to traditional methods, until issues like data governance, confidentiality or data representativeness are more widely addressed. It is in that regards, that REG is hiring a Company to do network as-built GIS data collection, customer mapping and indexing. The mapped data will help in updating the existing GIS network system, develop a network geodatabase and utility network model that can support in network planning, design, operations and maintenance of distribution network asset and any other related activities. Will also help in customer mapping and their indexing to support outage management information system, to estimate energy balance, customer management information system etc. 1.1 NETWORK BRIEF AND GIS BACKGROUND The electricity transmission network consists of 110 and 220 kV. The distribution system consists of both medium voltage (30 kV, 15 kV and 6.6kV) and low-voltage (0.4 kV) networks, distribution transformers, with a significant proportion being in Kigali and providing distribution services to up to 2,400,000 residential and businesses connections across the country. In 2012, the former Energy Water and Sanitation Authority (EWSA), which later split into water and electricity companies (REG and WASAC), received funding from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to implement GIS for asset management and electrical network planning on a desktop-based GIS on two separate databases. As the technology evolves, REG has revealed a potential to improve the current GIS to serve multipurpose activities with an integrated suite of software for visualizing the system data, tools for network optimization, and a range of automation and information processing systems which assist in the operation, maintenance, and planning of Electric network. 1.2 REASONS FOR UPGRADING REG GIS SYSTEM REG utilises standalone system/ tools to perform planning and design operation, and maintenance activities. The system cannot be integrated, resulting in stranded data, information, and inefficiencies. The lack of integration greatly hinders the effective implementation of planning, design, operation, and maintenance activities. Currently, REG utilises the geospatial information system GIS as a repository for network asset geospatial information. The existing GIS platform lacks integrated tools for distribution network planning and design. It does not support an electrically connected and traceable topological model for medium voltage (MV) and low voltage networks. The inability to connect to the existing GIS system to other engineering systems such as ADMS/SCADA also under print a need to move to a more robust system that support seamless integrations. 1.3 DESCRIPTION OF EXISTING GIS INFRASTRUCTURE EUCL and EDCL has implemented an enterprise Geodatabase where the data are accessed through ArcGIS Server web services. As this is a Multiuser geodatabase, it provides extra functionality called versioning that allows many users to edit the same data at the same time. Existing Database Architecture The data are stored in RDBMS (Microsoft SQL Server) software that provides a simple, formal data model for storing and managing information in tables. The schema of an enterprise geodatabase is persisted in the RDBMS as a collection of tables known as the Arc SDE Repository. Aspects related to data storage and retrieval are implemented as simple tables and certain aspects of geographic data management, such as disk-based storage, definition of attribute types, query processing, and multiuser transaction processing, are executed by the RDBMS. Microsoft SQL Server as an RDBMS manages the current REG electrical geodatabase and the database access is controlled through user accounts. Privileges are granted to user accounts based on the work users need to do in the geodatabase. Once accounts exist and privileges have been granted, users can connect to the geodatabase from client applications and begin working with the geodatabase and the data are edited through ArcGIS Desktop 10.8.1.
