title: Individual consultancy services to develop learner benchmarks for subjects and grades
notice_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR DESIGNING QUESTION ITEM BANK DEVELOPING LEARNER BENCHMARKS FOR SUBJECTS AND GRADE LEVEL. Brief description of the assignment Title of the Assignment: Designing question item bank and developing learners’ benchmarks for subject and grade level competencies. Duty station: Kigali/Rwanda Type of contract: International Consultant Expected starting date: January 2022 Duration: 9 Months Applicant deadline: Project Title: Rwanda Quality Basic Education for Human Capital Development Project. Background The Ministry of Education through Rwanda Education Board has been implementing a World Bank Funded Project (Rwanda Quality Basic Education for Human Capital Development) since 2019. The project seeks to contribute to improve teacher’s competency, student’s retention, and learning in basic education in Rwanda. The Rwanda Basic Education for Human Capital Development project’s main components are enhancing teacher effectiveness for improved student learning, improving the school environment to support student learning, and developing institutional capacity to strengthen teaching and learning whereby strengthening National Learning Assessment is highlighted. With a view to strengthening the quality and equity of learning country wide, Rwanda Basic Education Board has been administering Learning Assessment in Rwandan schools (LARS) every two years since 2011 to enhance the quality of education and to study the state of learning in literacy and numeracy in Rwandan schools. This instrument has provided decision makers with snapshots of students’ literacy and numeracy skills at specific points in time. The government of Rwanda is committed to meeting the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) including SDG 4.I, which states that by 2030, all girls and boys complete free, equitable, and quality primary and secondary education, leading to relevant and effective learning outcomes. The Rwanda Basic Education Board in Collaboration with the National Examination and School Inspection Authority (NESA) is seeking for a consultant with strong learning achievement assessment experience to design question item banks and develop learners’ benchmarks for subject and grade level competencies. Objectives of the Assignment The ultimate objective of this assignment is to have both benchmarks and question item bank for English (fluency and comprehension) for P1, P2, P4, P5, S1, and S2; in Mathematics, for P1, P2, P4, P5, S1, and S2, Social and Religious Studies (SST) and Science and Elementary Technology (SET) for P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 & P6, and in Biology, Chemistry, Physics for S1 and S2 and finally, Geography and History for S1, S2 and S3. Having benchmarks will strengthen assessment systems to better track learner performance as a basis for targeted remediation and investment as a common goal. This includes among other things developing the capacity of REB to design assessment tools that will enable us to accurately measure learning at different levels. Establish benchmarks across different grades and subjects against which we can measure learning outcomes and categorize students based on their performance. Benchmarks and cut scores will be used progressively in formative continuous assessment, Comprehensive assessment for learning and in National Examination. Developed benchmarks should be internationally comparable and enable REB to report globally on SDG 4 and HCI indicators as well as prepare the country to participate in regional and international assessments. Scope of work The purpose of this assignment is to develop learners’ benchmarks which will avail both the question item bank and standards for learning and achievement useful to track learner performance. this will serve in assessment for placement and performance. With a period of nine (9) months starting from the date of signing a contract, the Individual consultant will perform the specific tasks and deliverables described in the sections below, respecting the given timeline. As highlighted in the objectives of the assignment, this assignment will focus on the following subjects: SN Subject \ Grade P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6 S1 S2 S3 1 English (fluency and comprehension) X X X X X X 2 Mathematics X X X X X X 3 Social and Religious Studies X X X X X X 4 Science and Elementary Technology X X X X X X 5 Biology X X 6 Chemistry X X 7 Physics X X 8 Geography X X X 9 History X X X The individual consultant shall undertake the following specific tasks to develop benchmarks. Specific tasks To analyze the current assessment practices (both formative and summative) in Rwandan Primary and Secondary Education, identify the gaps vis-à-vis the Competence Based Assessment (refer to Competence Based Curriculum) To develop a detailed strategy white paper/framework on effective implementation of Competence Based Assessment and accountability in Rwandan Primary and Secondary Education with emphasis on “ EARLY DETECTION OF LEARNING GAPS ” To identify and conduct capacity building training/workshops for participants in the various stages of the process Assist NESA and REB to develop and digitize a question item bank for English (fluency and comprehension) for P1, P2, P4, P5, S1, and S2; in Mathematics, for P1, P2, P4, P5, S1, and S2, Social and Religious Studies (SST) and Science and Elementary Technology (SET) for P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 & P6, and in Biology, Chemistry, Physics for S1 and S2 and finally, Geography and History for S1, S2 and S3. To develop assessment benchmarks for P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, S1, S2 and S3 levels based on the Rwandan CBC To develop performance thresholds for assessment benchmarks To design tools and establish benchmarks for oral reading fluency and reading comprehension To draft cut scores and literacy benchmarks on oral reading fluency and comprehension To establish literacy metrics To establish texts aligned with the developed metrics To establish numeracy metrics To establish science metrics To establish social science metrics To document the entire process To pilot (performance thresholds) and benchmarks/assessment for P1 pupils, P2 pupils, P4 pupils, P5 pupils, P6 pupils, S1, S2 learners and S3. To pre-validate draft of cut score and benchmarks based on student/pupil performance To complete final technical validation and benchmarks Work closely with NESA assessment staff/specialists right from the preparatory phase of the consultancy to the reporting of the results. Expected deliverables. The consultant will provide the following deliverables within the stated timelines as presented in the table below to be done in two phases: Activity/output (Phase 1) Primary Schools Time allocated An inception report: This will include a brief review of the consultant’s understanding of the ToRs, Angoff process, together with any issues or constraints foreseen, as well as a proposed approach and work plan. NB : Inception report will cover two Phases (1&2) To be done in 15 days Develop the tools, assessment framework and cut scores to be used by Rwanda primary schools To be done in 40 days Avail the tools, cut scores for all levels and guide the workshop organized by REB-SPIU in collaboration with NESA in developing assessment framework to establish benchmarks for primary school levels. To be done in 5 days Preparation, development and digitization of learners’ benchmarks and question item bank for subjects and grade level of P1, 2, 4, 5 and for one core subject for P3 and P6 To be done in 45 days Develop and submit first draft report prepared using modified Angoff method to set cut scores and covering all the inputs from the workshops and field visits. To be done in 7 days Pilot the developed benchmarks in the selected schools in collaboration with REB-SPIU and NESA To be done in 5 days Develop and submit second draft report prepared using modified Angoff method to set cut scores covering all field results To be done in 22 days Lead validation workshop on consultant reports (Benchmarks reports and Angoff process) by client in collaboration with NESA and stakeholders) To be done in 6 days Submit final (benchmarks reports and Angoff process) reports for primary schools incorporating inputs from the validation workshop To be done in 5 days Total number of working days 150 days Activity/output (Phase 2) Lower Secondary Schools Time allocated Develop the tools and cut scores to be used by Rwanda secondary schools To be done in 22 days Avail the tools, cut scores for all levels and guide the workshop organized by REB-SPIU in collaboration with NESA in developing assessment framework to establish benchmarks for Primary school levels. To be done in 7 days Preparation, development and digitization of learners’ benchmarks and question item bank for subjects and grade levels of S1, S2 and remaining core subjects for S3 To be done in 48 days Develop and submit first draft report prepared using modified Angoff method to set cut scores and covering all the inputs from the workshops and field visits. To be done in 7 days Pilot the developed benchmarks in the selected schools in collaboration with REB-SPIU and NESA To be done in 5 days Develop and submit second draft report prepared using modified Angoff method to set cut scores covering all field results To be done in 20 days Lead validation workshop of consultant reports (Benchmarks reports and Angoff process) by client in collaboration with NESA and Stakeholders To be done in 5 days Submit final (Benchmarks reports and Angoff process) reports for secondary schools incorporating inputs from the validation workshop. To be done in 6 days Total number of working days 120 days Desired Technical Requirements The consultant is expected to have the following minimum qualification and experience in learning assessment, research, and in measuring progress of numeracy and literacy in basic education with the following key skills and competencies: Advanced degree (PhD) in Psychometrics, Learning Psychology, Measurement and evaluation or Education Sciences At least 5 years relevant experience in developing benchmarks and measuring international best practices Experience in quantitative analysis and psychometrics with proof/testimonials Background in literacy, numeracy and measuring progress in basic education Professional experience in developing and designing benchmarks and using Modified Angoff method to set cut scores. Experience in conducting similar works with proof/testimonial certificates of completion Advanced working knowledge of measuring international best practices in assessments Strong organization skills, with an ability to effectively manage multiple tasks simultaneously. title: Recruitment of a market facilitator firm for clean cooking technologies
buyer: Rwanda Energy Group - Energy Development Corporation Limited
notice_text: Kigali, on 24/08/2021 Ref: No 11.07.023/11298/11346/MD-EDCL/FG /ug/jr Country: Rwanda Project : Energy Access and Quality Improvement Project (EAQIP) Grant No: TB03589 Assignment Title : Request for Expression of Interest for Recruitment of a market facilitator firm for clean cooking technologies Reference No : RW-REG/EDCL-238721-CS-QCBS Background: The Government of Rwanda plans to partner with the private sector and facilitate a competition-based development of markets for clean-cooking products and technologies. MININFRA recently approved an ambitious new Biomass Energy Strategy (2019-2030) and an amendment to its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), with targets of reducing the percentage of households that use firewood for cooking from the baseline value of 79.9% in 2017 to 42% by 2024, and phasing-out the use of charcoal in urban areas. The clean cooking agenda has recently been moved to MININFRA and REG/EDCL have the mandate to implement it. The Rwanda Standards Board (RSB) is tasked with certifications and setting standards for cooking products and a testing lab is currently under development. In October 2019, MININFRA published the Biomass Energy Strategy: A Sustainable Path to Clean Cooking 2019-2030. In May 2020, the Government updated its NDC under the Paris Agreements which includes promoting the use of efficient domestic stoves as a mitigation measure since cooking accounts for 14% of the GHG emissions from the energy sector. Implementation of the Biomass Energy Strategy will require substantial grant resources be made available to the sector to address the affordability and awareness gaps, as well as addressing the unproven nature of many new technologies now available in Rwanda. Other than the richest 10 percent of households, cash expenditure on cooking fuel is rare in rural Rwanda as 97 percent of households use firewood with an insignificant number using purchased charcoal. This means that the market for clean cooking solutions will require partial subsidies to become commercially viable. Rwanda Energy Access and Quality Improvement Project (EAQIP) aims to increase access to clean cooking Solutions for 500,000 households. EAQIP’s Component 3b will set up a clean cooking Results-Based Financing (RBF-RBF Clean Cooking (reg.rw); https://www.brd.rw/brd/energy-investments/#tab-155bda93481865676fc) window to partially subsidize purchases of clean and efficient cooking solutions by eligible households. The clean cooking RBF window will initially support Tier 2+ solutions, with the objective to gradually increase the minimum performance level requirements as affordable Tier 3+ solutions become widely available. The RBF window will support both urban and rural households. In urban areas, the focus of the clean cooking RBF will be to reduce and eventually phase out charcoal as a cooking fuel and replace it with Tier 3+ clean cooking solutions. In rural areas, the focus will be on reducing the reliance on firewood as a cooking fuel by gradually introducing more efficient (Tier 2+) and clean cooking (Tier 3+) solutions. The two focus areas will contribute to the objectives of (i) phasing out charcoal use in urban areas; and (ii) reducing the reliance and consumption of, firewood. The performance of eligible cooking technologies will need to be demonstrated through laboratory testing and/or field-based data. The size of the RBF incentives will be linked to verified outputs, outcomes and impact level results, differentiated by cooking technology performance levels and consumer income categories (Ubudehe categories); and will be reviewed and adjusted periodically. The Energy Development Corporation Limited (EDCL) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: General experience: The firm shall prove that it successfully conducted consultancy services on energy Projects. Similar Experience: To provide at least two (2) completion certificates of similar tenders executed and supported with copies of related contracts. To provide a brief presentation of qualifications and number of key staff with their experience to be involved in the execution of the assignment. N.B : Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Objective of Assignment The project intends to put in place a process that would empower clean cooking companies in developing a sustainable market for clean cooking technologies by creating enabling conditions and support for improved products quality and realization of value addition opportunities. The function of the market facilitator is to engage and support clean cooking companies to participate in the clean cooking RBF program and successfully deliver clean cooking solutions. The duration of this is assignment is 2 years starting from date of signature of the contract. Selection process The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 revise November 2017, August 2018 and November 2020) (“Consultant Guidelines”) setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. notice_text: Kigali, on 06/08/2021 Ref: No 11.07.023/11298/2021/MD-EDCL/FG /ug/jr Country: Rwanda Project : Energy Access and Quality Improvement Project (EAQIP) Grant No: TB03589 Assignment Title : Request for Expression of Interest for recruiting a communication consulting firm to support the campaign for clean cooking awareness and behaviour change. Reference No : RW-REG/EDCL-238713-CS-QCBS Background: The Government of Rwanda plans to partner with the private sector and facilitate a competition-based development of markets for clean-cooking products and technologies. MININFRA recently approved an ambitious new Biomass Energy Strategy (2019-2030) and an amendment to its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), with targets of reducing the percentage of households that use firewood for cooking from the baseline value of 79.9% in 2017 to 42% by 2024, and phasing-out the use of charcoal in urban areas. The clean cooking agenda has recently been moved to MININFRA and REG/EDCL have the mandate to implement it. The Rwanda Standards Board (RSB) is tasked with certifications and setting standards for cooking products and a testing lab is currently under development. In October 2019, MININFRA published the Biomass Energy Strategy: A Sustainable Path to Clean Cooking 2019-2030. In May 2020, the Government updated its NDC under the Paris Agreements which includes promoting the use of efficient domestic stoves as a mitigation measure since cooking accounts for 14% of the GHG emissions from the energy sector. Implementation of the Biomass Energy Strategy will require substantial grant resources be made available to the sector to address the affordability and awareness gaps, as well as addressing the unproven nature of many new technologies now available in Rwanda. Other than the richest 10 percent of households, cash expenditure on cooking fuel is rare in rural Rwanda as 97 percent of households use firewood with an insignificant number using purchased charcoal. This means that the market for clean cooking solutions will require partial subsidies to become commercially viable. Rwanda Energy Access and Quality Improvement Project (EAQIP) aims to increase access to clean cooking Solutions for 500,000 households. EAQIP’s Component 3b will set up a clean cooking RBF window to partially subsidize purchases of clean and efficient cooking solutions by eligible households. The clean cooking RBF window will initially support Tier 2+ solutions, with the objective to gradually increase the minimum performance level requirements as affordable Tier 3+ solutions become widely available. The RBF window will support both urban and rural households. In urban areas, the focus of the clean cooking RBF will be to reduce and eventually phase out charcoal as a cooking fuel and replace it with Tier 3+ clean cooking solutions. In rural areas, the focus will be on reducing the reliance on firewood as a cooking fuel by gradually introducing more efficient (Tier 2+) and clean cooking (Tier 3+) solutions. The two focus areas will contribute to the objectives of (i) phasing out charcoal use in urban areas; and (ii) reducing the reliance and consumption of, firewood. The performance of eligible cooking technologies will need to be demonstrated through laboratory testing and/or field-based data. The size of the RBF incentives will be linked to verified outputs, outcomes and impact level results, differentiated by cooking technology performance levels and consumer income categories (Ubudehe categories); and will be reviewed and adjusted periodically. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website : www.reg.rw. title: Selection of a consultant(s) to conduct ESIA and RAPs for PW and EPW projects
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA LOCAL ADMINISTRATIVE ENTITIES DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (LODA) L’AGENCE DE DEVELOPPEMENT DES ENTITES ADMINISTRATIVES LOCALES B.P: 7305 Kigali, Tel: 5029, web site: www.loda.gov.rw & E-mail: info@loda.gov.rw REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST Country: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Project: IPF SOCIAL PROTECTION PROJECT Credit No: 61690-RWA Project number: (P162646) Reference : As per e procurement system CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR HIRING SSPP CONSULTANT ON RESETTLEMENT AND SOCIAL AUDIT FOR CPW SUBPROJECT IMPLEMENTED IN 2018-2019 The Local Administrative Entities Development Agency (LODA) is responsible for coordinating implementation of a wide range of socio-economic development activities funded by the government of Rwanda and its development partners. LODA is divided into two business areas: Social Protection and Local Economic Development (LED). Through a number of key social protection programmes namely: The Vision 2020 Umurenge Programme (VUP), the Minimum Package for Graduation and Ubudehe community project; LODA plays a major role in the implementation of Rwanda’s Social Protection policy and strategic framework and contributes to the achievement of range of national, regional and international commitments. The Strengthening Social Protection Project (SSPP) is a four-year Government of Rwanda Project funded by the World Bank that aims at improving the effectiveness of Rwanda’s flagship social protection system, notably the flagship Vision 2020 Umurenge Programme (VUP), for targeted vulnerable groups and expands access to Human Capital and Economic Inclusion Services to Rwandans. LODA and the Ministry of Local Government implement this project in close partnership with Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC), National Early Childhood Development Program (NECDP), National Identification Agency (NIDA), and Districts. As part of project preparation, Environment and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) were prepared as guiding instruments for preparation of subproject specific Environment and Social Impact Assessment Reports (ESIA’s) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAP’s), where required during project implementation. The Resettlement and Social Audit is required for projects implementation for the year 2018-2019 to ensure that the World Bank and national Safeguard requirements were adequately addressed for the completed projects of the above-mentioned Fiscal Year. These Terms of Reference (ToRs) for the Resettlement Audit under Strengthening Social Protection Project by an independent resettlement auditor is for the purposes of reviewing of the Strengthening Social Protection Project land acquisition, expropriation, compensation and resettlement exercise, and to report findings to LODA, thereafter LODA will report back to the Bank. The objective of the consultancy service is to provide LODA and the Bank with a review and audit of the resettlement exercise of Strengthening Social Protection Project. LOCAL ADMINISTRATIVE ENTITIES DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (LODA) now invites eligible Individual consultants to indicate their interest for providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The selection criteria are as follows: At least a bachelor degree in Social Sciences, development studies, community development, economics, political sciences, public administration, management, with 10 years’ professional experience in the area of environmental and social assessment, social audit, reviews, monitoring and or auditing of public or private investment projects, establishment or undertakings and having knowledge of World Bank and other development partners safeguards policies, social audit. Or a Master's Degree in the same fields with at least 5 years professional experience in the area of environmental and social assessment, social audit, reviews, monitoring and or auditing of public or private investment projects, establishment or undertakings and having knowledge of World Bank and other development partners’ safeguards policies, social audit. The consultant should have completed at least 3 assignments in Resettlement and Social Audit or conducting ESIA, RAPs, RPF, and ESMF with certificates of completion Excellent understanding of Rwanda’s environmental safeguarding legislation, policies, regulations and practices; Experience of working on large-scale community infrastructure programmes is desirable Understanding of Rwanda’s decentralized governance framework; Analytical & complex problem solving skills; High ethical standards, and capacity to exercise good judgment; Attention to detail, works meticulously in a systematic way; Excellent team working and team management skills; Good communication skills; Time management skills and capacity to adhere to strict reporting timelines by producing excellent audit reports with credible data and information; Fluency in Kinyarwanda, English and/or French, Knowledge of World Bank guidelines, social audit and reporting requirements; Experience in assessment of compliance with provisions of national regulations and involuntary Resettlement policies of the World Bank or development banks, especially those relating to consulting and involvement of PAPs, eligibility criteria for the PAPs, valuation and compensation of PAPs; Knowledge in reviewing the adequacy of institutional arrangement in implementing the resettlement; Capacity to review all necessary documents, contracts, records, list of PAPs, record of consultation of PAPs and with other stakeholders, and capture and record of grievances have been kept in accordance to established policies and legislation; Experience of physical audit of expropriated property and donated land; consult the PAPs and other stakeholders; Experience of Resettlement and Social Audit, providing recommendations /lessons learnt and correction measures/mitigations for the upcoming subprojects implementation Experience in screening of projects and preparation of resettlement instruments and implement appropriate safeguarding planning process; Practice of developing simple user manuals and training materials and train for local governments on Environmental and Social Safeguards The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 7.34 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation for IPF Project dated 2016, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Detailed REOI and Terms of Reference can be obtained on www.umucyo.gov.rw (e-procurement system) Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form through Umucyo system (e-procurement system), not later than as per e-procurement. title: Recruitment of Data Analysts Specialist
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA LOCAL ADMINISTRATIVE ENTITIES DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (LODA) B.P: 7305 Kigali, Tel: 5029, web site: www.loda.gov.rw / info@loda.gov.rw JOB ANNOUNCEMENT The Local Administrative Entities Development Agency (LODA) is a Government Agency under the supervision of MINALOC. It was established by law n°62/2013 of 27/08/2013 establishing the Local Administrative Entities Development Agency (LODA) and determining its mission, organization and functioning. LODA was established to coordinate the local development interventions of the local government's entities focusing on the Local Economic Development, Social Protection, Capacity Building of local administrative entities within the scope of LODA mission, and monitoring and evaluation of implementation process and programs in Local Administrative Entities with the view of contributing to the capacity building of population and decentralized entities as well as reducing extreme poverty in the country. In the process of fulfilling the Local Administrative Entities Development Agency (LODA)’s organizational structure as stipulated by the law establishing it, LODA hereby invites competent candidates who meet the requirements as stated below to apply for the following posts: Job Position 1: Data Analyst Level: 00.I Reports to: Coordinator of Social protection, SPIU Number of Position: 1 1.1 and responsibilities: Assist in the design of data collection tools to provide LODA management with systematic and robust data to support social protection planning, monitoring and evaluation; Assist in the preparation of guidelines to support data collection, including detailed training materials, which will be delivered by the Data Analyst directly and be used for “Train the Trainers” approach; Design development and application of tools and techniques to ensure quality data for SSPP: NSDS and CRVS databases, among others; Provide inputs to define the appropriate performance indicators based on the analyzed data, in order to achieve the objectives of the project; Responsible for a strategic oversight of compiling and visualizing statistical information to allow for easy interpretation of data and distilling insights related to social protection and nutrition programs; Make analysis and interpretation of such data to support program management and effective monitoring; Distill and contribute statistical and other analysis for presentation in graphical or tabular form, including statistical data for situational reports, periodical reports or any other reports required to be produced by the client or stakeholders; Contribute to the design of databases and management information systems; Support the World Bank missions to review the project by participation in field missions and preparation of reports and analysis. 1.2 Key Selection Criteria Advanced degree (A0) in statistics, Applied mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information and Communication Technology, Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering; A minimum of 5 years of experience in social-economic large data management and analysis; Deep understanding of various research methodologies and statistics concepts; Knowledge of various statistical and data visualization software packages, excellent knowledge of Excel; Preferable experience working in the public sector, particularly in social protection and/or health programs; Knowledge of data modelling, data cleansing, and data enrichment techniques; Excellent writing skills, and ability to “tell the story with data”; Proven ability to prepare statistical and technical reports for publication; Knowledge of the theory, systems and application of statistical research methodology; Excellent project management and organizational skills; High level of concentration and attention to detail; High level communication skills, experience in the design and delivery of training Time management Skills; Team working Skills; Fluent in Kinyarwanda and English, knowledge of French is an added advantage. HOW TO APPLY: The interested applicants who meet the above recruitment requirements should submit an electronic job application form using online E-recruitment process together with scanned copies of a relevant academic degree and a national Identity Card not later than …………/……./2018. Done at Kigali on ……./……./2018 Laetitia NKUNDA Director General

title: Hiring  a  consultancy firm to carry out  feasibility study for  construction works of  two roads in Karongi and  Kirehe  Districts
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FROM CONSULTANCY FIRMS Country : REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Project: SOCIO-ECONOMIC INCLUSION OF REFUGEES AND HOST COMMUNITIES PROJECT (JYAMBERE PROJECT) Credit No : D 64040-RWA Project ID : P164130 TITLE OF THE TENDER : HIRING A CONSULTANCY FIRM TO CARRY OUT FEASIBILITY STUDY FOR CONSTRUCTION WORKS OF TWO ROADS IN KARONGI AND KIREHE DISTRICTS Reference: RW-MINEMA-159488-CS-QCBS (STEP) be replaced by the Ref in e- Procurement System The Government of Rwanda under the Ministry in Charge of Emergency Management (MINEMA) (hereinafter called “Client”) wishes to apply the world bank funds to be used in upgrading of the two roads located in Karongi and Kirehe district to link the refugee camps with the economic opportunities areas. The construction and upgrading works of roads require the preparation of the subject of the consultancy firm to ensure that the implementation of activities are complying with the national and world bank safeguards policies and regulations, then MINEMA is going to “hiring a consultancy firm to undertake the feasibility study, environmental and social impact assessment and resettlement action plan for Rusozi-Mahama-Mpanga-Kabuye road (67 km) in Kirehe District and Kibuye-Karongi-Uwisumo-Gisovu road (43 km) in Karongi District”. The Client intends to apply a portion of the funds to eligible payments under the contract for which this EOI is issued. The consultancy services include but not limit to the following: Conduct the feasibility study of 110 km of the proposed paved road works in Karongi and Kirehe districts from an Engineering surveys including traffic count survey, alignment survey, road inventory survey and socio-economic perspective, including the assessment of the environmental and social impacts, prepare the Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) and to prepare the relevant required documents including two separate tender documents for each works execution. The consultancy firm shall look into the benefits of the road upgrading in terms of facilitating the entry of different modes of transportation. The assignment includes intensive field surveys, consultations with the local authorities and key stakeholders, preliminary concept design, preliminary cost estimates and economic evaluation. Conduct the feasibility study with social economic analysis, preliminarily design, technical specification and cost estimates for upgrading works of Rusozi-Mahama -Mpanga -Kabuye Nasho road (67 Km) in Kirehe District and Kibuye-Karongi-Uwisumo-Gisovu road (43 Km) in Karongi District; Preparation of ESIA/ESMP and RAP to guide the implementation processes, the documents are to be prepared in line with the WB environmental and social safeguard policies, the project Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF); Preparation of bidding documents for two roads works execution; Develop the ToRs for monitoring/supervision consultant for Design, Build, Maintain’ phases (DBM)/Output and Performance-based Road Contracts (OPRC) in line with the WB procurement Regulations. The assignment is divided into: Part A: Feasibility study of the two roads Part B. Preparation of ESIA/ESMP and RAP The detailed scope on the services can be found in the Terms of Reference (ToRs) herein attached in e-procurement system. The Ministry in charge of Emergency Management (MINEMA) now solicits expression of interest from the interested consulting firms to provide the above mentioned services. Interested Consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: The Consultancy firm shall have at least seven (7) years of general working experience in conducting feasibility study for rural roads construction with at least three (3) successfully completed assignments; Experience in rural and low volume roads design and bidding document preparation; Experience in preparation of ESIA and RAP for roads construction projects. Experience with Word Bank funded projects will be an advantage; Firm’s eligibility documents such as evidence of business registration/Trading license of the consulting firm and membership certificates from professional bodies for the firm and for the key personnel as required in ToRs. The key experts to conduct the ESIA/ESMP and RAP shall be a member of RAPEP (Rwanda Association of Professional Environmental Practitioners) or affiliated to an international institution for Environmental and social studies; The technical and managerial organization of the firm. (Provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications and number of key staff. Do not provide CV of staff); Availability of experienced personnel as per the ToRs. The consultancy firm will be selected under Quality Cost Based Selection method and procedures described in the Request for Expressions of interest in accordance with the paragraph 3.14 and 3.17 of the World Bank procurement regulations for IPF Borrowers, July 2016, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and the National Public Procurement Law . Bidding will be conducted through Open International Competitive Bidding and participation is open on equal conditions to all interested consultancy firms. The Terms of Reference containing detailed requirements and conditions for participation may be obtained from E-procurement system (www.umucyo.gov.rw), free of charge. Note: The consultancy firm must attach the certificates of completion for each reference of experience required and membership certificates from professional bodies for both consulting firm and key personnel. The consultancy firm shall provide a description of similar assignment executed. The consultancy firm(s) may associate with others firms in the form a joint venture to enhance the capacity to perform the assignment. This association should be indicated clearly in the expression for interest. For the skills and technology transfer, the international consultancy firms are encouraged to associate with local consultancy firms. Enquiries regarding this tender may be addressed only through the e-Procurement system (use the request for clarification button). Any clarification may be requested by writing using the procurement system before the fixed deadline for the submission of the expression of interest. All interested firms are requested to submit their Expression of Interest via E-procurement system (www.umucyo.gov.rw) before 01/04/2020 at 09:00 am local time. Any submission of expression of interest via other channels apart from the indicated above shall not be considered. KAYUMBA Olivier Permanent Secretary

title: Public awareness campain
notice_text: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) FOR THE SERVICES OF A 360 DEGREES PR AND CREATIVE AGENCY 1.0. Background The Renewable Energy Fund (REF) project was approved by the World Bank Board in June 2017. The objective of the REF project is to increase electricity access in Rwanda through off-grid technologies and facilitate private sector participation in renewable off-grid electrification. The REF project will be administered by the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD) and will provide access to local currency financing through three financing windows: (a) Window 1 – On-lending through SACCOs to households and micro-enterprises for purchasing Tier 1 and above solar systems; (b) Window 2 – On-lending through banks (commercial and microfinance) to households and small and medium enterprises (SMEs); and (c) Window 3 – Direct financing of mini-grid developers. Out of 2.5 million Rwandan households, 1.9 million are off the grid. These households rely on kerosene lamps, candles, torches, and wood fires for lighting. The REF project is aligned with the Rural Electrification Strategy (RES, 2016) whose objective is to ensure that 70% of Rwandans have access to electricity by 2018 and 100% by 2020. To achieve these targets, there is need to, among other programs, establish mechanisms to allow low-income households to access modern energy services through basic solar system, as well as to target the private sector such that solar products are made available on financial terms that are affordable to the Rwandan population. A technical assistance in form of an awareness campaign is necessary to sensitize the end user public as well as stakeholders to boost uptake of this project. Considering the early stages of development of the off-grid market in Rwanda, coupled with the ambitious objectives and design of the REF project involving wholesale and direct lending across multiple participating entities under three financing windows, BRD seeks to engage the services of a 360 degrees PR and Creative Agency to work closely and assist the PIU of the REF project. 2.0. Objective The objective of this Technical Assistance (TA) is to conduct a top-of-the mind awareness campaign on the REF in order to motivate and appeal to the end user public and stakeholders, educating consumers on the benefits and opportunities from off-grid electricity services (e.g., standalone solar systems and/or mini-grids), and on the benefits from quality-verified solar systems which will help communities make informed purchasing decisions. The Agency will also educate the target beneficiaries on the processes and requirements for accessing the local currency lending via the relevant financing windows. 3.0. Scope of services The primary responsibility of the Agency is to support the PIU to ensure there is timely, relevant, and up-to-date communication services to targeted stakeholders. The Agency will provide the necessary training and updates to the PIU to build institutional capacity and ensure the timely and effective delivery of the project’s awareness objectives as guided by the M&E framework. Specifically, the Agency shall undertake the following functions and duties but not limited to; Prepare complete brand and marketing strategy, develop creative ideas and production for relevant communication channels, including above the line and below the line activities. Campaigns will be carried out in English & Kinyarwanda and any other languages for various media as per the relevant target group and the requirements of BRD from time to time. The Agency should have access to local language experts proficient in regional languages. Based on a study of the target stakeholders, the Agency will provide a proposed plan of strategic and tactical activities which will enable the project to communicate effectively towards the delivery of project objectives. The Agency will identify priority localities, communication channels, and key messages to increase awareness on the benefits and opportunities from off-grid electricity services and on the benefits from quality-verified solar systems. The Agency will describe, plan, and quantify media and non-media activities. The Agency will also propose tools to measure the effectiveness of the communication campaign. To achieve the above therefore, the key outcomes to be delivered by the Agency are: Brand Creation Visual identity harmonization of REF financing products; Creating names and identity for the REF; Establish the brand architecture/ positioning / language / message / tone / promise and identity / that will be common across the organization and externally for campaigns; Creating semiotic approach for the brands through formulation of brand manual. Formulate creative positioning for all mediums of communication. Outreach and awareness Campaign The agency will be responsible for developing a 360-degree outreach campaign for the REF and its financing products, as well as awareness campaign on the benefits and opportunities from off-grid electricity services (e.g., standalone solar systems and mini-grids) and on the benefits from quality-verified solar systems. The planning will include concept development, designing the campaign, implementation of campaign, etc.; The Agency will be responsible to share their analysis (domestic/international) about payments/non-payments market scenario, growth trends and insights, consumer trends/patterns – which messages/method acts as a motivator and which does not, a presentation on case study on top international campaigns and the effectiveness of the campaigns; Public Service Announcements (PSAs) – draft 30 second PSAs and distribute to area radio stations, secure runs; Ad Space – coordinate with publications for potential free ads/remnant space; Coordinate with the PIU of the REF Project and other Stakeholders as needed; Offer consistent communications while pushing out a campaign on what makes the products so invaluable. Regional adaptation of creative content across all communication channels; Public Relations; Facilitate drafting & distribution of all press releases, media announcements, etc. Coordinate media attendance and management at events; Manage and act on all publicity opportunities such as community events, holidays, editorial calendars, etc. Monitor all media coverage of the products and related topics. Potentially implement social media for the campaign. Pitching – personally contacting editors & reporters for coverage based on their editorial calendars or a specific event/topic. News-Press Editorial Board – facilitate meeting with boards and relevant orgs /or publishing editorial features in relevant publications, event attendance/coverage. Press Release(s) - include selected messaging in all of the material (branding). Be the media liaison and keeping all relevant information organized. Meetings, conference or phone calls, etc 4.0. Shortlisting criteria Demonstration of at least three similar assignments proven by reference letters of successful completion indicating nature, type, and scope executed in the past five years (2017, 2016, 2015, 2014, 2013). In providing evidence of the similar assignments executed, the firm must indicate the scope of services executed, and value of the consultancy services, status of the assignment, and details of the client including client’s full name, physical address, telephone contacts, and email address, and written consent authorizing BRD to request feedback from the listed clients. Availability of appropriate skills/expertise among the Agency’s staff including expertise in: Socio-economic research and development, Project planning and market research, Strategic advisory services, Advertising, Marketing, Creative and PR, off grid electricity, etc. Experience of at least one (1) related assignment in Sub-Saharan Africa in similar campaigns in other off-grid solar markets in the region (e.g., Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia, etc.); Experience of at least one (1) related assignment in Rwanda with a similar institution will be an added advantage. title: Capacity building of SACCOs
notice_text: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) FOR A CONSULTING FIRM TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO SACCOs 1. Background The Renewable Energy Fund (REF) project was approved by the World Bank Board in June 2017. The objective of the REF project is to increase electricity access in Rwanda through off-grid technologies and facilitate private sector participation in renewable off-grid electrification. The REF project will be administered by the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD) and will provide access to local currency financing through three financing windows: (a) Window 1 – On-lending through SACCOs to households and micro-enterprises for purchasing Tier 1 and above solar systems; (b) Window 2 – On-lending through banks (commercial and microfinance) to households and small and medium enterprises (SMEs); and (c) Window 3 – Direct financing of mini-grid developers. SACCOs are expected to play a critically important role in stimulating the development of the off-grid sector. However, SACCOs have little experience in issuing loans for solar products due to lack of understanding of the solar market and technologies, as well as long-term finance constraints. SACCOs do not currently have technical expertise to work with solar suppliers to create solar lending programs on a large scale. The REF project was launched with only 20 SACCOs prequalified to access funding through Window 1, but considering the growing demand for solar home systems in rural areas, it is anticipated that additional SACCOs will be prequalified to participate in the project. SACCOs will enter into Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with one or multiple solar suppliers to coordinate their energy lending, disbursement, and customer service processes. The World Bank will appraise and prequalify eligible solar suppliers to participate in the REF project to install, provide warranty and after sales service of solar products meeting Lighting Global Quality Standards and offering Tier 1 and above access level. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION) Rwanda Feeder Roads Development Project (RFRDP) IDA Credit nº: 5405-RW Project ID: P126498 Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy to develop the feeder roads development strategy . Reference No .: FRDP/0315/S The Government of Rwanda (GOR) has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) and intends to apply a portion of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services ("the Services") include the following key tasks: To develop the national feeder roads policy that is geared towards the creation of all-weather access rural communities. The feeder roads are expected to be economically efficient, and will aid in the development of social as well as business services. This shall be done after careful analysis of all national existing policies and strategies for the roads sector. To develop a comprehensive national feeder roads development strategy and action plan/program that provides the framework for privatization of investments, maintenance of feeder roads, and defining the institutional and financial arrangements to implement the strategy. The assignment will take approximately 140 calendar days. Rwanda Feeder Roads Development Project now invites eligible Individual Consultants ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Eligible consulting firms are also invited tosubmit expressions of interest for a member of their technical team who fulfill the requirements. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience toperform the services. The short listing criteria are: The Individual Consultant should have a Masters' degree in Transport Economics or related field from a recognized university He/She should have a at least 15 years international expertise in road/transport field He/She should have a proven experience in preparation of roads policy and strategy documents Must have prepared at least two (2) policy and strategy documents related to the feeder roads transport sector. Proven experience in linking central and local government institutions to meet strategic development objectives demonstrating good knowledge of decentralized form of transport sector governance since in Rwanda the Districts are responsible to manage feeder roads Fluency in English is required and French language will be an added advantage An understandingof the challenges faced by public organizations in identifying and preparing quality programs and projects in the transport sector The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers ( January 2011 ) ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. title: Request for Expression of interest for hiring an Individual Consultant for the Supervision of Construction Works for Nyakagezi (Gatsibo-08) Hillside Irrigation Scheme, in Gatsibo District, Eastern province.

notice_text: REF. N O : 205/S/013/LWH SUBJECT : Request for Expression of interest for hiring an Individual Consultant for the Supervision of Construction Works for Nyakagezi (Gatsibo-08) Hillside Irrigation Scheme, in Gatsibo District, Easternprovince. Background The Government of Rwanda (GoR) represented by the Ministry of Agricultureand Animal Resources (MINAGRI) has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) for the implementation of Land husbandry, Water harvesting and Hillside irrigation Project (LWH). The project supports and promotes horticulture especially in irrigated areas. The aim of the project is to increase the production and commercialization of crops in target areas. The Project envisions the production of high-value (organic) horticultural crops with the strongest marketing potential on irrigated portions of hillsides of the watershed. It is in this regard that the Project will invest in water harvesting and irrigation infrastructure at the Nyakagezi site in Gatsibo District. The works do not include a dam but will utilize a combination of groundwater and stream flows to irrigate a newly designed hillside irrigation system with a gross command areas of 56ha (45ha net). The Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI) intends to apply part of the proceeds for the recruitment of an Individual Consultant for supervision of construction works. Brief description of nature of construction works: The works for the water harvesting and storage portion of the project includes construction of a groundwater collection system, a stream diversion weir, and a night storage reservoir. The irrigation system is a fully piped distribution network which includes PVC main and secondary pipelines with tertiary outlet hydrants. The groundwater harvesting system with a subsurface drainage collector pipe parallel to the stream, and secondary drain pipes perpendicular to the stream will be constructedfirst during the first 4 months of the project. Duties and responsibility of theIndividual Construction Supervisor Consultant: 1.1 Supervision of works: The Consultant shall supervise the construction works, erection and commissioning activities to ensure compliance with the contract drawings, specifications and recognized international standards. This shall include, but not be limited to, the following: a) Issuance of written Order to Commence as approved by LWH Project. b) Review and check the completeness of the design report, drawings, specifications, and bill of quantities. c) Approval of the contractor's authorized representative and key personnel on site and monitoring of their performance. d) Review, for conformance with the specifications, the Contractor's proposed site layout, camp facilities, construction roads, stream crossings, water supply, latrines and miscellaneous site facilities and temporary works. e) Review of the overall construction program, including detailed subprograms for construction, manufacturing, shipping, drawing submittals, etc., and their periodically updated versions according to mechanismsprovided in the Contract. f) Review and approve the manufacturer's designs, specifications, fabrication and shop drawings, civil design loads and analysis…etc for all mechanical works. g) Check and establish that the Contractor mobilizes and supplies to the site, all materials, equipment and machinery that have been committedin its bid, and ensure that all such items remain on site until their release has been authorized. Ensure that the Contractor properly records all equipment, materials and labor which have been supplied under the Works Contract, and keep and regularly update lists of the Contractor's equipment (and its condition) and personnel on site. h) Examination of the Contractor's Monthly Statements and preparation and issuance of Payment Certificates. i) Management and Preparation of Variation Orders, estimation of the cost of the variations, negotiation of prices with the Contractor's, and issuing of the Variation Orders, after obtaining approval from LWH Project. j) Evaluation and documentation of claims submitted by the Contractor, such as for extension of time, additional compensation, extra work or expenses. Attend claims meetings between MINAGRI/LWH and the contractor. The Consultant shall evaluateand respond, in timely fashion, to all claims, after consultation with LWH Project. k) Inspection of construction activities, site installations and infrastructure, management of temporary material dumps, spoil dumps, aggregate and concrete production, etc. l) Ensure that the Works are executed in accordance with the drawings and that the quality of workmanship and materials is in compliance with the technical specifications. m) Carry out design changes if necessary during construction (for unforeseen conditions during the feasibility and detail design stage) and issue construction drawings and related specifications to the Contractor in compliance with the provisions of the Contract Documents. n) Maintaining record of visits to site and meetings held; details of equipment standing or lost time; and any other matters affecting the progress or cost of the works. o) Inform the LWH project team about problems or potential problems, which may arise in connection with the Works Contract and make recommendations for possible solutions. p) Provide timely assistance and direction to the Contractor in all matters related to the interpretation or clarification of the Works Contract,ground survey controls, quality control testing and other matters related toWorks Contract compliance and progress of the Works; and ensure prompt responses when the Contractor calls for inspections and approvals. q) Ensure environmental protection measures are implemented to mitigate the impacts of construction and ensure health and safety regulations are complied with on site. r) Upon provisional completion of the works, carry out the necessary inspection, specify and supervise any remedial works to be carried out and, upon completion of remedial works, propose to LWH a date for a joint inspection, prior to the issuance of the Certificate of Completion. s) Approve the removal of Contractor's equipment, temporary structures and materials. t) Preparation of general record drawings for use in the Project Completion Report to supplement the As-built drawings prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Consultant. 1.2 Quality control of construction materials during execution of the works The Individual Consultant shall be fully responsible to insure quality control of construction materials as he carries out the following duties: a) Monitoring, for compliance with the specifications, of borrow and quarry operations to produce suitable materials. b) Sampling and testing of construction materials including fill materials, concrete, concrete aggregate from various sources, and cement of various types from different mills for concrete, mortar and grout. c) Review and approve mix designs for concrete, mortar and grout for all uses and placement conditions. d) Monitoring of concrete, mortar and grout batching operation and calibration. e) Update and improve the Operation and Maintenance Plan to guide the Water User's Association and LWH Project staff for operation and maintenance of the entire system. 1.3 Requirements for reporting In performing his duties, the Consultant shall submit to the Client the following reports (and others as may be required during the course of the Project): a) Implementation Program for Construction Work (2 hard copies & a soft copy). b) Monthly Progress Report, to be submitted latest by the first week of the subsequent month (2 hard copies & a soft copy). c) Draft Completion Report to be submitted before provisional inspection by Client (2 hard copies & a soft copy). d) Draft updated Operation and Maintenance Plan to be submitted before provisional inspection by Client (2 hard copies & a soft copy). e) Final Completion Report with all As-built Drawings to be submitted after final inspection by Client (4 hard copies & a soft copy). f) Updated Operation and Maintenance Plan to be submitted together with the Final Completion Report (4 hard copies & a soft copy). g) These reports and documents will be reviewed and approved by the Client. The reports will be reviewed and approved in a maximumperiod of 30 days. 1.4 Qualifications and experience required: The Consultant shall have the following minimum qualifications: a) B.Sc. degree in Civil engineering or related fields b) 10 years of relevant experience in construction works with at least 4 years in irrigation projects or other projects with hydraulic structures and pipelines c) Speak and write English well (knowledge of French will be an advantage); possess reporting and writing skills. 1.5 Duration of services: The expected time of this service is ten (10) months . The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers ( January 2011 ) (" Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with section 5 ( Selection of Individual Consultants )set out in the Consultant Guidelines. title: Hiring a consultancy firm to develop a horticulture and agribusiness database in Rwanda Development Board
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY PO.BOX 73 KIGALI RE-ADVERTISEMENT REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST COUNTRY: RWANDA NAME OF PROJECT: Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance (G4C TA) Project Credit: 65351 – RW Assignment Title: Hiring a consultancyfirm to develop a horticulture and agribusiness database in Rwanda Development Board Reference No : 005/S/SPIU/G4CTA-IDA/MINICOM/2013-2014 1. Background The Government of the Rwanda (GoR) through the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MINICOM) has received funds from the World Bank toward the cost of the Government for Competitive Technical Assistance Project (G4C TA), and through the Single Project Implementation Unit, an implementing agency of the Client, intends to apply part of the proceeds for the consulting services for a firm to develop a horticulture and agribusiness database in Rwanda Development Board. The assignment will be carried out in Rwanda and the consultant will develop an interactive database of horticulture and agribusinesssectors to help RDB and NAEB provide information to investors. 2. Objectives The overarching objective of this assignment is to develop an interactive database of horticulture and agribusiness sectors to help RDB and NAEB provide information to investors. Specifically, the Consultancy Firm shall: · Develop an interactive database that provides qualitative and quantitative data for investment promotion particularly for Horticulture cluster. · Develop an interactive database with qualitative and quantitative data for agribusiness investment promotion in general. 3. S cope of the services This data base will help RDB to provide information to investors in its day to day investment promotion work. The database is to be interactive and is to contain links to primary sources of information. There shall be 2 levels of access: general and member-only The proposed Agribusiness Database shall include various types of information sets, 'Quantitative' and 'Qualitative' and audio/visual. More specifically the database is to be created with the following coverage: Sub-sectors of horticulture and agribusiness; Horticulture subsectors is to include flowers and ornamental plants , fruits, vegetables and condiments and manufacturing industries including by-products; Agribusiness is to include tea, coffee, grains, cereals, oil seeds, beverages, dairy, meat, fisheries and poultry subsectors as well as promising new ventures such as beekeeping, stevia or other medicinal crops; Geographical scope for including the data is to include all five provinces (Kigali City, Northern Province, Western Province, Southern Province, and Eastern Province) as well as selected markets. 4. D uration of the Consultancy It shall be anticipated that the period of performance of this assignment shall be 40 workman days. 5 . Profile of the Firm The consultancy firm should have proven successful experience in economic data collecting and processing. Having done 2 similar assignments in Rwanda, EAC region or elsewhere. The firm should have 4 years' experience in database development. The firm should be able to mobilize a team of experts with a team leader and others experts. 6. Profile of the lead consultant Economist/Statistician. - A Master's degree in agricultural economics, business administration, statistics social sciences or related field. - At least 5-8 years' experience in value chain analysis, international trade analysis, database development, marketing and/or farming system analysis; Profile of other consultants (i) Three (3) enumerators/Data Feeding Associates; - A bachelor's degree in rural development, business administration, agriculture or social sciences or related field. - At least 3 years' experience in data collection/surveys/studies using participatory tools, with a background in data feeding and analysis. (ii) Database Expert. - Bachelor's degree in Information Technology - At least 3 years of experience in database design - Excellent English writing and speaking ability is required for all consultants. Fluency in French will be an advantage. - Thecandidates should have demonstrated capacity to communicate complex policy, strategy, and program issues both verbally and writing in a clear, concise, and well-organized manner. - Knowledge of participatory appraisal is essential. Skills in the use of MS Office are also essential. The consultant should be able to travel extensively withincountry. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: The shortlisting criteria are: (a) Experience in economic data collecting and processing, (b) Having done 2 similar assignments in Rwanda, EAC region or elsewhere, (c) Experience in database development, (d) Availability of qualified and skilled personnel for the assignment such as; Economist/Statistician, Enumerators/Data Feeding Associates and Database Expert. title: RECRUITMENT OF A CONSULTANCY FIRM TO PROVIDE TECHINCAL SUPPORT TO HORTICULTURE COOPERATIVES IN PROPER INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT IN RWANDA
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY PO.BOX 73 KIGALI Kigali, 2 nd August 2013 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST COUNTRY: RWANDA NAME OFPROJECT: Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance (G4C TA) Project Credit No.: 65351 – RW Assignment Title: RECRUITMENT OF A CONSULTANCY FIRM TO PROVIDE TECHINCAL SUPPORTTO HORTICULTURE COOPERATIVES IN PROPER INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT IN RWANDA Reference No .: 006/S/SPIU/G4CTA-IDA/MINICOM/2013-2014 1. Background The Government of the Republic of Rwanda (GoR) through the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MINICOM) has received funds from the World Bank toward the cost of Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance Project (G4C TA), and through the Single Project Implementation Unit, an implementing agency of the Client, intends to apply part of the proceeds for the consulting services fora firm to provide technical support to horticulture cooperatives in proper integrated management in Rwanda . The Rwanda horticulture sector accounts around 300 cooperatives, but many more unorganized farmers are also found in horticulture production for long time due to different challenges facing this sector. This constitutes a very big disadvantage in termsof input distribution, marketing, coordination at national level and above allraises not only cost of certification but lack of market access and uncontrollable horticultural products' prices which lead to the low profitability for farmers. For this reason the G4C project funded by the World Bank will fund a technical assistance to hire a firm/service provider to assist Horticulture cooperatives with aim of organizing and creating national Horticulture cooperatives, unions and a national Horticulture cooperatives federation . 2. Objective The objective is to support cooperatives working in Horticulture by assisting them to better organize themselves, accompany associations/organizations, temporary agreed cooperatives into the process of becoming nationally recognized as horticultural cooperatives, create their cooperative unions and federation which will help them proper management and better organized chain and market linkages . 3. SCOPE OF THE SERVICES The firm /service provider will work with Horticulture cooperatives and specific tasks are the following: · Organizationaldiagnostic of horticulture cooperatives. This will be in terms of directions, levelof competence, administrative procedure, organizational structure, functions and decision making process, financial situation and operations management including business incubation . · Make an exploration of possibilities and challenges of Horticulture cooperative systems in order to identify their potentialities or opportunities in Rwanda. · Training Horticulture cooperatives in management and leadership which will bring the excellent impact in proper management. · Analyze factors that contribute to success of Horticulture cooperatives and market access. · Help cooperatives in Horticulture all over country to join cooperativestructure for setting up their federation which will be an apex at national level and follow up the organization and management of Horticulture cooperatives. 4. Duration The assignmentis expected to last 6 months. 5. Profile of the Firm NAEB is looking for services of an experienced Consulting firm with experience in transforming horticultural organizations, association, and temporarily recognized cooperatives into strong, well-managed and operational cooperative unions and national federation. The following criteria will be considered to be selected; · A firm with experience in similar or related assignments especially organization/ setting up farmers 'cooperatives unions and federations · Experts' qualifications and their relevant experiences in similar assignments · Overall qualification of firm team members will be taken into consideration in selecting a firm to conduct an assignment. Qualifications and experience A) Team leader · Team leader with proven experience in cooperative and federation management and capacity building in agricultural cooperatives, holding at least a Master's degree in policy analysis, agricultural economist, agribusiness, socio economist or related qualifications in managementof cooperatives with 4 years' experience or Bachelor's degree with extensive experience of seven years in horticulture cooperatives in Rwanda or the region. · A strong knowledge of cooperatives movement, especially cooperative structure and formation requirementsin EAC region having a relevant experience in Rwanda would be an added advantage · Communication and facilitation; participatory planning processes and organizational and institutional development; · Agricultural production systems and integrated rural development/community development; and · Proven track record of experience in developing of micro-enterprises, SMEs, cooperatives and familiarity with cooperative structure and formation requirements Rwandan context. · Knowledge and experience of current issues relating to cooperative development and requirements · Good analytical skills and an ability to provide practical and sound advice on rural development issues · Proven experience to work with various stakeholders in cooperatives like RCA, MINAGRI, MINICOM, etc. · Proven experience of 2 years minimum in training of cooperatives in leadership and management, · Proven capacities to work in English and Kinyarwanda, · Excellent communications skills with ability to express ideas clearly, logically and effectively, both orally and in writing, · Proven experience on support/ creation of cooperative unions and federations · Proven experience in similar assignments, · Knowledge of Rwandan Agricultural sector and the NAEB mandates, mission and responsibilities is an added advantage. B) Team Members At least 3 team members with relevant qualification in sociology, agribusiness/Agri-economist and business administration with a relevant experience of 2 years working with cooperatives to ensure achieving the following deliverables: · Increase capacity building that lead to organization of unions and federation and developing a sustainabilityplan for the namely created unions and federations. · Cooperative organization and covering governance issues relating Horticulture cooperatives · Trainings in proper management and market linkages for cooperative members/leaders · Facilitate registration procedures of created unions and federation.
