RECRUITMENT OF A CONSULTANCY FIRM TO ENHANCE 
STAFF RETENTION AND HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT 
IN THE RWANDA PUBLIC SERVICE
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY PO.BOX 73 KIGALI Kigali, 28 th June 2013 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTANTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) COUNTRY: RWANDA NAME OF PROJECT: Governance forCompetitiveness Technical Assistance (G4C TA) Project Credit No.: 65351 – RW Assignment Title: RECRUITMENT OF A CONSULTANCY FIRM TO ENHANCE STAFF RETENTION AND HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN THE RWANDA PUBLIC SERVICE Reference No .: 027/S/SPIU/G4CTA-IDA/MINICOM/2013 The Government of the Rwanda (GoR) through the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MINICOM) has received funds from the World Bank toward the cost of the Government for Competitive Technical Assistance Project (G4C TA), and through the Single Project Implementation Unit, an implementing agency of the Client, intends to apply part of the proceeds for the consulting services for a firm to enhance staff retention and human resource management in the Rwanda Public Service . The consultancy services will ensure amongst that a competency framework,that is non-existent in Rwanda, is developed and implemented in priority institutions coupled with appropriate job descriptions for better management of competences. The career development prospects in the targeted sectors will also have to be considered as part of attraction and retention factors. In the same vein, the Pay and Retention policy will be implemented in priority institutions. While the Pay and Retention policy lays a foundation for a number of aspects that would significantly improve institutional capacity to attract and retain competent employees, much of this policy still needs to materialize beyond the pay aspect. It is this context that retention aspects will be focusedon during the implementation of this assignment to come up with working and practical retention schemes and provide government with adequate and appropriate mechanisms to enhance its capacity to retain competent civil servants. The consolidation of these aspects to improve capacity of priority institutions is anchored on the effective implementation of the Human Resource Management best practices from both the HRM policy under development and from international best practices and standards. 1. Objective The overall objective of the assignment is to enhance the capacity of priority institutions to attract and retain competentemployees with the requisite skills and experience to increase the capacity of the priority institutions to enable them to influence greater competitiveness and achieve Rwanda Government development aspirations. The project will be working in priority institutions responsible for horticulture, tourism and energy sectors namely NAEB,RDB and MININFRA as pilot institutions and MINICOM ensuring the project coordination since competitiveness, which is the ultimate goal of the project is under its responsibility. 1.1. Specific objectives v To develop the competency framework to be piloted in priority institutions in order to streamline the competency management, v To develop in priority institutions the role profiles/job profiles, job descriptions and appropriate job evaluation and ultimately career development plans for a more modernized human resource management, v To propose and develop an appropriate retention programs and schemes to be implemented as a pilot in priority institutions to help curb the current turnover in Rwanda Public Service in general and particularly in priority institutions, v To propose and develop an appropriate HRM strengthening programs and procedures (including trainings for HR Managers) for enhancement of the strategic HRM functions in the institutions and consolidation of the impact of professional human resource management and, v To collaborate with the Ministry of Public Service and Labour and in synergy with other components of Governance for Competitiveness project, ensure that priority institutions are endowed with organizational structures that fit their mandate andenabling to deliver on Government expectations. 2. Profile of the Firm The potential service provider shall demonstrate a minimum of 10 years of experience in similar assignments in the area of public sector management with a focus on public service reform; human resources management and development; organizational analysis and development; public administration; public sector policy and institutional development. Given the nature of the tasks covered under these ToRs, there is a need to assemble a team of consultants with complementary skills. Work experience in Rwanda and/or in the Eastern Africa region is preferred as is familiarity with public sector management. The consultancy firm will be invited to use a combination of skills which should be comprised of the following key staff: · A Team leader who is an International Expert with proven experience in public sector management holding at least a Master's degree in Human Resources Management, Public Administration, Labor Economics, Organizational Analysis and Development, Public Policy with a minimumof 10 years of public service management expertise. In additional to the above skills of the team leader, he/she should have demonstrated higher skills in human management and experience in organizational structure, Human Resource Planning/Capacity Audit/Organizational Development/Labour Market/Public Administration and/or Public Service Reform issues and strategies. He/ she should have experience in providing coaching and mentoring services in the aforementioned areas; · Three consultants holding at least a Master's degree: 1. Competency framework: Master's degree in Human resources management with a minimum of 10 years of experience in public sector management and public administration. S/he should demonstrate a proven track record and extensive experience in strengthening performance management and designing competency frameworks in the public service ideally in developing country contexts; 2. Career development: Master's degree in public administration or policy or a related area with a minimum of 7 years of experience in public sector management and public administration. S/he should demonstrate a proven and remarkable experience in career development and development of job profile, job descriptions and job evaluation in a developing country context; 3. Capacity building: Master's degree in human resources managementor related area, with a minimum of 7 years of experience in public service management, public administration and organizational analysis and development. S/he should demonstrate a proven track record and remarkable experience in publicsector capacity building. · The firm will require to include, in the team, at least one national consultant to ensure that the knowledge and competencies are transferred to local experts; · For the required professional language, full proficiency in English for everykey person is required; speaking French is an advantage; · The team leader will have to stay in the country to oversee/supervise all activities which will be implemented and ensure that they are well implemented. title: Recruitment of an International Consultant to perform a highly specialized and Rare Skill Audit in the Rwanda Public Service
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY PO.BOX 73 KIGALI Kigali, 26 th April 2013 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTANTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) COUNTRY: RWANDA NAME OF PROJECT: Governancefor Competitiveness Technical Assistance (G4C TA) Project Credit: 65351 – RW Assignment Title: Recruitment of an International Consultant to perform a highly specialized and Rare Skill Audit in theRwanda Public Service Reference No .: 022/S/SPIU/G4CTA -IDA/ MINICOM 2012-2013 1. BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT The Government of Rwanda accords the importance to improve the performance of the public sector. The Government hasdefined its development agenda through the Vision 2020 and EDPRS which are anchored to achievement of the MDGs. However, in order to achieve these development aspirations there is need to have the required capacity in the public sector. The enabling environment to enhance efficiency and effectiveness of Rwanda public sector lies mostly with the public service whichtherefore requires a special focus on its management. In this spirit,the Government of Rwanda through the Ministry of Public Service and Labour (MIFOTRA) has undertaken a series of transformational activitiesin the area of Public Service Management to institutionalize and harmonize the best practices utmost covering the main aspects of the Public Service Management. Given the importance of those issues, the Government of Rwanda received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of financing a Public Sector Capacity Building Project (PSCBP). This included a major component supporting "Civil Service Reforms" that has been used to establish a basis to address the above issues, particularly with the development of Rwanda Public Service Pay and Retention policy but on the other hand it has also highlightedfurther areas to attend to for expected Rwanda Public Service capacity. In the above context, the new vision of the reform in Rwanda is to have a public service enhanced in its human and organizational capacity in order to deliver improved public services for the achievement of the broad goals of national development. In support of these efforts, the Government of Rwanda has received an additional credit of $5m from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of financing a Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance Project (G4C) with its component 1 particularly focusing on Public Sector Capacity building, especially for theconsolidation of the outcomes of the Public Sector Capacity Building Project and their linkages with Private Sector development backed by capable Public Institutions. There is therefore a need to provide Government with appropriate strategic advice by identifying and mapping out the scarce and highly specialised skills required for development actions with the overall aim of at achieving sufficiently skilled, competent, professional and motivated personnel possessing required capacities for Government efficiency and effectiveness and its ability to drive set national priorities and anticipate future development needs. Hence the need for consultancy services to guide the Government on the appropriate information in this regard. The consultancy will be financed through the Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance Project coordinated by the Ministry of Trade and Industry in conjunction with beneficiary institutions of the Ministry of Public Service and Labour,the Public Sector Capacity Building Secretariat, the National Agriculture Export Board and the Rwanda Development Board. 2. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT The overall goal of the assignment is to fast track the successful implementation of the Rwanda Public Sector Pay and Retention Policy, particularly with regard to its retention related recommendations in alignment with the Strategic Framework for Public Service Reforms (2012 – 2015). The initiative is also intended to make a positive contribution to the implementation of the (i) National Human Capacity and Skills Development Strategy which set out an overall long term framework for national skills enhancement (2010) and (ii) Critical skills five year strategy for Rwanda (2012). The main objective of this assignment is to determine the rare and highly specialised skills requirement in the Rwanda Public Service to provide the Government of Rwanda with the empirical informationto develop appropriate mechanisms to attract, utilize and retain rareand specialised skills in its Public Service. 3. S COPE OF THE SERVICES The responsibilities shall include the following: · Development of a methodology, through which the determination of the rare and highly specialised skills required will be conducted; · Conduct desk research and specificallyreview, but not limited to, the following key documents: Vision 2020;Government Seven Year Action Plan; Strategic Framework for Public Service Reforms; Human Capital and Skills Development Strategy; Critical Skills Report and Strategy; Education Sector Strategies; Annual Leadership Retreat Recommendations (2012); Local Government Capacity Building Strategy and Implementation Plan; and Strategic Capacity Building Initiative (SCBI) Implementation framework. · Consult relevant stakeholders in the public sector that include, but not limited to; Office of the Prime Minister; Ministry of Public Service and Labour (MIFOTRA); Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN); Ministry of Education (MINEDUC); Ministry of Local Government (MINALOC); Ministry of Trade and Industry (MINICOM); Ministry of Infrastructure (MININFRA); Ministry of Natural Resources (MINIRENA); Ministry of Agriculture; Rwanda DevelopmentBoard; Rwanda Governance Board (RGB); Public Sector Capacity BuildingSecretariat (PSCBS); Rwandese Association of Local Government Authorities (RALGA); and Rwanda Institute of Administration and Management (RIAM). · Consult relevant stakeholders among the development partners as advised by the Client. · Based on the above desk research and stakeholder consultations, including reference to global best practices, establish objective criteria to guide the identification of rare andspecialised skills within the Rwanda Public Service and their categorization into the following: Scarce skills refer to areas within occupations in which there is a shortage of qualified and experienced people due to unavailability of such people or these people do not meet employment criteria. Scarcity may arise due to absolute scarcity in which few people hold the necessary skills or qualifications (such as those required in a new or emerging occupation). These skills are either impossible to replace or extremely difficult to replace should they exit the sector. Absolute scarcity results in low growth and productivity of companies in the sector and the sector itself. Relative scarcity of skills pertains to skills that are difficult to attain due to geographic location, equity requirements or the lead time on attaining the necessary skills. The term "priority skills" (incorporates both scarce and critical skills) which are those skills that the sector deems as absolutely necessary at any given point in time to resolve some issue around sector skills shortages. In most cases the term also incorporates scarce skills. · Perform a mapping assessment of the existing situation and future requirement in regard to the specialized and priority skills requirement in the public service. · Based on the above, develop a practical and feasible 'Technical Recommendation Framework' that shall guide Government to form the required policies; strategies; plans and associated budgets to implement the recommendations. The assignment should recognise that Sectors are different in their rare and specialised skillneeds but share a common commitment to the national development agenda. · Facilitate the validation process of the 'Rare and Specialised Skills Technical Recommendation Framework' · Facilitate and enable transfer of skills and knowledge to a counterpart team in MIFOTRA to enable them conduct similar assignments in subsequent periods. 4. title: CONSULTANT SERVICE FOR AN INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT A STUDY ON “TRENDS AND SKILLS NEEDS FOR THE TOURISM SECTOR IN        RWANDA.”
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY PO.BOX 73 KIGALI Kigali, 22 th February 2013 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTANTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) COUNTRY: RWANDA NAME OF PROJECT: Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance (G4C TA) Project Credit: 65351 – RW Assignment Title: CONSULTANT SERVICE FORAN INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT A STUDY ON "TRENDS AND SKILLS NEEDS FOR THE TOURISM SECTOR IN RWANDA." Reference No .: 018/S/SPIU/2012/MINICOM The Private Sector Federation (PSF) acknowledges the fact that tourism is very important for the Rwandan economy. Based on feedback from PSF's Chamber of Tourism, and similar stakeholders, PSF has also come to realize the need for perspective-oriented research and analysis of new and changing skill needs in the labour marketthat serves Rwanda's tourism sector. On that note, a study of this kind will require not just in-depth research, but also a thorough analysis at various levels, that is, the macroeconomic, regional, local, required skills, and enterprise levels. Relevant as it may be, this could also be particularly challenging as the occupations characterised in the sector are dominated by internationalisation, where the mobility of people, jobs, and services are high. Typically, tourism has one of the highest labour mobility rates; therefore, it has the potential to become a labour market with a truly East African (regional) dimension. It is generally and globally acknowledged as one of the few economic sectors that has significant growth prospects, and is characterised as a catalyst for peace, prosperity, and macroeconomic growth. Rwanda's growing private sector is already shortof trained workers in all sectors. This is reflected in increasingly growing disparities in the fee structure. Higher-educated workers command a market premium, and workers with vocational education earn 73 percent more, on average, than those who have completed primary school only. It has been realized, for reasons such as these, and several others, that there is a strategic need for specific areas and aspects within a sector as important as tourism to be accorded unique attention. The overall objective of the consultancy work therefore is to · The principle and main objectives of this research study is to provide insight into current and future trends for the development of tourism not only in Rwanda, with highlights in EAC region. · This assignment is expected to analyze the resulting skills-needs in the labour market that serves the tourism sector by offering a clear depiction of past, present, and future trends, specifically in relation to thesector's current demands for labor/skills, and also needs that are based on future tourism-related aspirations, expectations, and trajectories. · The purpose of this assignment is to promote an efficient tourism sector in Rwanda, which is adaptive to tourism labor-related needs not only within the country, but also regionally, that is, taking into account the nature of 'availability' or possible 'unavailability' of the human resource that can serve this sector in a complementary and progressive manner. · This assignment is also expected to identify and recommend long-term measures that are specifically aimed at strengthening both human and institutional capacity-building for development of the tourism sector in Rwanda. · This assignment will also identify the role of ICT in tourism and related changes in skills (e.g: electronic commerce and revenue management) Scope of services The scope of this study is therefore to cover three specific areas that are considered key for a full comprehension oflabour-related needs in the tourism sector. These three classifications or categories are; (i) Social trends and economic aspects; (ii) Required skillsfor the tourism sector and; (iii) Implementation of recommendations. It is within a period of three phases that theseareas should be diagnosed as thoroughly as possible with the intention of merging all three perspectives in a way that will offer prescriptive solutions for the tourism sector to be able to achieve progressively prognostic trends. Key tasks The specific activities and tasks will include: · The studyis expected to cover, all the above mentioned tasks within a methodology that will cover social trends (e.g., demographics, leisure patterns, etc.) and economic aspects (e.g., penetration of ICTs, changing distribution channels, etc.), which determine the future demand for skills and competences. It will discuss the question of "skills" and "qualifications" needs for the tourism sector in Rwanda, and compare with the wider EAC region. · The second part will look at required skills for tourism, and the new types ofskills demanded by these trends. Some of the possible specific required skills that may fall under broad titles such as skills in barrier-free tourism, tourism wellness services, revenue management, lodging, amusement and attractions management, etc. · Finally,the study will look at the transfer (or implementation) of study results into policy and practice, particularly concerning the identification of examples of "good practice" through which the "tourism chamber" will be able to formulate – for the tourism sector as a whole – strong, relevant, and sustainable long-term "advocacy programmes". QUALIFICATION & COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS · This consultancy must be undertaken by an individual consultant. · Should at least hold a Master's degree in economics, development studies or related fields, with specialization in tourism, environment or international trade or a Bachelor's degree with a working experience in similar assignment of 5 years. · Should have at least five years research experience in the national and regional arena (i.e., the wider EAC region). · Proficiency in English and Kinyarwanda would be preferred; working knowledge of French would be a great advantage. · High-level inter-personal, communication, writing, reporting, and presentationskills. · Evidence of publication of own written articles in either local or international journals. · Self-motivation and capability to work under tight deadlines in competitive environment. · A proven track-record of research and work in tourism would be an added advantage. · Strong computer skills and analytical skills with ability to write and review technical reports will be required. · For capacity-building purposes; during course of the assignment the consultant should beable to transfer skills and knowledge to the staff of tourism chamberby working with PSF staff. D URATION OF THE CONSULTANCY The consultant will be required to undertake this assignment within a period of ninety (90) days (three months). At the end of this time-frame, he/she should be able to produce all the outputs and deliverables stated in the aforementioned. Introduction and Background The Government of Rwanda through the Workforce Development Authority has received a Credit from the World Bank for the implementation of its Skills Development strategy. This Credit has been provided underthe Skills Development Project (SDP). The project supports three components which all focus on skills development by matching demand and supply. Component 1 targets medium-term systems building that would provide competency-based and demand-driven training in selected priority occupations in selected vocational training centers (VTCs). Component 2 supports the overall TVET system strengthening while component 3 addresses the Rapid Skills Delivery by acting as aquick delivery financing mechanism in response to priority skill needs. As a first step, the Workforce Development Authority would like to hirean individual consultant to identify skills bottlenecks by collectingand analyzing the existing literature that are related to the economic growth in the country, and design a clear plan of action for furtherstudies. 2. Objective of the Assignment The purpose of this consultancy is to carry out a deep review and analysis of the existing literature on TVET-related skills in Rwanda which are identified as critical bottlenecks to sustain and improve the competitiveness of the Rwandan economy. This will include: i. The collection and analysis of data and information on the economic trends, qualitative and quantitative labor demand for TVET trained workers and extent to which the training system produces demanded skills. ii. Identification of areas which need to be further analyzed and areas for which additional information needs to be collected to inform WDA and partners to better align their activities to resolve key skillsbottlenecks. iii. Design a Plan of Action for WDA to fill these information gaps and develop terms of reference for further data collection and analysis. 3. Scope of the Consultancy Services i. Collection and review of existing literature on demand and supply of TVET-related skills in Rwanda, from WDA, relevant public and private institutions as well as non-governmental organizations including Rwanda's development partners. ii. Collection and review of existing literature on economic trends and its relation to skills gaps from the same stakeholders iii. Presentation of draft and final report to WDA and relevant stakeholders iv. Development of a Plan of Action for further analytical studies and discussion with WDA and its stakeholders and development partners. 4. title: CONSULTANT SERVICE FOR AN INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO FORMULATE STRATEGIC PLAN FOR MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY (MINICOM)
notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY PO.BOX 73 KIGALI Kigali, 20 th December 2012 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ( CONSULTANTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) COUNTRY: RWANDA NAME OF PROJECT: Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance(G4C TA) Project Credit: 65351 – RW Assignment Title: CONSULTANT SERVICE FOR AN INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO FORMULATE STRATEGIC PLAN FOR MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY (MINICOM) Reference No .: 011/S/SPIU/2012/MINICOM The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MINICOM) has a wide-reaching mandate that is centralto the Government of Rwanda's economic development agenda as elaborated in national strategies such as Vision 2020, the Economic Development and Poverty Reduction Strategy (EDPRS) and 7-Year Government Plan. MINICOM leads the Sector Working Group on Private Sector Development under EDPRS and also assumes vice-chairmanship of the Economic Cluster. It is a leading institution in the development of the second five-yearEDPRS, which will come into effect in July 2013. MINICOM's vision is to achieve accelerated and sustained economic growth led by a dynamic and competitive private sector, and its mission is to facilitate Rwanda's economic transformation through enabling a competitive private sector integrated into regional and global markets, while ensuring a level playing field and the protection of consumers. The Ministry's keyactivities are clustered into three General Directorates, namely: Planning, Policy and M&E, (2) Trade and Investment and (3) Industry and SME Development. In addition, MINICOM has three affiliated agencies: the Rwanda Bureau of Standards (RBS, established in 2002), the Rwanda Cooperative Agency (RCA, established in 2008) and the National Inspectorate and Competition Authority (NICA, established in 2011). MINICOM also houses a Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU), which coordinates all internally and externally financed projects within the Ministry. MINICOM has also established a decentralization framework with local governments to allow them todeliver on issues regarding trade, industry, tourism and cooperatives. Provincial trade focal points are supplemented by District Cooperative and Business Officers (DCOs) as well as Rural Small and Medium Enterprise facilitators who coordinate the Proximity Business Advisory (PROBA) program in the district. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA Single Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) MINISTRY OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY PO.BOX 73KIGALI Kigali, 12 th December 2012 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTANTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) COUNTRY: RWANDA NAME OF PROJECT: Governance for Competitiveness Technical Assistance (G4C TA) Project Credit: 65351 – RW Assignment Title: CONSULTANT SERVICE FOR A TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR R WANDA HORTICULTURE INTER-ORGANIZATION (RHIO) Reference No .: 009/S/SPIU/2012/MINICOM The Rwanda horticulture sector accounts around 300 cooperatives, but many more unorganized farmers are also found in horticulture production for long time due to different challenges facing this sector. This constitutes is a very big disadvantage in terms of input distribution, marketing and above allraises cost of certification. One way to overcome these constraints is to organise horticulture farmers into strong cooperatives using appropriate structural and organizational models that worked elsewhere with modification to suit local realities. It is through these cooperatives that farmers will consolidate land, link with markets for their produce, input and credit suppliers and access extension services. These cooperatives will also facilitate registration of groups engaged in horticulture production for linkage with investors. Even though an important effort has been provided by former RHODA in collaboration with various actors; the Rwanda's horticultural value chains still face various constraints related to skills and knowledge, infrastructure and other areas of improvement in services sector. These constraints can be summarised at farmers' level, at processors' level as well as market level. At farmers' level : smallholders are largely unorganised, they have little access to adequate extension services and little linkages with research, resulting in a lack of knowledge on cultivation,plant protection and post-harvest handling, but also on market information and market linkages. Likewise, they have limited access to finance and capitalinvestment. They mostly practice rain fed agriculture, have limited access to inputs (planting material, manure, fertilizers, pesticides), which are costly and of limited quality. Finally, there is little value addition at farmers ‟ level. At processors' level and market level : although producecan be of very high quality, there is a lack of homogeneity on the quality offered, volumes are limited and there is limited capacity to ensure continuous supply. Access to good quality business development services, both financial and non financial (market information, testing,certification, technology and product development, business planning…) is difficult and there are consequently few skilled entrepreneurs. At market level: Traders/exporters have very few engagements with international exporters and have limited access to markets. Packaging is poor and affected by limitations regarding the use of plastic. Airfreight transport costs are high as well as the cost of energy. All these constraints call for a well organised sector with clear objectives and committed players. It is against this background that NAEB with funding from the G4C project funded by the World Bank is seeking services of a technical assistanceto support the RHIO to have a better organization that can respond toadvocacy role for all players in the sector. The overall objective of the consultancy work therefore is to support the RHIO to have a well-managed organization that can respond to the advocacy role for its member horticultural associations. The main objectives of technical assistance are as follows: 1. To develop a Long-term Feasibility Study for Commercialization and Export of Horticultural Products of RHIO Members, 2. To develop and helpin start up for a pilot Horticultural Products Distribution Point in Rwanda, 3. To carry out dialogue and market analysis with different stakeholders with an aim to increase local horticulture professionals presence on international markets QUALIFICATION & COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS The incumbent Consultant will haveto fill the following: • Holding at least Bachelor's Degree in Economics, Business Administration, Agri-Business or any other related field, • Having more than 5 years experience as TOT, preferably with support to the Horticulture SMEs and Cooperatives, especially those based in the rural areas, • Have proven experience in working with international organizations member Organizations • Have morethan 3 years experience in the field of Capacity Building Support to SMEs, Start-up Non-Profit Organizations, or NGOs • More than2 years experience in the field of Program or Project Management, • Having worked for an International Development Organization in Rwanda, • Having more than 3 years experience in Business Development Consultancy missions, • Having interacted with some key Public Institutions like RCA, RDB, MINAGRI and related donors, • Ability to work in English and Kinyarwanda languages; working knowledge of French is an added advantage. notice_text: REPUBLIC OF RWANDA RWANDA TRANSPORT DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (RTDA) P.O.BOX 6674 4 th Floor, Pension Plaza (CSR Building) Kicukiro-KIGALI REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST CONSULTING SERVICES Consultancy Services for ROAD SAFETY AUDIT OF THE NATIONAL ROAD NETWORK. Project Name : ROAD SAFETY AUDIT OF THE NATIONAL ROAD NETWORK Grant/Credit No : IDA Grant N H331-RW / ACGF Grant N0: TF 090451 RW / IDA CREDIT NO 4968-RW Project ID No : P079414 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST The Government of Rwanda has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Transport Sector Development Project and intendsto apply part of the proceeds for consultant services to carry out Road safety audit of the National Road network by an international consultant. . The available funds will be used for payment of audit to be acquired within the framework of this project. Infrastructure development and improving road transport services are the main strategic policy of the Government of Rwanda in terms of economic development and poverty reduction . In order to support programs and projects on rehabilitation and development of infrastructure the RTDA (Rwanda Transport Development Agency) is undertaking road safety audit and road safety strategy development as part of a comprehensive program to improve the safety performance of infrastructure and transport services. It is found, in fact, a large number of accidents on the classified road network which causes include: couter Lire phontiquement Dictionnaire insufficient consideration of road safety measures in design road standards and implementation of infrastructure projects; Lack of analysis of accidents records in order to map black spots andtake action to improve the safety level of roads. The audit will focus on road safety aspects of existing and classified road network (comprising urban sections), and of international corridors while the strategy will be for the entire road sector. The audit and strategy report, to be drafted, will be a document to, on the one hand, make the necessary technical improvements to the existing classified road network, and secondly, implement security measures on standards of future programs and projects on road infrastructure in Rwanda. The audit is expected to enable the Government of Rwanda to adopt themost advantageous option among the different improvements to the existing classified road network , implement security measures on standards of future programs and projects on road infrastructure. The objectives of the study : The objective of the audit is to reduce the number of fatal accidents, personal injuries accidents and damages throughout the classified road network in Rwanda, while the strategy outlines key road safety policies and actions to be implemented in the future to make Rwanda's roadnetwork safer. It will enable the improvement of road safety for all road users (pedestrians, motorists and passengers), and therefore the understanding of the causes of accidents on roads of the country. Thus, the audit shall: highlight all the gaps in safety on the whole classified road network(traffic engineering, traffic signing and road marking), that is to say, evaluate the potential insecurity of the existing classified road network, Offer, on the one hand, corrective measures to increase the safety level of the existing network and, on the other hand, necessary measuresto be considered in standards of projects and programs of national and community road infrastructures. carry out a detailed review of existing accident black spot lists; identify the worst accident black spots and prioritize accident blackspots by potential accident reduction and cost-effectiveness; carry out a detailed analysis of each site and design cost-effective measures to rectify the problems; assess the expected accident reduction impact of the program; develop a computerized monitoring system to measure the actual impactof various remedial measures to accident spots and to determine the corresponding coefficient of reduction in accidents; Outline enforcement strategies and action plans that would improve road safety in Rwanda, and Prepare complete bidding documents and cost estimates to implement the action plans. Republic of Rwanda General Procurement Notice WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY SKILLS DEVELOPMENT PROJECT The Government of Rwanda has applied for a Credit from the World Bankfor the implementation of its Skills Development strategy. This Credit will be provided under the Skills Development project which is likely to be effective in late July, 2011. The government of Rwanda has established a strong policy and institutional basis for the development of Technical, Vocational Education and Training (TVET). The Skills Development project will therefore build upon this basis, focusing on improving access to quality and relevant training. It will contribute to improving the enabling framework for training provision through systemsdevelopment and capacity building as well as finance the provision ofquality and relevant training. The project will be implemented by Workforce Development Authority (WDA), based in Kigali, Rwanda. The Skills Development project will support three (03) components which all focus on skills development by matching demand and supply. Since skill needs are constantly shifting, priority needs should be addressed rapidly, in a flexible manner and a quick delivery financing mechanism will be applied to respond to priority skill needs. The Government of Rwanda therefore intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Credit to contract payments for the procurement of goods, works, related services and the engagement of consulting services under this project. The three components are: Component 1 : Delivery of Quality and Relevant Vocational Training This component will strengthen the TVET system through interventions aimed at improving quality and relevance of training delivery in eightselected priority occupations and seven vocational training centers. Goods - Plumbing, electrical, masonry, culinary Art (cook), food & beverage (waiter/waitress), front office-1 (receptionist) and front office - 2 (housekeeping equipment) . - Culinary Art (Cook), food and beverage (waiter/waitress) and housekeeping. - Masonry, Carpentry, Electrical & Plumbing). Works - Construction & rehabilitation of various technical schools- ETO Busogo, ETO Kibungo, ETO Kibuye, Kabarondo Vocational Training Center (VTC), Kibari VTC, Kinihira and Kirehe VTCs. Consultancy - Supervision of construction works for the seven technical schools Component 2: TVET System Strengthening This component will aim at monitoring and evaluating training delivery and in particular the implementation and performance of the SDP. It will also inform strategic policy decisions and policy reforms by providing sound analyses concerning key aspects of the training system andthe labor market as well as build capacity for monitoring and evaluation within WDA and TVET Providers. Consultancy Consultancy firm to conduct baseline, Round I Evaluation, Data analysis, Tracer Studies and Employer Satisfaction Component 3: Rapid Skills Delivery The key objective of this component is to reduce skills gap by rapidly increasing the supply of skills that are in high demand in the labormarket. The instrument which will be used to achieve this objective is a Skills Development Facility that will provide sub-grants to eligible applicants on a competitive basis. Procurement here is in two areas of concern: Mini Surveys in 5 provinces to assess labor market needs Application for grants. Please note that specific notices inviting applicants will be advertised later. Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conductedthrough the procedures as specified in the World Bank's Guidelines: Procurement under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits dated January 2011, and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the guidelines. Consulting services will be selected in accordance with the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers dated January 2011. Specific Procurement Notices (SPN) for contracts to be bid for under the World Bank's international competitive bidding (ICB) procedures and for consultancy services contracts will be announced in the following media; Client Connection and dgMarket websites, Regional Newspaper (East African) and Local Newspapers (Imvaho and or the New Times) and on WDA website: http://www.wd.gov.rw Interested eligible bidders who wish to be included on the mailing list to receive invitations for bids under ICB/NCB procedures and those requiring additional information should contact WDA on the address below. notice_text: Specific Procurement Notice Request for Bids Goods (Two-Envelope Bidding Process) Country: Ethiopia Name of Project: Education and Skills for Employment Project (EASE) Contract Title: Procurement of Agricultural Machinery Equipment,Agro processing Equipements and Accessories for (Ardaita, Jinka,Shire,Bonga,Daye,Teppi and Jigjiga) Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IDA-74200 RFB Reference No.: ET-MOLS-545744-GO-RFB Issue Date: July 21, 2026 The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Education for Skills and Employment (EASE), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for procurement of Procurement of Training Equipment and Accessories of Honey and Spice, Coffee Processing, Tea Processing, Dairy products and Agricultural Mechanization Technology for PTCs (Shire, Bonga, Tepi, Jinka and other Colleges) The Ministry of Labor and Skills now invites sealed Bids from eligible and qualified Bidders for the Procurement, Supply, Installation, Testing, Commissioning, and Training of Laboratory Training Equipment and Accessories for selected TVET institutions and training centers under the following five Lots: Lot 1: Honey and Spice Training Laboratory Equipment and Accessories Lot 2: Coffee Processing Laboratory Equipment and Accessories; Lot 3: Tea Processing Training Laboratory Equipment and Accessories Lot 4: Dairy product Processing Training Laboratory Equipment and Accessories Lot 5: Agricultural Mechanization Technology Laboratory Equipment and Accessories; The Goods and Related Services shall be delivered, installed, tested, commissioned, and made fully operational within six (6) months from the Effective Date of Contract or as specified in the Delivery and Completion Schedule. No margin of domestic preference shall apply. Qualification Criteria Minimum Requirement Financial Capability The Bidder shall submit audited financial statements for the last three (3) years preceding the bid submission deadline, demonstrating the current soundness of the Bidder’s financial position. For a Joint Venture (JV), this requirement shall be met by each member. Specific Experience For each lot, the Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed at least two (2) contracts each with a value of not less than the amounts specified below; or one (1) contract with a value of not less than the amounts specified below, within the last Four (4) years prior to bid submission deadline, that have been successfully and substantially completed and that are similar in nature and complexity to the Goods and Related Services under the Contract. For a joint venture, this requirement may be met by all members combined, and each JV member shall have a minimum experience specified below. Lot Single Entity or All JV Members Combined Each JV Member Lot 1 Two (2) contracts, each with a value not less than US$ 600,000.00 or one (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 1,200,000.00 One (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 600,000.00 Lot 2 Two (2) contracts, each with a value not less than US$ 450,000.00 or one (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 900,000.00 One (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 450,000.00 Lot 3 Two (2) contracts, each with a value not less than US$ 300,000.00 or one (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 600,000.00 One (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 300,000.00 Lot 4 Two (2) contracts, each with a value not less than US$ 1,000,000.00 or one (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 2,000,000.00 One (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 1,000,000.00 Lot 5 Two (2) contracts, each with a value not less than US$ 1,250,000.00 or one (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 2,500,000.00 One (1) contract with a value not less than US$ 1,250,000.00 3. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Procurement in Investment Project Financing, Goods, Works, Non-consulting and Consulting Services, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.”. 4. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 60 % and for Bid cost: 40 % . 5. The document will be sent by e-mail or bidders can collect it in person from the Ministry of Labor and Skills, EASE project office. 7. The outer Bid envelopes marked “Original Bid”, and the inner envelopes marked “Technical Part” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on September 1,2026 at 14:30 hours Ethiopian Time . All envelopes marked “Second Envelope: Financial Part” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Purchaser until the second public opening. 8. title: Consultancy Service for Basin level study for strategic study basins to identify and prioritize physical flood risk reduction investments, feasibility study, and detailed design for prioritized investments (2 basins-Genalle-Dawa and Wabishebele)
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Ethiopia Flood Management Project (E-FMP) Grant No. E124-Et Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Basin level study for strategic study basins to identify and prioritize physical flood risk reduction investments, feasibility study, and detailed design for prioritized investments (2 basins-Genalle-Dawa and Wabishebele). Reference No.: ET-MOWE-522455-CS-QCBS The Government of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Flood Management Project (E-FMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the provision of Feasibility study and Detail design for selected investments in the Wabi-Shebele Basin & Genale Dawa Basin Flood Risk Reduction Investment. GENERAL OBJECTIVES:-The overall objective of this assignment is to conduct feasibility study and Detail design for selected investments in the Wabi-Shebele Basin & Genale Dawa Basin including evaluating the viability and effectiveness of proposed flood risk reduction interventions, ensuring that they are technically feasible, economically justified, environmentally sustainable, and socially beneficial for the affected communities. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES: To establish a technical baseline for flood risk assessment through validation of existing data and updated hydrological and hydraulic analyses, including climate change considerations and flood hazard mapping. To identify and develop priority flood risk reduction interventions by assessing risk hotspots, evaluating alternative solutions, and preparing detailed designs and cost estimates for selected measures. To enhance institutional readiness for sustainable flood risk management through preparation of operational frameworks, environmental and social safeguards instruments, stakeholder engagement mechanisms, and capacity-building activities. KEY DELIVERABLES AND INDICATIVE TIMING: The key deliverables include the Inception Report (Month 1); Basin Baseline Assessment and Updated Hydrological and Hydraulic Analysis Reports (Month 6); Flood Risk Reduction Options Assessment, Conceptual Design, Hydraulic Modeling and Hazard Mapping Reports (Month 10); Feasibility Study and Draft Detailed Design Reports (Month 12); Final Detailed Design Package, Environmental and Social Safeguard Instruments, Training and Capacity Building Outputs, and Final Consolidated Report (Month 15); and final handover of all data, models, and quality-assured outputs upon completion. SCOPE OF SERVICES: The scope of the service is to conduct the Feasibility Study and prepare the Detailed Design for flood risk reduction and related infrastructure in the Wabisheble and Genale Dawa Basins, in accordance with national and international standards, including those of the World Bank, while integrating environmental and social considerations such as ecological impacts, community livelihoods, resettlement, and gender and social inclusion. ESTIMATED PERSON MONTH & DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT: The estimated key staff input is 105 Person–Month and the implementation periods is 450 Calendar days from the commencement date of the contract which is estimated to be from end of July 2026. DETAIL TOR ATTACHED: The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at https://mowe.gov.et/en/resource_types/tor . The Ministry of Water and Energy now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. THE SHORTLISTING CRITERIA ARE: Firm’s Core business and years in business Relevant experience and Qualifications of the consulting firm in the field of the assignment Technical and managerial capability of the firm. Number and qualifications of professional staff of the firm. Not the number and qualification of key Experts proposed for the assignment as they will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Nov 2020 updated in September 2023. Procurement will also comply with “Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants” revised as of July 1, 2016. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Ethiopia Flood Management Project (E-FMP) Grant No. E124-Et Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Basin level study for strategic study basins to identify and prioritise physical flood risk reduction investments, and feasibility study for prioritized investments (2 basins-Abay and Baro-Akobo). Reference No.: ET-MOWE-411804-CS-QCBS The Government of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Flood Management Project (E-FMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the provision of strategic flood protection study, extending up to feasibility level, in both the Baro Akobo and Abay River Basins. GENERAL OBJECTIVES:-The overall objective of this assignment is to conduct a comprehensive flood protection feasibility assessment for selected investment projects in the Baro Akobo and Abay Basins including evaluating the viability and effectiveness of proposed flood risk reduction interventions; and to ensure that the recommended measures are technically viable, socially acceptable, environmentally sustainable, institutionally manageable, and economically efficient. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES: Review and update existing flood risk assessments, studies, and data for the Baro-Akobo and Abay Basins. Assess flood hazards, exposure, vulnerability, and climate change impacts to identify priority flood risk areas and investments. Evaluate and prioritize structural flood risk reduction measures and prepare conceptual designs for selected interventions. Undertake preliminary environmental, social, and economic assessments of prioritized investments. Recommend implementation arrangements and a roadmap for advancing prioritized flood risk reduction investments. KEY DELIVERABLES AND INDICATIVE TIMING: The key deliverables include the Final Inception Report including methodology, work plan, stakeholder engagement plan, data assessment, and training plan (1.5 months); Draft Interim Package covering Data Audit, Analysis and Survey, and Hydrological and Hydraulic Modeling and Hazard Mapping Reports (4–5.5 months); Options Identification and Selection Report including recommended concept design (7.75 months); and Investment Framework Application Report together with Draft Feasibility Study and Concept Design Report, Final Feasibility and Design Package, Final Training and Capacity Building Report, and Providing all data, models, GIS layers, and related outputs (10–13 months). SCOPE OF SERVICES: The scope of the service is to conduct a comprehensive basin-level study, with particular focus on assessing flood risks and vulnerabilities, including feasibility study for prospective flood protection and physical risk reduction interventions, ensuring alignment with nationally and internationally recognized standards, as well as bank-approved guidelines. ESTIMATED PERSON MONTH & DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT: The estimated key staff input is 118 Person–Month and the implementation periods is 390 Calendar days from the commencement date of the contract which is estimated to be from end of Sep 2026. DETAIL TOR ATTACHED: The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at https://mowe.gov.et/en/resource_types/tor. notice_text: GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE Country: Ethiopia Project : Ethiopia Program for Results for Strengthening Primary Health Care Services Sector: Health Sector GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE Loan No./Credit No./TF No./Grant No. E1210 Project ID No. P175167 The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing in the amount of US$ 447 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Program for Results for Strengthening Primary Health Care Services, out of which US$ 129 million is financed through IPF and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of the IPF part to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project. The project IPF component includes the following sub-components IPF Sub-component I: Provision of EHS Focusing on RMNCAH+N to Conflict-Affected population and IDPs (US$89 million IDA equivalent) IPF Sub-component II: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics43 (US$30 million IDA equivalent) Under the IPF component the following will be procured through open international competitive procurement 1. Procurement of Vital Sign Monitoring, Oxygen Delivery, Diagnostic and Hospital Equipment ($6,1 or equivalent) 2. Procurement of Furniture, Weighing Scales, Surgical Instruments, Operating Room, Laboratory, Sterilization, Imaging, and Related Equipment (estimated at USD 23.5 million or equivalent) 3. Procurement of Vital Sign Monitoring, Oxygen Delivery, Diagnostic, and Hospital Equipment (estimated at USD 6.1 million or equivalent) 4. Supply and Installation of data center and Procurement of IT equipment for ICS head quarter (estimated at USD 9.5 million) 5. Procurement of CRVS registration KI (estimated at USD 9.45 million) Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025 ) (Procurement Regulations) , and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection. Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available, in on the World Bank’s external website and Ethiopian herald news paper Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services for the above mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the address below: Ministry of Health Ethiopia Gemechisa Olani(Senior Procurement Specialist) Email: gemechisa.olani@moh.gov.et POBOX 1234 Sudan Streat Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Phone number (0251) 115517011 Website moh@moh.gov.et

title: Selection of Fayda Pass Product Owner
buyer: Prime Minster Office, National ID Program
notice_text: Request for Expression of Interest (Consulting Services – Individual Selection) Fayda Pass Owner for the National ID Program Country: Ethiopia Project: Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Project ID: P179040 Assignment Title: Fayda Pass Owner for the National ID Program Reference No.: ET-NIDP-524662-CS-INDV Duty Station: NIDP Head Office, Addis Ababa The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. National ID Program, the ultimate project implementer intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting of individual consultants. National ID Program as part of the project implementation program is looking Fayda Pass Owner that supports the NIDP. Experienced experts who have experience, passionate and innovative ideas for the position are invited to express their interest for the assignment. The Fayda Pass Owner will play a crucial role in supporting Senior Product Owner and the overall services for the National ID Program in Ethiopia. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including software engineers, designers, data analysts, and government stakeholders to deliver high-quality and user-centric solutions. The Fayda Pass Owner acts as the strategic architect and orchestrator of the trust ecosystem, bridging the gap between complex cryptographic infrastructure and seamless service delivery for Holders, Issuers, and Verifiers. S/he is responsible for ensuring key service and integration components are productized. This includes the technical integration layer such as the PKI-driven tools and SDKs to be deployed (reused) within partner environments (issuers as well as verifiers). The product environment must ensure that sensitive credentials like Digital IDs and Financial Accounts are issued securely via HSMs and verified instantly across the platform. Ultimately, the role is to balance rigorous regulatory compliance and security with a frictionless user experience, transforming a complex decentralized credential ecosystem into a scalable, interoperable, and daily-use framework and utility. Specific responsibilities for the Fayda Pass Owner will include, but are not limited to, the following core activities: Translate complex cryptographic requirements (like PKI certificate lifecycles and mTLS handshakes) into seamless business workflows for NIDP’s institutional partners. Make-sure that integration partner services have a smooth and simple as possible utilizing the current toolkit (Lightweight Org Agent), making it a repeatable, self-service experience that reduces the time-to-market for new partners (e.g., getting a new Bank live in a few days instead of weeks). Ensure that the platform and service remains the "Gold Standard" for compliance, ensuring our credentials are accepted throughout the country and across borders. Closely following evolving global standards such W3C, eIDAS, ISO, DIDComm, OIDC4* and other important to the platform. Maintain the brand integrity of Fayda Pass as the custodian of the platform’s security posture, managing the roadmap for key rotation, revocation registries, and data privacy features. Comfortably manage the variation in the two extremes (the technical depth and the user experience). There are instances where the product owner may be discussing Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) in the morning and End-User UX in the afternoon. Ensure the "Trust Triangle" functions seamlessly as a decentralized but unified ecosystem: (For the Issuer) - manage the APIs and SDKs that allow the issuer organization to securely publish credentials into the wallet. (For the Holder / End-User) - oversee the mobile/web interface where users store, manage, and share their data with privacy-preserving features (like Zero-Knowledge Proofs). (For the Verifier ) - manage the verification gateways that allow third parties (like a border agent) to instantly validate a credential without seeing unnecessary private data. Take responsibility for the roadmap that takes the wallet from a simple credential storage tool to a daily utility. This Includes the following key aspects: Onboarding: Designing frictionless flows for users to claim their first ID or link a bank account. Expansion: Identifying new use cases (e.g., adding "Academic Document" or "Health Record" credentials). Monetization: suggesting a reasonable cost-per-verification or subscription model for enterprise Verifiers. Reliability: Monitoring platform uptime and the performance of the underlying data and trust chain. National ID Program, Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project now invites eligible Individual Experts to indicate their interest to provide the Services. Interested Experts should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services for a period of one year with possibility of extension for additional period subject to outstanding performance of the consultant and availability of budget. The shortlisting criteria include the following; The ideal candidate for the role of Fayda Pass Owner will bring the following competencies and skills: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Software Engineering, or a related field. Minimum of 5+ years in Product Management or Technical Project Management, with a proven track record of defining, launching, and scaling complex digital services. Experience managing product oriented projects such as enterprise software systems that involve multiple external stakeholders (e.g., B2B2C models). Proficiency in translating high-level policy goals or business objectives into a phased technical backlog and a 12-month product vision. Ability to manage a "multi-sided market" (such as Issuers, Holders, and Verifiers in the case of Wallets), balancing the conflicting needs of institutional partners with the ease of use for citizens. Experience in "productizing" technical tools, specifically overseeing the delivery of APIs, SDKs, or on premise connectors that allow external partners to integrate with a central platform efficiently. A solid understanding of secure system design, including identity management (IAM), data encryption, and "Privacy-by-Design" principles. Ability to act as a bridge between high-level institutional partners and deep-tier engineering teams, translating complex requirements into seamless business workflows. Experience collaborating with UI/UX teams to simplify high-security actions (such as digital signing or identity recovery) into intuitive, frictionless experiences for the general public. General familiarity with (or a strong appetite to learn) global standards such as W3C Verifiable Credentials, ISO standards, and regional data protection frameworks. notice_text: Request for Expressions of Interest (Consulting Services – Firms Selection) Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Ministry Water and Energy Second Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Project (P156433) Credit No.: IDA-60070 Assignment Title: Development/Preparation of National Practice Manual for SEWERAGE and Sanitation Service Procurement Reference No.: ET-MOWIE-496687-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Second Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Project (IIUWSSP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting service (the service) includes preparing/developing the sanitation sub-sector design manuals to keep abreast with current and emerging technological advancements, as well as material science, onboard climate-resilient principles, integrating social and environmental considerations, and adapting to modern construction techniques and industrial engineering best practices in the operation and maintenance (O&M), especially electro-mechanical installations and automation. The Objective of the Assignment: The key objectives of this assignment include, but are not limited to: Identify the gaps/shortfalls in the existing policy, strategy, institutional and legal framework, enforcement mechanisms, Technical Guidelines, and manual related to Urban Wastewater Management and Fecal Sludge Management (FSM), sanitation services, and provide review recommendations and/or updates as required. Prepare/Develop a structured and well-organized Sewerage and sanitation manual aligned to existing water sector manuals and to Water sector Regulatory requirements, as well as facilitate Public Sector Partnerships (PPPs), amongst other innovative financing instruments. Ensure that the manual aligns with national/international sanitation standards, guidelines, and policies. Identify and incorporate emerging technologies and approaches, including eco-friendly and nature-based solutions and CWIS approaches. Extensively consult and engage key stakeholders as guided by the Ministry of Water and Energy (MoWE). Carry out a market survey and develop unit costs for sewerage and sanitation components. Conduct a market survey to gather current unit costs for sewerage and sanitation components, ensuring that the methodology is well-documented and includes input from suppliers, contractors, and industry experts. Conduct a comprehensive survey to assess market trends, unit costs, and availability of water supply components, and submit a report. The report should provide a breakdown of the cost data, market trends, and recommendations for future procurement strategies. Design the manual in a visually appealing format, utilizing appropriate graphics, illustrations, and diagrams to enhance understanding and engagement. notice_text: Request for Expression of Interest (Consulting Services – Individual Selection) Selection of Senior Legal Advisor for Digital Ethiopia under National ID Program Country: Ethiopia Project: Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Project ID: P179040 Assignment Title: Senior Legal Advisor - III Reference No.: ET-NIDP-502538-CS-INDV Duty Station: Addis Ababa The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. National ID Program, the ultimate project implementer intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting of individual consultants. The National ID Program is looking for a highly driven and passionate Senior Special Advisor for Digital Ethiopia Legal Support I to support the “Digital Ethiopia Transformation Council” that is in charge of aligning policy and execution of all things digital in Ethiopia. This council is chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister’s office and it is hosted by the Office of the Prime Minister, which is also the host institution of the “Digital ID” project. The advisors will also work closely with Fayda’s legal team, stakeholder and use-case development teams to deepen Fayda’s integration with various nation-wide sectors to engage in legal drafting and reviewing of various documents. The Legal Advisor is expected to have comprehensive legal expertise and will have the overall responsibility of collaborating with team members in the legal and policy unit to handle contract drafting and review, manage fraud cases, develop legal documents and respond to legal queries from departments of NIDP. Specific responsibilities for the Legal Advisor will include, but are not limited to, the following core activities: Support for Digital Ethiopia Council: the advisors shall provide legal support to the council. Upon request and as needed from time to time the advisors shall hold consultations with stakeholders, develop legal opinion and provide legal advice to the council. The advisors shall engage in review of documents and provide advice on the legal and regulatory aspects of activities conducted by the council. Legislative Drafting: The advisors shall have a good understanding of Ethiopian laws and legal principles, strong analytical skills, and effective communication skills. They will engage in drafting legal documents and will, together with other team members, undertake a review of the relevant legal documents, and lead consultations to be held with the pertinent bodies. Facilitate and take a leading role in providing legal advice and monitor the enforcement of proclamations and regulations. Conducting Legal Research: The advisors are expected to carry out legal research to support the legislative frameworks of the program and provide recommendations backed by the research conducted. Conduct an investigation regarding legal or enforcement gaps. He/she will work collaboratively with relevant stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of the existing digital ID laws. Providing legal opinions /Legal support: The advisors shall Provide legal opinion or legal support to the responsible departments upon request. They shall provide sound legal opinion and prepare thorough analysis and ensure that they follow principles of objectivity, clarity and strong understanding of relevant laws and facts. Present the opinion in a way that is easy to understand. National ID Program, Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest to provide the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services for a period of one year with possibility of extension for additional period subject to outstanding performance of the consultant and availability of budget. The qualification criteria include the following; LLB degree with a minimum of 6 years’ experience or LLM with 4 years’ experience. Proven experience in legal research, legal drafting, and writing legal opinions. Adept drafting and communication skills. Experience in drafting directives, manuals, standard operating procedures, contracts, and managing contracts. Good interpersonal skills. Experience in government office. Able to work full time. Ability to foster collaboration and teamwork Productive and resilient in a dynamic and challenging environment. Knowledge of one or more regional languages is an advantage. The selection method is based on para 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation. The attention of interested individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”) revised November 2017, August 2018, and February 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Expressions of interest (CV, cover letter and documentary evidence for fulfilling the qualifications) must be delivered in a written form to the address below by E-mail on or before December 10th, 2025. title: Individual Consultant for Technical Assistance on Grid Electric Tariff Study (Lead Energy Economist)
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES—INDIVIDUL CONSULTANCY SERVICE) Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Name of Project: Power Sector Reform, Investment and Modernization in Ethiopia (PRIME-1) Assignment Title : Individual Consultancy Services for Technical Assistance on Grid Electricity Tariff Study for Petroleum and Energy Authority (PEA). Procurement Ref No: ET-EEP-518549-CS-INDV Client: Ethiopian Electric Power (EEP) The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia /Recipient/ has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Power Sector Reform, Investment and Modernization in Ethiopia (PRIME-1) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for engaging Individual Consultancy Services for Technical Assistance on Grid Electricity Tariff Study. EEP is inviting Expression of interest (EOI) for International qualified individual consultants to provide Consultancy Services for Technical Assistance on Grid Electricity Tariff Study for Petroleum and Energy Authority (PEA). The scope of services includes, but is not limited to, the following key areas; Economic Analysis and Tariff Design: The Consultant will comprehensively review and assess utility-proposed current and future tariffs to ensure they are cost-reflective, equitable, and financially sustainable. This includes evaluating affordability thresholds, subsidy mechanisms, socio-economic impacts, and climate resilience considerations. Scenario Planning and Risk Management: The Consultant will develop “ Regulator’s Tariff Model ” with scenario planning tools to examine the robustness of utility-proposed tariffs under varying conditions, such as fuel price shocks or climate impacts. This includes proposing risk mitigation strategies to ensure long-term financial sustainability. Capacity Building: The consultant will strengthen the technical and operational capabilities of Ethiopia’s electricity regulatory authority and related institutions. This will include training staff, developing tools, and establishing methodologies for effective implementation and monitoring of tariff reforms, with a focus on long-term knowledge retention. Monitoring and Evaluation Framework for Economic Metrics: The Consultant will establish an M&E framework to track the economic and socio-economic impacts of utility-proposed tariffs. This includes defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and equity metrics to ensure inclusivity. Policy and Regulatory Framework Input: The Consultant will provide input on tariff-related aspects of existing policy, legal, and regulatory frameworks. This includes identifying gaps that impact affordability, equity, and financial sustainability, and proposing adjustments to ensure coherence between tariff reviews and broader regulatory reforms. Collaboration with the Regulatory Experts will ensure alignment with institutional governance and enforcement mechanisms. His/Her minimum qualification and experience requirement is elaborated below . Lead Energy Economist: At least 15–20 years of experience in energy economics, electricity pricing, and regulatory policy. Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in Energy Economics, Electrical Engineering, Economics, Finance, or a related field. Preferred Specialized Training: Training in regulatory economics or renewable energy integration (e.g., IRENA, World Bank courses). Project Experience: Proven experience leading similar assignments, particularly in developing countries or Sub-Saharan Africa. Strong knowledge of cost-reflective tariffs, regulatory frameworks, and policy reforms. Led at least2 similar projects in Sub-Saharan Africa or emerging economies (e.g., tariff restructuring, utility regulatory reforms) Technical Expertise Proven experience leading similar assignments, particularly in developing countries or Sub-Saharan Africa. Strong knowledge of cost-reflective tariffs, regulatory frameworks, and policy reforms. Led at least2 similar projects in Sub-Saharan Africa or emerging economies (e.g., tariff restructuring, utility regulatory reforms) Soft Skills Stakeholder Management: Ability to mediate conflicting priorities (e.g., affordability vs. cost recovery). Autonomous Work: Proven capacity to manage complex, multi-phase projects independently Communication: Fluency in English (written/spoken); proficiency in Amharic or local languages is an asset. Tools and Certifications Software: Proficiency in economic modeling tools (e.g., Excel,Python,etc..), and understanding of energy sector tools such as GIS for grid analysis, and data visualization (e.g.,Power BI). Note: Women applicants are highly encouraged to apply. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained refer to the following website: www.eep.com.et or can be obtained at the address given below. The shortlisting criteria are: General Qualification Relevant experience specific to the assignment Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM local time. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person or by carrier and Email on or before November 17, 2025, 4:00 PM local time (Addis Ababa, Ethiopia) The submittals should be presented in English. Note: In addition to the Email submission the applicants must submit One (1) original hard copy and One (1) electronic version on a flash drive physically or by courier to the address below.
