notice_text: Request for Expression of Interest- Re Advert (Consulting Services – Individual Selection) Country: Ethiopia Project: Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Project ID: P179040 Assignment Title: Senior Project Staff, Program Evaluation and Performance Management Expert (RFD) Reference No.: ET-NIDP-456626-CS-INDV The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. National ID Program, the ultimate project implementer intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting of individual consultants. National ID Program as part of the project implementation program is looking for an Individual Consultant that supports the National ID Program. Experienced individual consultants who have experience, passionate and innovative ideas for the position of Senior Project Staff, Program Evaluation and Performance Management Expert (RFD) are invited to express their interest for the assignment. The Senior Project Staff, Program Evaluation and Performance Management Expert (RFD) will play a pivotal role in driving the success of our digital identity products and services for the National ID Program in Ethiopia. This role will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including software engineers, designers, data analysts, and government stakeholders, to deliver high-quality analytical reports and real-time dashboards. The Senior Project Staff, Program Evaluation and Performance Management Expert will have the overall responsibility of leading the development of the reporting framework as per the analytics and reporting needs of the NIDP. The current core platform has default reporting tools and built-in components that generate source data for analytics and reporting. Hence, the role will need to evaluate the currently available tools and design the necessary improvements and additions. Furthermore, explore and integrate additional tools and technologies (preferably open source) to provide the desired level of analytics and reporting for both internal and external stakeholders. Specific responsibilities for the Senior Project Staff, Program Evaluation and Performance Management Expert (RFD) will include, but are not limited to, the following core activities: 1) Evaluate current Reporting Framework and reporting capabilities of the platform Understand the organization's reporting needs and requirements : Identify Key strategic expectations of the program in general and key stakeholders as indicators of key performance indicators as well as visual and tabular presentations of summary data. Design and develop the reporting framework : Collaborate with NIDP and its key stakeholders, understand their reporting and analytics requirements, and translate them into platform (framework) features and/or enhancements. Create and maintain the reports : Develop technical design of any extensions and/or additional features required, clearly showing where each new feature/extension is needed. Optimize the reporting framework for performance and efficiency : Explore the current capacity of reporting and dashboard tools and suggest improvements and/or other tools that can fulfil all required analytics and reporting requirements Define categories for the reporting framework and reporting audience so that appropriate types and granularity levels are properly presented to each audience (Ex: technical, operational, administrative, performance (KPI), public view, etc.). Train NIDP staff on how to use the reporting framework. 2) Implement the new extensions and integrate suggested tools Develop any missing platform component that can generate (extract) necessary source data for analytics Propose and develop a temporary/permanent data destination for the raw data generated for analytics. This will involve suggesting new data storage tools and mechanisms (such as a data warehouse) Integrate analytics and data visualization tools to provide appropriate and timely reporting framework and KPI data through informative dashboards. Develop the platform enhancements (including code extensions) as well as selected sequence of tool integrations for generating and presenting dashboards according to each major target audience Conduct evaluation and testing, collect feedback from target users, and iterate on designs, developments, tool configurations, and integrations to enhance usability and user satisfaction. Monitor overall performance and use insights to get points of enhancements and optimizations to the implemented reporting framework. Collaborate with the product owner to manage product launch activities and provide support. Stay updated on industry trends and emerging technologies related to reporting framework and Reporting across the digital identity ecosystem. 3) Play the leading role in maintaining the reporting framework Lead other teams involved in using the final reported data from the enhanced reporting framework Mentor the concerned team from engineering on how to maintain the platform and make it sustainable. Provide necessary training for the concerned Monitoring and Evaluation Unit to properly utilize the values of the platform. Harmonize development and delivery stages with agile based practices being exercised within the NID. National ID Program, Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest to provide the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services for a period of one year with possibility of extension for additional period subject to outstanding performance of the consultant and availability of budget. The shortlisting criteria include the following; Bachelor's degree with a minimum of 7 years’ experience or Master's degree with 5 years’ experience in any Engineering, Computer, Information Systems, Business analysis, or related field. Proven experience as a Business Analyst, preferably in a technology company working on digital identity solutions or government projects. Strong understanding of Business Analysis principles, methodologies, and best practices. Experience in the usage of reporting frameworks, and reporting tools, including integration as well as developing customizations. Extensive experience on Reporting and data visualization tools such as Elasticsearch, Metabase, and Kibana Experience on data management systems such as PostGreSQL Experience with data change capture and transmission tools such as Debezium, Kafka, and ActiveMQ as well as their integrations. Familiarity with agile development methodologies, such as Scrum or Kanban. Familiarity with and experience in the Ethiopian technology landscape and knowledge of the National ID Program are highly desirable. title: Assisting ECA to issue further class licenses and authorizations in specific market segments, including broadcasting - ECA
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Country : Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Name of Project : Ethiopian Digital Foundation Project (EDFP) Credit No.: IDA 68560 Assignment Title: Assisting ECA to issue further class licenses and authorizations in specific market segments, including broadcasting – ECA Reference No .: MINT/DE/QCBS/C-22/21 The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia digital foundation project (EDFP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include Assisting ECA to issue further class licenses and authorizations in specific market segments, including broadcasting - ECA Introduction The telecommunications sector in Ethiopia is currently experiencing a transformative shift, driven by technological advancements and increased competition among service providers. As the market evolves, the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) recognizes the critical need for a clear and comprehensive guidelines for class licensing. This guidelines will serve to streamline licensing processes, enhance regulatory compliance, and ensure robust consumer protection. By establishing comprehensive guidelines, the ECA aims to create an environment that fosters innovation and facilitates the growth of diverse telecommunications services. Purpose of the ToR The purpose of this Terms of Reference (ToR) is to outline the framework for engaging a consulting firm to develop Class License Guidelines for telecommunications services in Ethiopia. This document aims to provide a clear understanding of the objectives, scope, and expectations for the consultancy assignment. It serves as a guiding framework for the consulting firm and the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) to collaboratively work towards establishing effective class licensing regulations that support market growth and consumer interests. Background The Ethiopian telecommunications market is undergoing significant changes, characterized by the introduction of new technologies and the entry of multiple operators. Currently, the licensing framework is primarily focused on individual licenses, which has led to inefficiencies that hinder market entry and stifle innovation. In response to these challenges, the ECA is committed to developing comprehensive Class License Guidelines that will clearly define the requirements, rights, and obligations associated with class licenses. This initiative aims to simplify the licensing process, improve regulatory compliance, and promote a competitive market that fosters investment and technological advancements. Through the establishment of effective Class License Guidelines, the ECA seeks to empower service providers, enhance operational efficiencies, and ultimately contribute to the overall development of the telecommunications industry in the country. Objectives The primary objective of this consultancy is to develop comprehensive Class License Guidelines that will simplify and streamline the licensing process for telecommunications services in Ethiopia. These guidelines aim to enhance regulatory clarity, promote a competitive telecommunications environment, and ensure that the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) can effectively manage and oversee the licensing of multiple operators offering similar services. The new framework will reduce administrative complexity while maintaining the necessary regulatory oversight to protect consumers and ensure high standards of service. Specific Objectives: Streamline the Licensing Process: One of the key objectives is to create a simplified and efficient licensing process that reduces barriers to entry for new operators while ensuring compliance with regulatory standards. The class license framework will enable operators offering similar services to follow a uniform licensing process, minimizing the need for case-by-case evaluations, which can be time-consuming and complex. Define Services Eligible for Class Licenses: Establish Regulatory Requirements and Obligations: Promote Fair Competition: Encourage Investment and Innovation : Enhance Regulatory Oversight and Compliance : Facilitate Stakeholder Engagement : Align with International Best Practices : 4 . Scope of Work The consulting firm will be responsible for completing the following tasks to ensure the successful development of comprehensive Class License Guidelines for telecommunications services in Ethiopia. Review of Existing Framework Conduct an in-depth analysis of the current telecommunications regulatory and licensing framework in Ethiopia. Identify the existing laws, regulations, and directives related to telecommunications licensing, especially focusing on class licenses. Review any gaps, challenges, and opportunities for improvement in the existing framework. Benchmark the current framework against international best practices for class licensing, particularly in countries with similar market characteristics. Define Class License Services and Criteria Develop clear definitions for the types of telecommunications services that will fall under class licensing, distinguishing them from services requiring individual licenses. Establish criteria for which operators or services will qualify for a class license, ensuring consistency with regulatory goals such as market entry facilitation, competition promotion, and innovation encouragement. Propose a classification system for service types, ensuring each category aligns with national objectives for telecommunications development. Application and Issuance Process Development Design streamlined application procedures for obtaining a class license, focusing on transparency, simplicity, and efficiency. Develop a step-by-step guide for the issuance process, including application submission, review timelines, required documentation, and evaluation criteria. Propose digital/online solutions for application submissions to modernize and simplify the process for applicants. Outline clear pathways for the renewal, modification, or transfer of class licenses to ensure operational continuity and flexibility. Class License Fee Proposal Review Existing Fee Structures : Analyze current regulatory fees in Ethiopia’s telecommunications sector and compare them with other countries to establish benchmarks. Evaluate the effectiveness of existing fees in covering regulatory costs and promoting competition Propose Class License Fee Structure: Develop a fee structure for class licenses based on a thorough analysis of market conditions, operational costs, and international benchmarks. Justification of Fees: Provide a detailed rationale for the proposed fees, considering factors such as the expected impact on market entry, operator capacity, and regulatory sustainability. Compliance, Reporting, and Monitoring Framework Define the regulatory obligations and compliance requirements for class license holders, ensuring they meet technical, financial, and operational standards. Develop a reporting framework for class licensees, including mandatory reporting periods, key performance indicators (KPIs), and service quality metrics. Propose a system for monitoring compliance, ensuring that class licensees adhere to national and international telecommunications standards. Create methods for periodic audits and inspections to ensure ongoing compliance without burdening the operators. Enforcement Mechanisms and Dispute Resolution Propose a fair and transparent system for enforcing compliance, outlining specific sanctions, penalties, and corrective actions for license violations. Develop a dispute resolution mechanism for handling grievances from licensees, consumers, or other stakeholders, ensuring due process and fair outcomes. Establish protocols for the suspension, revocation, or modification of licenses in cases of non-compliance or regulatory breaches, including clear appeals procedures. Stakeholder Consultation and Engagement Conduct a series of consultations with key stakeholders, including telecommunications operators, regulatory authorities, consumer associations, and industry experts. Organize workshops, interviews, and focus group discussions to gather input on the draft guidelines and licensing criteria. Ensure stakeholder concerns are integrated into the guideline development process, promoting transparency, inclusiveness, and collaboration. Drafting of Guidelines Develop a comprehensive draft of the Class License Guidelines that details all aspects of the licensing process, including application, issuance, compliance, and enforcement. Ensure the draft guidelines reflect both international best practices and the unique needs of the Ethiopian telecommunications market. Create clear and precise documentation that is legally sound and accessible to both operators and regulatory staff. Validation Workshops Organize validation workshops with key stakeholders, including the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA), operators, and industry representatives. Present the draft guidelines for review, soliciting feedback and suggestions to refine the document. Incorporate feedback from the validation workshops into the final version of the Class License Guidelines. Finalization of Guidelines Submit the finalized version of the Class License Guidelines to the ECA after incorporating all stakeholder feedback and validation workshop results. Ensure that the final guidelines include clear implementation procedures, roles, and responsibilities for both licensees and the ECA. Provide supporting documents such as an implementation roadmap and a monitoring and evaluation framework. Training and Capacity Building for ECA Design and deliver training sessions for ECA staff on the new Class License Guidelines, covering all aspects of licensing, compliance, and enforcement. Provide training materials, manuals, and other supporting documents to help ECA personnel effectively manage the new framework. Develop a capacity-building plan to ensure ECA staff are well-prepared to implement and monitor the class licensing regime in the long term. Reference No. ET-EEP-454958-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia /Recipient/ has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Power Sector Reform, Investment and Modernization in Ethiopia (PRIME-1) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include but not necessarily limited to hereafter to overall detail study of Resettlement plans /RPs/ in the target project areas. Consultant’s investigation for the resettlement action plan involves conducting census of the affected persons and assessing socioeconomic conditions, identifying the vulnerable groups including special assistance they require, examining the legal framework, evaluating impact on land and natural resources (both private and public), assess the scope of displacement (economic and physical) and involuntary resettlement, conducting stakeholder analysis, developing livelihood restoration measures, establishing a functional grievance redress mechanism, and designing a monitoring and evaluation framework. Overall, the scope of work includes preparing a separate RP report for each of the four (4) projects mentioned above. The Ethiopian Electric Power (EEP) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Core business and years in business ; Relevant Experience in the field of assignment; and Technical and managerial capability of the firm. Individual experts’ bio data/CV is not required and Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The shortlist will contain five to eight firms. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (“Procurement Regulations”), dated July 2016 and revised in September 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT) Financial Officer to support the Program Management Unit (PMU) at the Digital ID Program Country: Ethiopia Project: Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Project ID: P179040 Credit No: 7463-ET Assignment Title: Finance Officer Reference No.: ET-NIDP-457247-CS-INDV 1. Background The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. National ID Program, the project implementer intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting and employment of individual consultant on Finance officer Post . Experienced individual consultants who have the required qualification and experience for the position of Finance Officer are invited to express their interest for the assignment. 2. Scope of Services, Tasks, and Expected Deliverables Specific tasks to be carried out by the Financial Officer include but are not limited to the following components: Overall Management Execute the overall financial management for the project consistent with agreements, manuals, and project documents; Work closely with the Financial Management Specialist on all financial management arrangements including budgeting, accounting, internal controls, fund flows, reporting, and audit reporting. Budgeting and Planning Involve in all budgets, including annual planning and budgeting, Support the process so that the project budget is proclaimed in the government budget; Maintain budget discipline; Report to Finance Management Specialist on variances from the established budget, and the reasons for those variances; Assist the submission of budget to secure all budgetary issues are captured in accordance to the development partners as appropriate; Accounting and Reporting Implement adequate financial management systems and procedures of the project; Ensure that books of accounts are maintained; maintain up to date and documented accounting system and policies and procedures; Support the periodic financial reporting for development partners as well as for the government as per reporting requirements and formats. Work professionally that unaudited financial reports are prepared to the financiers on time and up to standards; Funds Management Participate in mitigating financial risks; Comply and implement development partners’ disbursement procedures for the project as per agreements/requirements; Collect bank advice, and bank statements and prepare bank reconciliations on time. Internal controls Follow an internal control system on petty cash and bank management; Participate in safeguarding of assets and properties (including fixed assets and inventories); Handle monthly employee salary, manage income tax, and pension contribution Manage timely settlement of advances and prepayments and payables Timely report to the tax authority and other government organizations External and Internal Audit Support that internal and external audits are arranged as per the agreements; Ensure that all documents are ready for auditors as the need arises Support both External and Internal auditors during the stay of the auditors 3. Required Qualifications The candidate should have a minimum qualification of a Bachelor’s Degree (Master’s or above is preferred) in finance or accounting, and a minimum of 4+ years of progressively responsible experience for a major company, government, or non-government institution. The candidates should have prior experience in implementing World Bank-funded projects/programs for at least 3 years. Preference will be given to candidates with the Chartered Certified Public Accountant or Certified Management Accountant designations. Excellent communication skills are essential, particularly regarding presenting results of analyses to management. Ability to use Accounting Software such as IFMIS (Integrated Financial Management System), Peachtree accounting spreadsheets, and databases. Fluency in English and Amharic languages. The candidate must have the highest levels of personal integrity, and a reputation for a transparent and systematic work style; and The candidate must be able to work under pressure and willing to work on additional assignments assigned by NIDP/PMU. 4. Duration of Services The consultant will be hired full time initially for the contract period of twelve (12) months with possibility of extension based on performance and availability budget. 5. Salary :Negotiable 6. Reporting The individual consultant will be directly reporting to the PMU Coordinator, National ID Program. 7. Selection Method The selection method is based on para 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation. The attention of interested individual is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”) revised November 2017 and August 2018, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. title: Consultancy Service for Development of National Digital Risk Information Platform (NDRIP) for the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC)
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST ETHIOPIAN DISASTER RISK MANAGEMENT COMMISSION (EDRMC) Project No. P176327 Grant No.: E124-ET Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Development of National Digital Risk Information Platform (NDRIP) for the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC). Reference No.: ET-EDRMC-400530-CS-QCBS The Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Flood Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds Consultancy Service for Development of National Digital Risk Information Platform (NDRIP) for the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC). General Objective: The main purpose of the consultancy service is to develop a unified, robust, and user-friendly National Digital Risk Information Platform (NDRIP) to manage and share geospatial disaster risk information among government agencies and the public. Specific objectives: To design and develop a secure and scalable digital platform that can accommodate various types of risk level data and information for hazard types such like Flood, Drought, land slide, earthquake and wild fire. To implement data management functionalities, including data collection, storage, and retrieval. To develop data analysis and visualization tools to facilitate risk assessment and decision-making processes. To integrate mechanisms for real-time data updates and alerts to enhance situational awareness. To provide training and technical support to EDRMC staff and other relevant stakeholders for effective utilization of the NDRIP. Scope of Service: Conduct a gap analysis. Prepare needed technical specification for the relevant goods & systems to be procured under the Flood Management Project Design and develop the NDRIP Develop data analysis and visualization tools, including risk mapping and reporting capabilities. Design and incorporate user-friendly interfaces and intuitive navigation. Train the NDRIP’s key users, including preparation of users’ manuals for effective utilization of the NDRIP. The study team arrangements proposed in detail will be included in the Term of Reference. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained through e-mail when you request at the address given below. The Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information, including firm profile and brochures, demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The short-listing criteria are: Core Business (Areas of Expertise) Years in Business Experience in Similar Assignments Technical and Managerial Capability Key Experts will not be evaluated at the short-listing stage and, accordingly, CVs should not be submitted. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs,3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016 , revised November 2017, July 2018, November 2020 and September 2023) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultancy firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or a Sub-Consultancy . In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the selection based on Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: - 8:30 AM – 12:30 PM and 1:30 PM – 5:30 PM from Monday to Thursday and office hours on Fridays are 8:30 AM – 11:30 AM and 1:30 PM – 5:30 PM. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by not later than November 05, 2024 at 5:30 PM . Attn: Ato Haile Assefa (Senior Project Procurement Expert) and Ato Yared Amde (Project Coordinator) Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC); Email: haile.assefa2023@gmail.com Email: amde.yares@gmail.com Physical address: Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC) Office located at Nifas silk Lafto sub city, on the road Gotera to Saris next to Nifas Silk Polytechnic Collage, 1st Floor, Room No. 52, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

title: Contract staff hiring for key the position of Internal Auditor Specialist
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL NATIONAL) FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA ETHIOPIA FLOOD MANAGEMENT PROJECT (E-FMP) Grant No. E124-Et Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Individual consultant (IC) – Internal Audit Specialist for the ET-Flood Management Project -Management Unit (PMU). (Procurement Ref. ET-MOWE-411365-CS-INDV) The Government of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Flood Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include: provision of Financial Audit consultancy service to Ministry of Water and Energy (MoWE) as a general and in the E-FMP PMU. The Internal Auditor is to deliver expertise in Auditing activities of the E-FMP, under the Ministry of Water and Energy, E-FMP PMU program. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT: The objective of the audit of the Project financial statements (PFSs) is to enable the auditors to express an independent professional opinion on the financial position of the Project semiannually; and to ensure that the funds granted to the Project have been used for their intended purposes. SCOPE OF SERVICE The Internal Auditor will be dedicated to the EFM project, and will have the following duties and responsibilities but not necessarily limited to the following: Plan and perform audits for Flood Management Project Designs the audit plan for Flood Management Project with clear timelines; Develop audit processes and guidelines, standard tools and procedures to improve quality and effectiveness of deliverables as per the world Bank requirement Liaise with Internal Audit Department of the MoWE to ensure Annual Audit Plan Follow up and Ensure timely implementation of external audit recommendations as well as timely implementation of World Bank supervision mission recommendations; In collaboration with MOWE internal auditor and administrative staff ensure project complies with World Bank and Government of Ethiopia guidelines/ requirements; Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the adequacy and effectiveness of the accounting and overall internal control system to monitor expenditures and other financial transactions and ensure safe custody of project-financed assets and that they are being used for the intended purposes To assure that Special accounts have been maintained in accordance with the provisions of the financing agreement and in accordance with the Bank’s disbursement rules and procedures Auditor has to assure the effectiveness of operations, the reliability of financial reporting, deterring, and investigating fraud, safeguarding assets, and compliance with laws and regulations Give assurance that Bank funds have been used in accordance with the conditions of the financing agreement, with due attention to economy and efficiency and only for the purposes for which the funds were provided Verify Counterpart contribution (government budget) have been provided timely and used in accordance with the conditions of the Finance agreement, with due attention to economy and efficiency and only for the purposes for which they were provided; To insure goods, works and services financed have been procured in accordance with the FA and in accordance with the Bank’s rules and procedures; and have been properly accounted for To check appropriate supporting documents, records and books of accounts relating to all project activities have been kept, Clear linkages should exist between the books of accounts and the financial statements presented to the Bank Keep audit documentations according to established standards; perform any other related tasks as may be assigned. DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT The assignment will be for one year with possibility of extension based on evaluation of performance. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS/COMPETENCES The following skills are essential for this work: Required Qualification : BA/MA in Accounting and finance and related field from recognized universities Having Specific experience of at least 6 years in internal audit of World Bank and/or other development partners projects with additional of 3 years’ experience in financial management systems Experience: - 8 years for B.Sc. and 6 years for M.Sc. and above relevant work experience. Professional Accounting qualification and membership such as ACCA, CPA, CFA and CA will be an added advantage. At least eight (8) years’ experience in financial management, financial analysis and accounting, out of which three (3) years should have been spent in financial management systems at a project financed by Development partners such as the World Bank, AfDB, UN grants , etc and with at least 2 years internal audit experience Analytical skills Must be computer literate, preferably with knowledge of computer accounting packages like Peachtree proficiency of IFMIS has an added advantage The Project Accountant shall undertake the assignment on a full-time contract basis renewed yearly subject to satisfactory performance as shall be determined during the annual performance evaluations. Fluency in English and Amharic languages RESPONSIBILITY OF THE EMPLOYER The Employer- client will: Avail all necessary data and document available Facilitate to have access to data and documents available in the government’s institutions. Provide office facilities (Computers, space, table, and chair) Provide transportation for field visits Facilitate and organize stakeholders’ workshop MANAGEMENT PROCEDURES Contractually, the Individual consultant will report to the PMU Coordinator and work closely with other PMU staff. And shall also work closely with the World Bank’s, EMI, EDRMC /PIT/PCU Task Team Leader (Ethiopia) and other designated World Bank staff and consultants REPORTING The internal auditor reports to the PMU coordinator Submits reports of the field visits, workshops and meeting results (minutes) within agreed time frame Reports monthly, quarterly, and yearly project status. Communicational skills, both written and verbal. The Ministry of water and Energy now invites eligible “Individual Consultants” to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 updated in November 2020.Procurement will also comply with “Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants” revised as of July 1, 2016. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the individual consultants Selection method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 9:00 am to 12:00 noon and 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm from Monday to Friday Interested individual consultants may submit their CVs and credentials with written applicant to the address below (in person, by mail, or by e-mail) on or before 30 September 2024, 4:00 pm. title: Senior DevOps Expert
buyer: Prime Minster Office, National ID Program
notice_text: Expression of Interest (EOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT) Senior DevOps Expert to support the National ID Program at the Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project (P179040). The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, DIGITAL ID PROJECT Position: Senior DevOps Expert Ref. No: ET-NIDP-439413-CS-INDV Organization: National ID Program Project: Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Location: Addis Ababa Duration: 12 months, with a possible extension Expected Start Date: September, 2024 Application method: Submit expression of interest by e-mail to mesfin@id.gov.et 1. Background In Dec 2023, the Government of Ethiopia and the World Bank Group signed the financial agreement for the Ethiopia Digital ID Project . Digital ID is a USD 350 million, five-year initiative (2023-2029). The Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project (P179040) will support the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) to roll out Fayda, an inclusive and trusted digital foundational ID system and other digital public infrastructure. The Project will improve access to and delivery of public and private sector services and economic opportunities, especially for the most vulnerable, and to boost national resilience. The project pursues a holistic and multi-sectoral approach to digital development towards building a safe digital economy through five components. Component 2 focuses on Establishing Scalable and Secure Fayda ICT infrastructure, which includes software and biometric technologies. 2. Objective NIDP has developed a digital identification platform named Fayda based on the Modular Open-Source Identification Platform (MOSIP). The project is ongoing and scaling up its operations. As part of expanding the existing technical capabilities, the NIDP is seeking an experienced Senior DevOps Expert to lead the effort at NIDP to build a holistic DevOps culture utilizing associated tools, technologies and processes. 3. Main Responsibilities Overall, the Senior DevOps Expert will lead and assist the NIDP technical team enhance the currently ongoing efforts towards a comprehensive DevOps based technical environment and organization. Specific responsibilities for the Senior DevOps Expert will include, but are not limited to, the following activities: ·Study the current team organization process implementation and devise progressive stages to a fully transformed DevOps based working culture. Define NIDP’s baseline (current state) in practicing the DevOps culture including process characteristics and their nature. Plan and organize the team structure, activities, and involvement in project management activities. Set up tools and required infrastructure to automate the deployment, management and scalability of applications in container management platforms especially in Docker and Kubernetes Build repeatable technical methods to review, verify, validate and deploy the software code developed in the project. Lead the effort establishing the culture towards continuous improvement and build continuous integration, continuous development, and constant deployment pipeline (CI/CD Pipeline) Support teams manage code changes, track development progress, and make the software development process more efficient using Source control tools Git, GitLab, and Bitbucket Review the ongoing processes and practices for product development against adherence to standards and updating or creating new processes for improvement and minimizing the wastage and overheads. Encourage and build automated processes wherever possible. Identify and introduce refined processes for non-functional areas such as cyber security and quality assurance. Review the current process and environment for team coordination and communication within the team and external stakeholders. Select and deploy appropriate online and offline approaches as well as tools and technologies for a CI/CD pipeline. Build capabilities for concerned technical team members to strive for continuous improvement and build continuous integration, continuous development, and constant deployment pipeline (CI/CD Pipeline) Mentor and guide the team leads towards the planned changes along the DevOps culture. Deliver periodic reporting on the progress to NIDP’s management team.. 4. Qualifications Requirements The ideal candidate for the role of Senior DevOps Expert will bring the following competencies and skills: Bachelor Degree in a relevant technical discipline, including Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering. Over 15 years of extensive experience in the IT industry, with a dedicated focus of more than 10 years on cloud architecture and DevOps methodologies. Demonstrated proficiency in architecting, designing, deploying, and maintaining large-scale production systems across Private, Public, and Hybrid cloud environments. Successful contribution to various biometric based identification projects, including biometric device management (registration and authentication). Component 2 focuses on Establishing Scalable and Secure Fayda ICT infrastructure, which includes software and biometric technologies. 2. title:
Selection of a consulting firm that Develops a Plan for Implementing Mobile Number Portability,
Short Code Harmonization, and Migration Strategy
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Country : Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Name of Project : Ethiopian Digital Foundation Project (EDFP) Loan No.: IDA 68560 Assignment Title: To Hire a Consulting Firm to Develop Mobile number portability Implementation Plan, Review and Update the National Numbering Plan, Develop a National Short Code Plan, and Establish a Short Code Harmonization and Migration Plan Reference No .: ET-MINT-345612-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia digital foundation project (EDFP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include supporting ECA to Develop Mobile number portability Implementation Plan, Review and Update the National Numbering Plan, Develop a National Short Code Plan, and Establish a Short Code Harmonization and Migration Plan. Introduction The Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) serves as the regulatory body responsible for overseeing the telecommunications sector in Ethiopia. Given the rapid growth of this sector, it is of utmost importance for the ECA to prioritize the development of a comprehensive implementation plan for Mobile number portability. Additionally, the ECA recognizes the need to review and update the current national numbering plan, while ensuring the smooth harmonization and migration of short codes. To achieve these crucial objectives, the ECA will engage the services of a consulting firm to address the following terms of reference. The consulting firm will conduct a thorough analysis of the telecommunications sector in Ethiopia, aiming to identify any gaps and issues that may hinder the successful implementation of mobile number portability. Furthermore, the firm will be responsible for developing a detailed plan that outlines the necessary steps and timelines for implementing mobile number portability, considering international best practices and standards. Additionally, the consultancy will collaborate with relevant stakeholders to review and update the national numbering plan, ensuring its consistency with the evolving needs of the sector. This will enable seamless communications for both businesses and consumers. By engaging a consulting firm, the ECA aims to leverage their expertise and industry knowledge to drive the growth and development of the telecommunications sector in Ethiopia. Project Background The telecommunications industry is a dynamic and evolving sector that plays a vital role in facilitating communication and connectivity for individuals, businesses, and communities. As technology advances and consumer demands shift, regulatory frameworks and operational strategies within the industry need to adapt to ensure efficient and seamless services. In this context, the project aims to address key challenges and opportunities within the telecommunications sector by focusing on the development of essential plans related to mobile number portability (MNP), national numbering plan review, national short code plan development, and short code harmonization and migration planning. Mobile Number Portability (MNP) Implementation Plan Review and Update of the National Numbering Plan Development of a National Short Code Plan Short Code Harmonization and Migration Plan General Objective The general objectives of hiring a consulting firm to undertake tasks related to Mobile Number Portability (MNP), National Numbering Plan (NNP), National Short Code Plan (NSCP), and Short Code Harmonization and Migration Plan Specific Objective: Specific objectives for each task include the following: Development of Mobile Number Portability Implementation Plan Review and Update of the National Numbering Plan Development of a National Short Code Plan Establishment of a Short Code Harmonization and Migration Plan Provide Capacity Building Training for ECA Staff Scope of Work The consulting firm will be required to perform the following tasks to develop a comprehensive Mobile Number Portability (MNP) Implementation Plan. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.dfp.gov.et or can be obtained at the address given below. Ministry of Innovation and Technology- EDFP now invites eligible Consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are: core business and years in business, relevant experience, technical and managerial capability of the firm. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulation”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the QCBS (Quality and Cost Based Selection) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Interested and qualified consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours 08:30 to 12:00 & 14:30 to 17:00, Mondays to Thursdays; and 08:30 to 11:00 & 14:30 to 17:00 on Fridays. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) on or before August 23th, 2024. Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Innovation and Technology (MInT) ETHIOPIA DIGITAL FOUNDATIONS PROJECT Attn: Focal Person, Project Implementation Unit (PIU) Address: Arada Sub-city, Tracon Building 6th floor, in front of Tikur Anbesa Secondary School, Ato Habtamu Mekonen, Tel No. +251-913-050049, Email address: habtemek178@gmail.com Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

notice_text: Request for Bid (National) The federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Ministry of Agriculture – Resilient Landscape and Livelihood Project (RLLP) Project ID: P174385: Bid Reference No. ET-MOA-396156-GO-RFB Contract title: - Supply and Delivery of Farm Hand tools The federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Agriculture received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Resilient Landscape and Livelihood Project (RLLP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Supply and Delivery of Nursery Materials. The Ministry of Agriculture now invites sealed bids from eligible bidders for the following materials: Item No Description of Materials Quantity 1 Shovel Pcs 144,000 2 Pick Axe Pcs 144,000 3 Sprit level Pcs 4,730 4 String 2mm Pcs 1,440 5 Hammer 3kg Pcs 2,020 6 Hammer 2.5kg Pcs 2,090 7 Chopper/Gegera Pcs 4,800 8 Tap Meter (50m) Pcs 2,395 9 Crow Bar/ Dijino Pcs 2,400 10 Digging Hoe Pcs 10,150 Bidding will be conducted through National Request for Bidding (NRFB) procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers as indicated in ‘Procurement in Investment Project Financing, Goods, Works, Non-Consulting, and Consulting Services’, Fourth Edition, November 2020, and the World Bank’s ‘Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants’, revised as of July 1, 2016 all eligible bidders as defined in the procurement regulation. Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from Ministry of Agriculture Procurement Executive Block A, 2nd Floor, or SLMP project office Block B, 2nd floor and inspect the bidding documents during office hours 9:00 to 12:00 A.M and 2:00 to 5:00 P.M at the address given bellow. Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from Ministry of Agriculture Procurement Executive Block A, 2nd Floor, or RLLP project office Block B, 2nd floor and inspect the bidding documents during office hours 9:00 to 12:00 A.M and 2:00 to 5:00 P.M at the address given bellow. A complete set of bidding documents in English may be purchased by interested eligible bidders up on the submission of the written application to the address below and upon payment of nonrefundable fee of Birr 100.00 or an equivalent amount. The method of payment should be bank transfer through account number 1000009144009 for the beneficiary of Ministry of Agriculture. Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before August 22, 2024 at 2:00P.M. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. Late bids will be rejected. Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the bidder's representatives and anyone who interested to attend at the address below on August 22, 2024 at 2:15 PM. All bids must be accompanied by a bid security amounting ETB 450,000.00 for all items in a freely convertible currency in the form of CPO or unconditional bank guarantee. Insurance guarantee is not acceptable. title: Financial Advisor
buyer: Prime Minster Office, National ID Program
notice_text: Expression of Interest (EOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT) Financial Advisor to Support the Digital ID Program. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Digital ID Project Position: Financial Advisor Ref. No: ET-NIDP-436726-CS-INDV Organization: NIDP Project: Ethiopia Digital ID Project Location: Addis Ababa Duration: 12 months, with a possible extension Salary: Attractive/Negotiable Expected Start Date: September 2024 1. Background In Dec 2023, the Government of Ethiopia and the World Bank Group signed the financial agreement for the Ethiopia Digital ID Project . Digital ID is a USD 350 million, five-year initiative (2023-2029). The Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project (P179040) will support the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) to roll out Fayda, an inclusive and trusted digital foundational ID system and other digital public infrastructure. The Project will improve access to and delivery of public and private sector services and economic opportunities, especially for the most vulnerable, and to boost national resilience. 2. Context and objectives The objective of this assignment is to support the PMU with the proper financial advisor issues for all activities under its scope of the Digital ID Program and Digital ID Project. 3. Scope of Services, Tasks, and Expected Deliverables The Advisor will be expected to produce the following deliverables, among others include but are not limited to the following components: Ensure the application of proper accounting internal control systems and processes to facilitate financial monitoring and control in line with the Government guidelines and the World Bank financial reporting and auditing of projects; Assist in the preparation of operating budgets; Ensure that all supporting documents in respect of financial transactions are adequately authorized and has correct information; Ensure overall preparation of project accounting ledgers and project accounts in accordance with national and international best practices and standards; Ensure that books of accounts are maintained, maintain up to date and documented accounting system and policies and procedures; Ensure internal control arrangements are maintained consistently throughout the life of the program/project including proper controls with regard to approval and authorization, Review financial performance of the program/project and report on key issues to the respective management body, Review administrative bottlenecks and recommend changes to improve efficiency. Create additional analyses and reports as requested by management Ensures proper filing for all financial documents, Assist with audit preparation, and preparation of funder reports, Carries out any other tasks required by NIDP Management 4. Required Qualifications The qualification and experience required for applicant who would like to apply for the service should possess the following minimum criteria: The candidate should have Master’s degree in finance or accounting, and related fields, Minimum of 6+ years of progressively responsible experience for a major Company, Government or non-government institution, Knowledge on the Government financial procedures including the accounting systems like IFMIS, Clients Connection of the World Bank, etc. Prior experience in implementing World Bank funded project/programs, Preference will be given to candidates with the Chartered Certified Public Accountant or Certified Management Accountant designations, Excellent communication skills are essential, particularly in regard to presenting results of analyses to management, Fluency in English and Amharic languages The candidate must have the highest levels of personal integrity, and a reputation for a transparent and systematic work style; and The candidate must be able to work under pressure situations, in order to meet demanding deadlines. 5. Duration of Services The consultant will be hired full time initially for the contract period of twelve (12) months with possibility of extension based on performance and availability budget. 6. Remuneration Attractive/Negotiable, and based on the new directive of the Government. 7. Reporting: The individual consultant will be directly reporting to the NIDP Executive Director and working closely with the PMU Coordinator at National ID Program. 8. Selection Method The National ID Program now invites eligible individuals to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested individuals should send expressions of interest, together with information demonstrating that they have the required qualification and relevant experience to perform the service (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, qualifications, and so forth) by providing CVs, formal application letter and all supporting documents. The attention of interested individual is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations” ) revised November 2017 and August 2018 , setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest The Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant Section VII paragraphs, 7.34 to 7.37, set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained, by email at the address below during office hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM Addis Ababa time. Applicants should send expressions of interest, together with information demonstrating that they have the required qualification and relevant experience to perform the service (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, qualifications, and so forth) by providing CVs, formal application letter and all supporting documents to the address below in person, or by mail, on or before Aug 05, 2024 , but preferably by e-mail to be specified in the official announcement. Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, National ID Program (NIDP)- Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Attn: Project Management Unit (PMU) Address: Welosefer Bole, Ethio-China St, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, INSA Building, 15th Floor Tele- +251 911 791462 E-mail: mesfin@id.gov.et Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

title: Procurement Advisor for National ID Project at National ID Program (NIDP)
buyer: Prime Minster Office, National ID Program
notice_text: Expression Of Interest (EOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT) Procurement Advisor to Support the Digital ID Program for Inclusion and Services Project . The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Digital ID Project Position: Procurement Advisor Ref. No: ET-NIDP-425824-CS-INDV Organization: National ID Program Project: Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Location: Addis Ababa Duration: 12 months, with a possible extension Salary: Attractive/Negotiable Expected Start Date: September, 2024 1. Background In Dec 2023, the Government of Ethiopia and the World Bank Group signed the financing agreement for the implementation of Ethiopia Digital ID Project . Digital ID is a USD 350 million, five-year initiative (2023-2029). The Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project (P179040) will support the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) to roll out Fayda, an inclusive and trusted digital foundational ID system and other digital public infrastructure. The Project will improve access to and delivery of public and private sector services and economic opportunities, especially for the most vulnerable, and to boost national resilience. The project includes various complex and high value contracts to meet its objectives. 2. Context and objectives The objective of this assignment is to obtain the services of a highly qualified individual consultant who will advise NIDP in leading the procurement management in an efficient , professional and effective manner as well as to provide all the necessary capacity building for the procurement of goods, works and non-consulting services and consulting services required for the project. 3. Description of the Assignment The key role of the procurement advisor is to ensure that quality, completeness and timeliness of the procurement management of the project. Under the overall guidance of the project coordinator, the Procurement advisor has an advisory role with clear responsibility to check and ensure that quality and complete procurement plan, procurement documents, evaluation reports, draft contracts and progress reports are prepared and ensure that the planned procurement activities are implemented without any delays. 4. Scope of Services, Tasks, and Expected Deliverables The Advisor will be expected to produce the following deliverables, among others include but are not limited to the following components: The advisor should be versed in and work independently to ensure the procurements are conducted in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation (recent edition) and the financing agreement. Coordinate with the project coordinator and ensure that suitable procurement and contract management organization and system is established in the project office. Leading and managing the procurement management of the Project for procurement of goods, works and non-consulting and consulting services in accordance with agreed procurement procedures for the project. Ensure that the PPSD is regularly reviewed considering the changes and needs during the implementation of the project by analyzing the market situation and any changes that require the revision of the PPSD. Review all procurement documentation, including procurement plans, ToRs, Request for expressions of interest, Invitation of Bid, Bidding documents, Request for Proposals, shortlisting reports, technical and combined proposals evaluation reports, negotiated contracts and ensure quality and completeness of these documents Review of technical, legal and commercial aspects of procurement (in consultation with others as necessary) at all stages of the project cycle, including planning, reasonable of cost estimate, contract duration, design, implementation and management; Lead, initiate and coordinate training for implementing agencies in procurement with particular focus on the World Bank procurement regulations. Lead the development of procurement processing, monitoring and reporting system and taking a lead in the preparation of quarterly reports on the status of procurement activities in the Project. Attending and contributing to procurement enquiries and complaints by bidders/consultants and ensue appropriate responses on time are provided to the complainants. Carry out a review to identify constraints and opportunities to the effective and efficient procurement and contract administration of works, goods and consultancies required for the project and an implementation capacity assessment to identify gaps. Participate in different supervision and support missions; lead consolidation of complete progress report, procurement challenges and recommendation to improve the implementation of procurement. Lead and carry out effective coordination and timely delivery of and put in place systems to guide procurement management and monitoring the performance of procurement activities of the project. Producing compiled reports on regular basis in accordance with reporting requirements to be forwarded to the concerned stakeholders. Ensure planned procurement activities are initiated timely and all milestones are performed in accordance with the timelines indicated in the procurement plan Assist in resolution of complex procurement issues, including questions and complaints from firms; and Monitor completed procurements to ensure the contracted firms meet expectations; and Oversight the uploading of complete and quality procurement documents in STEP at each stage of the procurement process. Assist in the preparation of procurement related activities of the project; Ensure that all supporting documents in respect of procurement are adequately authorized and has correct information; Oversight the procurement processes and contract administrations of each activity and ensure they are performed timely, in quality and with the estimated/contract amount. Carries out any other tasks required by NIDP Management 5. Required Qualifications The qualification and experience required for applicant who would like to apply for the service should possess the following minimum criteria: A Master’s degree in Marketing Management, Engineering, Procurement and Supplies Management, accounting, Law, and related fields, 8 years of progressively responsible experience in public procurement, especially in the projects financed by the Multilateral financiers Knowledge on the Government procurement rules and procedures. Prior experience in implementing World Bank funded project/programs, knowledge on the World Bank Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) and experience working on STEP is an added advantage, Working experience on the IT procurement is an added advantage. Excellent communication skills are essential, particularly in regard to presenting results of analyses to management, Fluency in English and Amharic languages The candidate must have the highest levels of personal integrity, and a reputation for a transparent and systematic work style; and The candidate must be able to work under pressure situations, in order to meet demanding deadlines. 6. Duration of Services The consultant will be hired full time initially for the contract period of twelve (12) months with possibility of extension based on performance and availability budget. 7. Remuneration Attractive/Negotiable and depends on qualification and experience of the candidate. 8. Reporting: The individual consultant will be directly reporting to the NIDP Executive Director and working closely with the PMU Coordinator at National ID Program. 9. Selection Method The selection method is based on para 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation. The attention of interested individual is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”) revised November 2017 and August 2018 (September 2023), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained, by email at the address below during office hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM Addis Ababa time. Applicants should send expressions of interest, together with information demonstrating that they have the required qualification and relevant experience to perform the service (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, qualifications, and so forth) by providing CVs, formal application letter and all supporting documents to the address below in person, or by mail, on or before Aug. 05, 2024 , but preferably by e-mail to be specified in the official announcement. title: Strategic Education Consultant
notice_text: Request for Expression of Interest (Consulting Services – Individual Consultant Selection) Selection of Strategic Education Consultant to support the Program Implementation Unit at the Education for Skills and Employability, Office of the Ministry of Labor and Skills Services (P17 7881) GOVERNMENT OF THE FEDERAL REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA Ministry of Labor and Skills (MoLs) Education and Skills for Employment (EASE) Terms of Reference (ToR) for Strategic Education Consultant Position: Strategic Education Consultant Duty station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia BACKGROUND The Ministry of Labor and Skills (MoLs) is implementing the Education and Skills for Employment (EASE). EASE is a national project that focuses on practical, work-related skills to enhance employability of youth in Ethiopia while addressing skills constraints to respond and adapt to megatrends. Through a well-functioning TVET system, the project will support better alignment of skills supply and demand and adjust offerings to meet the demands of the changing labor market. The Project is thus expected to help Ethiopia meet the Sustainable Development Goal of “promoting sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all.”. The objectives and results of the project will be achieved through: Strengthening public polytechnics for improved labor market outcomes Support short-term skills programs through a competitive and performance-based financing model that links payments to the employment outcomes. System Strengthening OBJECTIVE OF THE Assignment Establishing the National Delivery Unit (DU) is one of the primary task to coordinate and effectively implement the project in conjunction with the relevant functional structure of the ministry and the PIU, Mols hereby invites applications from qualified candidates for the position of Strategic Education Consultant . The appointment of the specialist will expedite project implementation at the Ministry. The specialist is specifically mandated to provide strategic guidance and support in the development and implementation of education and skill development initiatives under the project. The consultant will focus on fostering innovative skill development strategies, , collaborating with stakeholders, setting strategic priorities, mitigating risks, developing innovative training plans that can be be piloted at the selected poly technique collages . 3. Duties and Responsibilities Conducting an analysis of the current education and skills landscape in Ethiopia, including an assessment of skills gaps, labor market trends, and industry needs. Developing a strategic plan and roadmap for the implementation of the EASE project, including clear objectives, targets, and key performance indicators. Providing technical guidance on the design and implementation of performance-based financing models for short-term skills programs, including monitoring and evaluation mechanisms. Supporting the strengthening of public polytechnics through curriculum development, teacher training, infrastructure upgrades, and quality assurance mechanisms. Facilitating stakeholder consultations and workshops to gather input and feedback on the strategic direction of the project. Monitoring progress and evaluating the impact of interventions, and making recommendations for adjustments and improvements as needed. Providing capacity building and training to Ministry staff and project partners on strategic planning, education policy, and best practices in skills development. Develop and oversee growth strategies to advance the goals of the program. Strengthen core programs to maintain a competitive advantage in the education and skill development landscape. Formulate educational strategies to foster collaboration with internal and external stakeholders. - Establish and review key strategic educational priorities and translate them into actionable plans. Mitigate potential risks associated with strategic planning and program execution. Develop individual educational plans to promote educational and social development among trainees. Establish and communicate clear objectives to TVET trainers and administrators. Facilitate monitoring and evaluation work for various teaching skill-building projects. Facilitate the development of training materials for TVET trainers and administrators. Build annual and long-term strategic plans to guide program implementation. Collaborate with consultants to develop educational reform plans aligned with program objectives. Advise industry and TVETs on training matters to ensure relevance and effectiveness. Develop appropriate goals for TVET institutions and industries affiliated with training institutions. Design and facilitate educational forums focused on training quality improvement, innovation and technology transfers. Innovate approaches to improve trainees' achievement and success. Formulate and propose new assessment techniques to ensure a quality learning experience for trainees. 4. Deliverables: Growth strategies and plans for advancing program objectives. Strengthened core programs with documented improvements and outcomes. Formulated educational strategies and collaborations with stakeholders. Strategic educational priorities translated into actionable plans. Risk mitigation strategies and contingency plans. Individual educational plans promoting trainee development. Clear objectives communicated to TVET trainers and administrators. Monitoring and evaluation reports on teaching skill-building projects. Developed training materials for TVET stakeholders. Annual and long-term strategic plans for program implementation. Educational reform plans in collaboration with consultants. Advisories on training matters for industry and TVETs. Goals set for schools and educational institutions. Educational forums designed and facilitated for quality improvement. Innovative approaches proposed to enhance trainees' achievement. New assessment techniques proposed for quality learning experiences. 5. Duration: The length of this position is initially for one year and subject to the satisfactory performance; the contract period shall be extendable. 6. Qualifications : - Advanced degree in education, Science Degree, workforce development, or a related field and with work experience minimum of 5 years for BA or 3 years for MA. In addition to the qualifications the applicant must have: Extensive experience in strategic planning and program development in the education sector. Proven track record of fostering collaborations and partnerships with stakeholders. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to mitigate risks and devise effective solutions. Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas clearly and concisely. Demonstrated ability to innovate and adapt approaches to meet evolving needs and challenges. - Experience in monitoring and evaluation, curriculum development, and training facilitation is desirable. 7. Reporting : The consultant will report to the delivery unit coordinator within the Ministry of Labor and Skills, providing regular updates on progress and deliverables. 8. INPUTS PROVIDED BY THE EMPLOYER The employer will avail office furniture, office equipment, communication facilities and other materials required by the Finance specialist to perform his/her duties as specified in this TORs. 9. LEVEL OF EFFORT AND TIMETABLE It is expected that the assignment will start as soon as possible depending on availability. The Specialist will be based at Mols with travel to regional cities as necessary. Contract: one-year contract, with possible extension upon satisfactory performance of the Specialist. Remunerations: Negotiable / dependent on qualifications and experience. DEADLINE OF SUBMISSION Within 10 working days from date of announcement. title: Selection and Employment of #2 Procurement Specialist for Regional WaSH, by Amahara region Bureau of Water and Energy.
notice_text: VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT Amhara National Regional State Water & Energy bureau One WaSH National Program- Consolidated WaSH Account Phase II The Government of Ethiopia has received loan and grant from different funding/lending agencies through One WaSH National Program Consolidated WaSH Account Phase-II (OWNP CWA-II) towards the cost of water supply and Sanitation and hygiene and intends to apply a portion of this loan and grant to eligible payments under this contract. The Water supply and sanitation Program Management Unit Coordinator with the collaboration of WASH Procurement and Contract Administration Team leader would affirm that work plans drawn by the Senior Procurement Specialist in order to discharge their contracted duties are logically compatible with their respective job descriptions and would monitor that the planned services are delivered by the expert in a manner in line with the objective of the project/program. Specific Duties and responsibility Reports to and work closely with the Regional PMU coordinator. Get acquainted with the WaSH legal documents: Review and get acquainted with the OWNP and WaSH project implementation documents: The CWA II POM, other manuals, region specific implementation plans and assist woredas and towns to adhere to these documents during project implementation. Review the standard procurement documents prepared for the project, ensure the appropriate use of them by the implementing agencies and provide inputs for updating and enriching the documents. Review the procurement manual, prepares capacity building training materials and provide formal and on the job training for procurement staff at Woreda and town level on the application of the manual and standard procurement documents. Monitor adequacy of the number and qualification of procurement staff at Woreda and town level and recommend action and closely work with procurement staff Woreda and town levels. Review and Prepare procurement documents for the project, the bidding documents, bid evaluation reports and the Contract documents and give no objection based on the threshold limit of the project. Conduct frequent travel to woredas and towns (not less than 50% of the contract time) to review and ensure the quality of the Woreda and town procurement performance and reporting. Ensure that the program procurement plan, woreda and towns procurement plans are updated and maintained. Compile procurement plan of woredas, towns, and regions and forward to the MOWE for no objection. Visit all woredas and towns of the program in the region to review the procurement manual application and get feedback for the procurement manual and the POM improvement. Provide input to the regional PMUs quarterly report on procurement. Ensures the proper integration of the procurement information into the overall program monitoring and evaluation system. Provide assistance to the independent auditors as wells as to the World Bank’s procurement reviewers while reviewing procurement activities at Woreda, town and regional levels. Compile quality assured Procurement Plans and Contract Registers from woredas and Towns. Prepare procurement process tracking and follow-up system, and prepare contract status tracking system, and monitor and report on procurement and contract activities. Organize, Support and implement all procurement activities at regional level based on the applicable procurement procedures. Keep records of procurement document In addition to the above-mentioned activities, the Procurement Specialist performs other related and relevant assignments. Duration of the Assignment : The assignment will be for one year with possibility of extension based on evaluation of performance Required Qualification and Work Experience The Specialist to be hired shall have of work experience in procurement and shall have BSc/BA /MSc/MA or above in Engineering or procurement and other related relevant fields with 10/8 years or above experience at least 3 years in the water supply and sanitation sub-sector with a high credit to experiences in procurement, analysis and development of Manuals and strategies for the sub-sector. Proven familiarity with World Bank procurement guidelines and procedures including the World Bank Standard Bidding Documents for procurement of goods, works and services. Strong capability of communication on the subject matter, and capacity to offer trainings. The Procurement specialist working within the team of PMU, the specialist will have responsibilities in all water supply and sanitation works and a lead responsibility for the outputs in that area. Reporting The specialist reports to the PMU under the water supply, and sanitation Directorate. Submits reports of the field visits, workshops and meeting results (minutes) within agreed time frame Reports monthly, quarterly, and yearly project status. Remuneration /Salary & Benefits / As per the scale of the program Place of Work Bahir Dar with frequent field works in the region. Senior Water Supply Engineer Quantity: 1(One) Roles and Responsibilities The role of the Senior Water Supply Engineer working under the OWNP CWA Phase II is to support & facilitate the effective implementation of the Water Supply, Hygiene & Sanitation Program.
