As such, under the WASH program the role of The Senior Water Supply Engineer will be to support the National PMU in communicating with Regional PMUs, Woreda WASH Team and Town Water Utilities and providing them with the directions, information, systems and skills. The Water supply and sanitation Program Management Unit Coordinator would affirm that work plans drawn by the Senior Water Supply Engineering order to discharge their contracted duties are logically compatible with their respective job descriptions and would monitor that the planned services are delivered by the expert in a manner and in line with the objective of the project/program. Specific Duties and Responsibilities The Senior Water Supply Engineer will report to the Regional PMU Coordinator , Contribute to the overall Technical aspects of the rural and urban WSS project, including: planning, Implementation, follow up and monitoring of the contract effectiveness with respect to program Guide line, manuals & standards. Participate in the production or updating of the necessary manuals and guidelines; Support the regions, woredas and towns in the study and design of water supply projects Prepare training documents, training plans and deliver trainings in priority areas ; Identify the woredas and towns program gaps and management deficits and provides them with the technical assistance or the capacity development they require; Frequent field visit (60% of the assignment duration) and follows up the Program activities at all stages: pre design stage, design stage, construction tendering stage, construction stage, completion & handover stage & maintenance (liability) period Production of contract management & Supervision manual for the consumption of Regions, Woredas and town, particularly for contract administrator and construction supervisor; Assist the Regions /WWTs/Town Water Boards & Utilities in tender advertisement, analysis & award, evaluation, contract negotiation and Contract Signing and implementation; Follow up and assist the Regions, Woredas and towns on overall program management starting from ToR and RFP preparation, negotiation and agreement up to end of contract implementation and final acceptance of the project includes follow up of payment modality and payment certificate review etc.; Produce and submit monthly, bi-monthly and back to office report to the CWA Phase II-PMU and; Performs other related and relevant assignments Program Planning and Management Prepare the Regional PMUs annual plan and budget for the Regional CWA Phase II project; prepare and consolidation of quarterly progress reports Prepare an annual work plan for his support to the MOWE, CWA Phase II PMU, and support the Regions in the preparation of their own PMU work plans and budgets; Promote learning between woredas and between towns by sharing information, progress reports and best practices; Foster integration under the sanitation projects by supporting efforts to integrate water supply, and sanitation interventions and coordinate planning across sectors; Provide technical backup support to all planning and management activities of the NWSC and NWTT, Update data on WaSH physical and financial performance, including number of user communities and beneficiaries vs planned activities considering integration of sanitation performance. Timely track allocated budget, received, used and liquidated to get additional funding. Sector Training and Capacity Building Work extensively with Regional, Woreda and Town implementing agencies to ensure they have the necessary skills and trainings to perform their duties; Produce or update the necessary technical training materials and manuals for use by implementing agencies (e.g. Cost-effective designs, operation and maintenance, etc.); Produce or update the necessary program management training materials and manuals for use by implementing agencies (e.g. Procurement process, contract management, etc.); Provide technical backup support and training to WWT/Town Water Boards/Utilities (urban) during the early phase of project support (up to the first phase of construction); Duration of the Assignment: The assignment will be for one year with possibility of extension based on evaluation of performance Required Qualification and Work Experience The Specialist to be hired shall have experience in Design, construction supervision, assessment, analysis and development of Manuals and strategies of public services with a high credit to experiences in water supply and sanitation. Specialist shall have MSc or above in Water Supply Engineering, Sanitary Engineering, Hydraulic Engineering, Water Resource Engineering, Hydraulic and Hydropower Engineering, Water & Environmental Engineering, Irrigation Engineering, Civil Engineering fields with 8 years or above experience in the water supply and sanitation sub-sector with a high credit to experiences in Design construction, assessment, analysis and development of Manuals and strategies for the sub-sector. The specialist shall have strong capability of communication on the subject matter, and capacity to offer t rainings. Specialist will be contracted: Working within the team of the water supply and sanitation directorate, the specialist will have responsibilities in all water supply and sanitation works. The Specialists will be contracted and supervised by the PMU. Operationally will collaborate and work closely with the Federal, Regional Water Bureaus, WWTs, and Urban Water Boards and Utilities. Reporting The specialist reports to the PMU Submits reports of the field

title: Consultancy service for the Development of Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission's (EDRMC) Digital System for Tracking Progress Made on Disaster Risk Management (DRM)
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST ETHIOPIAN DISASTER RISK MANAGEMENT COMMISSION (EDRMC) Project No. P176327 Grant No.: E124-ET Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for the Development of Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC) Digital System for Tracking Progress Made on Disaster Risk Management (DRM). Reference No.: ET-EDRMC-400532-CS-QCBS The Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Flood Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds Consultancy Service for the Development of Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC) Digital System for Tracking Progress Made on Disaster Risk Management (DRM) . General Objective: The main purpose of the consultancy service is to develop a user-friendly and robust digital system that will enable EDRMC to effectively track and monitor progress made on DRM initiatives. Specific objectives: To provide accurate and up-to-date information on various DRM activities, including risk assessments, risk reduction, early warning systems, disaster response, recovery, and resilience-building efforts. To conduct a comprehensive assessment of EDRMC's existing DRM tracking processes and requirements. To design and develop a web-based digital system for tracking DRM progress. To integrate the digital system with relevant databases and information sources. Scope of Service: Conducting a comprehensive assessment of EDRMC's existing DRM tracking processes and requirements. Designing and developing a web-base that will serve as the digital system for tracking DRM progress. Integrating the digital system with relevant databases and information sources. Formulating M&E guidelines. Incorporating features for data analysis, reporting, and decision-making support. Conducting user testing and gathering feedback for system refinement. Providing training and technical support to EDRMC staff for system usage. The study team arrangements proposed in detail will be included in the Term of Reference. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained through e-mail when you request at the address given below. The Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services. title: Recruitment of Financial Management Specialist at MUI for FPCU
buyer: Ministry of Urban Development and Infrastructure
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES -INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) MINISTRY OF URBAN AND INFRASTRUCTURE URBAN FOOD SECURITY AND SAFETY NET OFFICE Urban Productive Safety Net and Job Project (UPSNJP) Grant Number D732-ET Assignment Title: Financial Management Specialist Ref #. ET-MUI-401086-CS-INDV Number of vacant position: One (1) The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (FDRE) has received financing from the World Bank to the cost of the Urban Productive Safety Net and Job Project (UPSNJP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Consulting Service (The Services) include to obtain the services of a qualified and experienced Financial Management Specialist who will assist in providing and expected to engage in collaboration with MoF, responsible for financial issues of the UPSNJP-financed activities through planning, budgeting and coordinating disbursement of funds of the City and its accountability according to finance and accounting regulations of the UPSNJP and achievement of project development objectives. In addition, capacity building and monitoring services to the federal implementers, regions and their respective UPSNJP cities in areas involving of local government finance, accounting and audit. The Financial Management Specialist among others will have the following duties and responsibilities: Reviews and gets acquainted with the Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project (UPSNJP) implementation documents: The project Implementation Manual (PIM), Financial Management (FM) and other manuals, region and City specific implementation plans. In conjunction with MoF, will involve in reviewing the financial management manual, prepare training materials and provide training to the UPSNJP accountants at the Regional Bureaus of Finance and Economic Development and Cities. Facilitates and ensures timely release and flow of resources to Project implementing agencies by writing fund flow release instruction to MoF based on the annual work plan and budget approved for the project. Ensure timely submission of expenditure documents of the Ministry to MoF. Prepares the Interim Financial Report (IFR) of the UFSSNO for the funds it has received and disbursed and submits to MoF within the set timeline. Prepare quarterly expenditure forecast and cash requirement. Prepare periodic Financial report and additional statement as per the UPSNJP Financial reporting relating to the ministry (as stated in the UPSNJP Financial Management Manual) Ensure that the Project budget and disbursement schedules are regularly updated and maintained. Ensure that proper financial records are maintained at the Ministry; Ensure the quality and consistency of all financial data reported by the Ministry; Reconcile monthly UPSNJP bank accounts managed by the Ministry with the bank statements. Strengthen the Capacity of UPSNJP accountants in collaboration and under guidance of MoF; Prepare annual consolidated financial statements as determined in the FM Manual and ensure that these are submitted to MoF for consolidation; Copy financial reports to MUI for proper follow-up of the implementation and the Project fund utilization; Assist regions and cities in producing and getting approval of annual work plan and budget Assist, together with MoF, regions and cities in submitting their financial statements on time; Assist regions in facilitating project audits and addressing audit findings Monitoring implementing entities for compliance with UPSNJP FM manual and PIM ; Together with MoF and under MoF’s guidance, conduct supervision, provide technical support and guidance to Regions and Cities including management on financial matters; Perform other duties assigned by the Project Coordinator. Level of effort and Timetable It is expected that the assignment is a full time job and will start in April 2024 depending on availability. The specialist will be based at UFSSNO under Ministry of Urban and Infrastructure with frequent travel to cities and regions and other destinations as necessary. Contract: one year contract, with possible extension upon satisfactory performance of the specialist /consultant. Expected Deliverables Review reports and comment on the Projects' financial progress. Monthly Progress Reports within 7 (seven) days of the end of the month on the consultant activities/ achievements during the month and plans for the next month. Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-annual and annual UPSNJP, Ministry level Project financial statements, semiannual financial reports, internal audit reports, annual external audit reports Quarterly expenditure forecast and cash requirement. Semiannual accounting reports, the format of which has been agreed, will be used to report on the use of Project resources. These reports will be submitted to the MoF based on agreed timetable on the FM manual Internal audit reports to the MoF and MUI within 30 days of completion of the audit report together with a proposed action plan. Summary of progress against UPSN&J PROJECT’s performance indicators semiannually. Regular semiannual financial report including variance analysis. Quarterly reports to identifying poor implementation and budget utilization Reconciliation of fund disbursed to the Project with the expenditure. Draft Final Report of the specialist/consultant’s work three weeks before the end of the assignment; and Final Report of the Consultant’s deliverables, one week after receiving comments from the coordinator. Qualifications Required The UPSNJP Financial Management Specialist/Consultant should have experience in financial management of Projects. He or she should have adequate knowledge and understanding of Project implementation, and experience with financial management. The Financial Management Specialist/Consultant should possess the following qualifications/competencies: MSc/BSc degree or equivalent in Accounting, Economics, Financial Management or related field of studies plus a minimum of a Post graduate diploma in Financial Management or Business Administration preferred. A minimum of 8/10 years’ experience for masters and bachelor respectively in GOE/IDA funded Projects thorough understanding of World Bank’s, Federal and regional government FM procedures, public sector finance and financial audit, including experience in similar Projects and geographic areas, with 5 years of experience in aspects of local government finance, accounting, internal and external audit. Training in FM or a professional qualification in Financial Management. At least 4 years’ experience in GOE/IDA funded Projects thorough understanding of World Bank’s, Federal and regional government financial management procedures Excellent report writing skills in both Amharic and English. Excellent command of computer Projects and applications with significant capabilities in computerized database, spreadsheet constructions and preferably knowledge of IBEX and IFMIS system. Excellent change management skills and strong commitment to sharing expertise and experience in order to develop others (helping others to achieve goals), resolving conflict successfully. Knowledge of the urban sector issues in Ethiopia is an advantage. Urban Productive safety Net and Job Project under Urban Food Security and Safety Net Office now invite eligible individual consultants/Specialists to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Specialist/Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Qualification and Experience as Financial Management Specialist in GOE/IDA funded Projects thorough understanding of World Bank’s, Federal and regional government FM procedures, public sector finance and financial audit, including experience in similar Projects and geographic areas and their capability on the basis of academic background, general and relevant experience, and knowledge of local condition. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III paragraph 3.16 and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Procurement In Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (recent Edition) (“Procurement Regulation”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance to Section VII para 7.34 to 7.39 of The World Bank Procurement Regulation based on qualification and relevant experience of the applicants to the assignment. Remunerations: will be as per the Ministry of Finance channel one salary scale. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 8:30 am to 12 in the morning and from 2:00 to 5:00 pm local time in the afternoon. Expressions of interest (including recent and comprehensive CV with a letter of application and other relevant supporting documents) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by April 01, 2024 on or before 4:00pm The address:-Attn:Ato Birhanu Teshome, Head, Urban Food Security and Safety Net Office Email- sbirhanu1@gmail.com and Ato Mesfin Ekubu, Urban Productive Safety Net and Job Project Procurement Specialist Email- mesfinekbupsnjp2@gmail.com In front of National Bank of Ethiopia, Ministry of Urban and Infrastructure, 5th floor, UPSNJP Procurement Section, Country: - Ethiopia.

title: Consultancy Service to Conduct Needs Assessment for Improving Child Stunting and Learning Poverty in SPG Woredas
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) COUNTRY : ETHIOPIA PROJECT: ETHIOPIA HUMAN CAPITAL OPERATION(HCO) Credit No./ Grant No.: 7341-ET/E206-ET/TF0C1474 Assignment : Consultancy firm selection to conduct Needs Assessment at Federal, Regional and the Human Capital Operation SPG woredas and areas affected by conflict, drought, and high level of refugees Reference No . - ET-MOF-HCO-003-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance has received financing from International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Ethiopia Human Capital Operation and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include conduct a needs assessment at the three levels of government (Federal , reginal and Woreda ) to identify, define and prioritize interventions for areas affected by conflict ,drought and high level of refuge in the most affected regions. The assessment is expected to cover all regions , all 42 Specific purpose grant(SPG) woredas and at least 23 of high risk non-SPG woredas. Scope of the service is limited human capital and related sectors at each level . The sector includes education, health, water, agriculture, women and social affairs, planning and development and refuges and returnees service. At woreda level it will cover selected SPG woredas and non -SPG woredas affected by conflict ((i.e. in Tigray, Amhara, Afar and Oromia) and woredas affected by drought and the internally displaced persons (i.e. in Somali, Afar, Oromia, South Ethiopia Region, South Western Ethiopia Region and Central Ethiopia Region) The specific tasks of the consultancy service include the following but not limited to :- Conduct needs assessment and review models of innovation to address learning poverty and reduce stunting in the selected SPG woredas which includes compile woreda profile in terms of human capital (population by age , number of facilities by functionality status) identify major factors for levels of stunting and learning poverty in the woreda, identify potential interventions for stunting and learning poverty and learning and nutrition windows in order prioritization for each woreda with cost estimate and review existing service delivery models in education and health sectors focusing on SPG woredas and list project interventions and activities Conduct needs assessment in at least 23 of woredas affected by conflicts, drought, IDPs and high levels of refugees covering identify accessibility, compile woreda profile in terms of human capital , identify facilities and materials in human capital sectors damaged by conflicts, estimate the proportion of the damage by conflict relative to total in woreda, main challenges in provision of basic service by Woredas, identify and prioritize key support areas with cost estimate and other as necessary, Assess needs for system strengthening and accountability for improved service delivery at all levels of government (identify technical expertise required , capacity gaps, identify challenges and capacity need for multisectoral coordination, planning and budgeting, assess needs in PFM (include PBB, government, procurement, reform, and environmental and social management ) and prioritize interventions at all levels. The estimated level of effort required for the consultancy service is 588.5 staff months for the period of 15 weeks of consultancy service period. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below. The Ministry of Finance is now inviting eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Demonstrated core business of the firm relevant to the assignment, with extensive experience of at least 5 years carrying out large-scale needs assessment at sub-national level in Ethiopia. Demonstrated Strong analytical skills and experience in using major survey software application, and a demonstrated ability to conduct interviews with a range of stakeholders, experience in pulling together analysis and data into reports. Demonstrate execution of three similar assignments and nature in the last five years Experience in reviewing and compiling multiple data sets and strong understanding of quantitative and qualitative analysis with Social Assessment A strong track record of delivering intensive large-scale fieldwork to a high standard and on-time delivery of services. A strong track record of continuous field presence in the geographical area, for at least the last 2 years A strong track record of delivering intensive large-scale fieldwork to a high standard and on-time delivery of services. Experience in carrying-out quantitative research and data collection an in Ethiopia is preferred, The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (edition ) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and cost Based Selection (QCBS) methods set out in the Procurement Regulations. title: Recruitment of individual consultant for Environmental Save guard Specialist Position for Digital Foundations Project
notice_text: Request for Expression of Interest (Consulting Services – Individual Consultant Selection) Selection of Environmental Safeguard Specialist for the Ethiopian Digital Foundations Project – Ministry of Innovation and Technology Country: Ethiopia Project: Ethiopia Digital Foundations Project Project ID: P171034 Credit No. IDA – 68560 Salary: Based on the directive of MoF Project staff Salary Scale Assignment Title: Environmental and Social Safeguard Specialist for Ethiopian Digital Foundations Project at the Ministry of Innovation and Technology Reference No.: ET-MInT-396966-CS-INDV The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital Foundations Project (“Digital Foundations”). The Ministry of Innovation and Technology, the host of the project intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting of individual consultants. Ministry of Innovation and Technology as part of the project implementation program is looking for an Environmental Safeguard Specialist that support and provide the program management with technical advice on environmental and social risk management (ESRM) issues that are under the scope of the Ethiopia Digital Foundations Project including all beneficiary institutes and stakeholders that support the project throughout its lifecycle. Experienced Environmental Safeguard Specialist who have relevant experience in the area of Environmental Safeguard (knowledge and experience in the World Bank financed projects is a plus) are invited to express their interest for the assignment. Manage procedures including the establishment of suitable field structure to ensure the appropriate level of support to technical and program management team Establish a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) / feedback mechanism and advise the Program Management Office and key stakeholders in the best practice of monitoring and reporting on the environmental impact of the project. Support in the coordination of capacity building and training activities to ensure the principles and procedures for Environmental Management Framework (EMF) are well understood and complied with by beneficiaries and project relying parties. Advice/guide the program office and the consultancy firm recruited to conduct the ESIAs on appropriate standards in line with Ethiopian Government, other institutions and World Bank policies. Ministry of Innovation and Technology now invites potential Environmental Safeguard Specialist’s to indicate their interest to provide the Services. Interested Candidates should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services for a period of one year with possibility of extension for additional period subject to outstanding performance and availability of budget. The shortlisting criteria include the following; At least a BA degree in a field relevant to Environmental sciences, preferably in Environmental System Analysis. At least 5 years of experience in Environmental studies . Demonstrated experience in large-scale development project management at various levels of Environmental Risk management activities, preferably for World Bank-funded infrastructure projects. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES -INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) GOVERNMENT OF THE FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA Position Public Employment Services (PES) Analyst / Expert / Consultant Organization: Ministry of Labor and Skills Project: Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project Location: Addis Ababa Duration: One Year (with possibility of extension upon satisfactory performance of the Consultant) Salary: As per the Ministry of Finance the channel one salary scale Reference No.: ET-MOLS-291139-CS-INDV Background The Ministry of Labour and Skills (MoLS) is a public and federal institution established under the newly proclamation in Ethiopia since 2021, with a mandate to govern, monitor, and coordinate all government and non-government efforts in labour and skills. The MoLS works specifically on: Identifying and designing new labour and skills opportunities; Building a coordination-platform for all labour and skills initiatives in Ethiopia; Developing and implementing sectorial labour and skills strategies; Formulating and adopting policies that favour job creation, private sector development, and the bridging of skill mismatch in the Ethiopian Labour Market. MoLS, in collaboration with the Ministry of Urban Development and Infrastructure (MoUDI) and the Ministry of Women and Social Affairs (MoWSA), is currently implementing the Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project (UPSNJP). UPSNJP builds on the successful Urban Productive Safety Net Project (UPSNP), which has been rolled out in 11 cities throughout the country. UPSNP’s objective is to improve the income of targeted households and establish urban safety net mechanisms through public works and livelihood support. The UPSNJP builds on the UPSNP by expanding the number of cities covered through the urban safety net mechanisms as well as strengthen social services to the urban poor and destitute. This component supports key elements of Ethiopia’s National Plan for Job Creation, through fostering the development of human capital (Subcomponent 2.1) and strengthening labor market intermediation (Subcomponent 2.2). Through active involvement of the MOLS in both subcomponents, the component will closely follow the road map envisioned under the national plan and seeks to institutionalize the project into wider systemic changes. The proposed interventions are based on rigorous research on urban labor markets in Ethiopia and in line with international best practices (see section II.F for lessons learned).[1] Subcomponent 2.1: Provide a First Work Experience for Less Educated Urban Youth (US$65.8 million equivalent) This subcomponent seeks to address key obstacles to labor market integration of young, less educated adults by providing a first work experience in the form of six-month apprenticeships in up to 11 cities. Certain obstacles to enter the labor market are particularly apparent for certain demographic groups, and the project will therefore target youth with a high school diploma or lower qualifications. Through apprenticeships, youth are expected to learn valuable soft and technical skills. The apprenticeship combined with soft skill training, basic digital literacy training, job search support, and certification at the end of the program are designed to substantially improve labor market prospects and signaling ability of the young beneficiaries. The apprentices will work 22 days per month for six months and receive a stipend of $2 per day, which will continue for three more months after successfully completing the apprenticeship to help with job search. This model is currently being piloted under the UPSNP in Addis Ababa, and lessons from this pilot will be used to scale up the intervention under the UPSNJP. The program has distinct features that together will provide a multifaceted approach to build skills and provide firms with potential apprentices: Selection of apprentices and firms will consist of several stages of registration, matching, interviews, and final selection, ensuring a high value proposition to apprentices and firms. Interested firms will be screened for their suitability for offering apprenticeships, including considerations of occupational health and safety (OHS) as well as Gender-Based Violence. Life skills, digital, and job search training will be provided through government entities and third parties as required based on a harmonized curriculum to guide potential beneficiaries in workplace behaviors, develop basic digital literacy skills, and strengthen their job search ability. Apprenticeships will be offered by private and public sector firms (MSMEs and large firms). A work and training plan will be required for each apprentice which will be supervised by a firm mentor and by local OSSCs. Successful apprentices and firms will receive a certificate of completion. Firms that successfully participate in the apprenticeship program and have potential for job intensive growth will be able to participate in a matching grant competition. This will be organized by the MoLS in collaboration with private sector representatives, building on successful models in Nigeria and elsewhere. Subcomponent 2.2. Strengthen Employment and Intermediation Services Effective labour market intermediation and employment services represent a necessary component of a well-functioning labour market, in which workers can explore and develop their full economic potential. The Government of Ethiopia is currently working on a comprehensive reform of Public Employment Services (PES) to support the job search process and improve job readiness in Ethiopia. The reform involves the establishment of a new PES structure with three levels of hierarchy: National Employment Agency, clusters/regional offices and job centres. The job centres will act as a single-window of service delivery for all job seekers either (i) looking for wage-employment or (ii) aiming to start their enterprises or (iii) looking for employment overseas, and in addition, the job centres will provide (iv) services for employers. The PES reform is composed of two components: rural and urban component. The urban component of the reform is being implemented starting from February 2021. The implementation of the urban component will be done in two phases: the inception phase and the scale-up phase. The core part of the inception phase will be the establishment of 15 job centres and 3 clusters/regional offices as a pilot in order to test different models of service delivery, reporting lines, and monitoring. The offices will be build using the existing infrastructure and human resources mainly of One Stop Service Centers (OSSC) and other offices where appropriate. The pilot will last for 18 months and will be subsequently evaluated using a combination of qualitative and quantitative methods. The information collected during the pilot and through the evaluation will be used to inform the design of the scale-up phase. To maximize program effectiveness, careful attention will be paid to the selection of participating youth and firms, and participants will be provided with necessary support including relevant training and stipends . The selection of beneficiaries will be based on multiple rounds of screening and interviews. Beneficiaries will be provided with financial support through stipends as part of the project. Participating firms will be selected based on suitability for providing apprenticeships and will be monitored throughout the course of the program by private sector associations to ensure adherence to work plans and relevant safeguards. To ensure successful matches between beneficiaries and firms, matching algorithms based on innovative tools including profiling surveys and behavioral games will be used.[2] About the Role The PES Analyst / Expert / Consultant will support the MoLS as a member of the management team responsible for supervising the establishment and operations of the pilot job centres and clusters/regional offices. He/she will support the Project Manager in coordinating different partners to ensure that offices have the required infrastructure, equipment and human resources to begin operations within a pre-specified timeline. Subsequently, the analyst will support the monitoring of the operations of the job centres to ensure effective and efficient service delivery, including by monitoring the process of service delivery, reporting and communication mechanisms within and between the offices, communication with clients, data collection processes etc. The Analyst will provide inputs as requested by the Project Manager. In addition, he/she is expected to provide just-in-time analytical advice on sub component 2.1 under the project as well. He/she will participate in meetings with MoLS and other stakeholders as required. Expected Deliverables The mission of the Analyst / Expert is to support the Project Manager in supervising the implementation of the pilot of 18 job centres and 3 clusters/regional offices. This includes: Contribute to the development of an implementation plan for the pilot job centres and clusters/regional offices, prepared in cooperation with MoLS. Prepare all necessary TORs, specifications for job centre design and infrastructure. Support the supervision of the preparatory phase (i.e., before opening the offices (refurbishment and procurement, recruitment and training, setting up the communication channels and reporting mechanisms, communication campaigns etc.). Support the supervision of the job centres during the service-delivery phase (service delivery to clients, reporting mechanism within and between offices, information collection, performance evaluation etc.). Contribute to the preparation of monthly reports on work accomplished, identification of problems and issues to be addressed and proposing corrective actions. Contribute to the preparation of written financial outputs, e.g. statements, projections etc. Contribute for the development and functionality of the Youth Employment MIS, and Labor Market Information System (LMIS). Prepare operational documents, manuals and guidelines. Support the project evaluation team by providing any information required. Contribute to developing a scale-up plan based on the learnings from the pilot. Perform other duties as assigned by MoLS. Requirements Academic specialization: A Master’s degree in business administration, management, economics, sociology, social science or a related field required. Experience: A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in public employment services, youth employment and job creation. Experience in implementing activities related to the labour market and social protection desired. Previous experience as public employment services specialist, youth employment specialist or similar positions with a strong reputation for developing excellent collaborative working relationships with Government Ministries and development partners. Strong analytical skills in economic and social dimensions of development, and basic understanding of Ethiopia’s economic and labor market policies. Excellent interpersonal communication skills and a strong set of personal values. Language: Fluent written and oral communications skills in English and Amharic required. Other skills: Software: Proficiency in standard word processor, spreadsheet editor, and presentation applications such as Microsoft Office required. Teamwork: Excellent interpersonal skills, with proven ability to work in an intercultural environment required. Client orientation: Ability to advise, influence and promote consensus among different stakeholders in the face of conflicting demands or directions required. Evaluation Criteria The following evaluation criteria will be used to select the procurement specialist: A. Educational Background – 20 % B. General Work Experience - 20 % C. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) COUNTRY: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia NAME OF PROJECT: CR-WaSH Credit No.: IDA-64450 Assignment Title: Consultancy service to Support Capacity Building Needs for Regional Climate Research and Modeling for Improved Climate Information for Ethiopian Meteorology Institute (EMI) Reference No .: ET-MOWE-383949-CS-QCBS Re-bid The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (FDRE) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementation of CR-WaSH (Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for this consulting service. Capacity Building Needs Objectives The objective of the advisory services is to enable EMI to equip skill and knowledge of RCM in order to produce high resolution climate information and apply it for local level impact assessment. The specific objectives of this assignment are: - To support long term climate change analysis To provide guidance to design a training program for regional climate modelling and impact assessment studies and the necessary computer programming skills necessary to implement regional climate modeling. In partnership with national experts, to contribute to building capacity in the use of regional climate modeling for different applications over Ethiopia. To strengthen the capacity of a Regional Climate Modeling Center at EMI. To lead the design of a strategic research program for EMI on regional climate modeling, in conjunction with partners from a national university. To develop and initiate working relationships on research with local and international universities Scope of the firm technical advisory The objective of the firm advisory services is to enable EMI to equip skill and knowledge of climate modeling to forecast long term climate scenarios with RCM/GCM and produce high-resolution climate information and apply it for local level impact assessment. In general, the consulting firm will cover the following task: - Review previous work to recommend best options that can be used for context of Ethiopia climate change analysis. Present the output and review the finding and selection of the approach, model, resolution, methodology, etc.. Develop a program on hands on training for EMI staff on regional climate modeling. The training program should not be limited but at least it should cover this aspects i.e background and purpose of GCM, RCM, model installation, data preparation/pre-processing, post processing of model outputs, and model verification. Support EMI to establish a regional climate modeling center by building staff capable of running RCMs. The advisor will guide EMI on the choice of appropriate RCM. Contribute to training technical staff on an overview of GCM, RCM and downscaling techniques, in partnership with national experts. Lead the development of a medium-term research agenda for EMI (5 years) Identify a clear research working environment on regional climate science between EMI, local and international universities and research institutes Assist EMI to develop full grant research proposal on the identified research agenda The assignment will perform in the form of Lump sum. The short listing criteria are: - core business and years in business, relevant experience, technical and managerial capability of the firm. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers of the World Bank. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT The major objective of the consultancy assignment is to assess and identify the development level or changes of Project Development Objective (PDO) indicators for consecutive three years in a yearly basis including intermediate results indicators by components which are targeted to increase the inclusiveness and affordability of digital services and digital job creation in Ethiopia. The analysis will have to cover the following specific objectives in the assignment: To analyze sustainability of results and outcomes of the project, To assess the capacity building efforts provided to the implementing agency (MInT) and other four beneficiary institutes, To assess the intervention / support given to the Small and Medium Scale Enterprises (SMEs) and startups in strengthening their capacity and able them to digitization, To examine the effectiveness of pre job and other trainings provided to the potential employees and jobs opportunity created and its contribution to productivity, To assess the extent of the environmental compliance issues during project implementation, To assess the performance of the project in terms of timeliness, quality, quantity and cost effectiveness of the activities undertaken including project procurement, To analyze the efficiency of fund utilization, To develop yearly M & E document regarding the indicators development, To publish yearly assessment results report in a good form (hardcover in both sides with some graphics). SCOPE OF SERVICES INCLUDES: The scope of the consultancy assignment is limited to assess, analyze and produce PDO indicators results reports by focusing on the indicators already set in the Project Appreasal Document /PAD/. Regarding the assessment and area coverage, a comprehensive review of the development and specific components objectives of the project at national level across all regional governments, i.e., to Woreda administrative level should addressed and all listed indicators will be covered. title: Selection and Employment of consulting firm for training and support to Operationalization of existing Ethiopia Meteorological Institute (EMI) Numerical Weather Prediction System with European Centre for Mid-Range Weather Forecasting for EMI, by MoWE.
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) COUNTRY: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia NAME OF PROJECT: CR-WaSH Credit No.: IDA-64450 Assignment Title: Selection and Employment of a consulting firm to provide Training and Support to Operationalization of existing Ethiopia Meteorological Institute (EMI) Numerical Weather Prediction System with European Centre for Mid-Range Weather Forecasting (ECMWF) Data Stream. Reference No .: ET-MoWE-343032-CS-QCBS Re-bid The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (FDRE) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementation of CR-WaSH (Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for this consulting service. Objectives of the Consultancy Services The objective of the consultancy services is to provide technical assistance for EMI to develop and improve their capacity on operational weather forecasting and the provision of weather services through training and operationalization. The specific objectives are: To assess capabilities for the existing NWP activities and identify knowledge gaps To propose activities to reduce identified knowledge gaps with and improving the weather and climate prediction capabilities / processes. To implement and operationalize the revised WRF modeling schemes To develop, demonstrate and help operationalize a forecast verification system and a verification procedure. To conduct training on NWP/using WRF package, and also on the use of GCM for generating seasonal forecast products. To develop WRF and GCM training material and operational manual. To identify the data which is essential for operation, research and training from ECMWF data stream To support EMI forecasters to provide accurate and reliable weather and climate forecasts in Ethiopia Scope of the consultancy Ethiopia had been struck by different weather and climate-related extremes at different times in its history. Most of the hazards are mainly drought and flood. As mentioned above, the purpose of this assignment is to improve the quality and timeliness of weather and climate forecast at different time scales in Ethiopia. This encompasses the assessment of Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models and climate modelling. The spatial and temporal extent of NWP and climate modeling need to be analyzed and should be ultimately presented in an easily understandable way appealing to EMI users. The consultancy work should give great emphasis on on-the-job training and operationalizing weather and climate forecasting. More specifically, the consultancy work should include the following but not limited to: Review available forecasting and climate modeling Consult all available works on weather and climate prediction modelling in Ethiopia including the current system at EMI, other technical agencies/ministries and research institutions/universities. Identify opportunities to consolidate national capacity and gaps Conduct a literature review ofgood practice in worldwide with comparative analyses on the advantages and disadvantages of the available forecast systems, data needs, reliability, etc… Reach out relevant contacts, as appropriate, to have their view and advice on the potential future system for Ethiopia. Capacity and gap assessment Identify knowledge and capacity gaps in coping with NWP, climate modeling as well as weather and seasonal to sub-seasonal forecasting. Develop a training program to improve he EMI capacity on NWP and GCM as well as weather and seasonal to sub-seasonal forecasts Prepare a detailed module for the training activities on weather and seasonal to sub-seasonal forecasts. Develop recommendations with prioritization of actions based on the review and assessment above, and translate them into a work plan to be implemented under this consultancy to provide technical support for EMI to improve their capacity on NWP and seasonal climate modeling as well as forecasting, noting there might be recommendations and actions beyond the scope of this consultancy. The work plan needs to be discussed and agreed with the client. Improvement of NWP, seasonal climate modeling and forecasting based on the work plan agreed with the client Integrate and use all available and usable data i.e. automatic weather station data, upper air data, ICPAC products… EMI has several types of data recording stations both digital and manual. Among 250 Automatic weather stations, currently data from only 50 stations are used for model verification and bias correction and for dynamical forecasting model (WRF) that has short term and seasonal forecasts. The consultant is expected to assess the feasibility to integrate the rest of data from other stations, preferably data from more AWS, aiming for 100% of AWS stations, should be usable for i) data assimilation, 2) model bias correction, and 3) verification to have a better representation of Ethiopian complicated topography in the model. The use of data for the model requires the understanding of the format of each data set and customize it by developing and applying specific script to fit for purpose. Modeling and Downscaling dynamical forecast for sub seasonal to seasonal scale (S2S) climate prediction. Customize and operationalize the WRF model with better initial and boundary conditions and help create sustainable modeling environment. The scale of model configuration will be consulted with the client to ensure an appropriate resolutions achieved Integrating a data assimilation module using 3Dvar and 4Dvar Use ECMWF initial condition data for WRF model initialization Test and verify the WRF model outputs for daily, sub seasonal to seasonal scale and recommend the verification methods. Apply the results of verification to re-calibrate WRF for better performance Configure the model on High Performance Computerin such a way that ensures sustainable operational work Downscaling of different regional and dynamical forecasting models for National consumption (regional organization like ICPAC have seasonal forecast for the region that can be downscaled for national consumption. Select a regional product that is suitable for Ethiopia Consult with a client to select the recommended forecast product, downscaling and bias correction techniques for S2S forecasting Recommend and set out ensemble of the multiple model products Develop operational schemes for the revised NWP and GCM modeling and forecasting that implement in national, zonal and district level. Operationalize the ensemble forecasting techniques of the WRF and GCMs both for short term (1day-9day), sub-seasonal to seasonal scale. This task should include documenting approaches, methods, and a training plan. The documentation of approaches and methods should follow standard scientific reporting techniques. Configuration should include automated system that enables the WRF model to start by itself and produce output with agreed format The consultative work should have documentation that comprises all approach and methods on model development, training and implementation parts. It should follow standard scientific reporting techniques Develop a user guide for model user and developer that can be used for any update needs and future uses. The user guide should include all model input data, configurations, calibration and verification assumptions, etc… WRF output with different options i.e EMI dissemination; MoWE that can be used for purpose of hydrological forecast WRF Hydro, etc,,, Providing training Provide training for all the activities that is conducted under this consultancy. Implement training according to the above mentioned and the greater emphasis should be put on operational on-the-job training, at least for three rainy seasons. The contract is Lump sum contract. The required professional staff-months are 21. The implementation period is also 7 months. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) & evaluation criteria for the assignment can be obtained from the Ministry Web site, https://www.mowe.gov.et/en/resource_types/tor The Ministry of Water and Energy (MoWE) now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. title: Additional Procurement and Contract Management Specialist at the Region PCU .
buyer: Oromia National Regional State Bureau of Agriculture
notice_text: Vacancy Announcement Oromia Bureau of Agriculture invites qualified applicants for the Resilient Landscapes and Livelihoods Project (RLLP) in the region for the following vacant position. Position Title: Regional Procurement Specialist Project Name: Resilient Landscapes and Livelihoods Project (RLLP) Project ID: P163383 Required number of positions: One Required Qualification She/he should have a minimum of First Degree in Purchasing Management, Logistic Management, Supplies Management, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management, and Public Procurement and Asset Management from recognized university. She/He should also have at Six years of practical experience in procurement management. The candidates should have sufficient experience working in projects financed by external donors. Knowledge of procurement policies and procedures of the Ethiopian Federal Public Procurement and that of the World Bank would be a requirement. Proficiency in computerized procurement management systems (STEP) is an mandatory. Excellent Communication and team working skills and proficiency of English and Afaan Oromo language (both written & spoken) are essentia. Tasks Summary The Regional Procurement Specialist will be responsible for procuring materials, planning, supervising and supporting the procuring entity to carry out the procurement activities in line with the World Bank procurement policy and procedure under the supervision of the Regional Procurement and Contract Management Specialist and National Senior Procurement and contract Management Specialist and BoA Procurement Department. Specific Tasks Procurement planning Initiate procurement requirements by different stakeholders of the project at all levels Ensure implementation of annual procurement plans consistent with PAD and Annual Work Plans respectively and in consultation with the concerned stakeholders; Monitor the status of the approved procurement plans on quarterly basis and update the plan accordingly Conduct market assessment and price trend analysis including the procurement of the project Support woredas to implement procurement in accordance with the agreed regulations and to use STEP properly. Provide inputs for the preparation annual work plan and budget Capacity building responsibilities Ensure the functionality of the Procurement Strategy Document (PPSD) Capacity the sub national team in managing and develop skill for STEP Develop systems and procedures of procurement functions and give advice to all implementing agencies (e.g., MoA and BoAs) to ensure that procurement is carried out according to World Bank and Government guidelines acceptable to the World Bank; Providing training and technical support to procurement staffs of the respective regional RLLP implementing Bureaus as required; Coordinate and conduct procurement training workshops for staff at all levels; Procurement Delivery and contract management Coordinate Tender/Evaluation Committee meetings, participate in tender evaluation and negotiation process and prepare evaluation reports and minutes; Ensure timely delivery of the procurement as per the contract time period Ensure timely payment of for the suppliers according to the contract and quality of delivery Prepare contract agreements to be signed by the BoA Respond to procurement enquiries and complaints by prospective bidders and/or bidders; Ensure annual and periodical procurement and finance audits and attend all audit queries on procurement Following the World Bank Standard Bidding Documents, prepare Request for Quotation, prepare bid documents and obtain the World Bank’s No Objection: Float tender and collect bid documents and prepare relevant paper work; Monitoring and support Update and maintain project procurement information, including: updated and consolidated project PP, contract registers; any logged project complaints with its resolutions and copies of all major documentations of the procurement process Assure the timely implementation of procurement related action plans Establish Procurement tracking system, STEP and monitor project procurement activities including dispatch of procurement documents; short-landings, damages and necessary arrangements for insurance; Conduct periodical supervision to the regions and project woredas on regular basis Documentation and reporting Prepare periodic status reports on the procurement of goods and services under the Project for submittal to MoA and the World Bank; Review project report, the Project Appraisal Document, the financing agreements, Implementation Support Mission aid memories, post procurement review mission reports to ensure that she/he is aware of the elements of established project agreements concerning procurement; issues arising and the requirements of governmental procurement systems; Carry out post procurement review, prepare reports and participate in the Mid-term Reviews of the World Bank Establish both hard and soft copy documentations mechanism for procurement documents at all levels Prepare and keep contract registration and filing procurements document Property administration Ensure annual inventory report of the fixed asset for next year procurement planning including the periodical fixed asset registry in line with financial management team Perform any other relevant duties that may be assigned by national and regional Procurement and Contract Management Specialists and National and Regional Project Coordinators; and Carry out all project procurement as assigned by the National and Regional Procurement and Contract management Specialist and the project coordinator. Deliverables The Procurement Specialist will be responsible for overall low to no risk procurement steps and outputs at all levels (Region, woreda and Community). Reporting Line/Communication The Procurement Specialist will report to the Regional Program Coordinators, and work closely with BoA procurement Directorate, other regional project implementing Bureaus, Woreda procuring entities and development partners mainly with the World Bank’s procurement staff. Duration of the Assignment The duration of the assignment will be for one year, but extendable depending on the satisfactory performance until the project period. Place of Work Oromia of Bureau of Agriculture at the Region with frequent travel to project woredas. Salary 29,625 (Twenty -Nine Thousand Six Hundred Twenty-Five Birr Only) per month.

title: Consultancy service fo Basin level study for Awash basin to identify and prioritize physical flood risk reduction investments and  conceptual design, detailed design, bidding document of selected physical investments (not including supervision )
notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA Ethiopia Flood Management Project (E-FMP) Grant No. E124-Et ASSIGNMENT TITLE Consultancy service for Basin level study for Awash basin to identify and prioritize physical flood risk reduction investments and conceptual design, detailed design, bidding document of selected physical investments. REFERENCE NO.: ET-MOWE-368687-CS-QCBS The Government of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Flood Management Project (E-FMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the provision of Feasibility Study, Detail Design and Tender Document Preparation of Upper, Middle and Lower Awash River Flood Risk Reduction Investment. GENERAL OBJECTIVES:-The overall objective of this project is to Feasibility Study, Detail Design and Tender document preparation for Awash River Flood Protection and Control. The principal objective of the intended scope of work is to carry out the feasibility study and detail design of Awash river flood risk reduction and associate infrastructures in order to safeguard the assets and life of the community and business sector that depends on Awash river. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES: Review of existing studies, including Upper, Middle & Lower Awash, as well as several dam projects Data audit, analysis and survey for facilitating the hydrological and hydraulic modelling Update of hydrological and hydraulic analysis and setting target flood events and sites Identify multiple options, select recommended option, and conceptual design covering associated infrastructures Carry out Hydraulic modelling and hazard mapping Study Application of the principles, methodology and structure of the Strategic Investment Framework for Flood Risk Reduction in Ethiopia Conduct Detailed Design Conduct Training and Capacity building throughout the consultancy SCOPE OF SERVICES: The scope of the service is limited to the geographic domain of the works that lies on Awash River main course starting from upstream starting point of the river up to the end of the river and near the confluence point of the major tributaries in the specified reach length. The major task of consultant firm is to carry out the Feasibility Study and Detailed Design of the Flood Risk Reduction and Associated Infrastructure with nationally and internationally known and Bank accepted standards. PERSON MONTH AND DURATION: It has 17 Person–Month implantation periods of 360 Calendar days from the end of January 2024. DETAIL TOR ATTACHED: The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at https://www.mowe.gov.et/en/resource_types/ToR-files-. The Ministry of Water and Energy now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. THE SHORTLISTING CRITERIA ARE: Firm’s core business and years in Business General and Similar Experience of the firms in the area of the assignment Technical and Managerial capability of the firm The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 updated in November 2020. Procurement will also comply with “Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants” revised as of July 1, 2016. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the QCBS method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 9:00 am to 12:00 am and 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm from Monday to Friday. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) on or before September 04, 2023 4:00 pm. notice_text: Request for Expression of Interest (Consulting Services – Firm Selection) Country: Ethiopia Project: Ethiopia Digital Foundations Project Project ID: P171034 Credit No. IDA - 68560 Assignment Title: Selection of a Consulting Firm that Develops the Government Office Modernization Roadmap Reference No.: ET-MINT-320079-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital Foundation Project (“Digital Foundations”). The Ministry of Innovation and Technology as one of the beneficiaries of the project intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) are expected to develop the Government Office Modernization Roadmap. The Ministry of Innovation and Technology/Ethiopian Digital Foundation Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants are requested to provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Core Business and Years in Business, proven direct experience in development of Government Office Modernization Roadmap, having at least five years of experience in developing ICT strategy and roadmap in general and at least two years of ICT modernization roadmap development in specific, and having a good Technical and Managerial Capability. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT The objective of the assignment is to develop the government office modernization roadmap, in relation to digital transformation, that will be expected to fill this gap in the existing body of knowledge regarding current status, existing challenges, weakness, strengths, opportunities and enabling the conditions of its services in the Ethiopian government offices using SWOT analysis. SCOPE OF SERVICES INCLUDES: The scope of this assignment is limited to the development of digital office modernization. It means that the project focus areas are digital integration of government offices for its smartness, workflow and process automation and IT modernizations. In the scope of this assignment, we may use digital office modernization, office modernization or IT modernization interchangeably in which they refer to the same. Furthermore, in this ToR, the term government office refers to all level of Ethiopia’s government offices, including federal and sub-national(regional) offices. However, inventory of Ethiopia’s government offices and sample size determination requires to apply scientific methods in the situational analysis, which will be considered as part of the roadmap development. The main scope of the assignment includes; Infrastructure Modernization: One of the most significant opportunities for government offices is to transform its office environment and its legacy IT either by upgrading or adopting/adapting the infrastructure. It is the backbone of an operating environment (e.g. workspace and IT/OT integration to create smart offices), storing vital data and applications. Data centre Migration Modernization : One specific and significant infrastructure modernization motion is data-centre migration. While migration efforts can involve the cloud adoption approaches detailed above, you can also upgrade your traditional, siloed, on-premises storage to more effective, high-performing options that better align to the desired government offices and agencies goals. Network Modernization: Legacy enterprise networks often lack the agility that today’s fast-moving, always-evolving business landscape requires. While transitioning to innovative solutions, such as Software-Defined Wide Area Networks (SD-WAN), which can be a complex process, newer connectivity solutions ultimately shall streamline and simplify the network environment. Application Modernization: Applications can build connections and improve engagement among government offices’ employees and customer base, but it becomes more challenging to support, scale and maintain apps as they age. These management roadblocks lead to frustrating user experiences that complicate customer interactions and stall internal collaboration - a pain point that can be amplified for younger users, who have grown acclimated to seamless digital engagement. Device Modernization: Along with the productive and collaboration applications, devices equip governments’ workforce with substantial impact on the employee experience. If end-user hardware is performing inadequately, reaching end-of-life imminently or failing to support a hybrid approach to work, a device refresh may be in order. Life-cycle Modernization: IT modernization isn’t limited to upgrading platforms and hardware. It can also reshape operational processes, including life-cycle management. The IT life-cycle describes the routine practices involved in keeping endpoints functional and equipped to meet business needs. Streamlining these practices is a key site of IT modernization that also simplifies other transformation efforts by optimizing resources and bolstering the organization’s ability to scale and adapt. Security Modernization: When IT leaders raise the subject of modernizing manual and legacy systems; they often hear stakeholders voice their fears that introducing new technologies will mean introducing new cyber-security risks. However, innovative technologies are not inherently riskier than their legacy counterparts - in fact, they may be easier to protect than existing systems, which can have security gaps of their own and often require a fragmented approach to threat defense. KEY DELIVERABLES; The expected output from the assignment is government office modernization roadmap for government offices to address the identified gaps and enhance existing legacy workflow and process managements, IT systems, infrastructures, platforms, management styles as detailed in the scope and background. The detail and appropriate methodology of the assignment is expected to be submitted as part parcel of the technical document (during the competition). The following are the main components of the deliverables of the assignment. Inception Report Present Situation (Gap) Analysis Government Office Modernization Roadmap Detailed and well documented methodology to address the gap analysis and to develop the roadmap The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing, Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016, Revised November 2017 and August 2018 “Procurement Regulations”, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. buyer: Ministry of Energy and Water Resource
notice_text: The Federal Government of Somalia Ministry of Energy and Water Resources REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) Country: Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) Name of Project: Somali Electricity Sector Recovery Project (SESRP) and Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Somalia (ASCENT Somalia). Project ID : P173088 Grant No.: IDA – D9310 Assignment Title: Technical Consultant for Women Incubators in the Energy Sector of Somalia Reference No.: SO-MOEWR-488742-CS-INDV Place of assignment: Mogadishu, Somalia 1. Background The Government of Somalia has received a grant from the World Bank to implement the Somali Electricity Sector Recovery Project (SESRP) and Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Somalia (ASCENT Somalia) projects. The Project Development Objective of SESRP is to increase access to electricity services and to re-establish the electricity supply industry in the Project Areas and the Project Development Objective of ASCENT Somalia is to increase access to sustainable and clean energy through private sector participation in Somalia. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources (the Ministry) has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) to carry out the day-to-day activities of project planning, coordination, and implementation of the Somali Electricity Sector Recovery Project (SESRP) and Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Somalia (ASCENT Somalia) projects. The SESRP comprises of the following four components: (i) Sub-transmission and distribution network reconstruction, reinforcement, and operations efficiency in the major load centers of Mogadishu and Hargeisa; (ii) Hybridization and battery storage systems for mini grids; (iii) Stand-alone solar off-grid access to public institutions (Health and Education); (iv) Institutional Development and Capacity Building. The ASCENT Somalia project comprises three components: (i) Distributed Renewal Energy (DRE) with Solar PV (SPV) and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in the capital city of Mogadishu and other major load centers in the Federal Members States (FMS); (ii) Electricity Distribution Network Rehabilitation and Reinforcement of the mini grids serving the Mogadishu capital city area and other FMS major load centers and, (iii) Sector Capacity and Institution Enhancement and Project Implementation Support. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources (MoEWR) therefore intends to apply part of the proceeds of the SESRP project to hire a consultant to work as a Technical Consultant for Women Incubators in the Energy Sector of Somalia at the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, FGS, for the World Bank – financed electricity sector recovery project. 2. Scope of Work and Responsibilities: The scope of work for the assignment includes but not limited to the following tasks: The Technical Consultant shall provide technical guidance, and support to the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources (MOEWR) and the Project Implementation Unit (PIU). The consultant shall perform the following but not limited to: (i) Conduct a Thorough Analysis and Assessment of Skills Gaps, (ii) Develop the Blueprint for the Design of the Incubator, (iii) Establish a Program Framework; (iv) Develop a Pilot Program for Bridging Skills Gaps; and (v) Develop a Pilot Program for Integrating Gender Perspectives in Private Sector. The Technical Consultant shall perform all other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment that can be found at the following website: www.sesrp.moewr.gov.so or can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail provided below. 3. Selection Criteria: Selection shall be based on qualification and experience of the candidate and followed by an interview. The minimum qualification, experience and skills should include: A minimum of a master’s degree in Gender Studies, Educational Leadership, Social Sciences, or a related field. A master's degree is an added advantage; Minimum of 8 years of combined experience in gender equality, women’s empowerment, social inclusion, education, and engineering, with a focus on leadership roles; Demonstrated experience designing and implementing leadership development programs, mentoring, coaching, and capacity-building initiatives for women, especially in traditionally male-dominated sectors such as STEM fields; Experience collaborating with national and international organizations, government entities, and private sector stakeholders to advance gender and inclusion objectives; and Familiarity with international and national policies on gender equality, women’s rights, leadership, and energy sector standards. 4. Duration: The consultant will be engaged for a period of six (6) months from the effective date of the contract. 5. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing these services. Interested Individual Consultants must submit the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV), (ii) Copies of certificates of academic qualifications, (iii) 3 reference persons; and (iv) Expressions of Interest (EOI) indicating that they are qualified to perform the services. 6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultants Selection method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations . 8. Mode of submission of Applications and deadline: Interested Consultants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference at the address given below from 8:30 to 3.30pm Mogadishu time (Excluding public holidays). Interested Individual Consultants must submit (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV), (ii) Copies of certificates of academic qualifications, (iii) 3 references persons, (iv) Expressions of interest (EOI), and must be delivered (in person or by e-mail) in a written form in three (3) hard copies (if not by e-mail) to the address below by 10th June 2025 at 4:00 PM (Mogadishu Time) – Subject marked clearly as – Application for Technical Consultant for Women Incubators in the Energy Sector of Somalia Project Implementation Unit (PIU) Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, Federal Government of Somalia, Email: sesrp.procurement@gmail.com
